pages.title: Tema 161, Cómo devolver un reembolso erróneo, Cheque impreso o depósito directo | Internal Revenue Service
pages.description: Tema 161, Cómo devolver un reembolso erróneo, Cheque impreso o depósito directo
pages.text: Tema 161, Cómo devolver un reembolso erróneo, Cheque impreso o depósito directo | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Tema 161, Cómo devolver un reembolso erróneo, Cheque impreso o depósito directo English Español 中文 (繁體) 한국어 Русский Tiếng Việt Más en Ayuda Asistente tributario interactivo Herramientas Denunciar fraude (en inglés) Estafas tributarias Robo de identidad Avisos y cartas Apelaciones Preguntas Frecuentes (en inglés) Accesibilidad Comuníquese con su oficina local del IRS Comuníquese con una oficina internacional del IRS Temas Tributarios Otros Idiomas (en inglés) Se considera que es un reembolso erróneo si recibe un reembolso al cual usted no tiene derecho de recibir o si recibe una cantidad mayor de la que tiene derecho de recibir. Si su reembolso fue expedido en forma de cheque impreso y dicho cheque del Tesoro no ha sido cobrado : Escriba la palabra " Void " (Inválido) en la sección de la firma de endoso, al dorso del cheque. Devuelva el cheque inmediatamente pero no más tarde de 21 días, a la oficina del IRS correspondiente. El lugar de envío depende de su estado de residencia. Utilice la dirección postal que aparece en la página de Información sobre el Formulario 3911 (en inglés) del estado en el que vive. No engrape, doble ni le ponga presillas al cheque. Incluya una nota que diga " Return of erroneous refund check " (Devolución de un cheque de reembolso erróneo) y explique brevemente el motivo por el cual devuelve el cheque de reembolso. Si su reembolso fue expedido en forma de cheque impreso y dicho cheque del Tesoro ha sido cobrado: Visite nuestra página de pagos para encontrar formas de pagar electrónicamente. Si no puede pagar electrónicamente, envíe un cheque personal, giro postal o cheque de caja inmediatamente, pero no más tarde de 21 días, a la oficina del IRS correspondiente. El lugar de envío depende de su estado de residencia. Utilice la dirección postal que aparece en la página de Información sobre el Formulario 3911 (en inglés) del estado en el que vive. Escriba en el cheque o giro postal: “Payment of erroneous refund” (Pago de reembolso erróneo), el período tributario para el cual se expidió el reembolso, el tipo de cuenta ya sea archivo maestro de personas físicas (IMF, por sus siglas en inglés) o archivo maestro de negocios (BMF, por sus siglas en inglés) y su número de identificación del contribuyente (número de Seguro Social, número de identificación del empleador o número de identificación personal del contribuyente). Incluya una breve explicación del motivo por el cual devuelve el reembolso. Cobrar un reembolso erróneo de esta manera podría resultar en intereses adeudados al IRS . Si su reembolso se hizo por depósito directo : Comuníquese con el Departamento de Cobros Automáticos ( Automated Clearing House ) ( ACH , por sus siglas en inglés) del banco o la institución financiera que recibió el depósito directo y pídales que le devuelvan el reembolso al IRS . Llame al IRS gratuitamente al 800-829-1040 (personas físicas) o 800-829-4933 (negocios) (consulte la asistencia telefónica para conocer los horarios de atención) para explicar por qué devuelve el depósito directo. Los intereses se pueden acumular en el reembolso erróneo. Cuando la cantidad del reembolso (ya sea por cheque impreso o depósito directo) difiere de lo que esperaba, lo que indica que el IRS cambió la cantidad, se le enviará por correo un aviso explicando el ajuste, a su dirección que figura en el registro. Por favor revise la información del aviso para determinar si el cambio al reembolso es correcto. El aviso incluye un número telefónico gratuito, en caso de que necesite asistencia adicional. Living with Asthma For Everyone Aug. 28, 2026 Español Key points Everyone with asthma needs their own Asthma Action Plan. Work with your health care provider to create a plan that works for you. You can prevent and control asthma attacks. Asthma Action Plans Everyone with asthma needs their own Asthma Action Plan. Work with your health care provider to create a plan that works for you. Your goal is to prevent and control your asthma attacks. Create your own Asthma Action Plan Click below to download a fillable PDF for your use. CDC's Asthma Action Plan Tool Green Zone: Doing Well? If I'm doing well... I don't have cough, wheezing, chest tightness, or trouble breathing at any time. I can do all the things I usually do. When I use a peak flow meter my peak flow* is more than 80 percent or more of my best peak flow. Continue taking your daily controller medicine. *Peak flow measurement is a quick test to measure air flowing out of the lungs. Yellow Zone: Getting worse? If my asthma is getting worse... I have some cough, wheezing, chest tightness, or trouble breathing. Or I wake up at night because of my asthma. Or I can't do some of the things I usually do. Or When I use a peak flow meter my peak flow* is half to about three quarters of my best peak flow. Add your reliever medicine and continue your daily controller medicine. If your symptoms get better after an hour keep checking them and continue your daily controller medicine. Red Zone: Medical alert? If I'm having a medical alert... I have a lot of trouble breathing. Or My reliever medicines don't help. Or I can't do any of the things I usually do. Or I was in the yellow zone for 24 hours and I'm not getting better. Or When I use a peak flow meter my peak flow* is less than half of my best peak flow. Add any other medicines your doctor has prescribed and call your doctor. If your symptoms don't get better and you can't reach your doctor, go to the hospital. *Peak flow measurement is a quick test to measure air flowing out of the lungs. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Public Input & Actions BLM and USWFS Plan Prescribed Fire Treatments near Parker Reducing wildfire risk and maintaining public access along the Colorado River Arizona Colorado River DO Lake Havasu FO Media Contact BLM Arizona Newsroom BLM_AZ_Newsroom@blm.gov BLM Office: Lake Havasu Field Office October 20, 2026 LAKE HAVASU CITY, Ariz. — The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the U.S. Wildland Fire Service (USWFS) plan to conduct prescribed fire treatments near Parker periodically from late October through Dec. 31, 2026, as weather, fuel and air quality conditions allow. The treatment area is about seven miles northeast of Parker and a half mile west of Parker Dam Road near Crossroads Campground , on the California side of the Colorado River. USWFS personnel will conduct the prescribed fire and monitor the area throughout the operation. Information about specific upcoming and active burns is available online . The use of prescribed fire will dispose of piles of cut vegetation accumulated during site maintenance and firebreak construction. Removing these hazardous fuels will help reduce wildfire risk and improve access to the river in this recreation area. Multiple burn sessions may be needed to complete the work. What the public should know: Smoke may be visible during operations and may settle in low-lying areas overnight. Nearby residents are encouraged to close windows if smoke affects their area. Motorists encountering smoke should slow down and use headlights. People with heart or lung conditions or other smoke sensitivities should monitor local air quality and follow guidance from their health care providers. Access to the treatment area may be temporarily restricted for public safety. Firefighters will ignite vegetation piles only when weather, fuel and air quality conditions meet prescribed fire requirements. USWFS personnel will stay on-site to monitor prescribed fire and ensure public and resource safety. For information about prescribed fire activities and potential recreation impacts on lands managed by the BLM Lake Havasu Field Office , call 928-505-1200 . Follow our social media for updates on prescribed burn activities and more on BLM Arizona Facebook or X . The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations. pages.title: Driver drinking from wine bottle among shocking images captured by AI cameras British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The technology could be widely rolled out after nearly 19,000 offences were spotted in two weeks.
pages.text: Driver drinking from wine bottle among shocking images captured by AI cameras Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Wine-drinking driver among shocking images caught in AI camera trial 1 day ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Shehnaz Khan West Midlands PA Media The trial captured one image showing a front-seat passenger holding a small child who was unrestrained with no seatbelt on An artificial intelligence trial has uncovered nearly 19,000 potential driving offences in two weeks, including a driver drinking from a bottle of wine and another inhaling from balloons. AI-powered cameras installed outside Ladywood fire station in Birmingham and Fallings Park in Wolverhampton also captured drivers holding mobile phones at the wheel and failing to wear seatbelts. Mat MacDonald, the West Midlands Road Safety Commissioner, described the findings highlighted a "huge problem" with driving behaviours in the region. He said another image, which showed a child "sitting unrestrained on a front passenger's lap", was "particularly shocking". He said the findings pointed to a "widespread culture" of dangerous driving behaviours. "What this trial has shown to me more than anything else, is we have a huge problem with these potentially lethal behaviours behind the wheel," he said. WMCA The cameras were installed outside Ladywood fire station in Birmingham and Fallings Park in Wolverhampton The AI cameras have been "trained to recognise certain patterns", such as drivers who appear to be using mobile phones Speaking about images that were captured during the two-week trial, which took place in March, MacDonald said he was not surprised by the number of drivers that were captured using mobile phones. "I was equally disturbed, but not entirely surprised by numbers around mobile phones, specifically," he said. "I travel by foot a lot, and it is almost impossible to get as far as the end of your street without seeing someone who is dialling and driving." MacDonald added: "There was one particularly galling photo of someone drinking from a bottle of wine." Press Association AI cameras captured drivers holding mobile phones behind the wheel and failing to wear seatbelts Simon Foster, West Midlands police and crime commissioner previously said the findings of the trial were "deeply concerning". "We are closely evaluating these trial results to consider how this advanced AI technology can be deployed for future police enforcement," he said. Road safety data from 2025 showed mobile phone use was linked to 32 deaths on UK roads while unfastened seatbelts were linked to 133 deaths, the WMCA said. MacDonald, former chairman of campaign group Better Streets for Birmingham and an NHS doctor, said he was hopeful of the potential to roll the AI cameras out more widely in the future. "I am working very hard to see what we can do to make this technology a reality on the roads in the West Midlands," he told the BBC. "Hopefully this is the first step towards something that will enable us to start getting a grip of these types of behaviours, which... can end lives and ruin people's futures." WMCA Images captured includes a driver who appears to have his seatbelt plugged in behind him and is holding a mobile phone at the wheel MacDonald said the trial was actually stopped earlier than planned because of how many possible road offences were being detected. The technology identified 11,045 potential seatbelt offences and 1,163 potential mobile phone offences at Ladywood, and 6,030 potential seatbelt offences and 757 potential mobile phone offences at Fallings Park. No enforcement was planned as a result of the trial, which was funded by the West Midlands Combined Authority (WMCA) working with the police and fire service. pages.title: Oakland homicides fall to 25-year low – how did it stem the violence? | California | The Guardian
pages.description: Despite Trump’s claims, California city has found success in lowering deadly violence, thanks to pioneering efforts to steer people down a different path
pages.text: Oakland homicides fall to 25-year low – how did it stem the violence? | California | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation A view of Oakland looking east. Photograph: Tim Hussin/The Guardian View image in fullscreen A view of Oakland looking east. Photograph: Tim Hussin/The Guardian Guns and lies California This article is more than 7 months old Oakland homicides fall to 25-year low – how did it stem the violence? This article is more than 7 months old Despite Trump’s claims, California city has found success in lowering deadly violence, thanks to pioneering efforts to steer people down a different path Supported by About this content Abené Clayton in Oakland Mon 16 Mar 2026 10.00 EDT Last modified on Mon 16 Mar 2026 12.56 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google I n the summer of 2025, as Donald Trump rolled out his plan to deploy the national guard to Washington DC and Chicago, he suggested other American cities were overrun with violence and could soon see federal troops: Memphis, Los Angeles, New York. Oakland, the president argued , was beyond saving. “And then you have, of course, Baltimore and Oakland. They’re so far gone. We don’t even talk about that any more,” Trump said. But as Trump was making these comments, Oakland was in the midst of a historic drop in homicides. The Bay Area city ended 2025 with 67 people killed, according to data from the Oakland police department, half of its 2021 high of 134. It’s the lowest number of violent deaths recorded in 25 years. Chart showing the drop in homicides in Oakland The news has been held up by city officials, community advocates and non-profit leaders as a sign that their respective and – sometimes combined – efforts to stem the violence are making a difference for those living in the city. And it has proved especially meaningful given the ground that was lost during the Covid pandemic, when the city faced deep economic woes and more than 100 people were killed in a single year for the first time since 2012. “There was this narrative after the pandemic – and it carries into today – that things [in Oakland] are worse than they’ve ever been,” said Nicole Lee, the founder and executive director of Urban Peace Movement (UPM), a local non-profit. “And sometimes these narratives get hijacked so people can use fear to control others. People sell products using fear, they win elections using fear. So it’s important to acknowledge when we see improvements.” Local leaders each credit different trends when discussing the decline. Lee and other non-profit leaders emphasize the city’s strong community networks and investments in historically neglected neighborhoods. The police chief says new technology and better coordination with departments in neighboring cities has helped to solve crimes. They all agree, though, that there’s no one magic solution to stopping shootings, car break-ins and burglaries. Rather, they say, cooperation among city leaders, community organizations and law enforcement has helped steer the people police have identified as driving the violence down a different path. While the decrease is a promising sign, it does not completely capture the experiences of people living in the city of over 443,000, especially of those who have lost loved ones to violence. Earlier this month, a 33-year-old woman and a 25-year-old man were killed and seven others were injured in a mass shooting at a bar in the city’s downtown. “It’s about trying to hold two perspectives at the same time, which is not an easy thing to do,” said Lee. “Even though there have been some gains made, even one loss of life to gun violence is devastating. For families, their life is never the same, and that has a real impact on our community and how we relate to each other in our day-to-day lives.” Nor has the decline been equally distributed. Residents of East and West Oakland, where shootings have historically been concentrated, are still subject to the lion’s share of the gun violence. Twent

pages.title: Inside Paul Sereno's dinosaur hunt through the world’s fiercest desert | National Geographic
pages.description: Inside the boldest fossil hunt ever attempted.
pages.text: Inside Paul Sereno's dinosaur hunt through the world’s fiercest desert | National Geographic By Paul Sereno Photographs by Keith Ladzinski Published July 15, 2025 As the Saharan sun rose on my waylaid team, one morning in September 2022, it seemed to burn with particular intensity. For nearly three weeks we’d been holed up in a mud-walled compound in the oasis town of Agadez, in central Niger, stalled because of officials’ insistence on assembling for us a large armed escort. Now, as dawn broke, we were finally ready to embark: Nearly a hundred people packed into 15 vehicles, a motley caravan of SUVs, pickups, and one large dump truck, all strapped with sand ladders and spare tires, heading out on an extraordinary desert dinosaur hunt—without question, the most ambitious of my career. ( "Lost" Fortresses of Sahara Revealed by Satellites) Among our number were Tuareg guides and drivers, a film crew, 64 armed guards, and my paleo dream team of 20 students and freshly minted professors, recruited to spend three months venturing across one of the planet’s least hospitable landscapes. Our mission was to explore and excavate three distinct sites, spread across hundreds of miles of blazing, roadless desert. The fossils we found we would ship to my University of Chicago Fossil Lab for careful cleaning and study, later returning them for display in Niger, to celebrate the country’s stunning ancient heritage. ( Out With the Old Stegosaurus) I had crisscrossed Niger’s Sahara during 11 previous expeditions going back 32 years. The last two, in 2018 and 2019, had been for reconnaissance, and I’d spotted bone-rich pockets in some of the desert’s most remote and sandswept corners, with dinosaur skeletons jutting from the desert floor. But without the team or tools to collect them, I could only log the sites and imagine our return trip. Then a global pandemic shut down the world, and I spent two years drawing up an audacious plan—and fundraising, with little success. That is, until a benefactor, requesting anonymity, agreed to fully fund the quest. My appeal had aimed at our innate human curiosity, a chance to uncover creatures from paleontology’s last great frontier. ( This incredibly rare burial ground reveals new secrets about the Sahara's lush, green past. ) Ancient mud captured the footprint of an unknown species of sauropod. The expedition found fossils from what Sereno says are many newly identified species. Niger is a dino wonderland because of two chance geologic events. The first unfolded 180 million years ago, during the early Jurassic, when the great landmass Gondwana began to break apart, forming a massive depression in the center of what is now the West African nation, then a verdant region teeming with life. For millions of years, the depression took in sediment and the skeletons of dinosaurs and other creatures. The second event happened 20 million years ago, when a volcanic hot spot raised what’s known as the Aïr Massif on the edge of this depression, tilting the strata upward and returning to the surface the now fossilized skeletons. Driving across these rock layers today, heading from Agadez into the open desert, is a journey through deep time. Our timeline was ambitious even before the delay in Agadez, and the expedition’s success would hinge on benefiting from lessons I’d learned in the past, along with some novel technology we would deploy in the field. Our perseverance would be tested—many of my young colleagues had never set foot in the Sahara, worked under armed guard in 130-degree heat, or gone a month without a shower. Those with me on previous expeditions, meanwhile, had seen it all: food poisoning, malaria, sandstorms, expedition-ending breakdowns, gun-toting bandits, government coups. And yet I am always eager to go back. Gusty winds make operating drones tricky in the Sahara, but Sereno’s team used aerial footage to prospect, map digs, and find campsites. pages.description: Perdí mi cheque de reembolso. ¿Cómo consigo uno de reemplazo?
pages.text: Preguntas sobre Reembolsos | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content English Español Más en Ayuda Asistente tributario interactivo Herramientas Denunciar fraude (en inglés) Estafas tributarias Robo de identidad Avisos y cartas Apelaciones Preguntas Frecuentes (en inglés) Accesibilidad Comuníquese con su oficina local del IRS Comuníquese con una oficina internacional del IRS Temas Tributarios Otros Idiomas (en inglés) Pregunta Perdí mi cheque de reembolso. ¿Cómo consigo uno de reemplazo? Respuesta Si ha perdido su cheque de reembolso, debe iniciar un rastreo del reembolso: Utilice Dónde está mi reembolso , llámenos al 800-829-1954 y utilice el sistema automatizado o hable con un representante llamando al 800-829-1040 (consulte la ayuda por teléfono para conocer las horas de operación). Sin embargo, si usted presentó una declaración de casado en conjunto, no puede iniciar un rastreo utilizando los sistemas automatizados. Debe llamar y hablar con un representante para iniciar el proceso o descargue y complete un Formulario 3911, Declaración del Contribuyente sobre el Reembolso PDF . Su reclamo por un reembolso perdido se procesa en una de dos maneras: Si el cheque no fue cobrado, recibirá un reembolso de reemplazo una vez que se cancele el cheque original. Si el cheque de reembolso si fue cobrado, la Oficina del Servicio Fiscal (BFS, por sus siglas en inglés) le proporcionará un paquete de reclamación que incluye una copia del cheque cobrado. Siga las instrucciones para completar el paquete de reclamación. La BFS revisará su reclamo y la firma en el cheque cancelado antes de determinar si pueden emitir un reembolso de reemplazo. La investigación de la BFS puede tardar hasta seis semanas en completarse. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Public Input & Actions BLM and USWFS Plan Prescribed Fire Treatments in the Hualapai Mountains Reducing the threat of wildfire, protecting communities, and restoring public lands Arizona Colorado River DO Kingman FO Media Contact BLM Arizona Newsroom BLM_AZ_Newsroom@blm.gov BLM Office: Kingman Field Office October 20, 2026 KINGMAN, Ariz. — The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the U.S. Wildland Fire Service (USWFS), in cooperation with the Pinion Pine Fire District, Pine Lake Fire District, Mohave County Parks, and Mohave County Emergency Management, plan to conduct prescribed fire treatments from late October through Dec. 31, as weather, fuel and air quality conditions allow. Operations are planned near the community of Pine Lake, Hualapai Mountain Park, the Potato Patch and Getz Peak communication sites, and BLM's Wild Cow Springs Campground . These carefully planned treatments will reduce hazardous fuels, help protect nearby communities and improve the health of public lands. Information about specific upcoming and active burns is available online . To ensure the safety of residents and visitors, USWFS fire personnel will conduct prescribed fire only when weather, fuel and air quality conditions meet established parameters. Fire personnel use natural features and constructed control lines to help keep fire within planned treatment areas and take steps to minimize smoke impacts on nearby communities. Smoke management will follow Arizona Department of Environmental Quality regulations. What the public should know: Smoke may be visible during operations and may settle in low-lying areas overnight. Nearby residents are encouraged to close windows if smoke affects their area. Motorists encountering smoke should slow down and use headlights. People with heart or lung conditions or other smoke sensitivities should monitor local air quality and follow guidance from their health care providers. Access to the treatment area may be temporarily restricted for public safety. Follow our social media for updates on prescribed burn activities and more on BLM Arizona Facebook or X . The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations. pages.title: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.
pages.text: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Getty Images The leaders of the US, Russia and China will meet late next week, according to the White House Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping are planning to meet on the sidelines of a summit in China next week, the White House has said. The historic meeting between the respective leaders of the US, Russia and China will take place as Trump attends the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (Apec) summit in the southern city of Shenzhen, spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters. "The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous," she said. It is understood Iran may also be discussed during the meeting of the world's biggest nuclear powers, but not Ukraine. Russia has confirmed the meeting. China has yet to react. No agreement was expected to follow the talks, an unnamed, senior US official said, according to news agencies AP and Reuters. Trump will arrive in Shenzhen late on Wednesday for the two-day summit between the 21 member states. He will also take part in bilateral talks with Xi on Thursday - their fourth meeting since the US president returned to office in 2025. "President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the president of the United States, the president of the People's Republic of China, and the president of the Russian Federation," Wales said. She said Trump's trip, which will also include attending an Association of South-east Asian Nations (Asean) summit in the Philippines on Tuesday, would "secure historic wins to the American people and advance America's interests in the Indo Pacific". A nuclear weapons control treaty between the US and Russia expired in February, leaving the world's biggest nuclear arsenals without major guardrails and effectively marking an end to the arms control co-operation that helped resolve the Cold War. The UN has urged both sides to agree a new framework without delay. Trump however said he could replace the deal with a better agreement that included China , which has been building up its arsenal. Former senior US officials and analysts told the BBC at the time that seeking Beijing and Moscow's co-operation could create major hurdles and take years. Xi separately hosted both Putin and Trump in Beijing just days apart earlier this year, while the US president welcomed his Chinese counterpart to Washington in September. Beijing has become a crucial trading partner for Moscow since it launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, which has isolated Russia and left it subject to Western sanctions. But a controversial US deal to import Russian diesel and the suspension of sanctions targeting the biggest buyers of Moscow's oil and gas - including China - heightened European concern about the Trump administration's softening towards the Kremlin last month. Trump and Xi have meanwhile sought to project warmer ties at summits in Beijing and Washington this year - though little significant progress appeared to have been made on key issues such as trade, their race for AI dominance, and Taiwan. The war in Iran has also been a sticking point, with Beijing the largest buyer of Tehran's oil and its largest trade partner. Chinese state media reported on Friday that Xi would take part in "bilateral" talks on the sidelines of the Apec summit, citing a foreign ministry spokesman, but has not reported on the trilateral meeting. pages.title: Barbara Lee forged a historic path in Congress. Does Oakland want her back for mayor? | Oakland | The Guardian
pages.description: The progressive icon, 78, may be the frontrunner, but a more moderate contender may represent much-needed change
pages.text: Barbara Lee forged a historic path in Congress. Does Oakland want her back for mayor? | Oakland | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Barbara Lee in Oakland, California, on 25 February 2023. Photograph: Melina Mara/The Washington Post via Getty Images View image in fullscreen Barbara Lee in Oakland, California, on 25 February 2023. Photograph: Melina Mara/The Washington Post via Getty Images Oakland This article is more than 1 year old Barbara Lee forged a historic path in Congress. Does Oakland want her back for mayor? This article is more than 1 year old The progressive icon, 78, may be the frontrunner, but a more moderate contender may represent much-needed change Lauren Gambino Mon 14 Apr 2025 10.00 EDT Last modified on Mon 14 Apr 2025 10.19 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google B arbara Lee represented Oakland in Congress for a quarter-century. Now, in what would probably be the capstone of her storied political career, the 78-year-old progressive icon is vying for the chance to lift the “city I love” out of crisis. “I’m always ready to fight for Oakland,” Lee said, announcing her bid to lead the city of roughly 440,000 residents, known for its liberal politics and deep legacy of civil rights activism. When she entered the mayoral race in January, she was widely seen as the presumptive frontrunner. But in the months since, the race has tightened considerably, as her leading opponent, the former city council member Loren Taylor, gains ground. The 47-year-old engineer is aiming for an upset in Tuesday’s special election, tapping into a wave of discontent with progressive leadership that has swept the San Francisco Bay Area in recent years – and led to the recall of Oakland’s mayor, Sheng Thao , in November. “It’s not about whether or not we appreciate her service in Congress,” Taylor said in an interview as he made his final pitch to voters in east Oakland over the weekend. “It’s about what we need right now to fix Oakland’s problems – and particularly with the urgency that Oaklanders need.” The next mayor of Oakland must immediately confront a gaping budget deficit as well as a housing crisis that has given rise to sprawling homeless encampments. While violent crime fell sharply in 2024, persistently high rates of property crime – coupled with the widespread perception that Oakland is unsafe – continue to take a toll on the city. Over the last decade, Oakland has seen an exodus of its professional sports teams . Many businesses and retailers have left town, citing safety concerns. In-N-Out closed its only Oakland location last year, a first in the burger joint’s history. Kaiser Permanente, one of the city’s largest employers, has scaled back its downtown presence. Adding to the turmoil, Thao was recently indicted on federal bribery charges; she has pleaded not guilty. View image in fullscreen Loren Taylor gets a smile from his mom, Linda Taylor, before canvassing in Oakland, on 14 October 2018. Photograph: San Francisco Chronicle/Hearst Newspapers/Getty Images In her homecoming pitch, Lee has presented herself as a unifying force, steeled by a decades-long political career that began in Sacramento and took her to Washington, where she championed racial justice and antiwar causes that set her apart – and sometimes at odds with her own party. Her most famous stand came in 2001, when she cast the sole vote in Congress against the authorization for the use of military force following the 9/11 terrorist attacks – a decision that resulted in hate mail and death threats but is now seen as prescient. And yet she built a reputation as a principled collaborator beloved by Democrats, with a record of working across the aisle with Republicans. Lee, who retired from Congress in January after an unsuccessful run for the US Senate last year, is now promising to bring that experience home. pages.title: Inside the making of the Natural History Museum Abu Dhabi | National Geographic
pages.description: At the new Natural History Museum Abu Dhabi, curators want to bring visitors astonishingly close to the most fascinating creatures the Earth has ever seen.
pages.text: Inside the making of the Natural History Museum Abu Dhabi | National Geographic By Richard Conniff Photographs by Craig Cutler Published July 2, 2026 Dinosaurs are winging in at 550 miles an hour from across the planet: Diplodocus , Stegosaurus, a herd of Triceratops , and a pair of Tyrannosaurus rex (plus a carcass for the tyrannosaurs to do combat over). The museum has them in a queue, along with thousands of other specimens, from a fog-basking beetle to a reconstructed dodo. Some of them are awaiting takeoff, and some are in flight. Others are being uncrated, condition-checked, 3D-scanned, and quickly moved out for reassembly on the museum floor, all to make room for the next specimens just rolling through the delivery bay door. It’s early November 2025, and there are 20 days left until the opening of the Natural History Museum Abu Dhabi (NHMAD), a 377,000-square-foot structure being built and populated on what even the museum’s managers admit is an “insanely short” five-year timeline. With luck, the final major specimen—the last of five 75-foot-tall sauropods greeting visitors at the entrance—will arrive in time to go on display a day or two before the soft opening. That’s when Abu Dhabi’s royal families will arrive, fully expecting to be impressed. At the moment, however, that dinosaur, a Diplodocus, is still in Canada. And the mount is not yet complete. No pressure, though. The new museum stands on a sandy, low-lying island named Saadiyat, separated by an inlet off the Persian Gulf from metropolitan Abu Dhabi , the capital city of the United Arab Emirates (U.A.E.). Nearby in the neighborhood: the Louvre Abu Dhabi, opened in 2017, plus the Guggenheim Abu Dhabi and a new national museum, both rushing to completion at the same time as the natural history museum. Much of the rest of the island is also under construction, with high-end hotels and housing for the crowds all these vaunted institutions are expected to attract. Building out a world-class museum means constantly acquiring, transporting, and storing specimens before getting to install them. This grouping of taxidermied birds, foxes, a wolf, a hare, and a squirrel was destined for the museum’s Our World biome. Name brands, celebrated architects, and superlatives clearly matter. Ride a hotel elevator in town and a 30-second film on loop will remind you that Yas Island, Abu Dhabi’s entertainment counterpart to Saadiyat, boasts a Formula One racetrack, the world’s fastest roller coaster (in a Ferrari World theme park), and the “world’s largest indoor skydiving flight chamber.” It’s all part of a well-financed push to transform Abu Dhabi from a sandy desert petrostate into a travel destination and a cultural heavyweight, on a par with Paris and London. Or rather, ahead of Paris and London, if Abu Dhabi achieves its declared goal of attracting 39.3 million visitors a year by 2030, up from 6.6 million in 2025. That doesn’t mean the U.A.E. is backing away from its chief business of gas and oil exports; the opposite, in fact. But the heavy spending to promote tourism and other industries marks a deliberate shift away from dependence on fossil fuels , which now account for just 30 percent of the national economy, down from 85 percent as recently as 2009. The natural history museum will be the first of its scale in the Middle East. The people planning it mean to acquire “some of the most incredible specimens known to mankind”—like a chunk of the Murchison meteorite containing grains of a universe from before our sun existed, or fossils of a miniature horse that once wandered Abu Dhabi itself. They also want to reveal those specimens in ways that bring the public much closer to the natural world than other globally renowned museums have dared. Preparing massive, heavy, and priceless dinosaur fossils for an international voyage requires multiple teams to coordinate on each leg of the journey, from museum curators to fossil preparators to shipping specialists. pages.title: 联合国纪念活动 | 联合国
pages.description: 联合国在指定的某些日子、星期、年份、十年、甚至周年围绕特定主题或话题举办纪念活动。通过举办特别的纪念活动，联合国希望能激发公众对特定领域的联合国活动和方案的兴趣，提升全球的相关意识和行动力。大多数纪念活动由联合国大会的决议提出设立，一些活动则由联合国专门机构指定。
pages.text: 联合国纪念活动 | 联合国 Skip to main content body 国际日是提高公众对有关问题的认识、调动政治意愿和资源应对全球性问题以及庆祝和加强人类成就的机会。 来自科特迪瓦各地的妇女相聚在阿比让文化宫庆祝国际妇女节。联合国图片/Ky Chung 联合国纪念活动 国际日在联合国成立之前就已存在，但联合国将国际日视为一种有力的宣传工具。联合国在指定的某些日子、星期、年份、十年、甚至周年围绕特定主题或话题举办纪念活动。通过举办特别的纪念活动，联合国希望能激发公众对特定领域的联合国活动和方案的兴趣，提升全球的相关意识和行动力。每个国际日都为多方提供了组织相关主题活动的机会。联合国系统下的各组织和办事处携手各国政府、民间社会、公共和私营部门、学校、大学以及更广泛的公民，把国际日打造成为提高人们认识的跳板。大多数纪念活动由联合国大会的决议提出设立，一些活动则由联合国专门机构指定。 国际日和国际周 国际年 国际十年 周年纪念 国际日由谁设立？如何设立？ 作为联合国最具代表性的机构，大会指定某个特定的日期为国际日。设立国际日的提议由会员国向大会提出，然后大会以协商一致的方式决定是否通过决议设立该国际日。 国际日的主题往往和联合国的主要行动领域有关，包括维持国际和平与安全、促进可持续发展、保护人权以及保障国际法或人道主义行动。 大会决议通常会解释宣布设立某一国际日的原因。例如，宣布将5月23日设为 根除产科瘘国际日 的决议指出：“贫穷、营养不良、保健服务缺乏或不足或无法获取、早育、童婚、暴力侵害年轻妇女和女孩行为和性别歧视之间彼此关联，是产科瘘的根源所在，而贫穷仍是主要的社会风险因素。” 产科瘘可能在分娩过程中造成最严重的一些危害，发展中国家约有200万妇女患有这种疾病，且这一数字正在以每年5万至10万例的速度增长，但是许多人可能从未听说过这种疾病。这很好地说明了通过国际日提高人们意识的必要性。 此外，大会决议也会指出某一问题的哪些方面与会员国最为密切相关，也可以说与全人类最为密切相关，因为大会由193个国家组成，囊括了世界上的大多数国家。在这方面，宣布将6月23日设为 国际丧偶妇女日 的决议是个很好的例子。大会在该决议中表示：“深为关切千百万丧偶妇女的子女忍饥挨饿，营养不良，做童工，难以得到保健服务、水和环境卫生，失学，成为文盲，以及遭到人口贩运。” 某些国际日不是由大会而是由联合国专门机构宣布设立的，目的是提请公众关注该机构专业领域内的问题，如健康、航空和知识产权等。例如，总部位于巴黎的 联合国教育、科学及文化组织 宣布每年5月3日为 世界新闻自由日 ，然后由大会确立该国际日。 除了提高人们的意识外，联合国还借助国际日建议各国该采取什么行动，解决这些国际日所围绕的严重问题。例如，在宣布将5月22日定为 生物多样性国际日 的决议中，大会邀请各会员国签署并批准旨在保护生物多样性的 《卡塔赫纳议定书》 。 我们如何衡量这些国际日的影响？ 国际纪念活动（也包括国际周、国际年和国际十年）网页是联合国网站中访问量最大的页面。每个国际日都有一个专门网站，提供联合国六种正式语文的版本。 国际日也是衡量世界各地对某一特定主题关注程度的指标。为此，我们会研究全世界不同地区、不同语言人群对各种国际日纪念活动的参与程度。特别值得一提的一个例子是12月10日 人权日 。这一天，世界各地会举办纪念活动，例如 南苏丹 的军队和警察“放下枪支，换上跑鞋”活动、 俄罗斯 的学生竞赛以及 巴西 的展览活动。总之，来自各行各业的众多人士会通过不同的方式参与纪念这个特殊的日子。 其他最受欢迎的国际日包括： 国际妇女节 （3月8日）、 世界水日 （3月22日）和 国际和平日 （9月21日）。 你知道吗？有五个国际日设在3月21日，而六月是国际日最多的月份。 庆祝对多种语文的使用 有一类特殊的国际日庆祝 联合国对六种正式语文的使用 。 全球传播部 为联合国六种官方语言分别建立了语文日。联合国语文日旨在庆祝 多种语言 和 文化多样性 ，并促进六种正式语文在联合国的平等使用。在这一倡议下，世界各地的联合国工作地点都会举办六次庆贺活动，以纪念每一种联合国工作语言。联合国语文日既是为了娱乐，也是为了提醒大众要加强对联合国六种工作语言的历史、文化和成就的尊重。 六个语文日： 3月20日 法文 4月20日 Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Public Input & Actions BLM and USWFS Plan Prescribed Fire Treatments on BLM-Managed Lands in Arizona Reducing the threat of wildfire and restoring public lands Arizona Phoenix DO Arizona Strip DO Colorado River DO Gila DO Media Contact BLM Arizona Newsroom blm_az_newsroom@blm.gov BLM Office: Arizona State Office October 19, 2026 PHOENIX — The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the U.S. Wildland Fire Service will begin prescribed fire treatments on BLM-managed land in Arizona . Treatment operations will be conducted throughout the fall and winter as weather, fuel, and air quality become favorable. These treatments are carefully planned to reduce hazardous fuels, protect nearby communities, and restore native ecosystems. Information about specific upcoming and active burns is available online . Prescribed fire is one of the most effective tools for reducing wildfire risk and improving habitat. Prescribed fire treatments are carefully planned and executed within the U.S. Wildland Fire Service to help protect communities and strengthen the health of our public lands. Techniques range from broadcast burning, which is the application of fire to an entire area, to hand and machine pile ignitions. These burns focus on increasing safety in the wildland-urban interface and restoring ecological function to the landscape. Targeting built-up fuels and residual materials from previous thinning operations decreases the load of dead trees, branches, and underbrush that pose significant wildfire risks. What the public should know: During prescribed burns, smoke may settle in low-lying areas overnight. Residents are encouraged to close windows at night to avoid smoke impacts. When driving in smoky areas, drivers should slow down and turn on headlights. People with heart or lung disease, asthma, or other chronic conditions should ask their doctors about protecting themselves from smoke and should monitor their local air quality map. All burns are carried out when weather, fuel conditions, and air quality are within specific parameters. Firefighters use a combination of natural features and constructed control lines to keep the fire contained, with protocols in place to minimize smoke impacts on nearby communities. For more information, contact the BLM district office or the U.S. Wildland Fire Service Geographic Area associated with the burn. The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations. pages.title: Rare Chinese vases found in Oxfordshire could fetch £50,000 British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The porcelain, which was found at a house in Oxfordshire, go up for auction on Wednesday.
pages.text: Rare Chinese vases found in Oxfordshire could fetch £50,000 Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Rare Chinese Qing dynasty vases could fetch £50,000 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Ethan Gudge South of England Mallams The vases are expected to fetch up to £50,000 at an auction next week A pair of rare Chinese vases thought to date back from the 17th Century are estimated to fetch up to £50,000 when they go under the hammer next week. The two Chinese Famille Verte 'Ladies' Vases are thought to date back to the Kangxi period of the Qing dynasty, between 1662 and 1722. Auction house Mallam's explained that the vases had been in an Oxfordshire country house and represented "an extraordinary rediscovery of Chinese porcelain". The auctioneers, based in Cheltenham, estimate the "magnificent and important" pair of vases could sell for between £30,000 and £50,000 when they go up for sale on Wednesday. Robin Fisher, Mallams' Asian art expert said the sale offered "a rare opportunity to acquire a piece of documented collecting history" for potential buyers. Getty Images The pair of vases date back to the reign of the Kangxi Emperor Explaining the porcelains provenance, the auction house said they had been painted "in exceptionally vibrant famille verte enamels". Each vase features panels depicting elegant ladies as they take part in different activities, including strolling through gardens, and playing with a cat. They each date back to the reign of the Kangxi Emperor, who was the longest-reigning emperor in Chinese history - ruling from 1661 to 1722. Research led by Fisher found the vases had once been part of "one of the most historically lauded private collections of Chinese porcelain in Great Britain", Mallams said. It said they had originally been owned by Victorian industrialist Richard Bennett - who used his fortune to amass "a premier collection of Qing dynasty imperial wares". In 1911, the collection was sold in its entirety to London art dealer Edgar Gorer, who catalogued each piece. Over the intervening years, the vases were sold off separately - including individual masterpieces which were purchased by museums and estates, including the Rockefeller family. pages.title: Scientists find a new titanosaur dinosaur species in Patagonia | National Geographic
pages.description: The new Argentine dino might give us clues to what the world was like before the asteroid wiped out their kind.
pages.text: Scientists find a new titanosaur dinosaur species in Patagonia | National Geographic Premium SCIENCE Scientists find a new titanosaur dinosaur species in Patagonia The new Argentine dino might give us clues to what the world was like before the asteroid wiped out their kind. Hundreds of fossils found at a quarry in Northern Patagonia provide a snapshot of what a desert pond ecosystem might have looked like in the late Cretaceous period. Researchers found a previously undiscovered species of titanosaur (illustrated above) among other fossilized creatures at the site. Illustration by Gabriel Lio By Meghie Rodrigues Published March 5, 2025 In Northern Patagonia, paleontologists have unearthed an ancient lagoon ecosystem surrounded by sand dunes and palm trees where prehistoric creatures thrived. Excavations of 78 million year-old rocks, from a quarry just outside General Roca city in Argentina, yielded a treasure trove of 432 fossils belonging to over a hundred animal groups. The majority of the fossils belonged to turtles, but other residents were fish, crocodile relatives, slugs—including the first fossil record of the Neocyclotidae , a family of tropical land snails, and the first record of Leptinaria , a genus of small tropical air-breathing land snails—and dinosaurs . The most important find among them all: a new titanosaur called Chadititan calvoi. Chadititan calvoi recreation A 3D reconstruction shows what the new titanosaur and its habitat might have looked like. Video by Gabriel Díaz Yantén Though researchers have known the Anacleto rock formation where the fossils were discovered for decades, there had never been a finding with such diversity in a single place in Northern Patagonia, says coauthor Diego Pol , a paleontologist at the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales Bernardino Rivadavia in Buenos Aires and a National Geographic Explorer. Today, the team of Argentinian and Uruguayan researchers published their findings on the new titanosaur and the site in Revista del Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales. “The fossil fauna there is diverse, and our understanding of Southern Hemisphere ecosystems from near the end of the Age of Dinosaurs is still very incomplete,” says paleontologist Matthew Lamanna of the Carnegie Museum of Natural History in Pittsburgh who was not involved in the research. An ancient watering hole The site is so rich because it was probably an oasis amid harsh environments in the Argentinian Patagonia in the late Cretaceous period. At the time, temperatures were about five to 10 degrees Celsius higher than today, and biodiversity hotspots would concentrate in higher latitudes, as tropical regions were too hot for most species. “This is a very particular environment, with deposits of sand dunes interspersed with small lakes—and just like we see today in arid places, water concentrates biodiversity,” Pol says. Of the more than 400 fossil records found, about 20 belong to Chadititan calvoi . “Chadi”, or “salt” in the Mapudungun language spoken by Mapuche groups refers to the excavation site, located at the margins of a salt flat, the Salitral Moreno lowlands.The full genus name translates to "Titan of the Salt.” The species calvoi is a tribute to the late Argentinian paleontologist Jorge Calvo, who described several titanosaurs and coined the clade Rinconsauria , to which the new species belongs. Titanosaurs are known for their exceptional proportions, ranging from cow-sized one metric ton animals to whale-sized beasts of about 60 metric tons, says Lamanna.While the largest titanosaurs reached over 100 feet in length, the new species is around 22 feet or seven meters long—about the same length as a minibus or RV. “ Chadititan is on the small side as titanosaurs go, though it still would’ve been big compared to most of today’s animals,” he adds. Informational Webinar: Accelerating Scale-up and Pre-piloting of Emerging Chemical Technologies (ASPECT) September 11, 2026 01:00PM to 02:00PM EDT Banner Color Light Text on a Dark Overlay (Default) The Department of Energy’s Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office held an informational webinar on the recently announced Accelerating Scale-up and Pre-piloting of Emerging Chemical Technologies (ASPECT) funding opportunity on Friday, September 11, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. ET . The funding opportunity provides up to $58 million to fund research, development, and pre-pilot testing of innovative chemical technologies that use alternative and waste feedstocks and accelerate domestic chemical manufacturing. Through this funding opportunity, AFFO aims to accelerate chemical technologies that lower costs, enhance performance, reduce reliance on U.S. imports, and unlock strong market growth potential. The funding opportunity uses a phased approach to move projects from laboratory research to pre-pilot scale testing and avoid delays. It includes two main topic areas: Topic Area 1: Bench ASPECT Topic Area 2: Pre-pilot ASPECT To learn more about topic areas, registration requirements, applicant eligibility, webinar registration, and the Teaming Partner list, visit the ASPECT web page . Download the presentation and listen to the recording.

pages.text: Preguntas frecuentes sobre el Formulario 1040-X, Declaración Enmendada del Impuesto Estadounidense Sobre los Ingresos Personales de los Estados Unidos | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Preguntas frecuentes sobre el Formulario 1040-X, Declaración Enmendada del Impuesto Estadounidense Sobre los Ingresos Personales de los Estados Unidos English Español 中文 (简体) 中文 (繁體) 한국어 Русский Tiếng Việt Kreyòl ayisyen Más en Presentar Individuos Quién debe presentar Pasos para presentar sus impuestos Presente su declaración de impuestos Obtener una prórroga Enmendar la declaración Actualice mi información Acontecimientos de la vida (en inglés) Estudiantes Empleados Padres Militares Jubilados y Personas de edad avanzada Negocios y trabajadores por cuenta propia Organizaciones caritativas y sin fines de lucro Contribuyentes internacionales Enlaces gubernamentales (en inglés) Gobiernos federales, estatales y locales (en inglés) Gobiernos tribales indígenas (en inglés) Bonos exentos de impuestos (en inglés) Números de identificación del contribuyente (TIN) Verifique el estado de su declaración enmendada Usted puede verificar el estado de su declaración enmendada con la herramienta ¿Dónde está mi declaración enmendada? Puede tardar hasta tres semanas antes de que su declaración enmendada aparezca en nuestro sistema. ¿Puedo presentar electrónicamente mi declaración enmendada? (actualizada el 28 de mayo de 2025) Sí. Si necesita enmendar su Formulario 1040, 1040-SR, 1040-NR, 1040-SS, o (antes de 2023) 1040-PR para el período tributario actual o los dos períodos tributarios anteriores, puede enmendar estos formularios electrónicamente utilizando los productos de software tributario disponibles. ¿Cuáles son algunas de las razones por las cuales una declaración enmendada no se puede presentar electrónicamente? (actualizada el 28 de mayo de 2025) Tiene que presentar las declaraciones enmendadas en papel en las siguientes situaciones: Cualquier declaración enmendada de los Formularios 1040, 1040-SR, 1040-NR, 1040-SS o (antes de 2023) 1040-PR anterior al período tributario actual o a los dos períodos tributarios anteriores no se puede enmendar electrónicamente. Las declaraciones enmendadas correspondientes a esos años tributarios anteriores se tienen que presentar en papel. Si enmienda una declaración de un año anterior presentada originalmente en papel durante el año de trámite actual, entonces la declaración enmendada se tiene que presentar en papel. ¿Cómo presento electrónicamente mi declaración enmendada? Comuníquese con su proveedor preferido de software tributario para verificar su participación, responder cualquier pregunta y recibir instrucciones específicas necesarias para presentar su declaración enmendada. ¿Cuántas declaraciones enmendadas se pueden presentar electrónicamente? (actualizada el 2 de enero de 2024) Usted puede presentar electrónicamente hasta tres declaraciones enmendadas por año tributario. Si presenta una tercera declaración enmendada que es aceptada, todos los intentos subsiguientes se rechazarán. ¿Puedo presentar electrónicamente mi declaración enmendada para años tributarios anteriores? (actualizada el 28 de mayo de 2025) Puede enmendar electrónicamente su Formulario 1040, 1040-SR, 1040-NR, 1040-SS o (antes de 2023) 1040-PR para el período tributario actual o los dos períodos tributarios anteriores. ¿Se tramitará más rápido mi declaración enmendada si la presento electrónicamente? (actualizada el 4 de junio de 2024) Posiblemente en una o dos semanas, por que elimina el tiempo de envío por correo. Por lo general, debe esperar entre ocho y doce semanas para que se procese su Formulario 1040-X. Sin embargo, en algunos casos, el procesamiento podría demorar hasta dieciséis semanas. Puede consultar el panel del estado de la tramitación para más información en el tiempo de tramitación actual. ¿Qué formularios se requieren con una declaración enmendada presentada electrónicamente? PHOENIX – The Bureau of Land Management today announced an oil and gas lease sale scheduled for Dec. 15, to offer 40 oil and gas parcels totaling 78,708 acres in Arizona. The BLM completed scoping on these parcels in June and held a public comment period that closed in September on the parcels and the related environmental analysis. A 30-day public protest period to receive additional public input opens Oct. 16 and will close Nov. 15. Leasing is the first step in the process to develop federal oil and gas resources. Before development operations can begin, an operator must submit an application for permit to drill detailing development plans. The BLM reviews applications for permits to drill, posts them for public review, conducts an environmental analysis and coordinates with state partners and stakeholders. All parcels that are included in a federal oil and gas lease sale include appropriate stipulations to protect important natural resources. Information on current and upcoming BLM leases is available through the National Fluid Lease Sale System . BLM lease sales are held online through Efficient Markets . The parcels BLM analyzed, as well as maps and instructions on how to submit a protest, will be available on BLM’s ePlanning website at: https://eplanning.blm.gov/Project-Home/?id=C5F10790-8349-F111-88B4-001DD8084607 . The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.

pages.title: Nvidia: How the Jensen Huang scandal exposed a headache for business-friendly Singapore British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.
pages.text: Nvidia: How the Jensen Huang scandal exposed a headache for business-friendly Singapore Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Tessa Wong and Osmond Chia , Singapore Getty Images A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade. On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips. For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets. With the AI boom, it has become a major hub for the trade of high-end semiconductor chips in recent years. Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the US chip giant earns. But notably, less than 1% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, as the island acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere. Since 2022, when the US restricted advanced American semiconductors from being exported to China or acquired by Chinese companies, US officials have been concerned that other countries such as Singapore could be used by Chinese companies to gain access to the chips. Megaspeed is a case in point. It became the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia and is suspected of giving backdoor access to these chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls. Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations. The city-state has had some success in policing this. It has charged four companies and five individuals - including Chinese nationals - for various offences including fraud, following US concerns that Chinese AI company DeepSeek had been buying Nvidia chips from third parties in Singapore, among other places. They also tried to probe Megaspeed, but were faced with a number of difficulties. AFP via Getty Images Megaspeed's office in Singapore In a statement released on Thursday, the government said that since February 2025, they had been looking into whether Megaspeed and other firms had made false declarations about data servers which were purchased and exported through Singapore. The companies stated the equipment would end up in neighbouring Malaysia, but Singapore authorities suspect the equipment's final destinations were elsewhere. Singapore said it sought assistance from US authorities several times to get more information from one of the investigated companies - Supermicro, a US-based company which the BBC understands was supplying computer servers to Megaspeed. But "despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance", it said in its statement. The BBC has sought comment from the US State Department. Singapore authorities said they had also investigated Alice Huang - not for espionage, but for any possible role in Megaspeed's suspected fraud. In the end, they found "insufficient evidence" of crime and let her leave Singapore in February this year, after holding her passport for several months. Since launching their probe nearly two years ago, Singapore has yet to bring any charges against Megaspeed or any of the companies and individuals l

Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to the main content Skip to the footer section National Park Service Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Contact Us The NPS App One app, every park at your fingertips. The NPS App is the official app for the National Park Service with tools to explore more than 400 national parks. Find interactive maps, tours of park places, on-the-ground accessibility information, and much more to plan your national park adventures before and during your trip. Download the NPS App The first step to begin your national park app adventure is to download the NPS App onto your mobile devices, such as phones or tablets. The NPS App is currently available for iOS- and Android-powered devices. It can be downloaded for free through the App Store and Google Play . The National Park Service app Features The NPS App was created by park rangers to help you make the most of your visit. Here’s a quick look at some of those features. Interactive Maps: Detailed maps with points of interest, roads, trails, and more. Park Tours: Discover popular destinations as well as places off the beaten track on self-guided tours. It’s like having a ranger by your side to guide your trip, giving you suggestions for places to go, directions to get there, and things to do once you arrive. Amenities: It's the little—and sometimes not so little—things that can make or break a park visit. Learn where you can find and access transportation, food, restrooms, shopping, and more. Accessibility: The app offers a fully accessible experience with tools such as audio descriptions of exhibits along trails and roads and in visitor centers. Offline Use: No internet access? No problem! You can download content from entire parks for offline use. It’s especially handy if you’re exploring remote areas in parks or concerned about data limits. Personalized Lists: Create lists, save park sites, places, and add notes to trip plan or remember your national park adventures. Things to Do: What do you want to do in a park? Hike? Take a bus tour or scenic drive? Visit a museum? Become a junior ranger? Discover all the fun, entertaining, and educational activities parks have to offer. News, Alerts & Events: What’s happening? Get news and events for all parks—or selected parks of your choosing. What’s Next We’re just getting started. If you don’t find what you are looking for now, check back regularly as our rangers continue to add more ways for you to experience each of our parks through the NPS app. The National Park Service is also planning to expand features, so stay tuned for more! Funding Notice: Accelerating Scale-up and Pre-piloting of Emerging Chemical Technologies (ASPECT) Banner Color Light Text on a Dark Overlay (Default) DOE will fund research, development, and pre-pilot testing of innovative chemical technologies that use domestically-sourced alternative and waste feedstocks Office: Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office Funding Opportunity Number : DE-FOA-0003647 Link to Apply : DOE eXCHANGE ASPECT Funding Amount : Up to $58,000,000 Webinar Recording: ASPECT Webinar The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office (AFFO) announced up to $58 million in funding to advance novel, high-impact chemical technologies that use domestically sourced alternative and waste feedstocks. Projects funded through this initiative will advance new methods of chemical production that maximize the use of America’s vast biomass and waste resources. This funding supports President Trump’s Executive Order, Unleashing American Energy , which calls for targeted federal investment in technology innovation that strengthens the U.S. chemical sector. The Accelerating Scale-up and Pre-piloting of Emerging Chemical Technologies (ASPECT) funding opportunity promotes the development and commercialization of chemical technologies that lower costs, enhance performance, reduce reliance on imports, and unlock strong market growth potential. ASPECT seeks to reduce time to market by moving projects from laboratory research to pre-pilot scale testing with two primary topic areas, BENCH ASPECT and Pre-pilot ASPECT. TOPICS Topic Area 1: Bench ASPECT The Bench ASPECT topic area will move technologies beyond proof-of-concept to bench and pre-pilot scale seeking proposals that validate and optimize technologies and provide economic assessment for further development. Applicants can choose between two sub-topic areas: 1a: Bench-Scale Technologies 1b: Bench-Scale and Unit Operation Pre-piloting Topic Area 2: Pre-pilot ASPECT Pre-pilot ASPECT topic area proposals should accelerate the development and market entry of strategically valuable, domestically produced chemicals. Proposals will focus on the design, construction, and operation of pre-pilot scale facilities that convert alternative feedstocks into chemicals. Applicants can choose between two sub-topic areas: 2a: Unit Operation Pre-piloting and Pre-pilot System Integration 2b: Pre-pilot System Integration Applicants must submit concept papers by October 9, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET, to be eligible to submit a Stage 1 full application . More information on the ASPECT funding opportunity (DE-FOA-0003647) can be found on DOE eXCHANGE . The full ASPECT funding opportunity application is also available on Grants.gov . Más en Noticias en Español Reducción de impuestos para las familias trabajadoras (en inglés) Notas de Prensa Alivio en situaciones de desastre Temas en las noticias Hojas de datos Declaraciones y anuncios del IRS Consejos tributarios del IRS Directrices del IRS (en inglés) Centro de medios Artículos sobre impuestos para compartir Pósteres para compartir El Servicio de Impuestos Internos (IRS) reconoce que muchas personas podrían estar atravesando un periodo difícil financieramente. Eventos como la pérdida de empleo, deudas perdonadas o retirar dinero de un fondo de jubilación pudieran tener un impacto tributario. Si sus ingresos han disminuido, usted podría ser elegible por primera vez para ciertos créditos tributarios, tales como el Crédito Tributario por Ingreso del Trabajo. Lo más importante es que si usted cree que pudiera tener dificultades para pagar sus cuentas tributarias comuníquese inmediatamente con el IRS. Hay medidas que podemos tomar para ayudarle a reducir la carga. Además, usted debería presentar su declaración de impuestos a tiempo aunque no pueda pagar para evitar multas adicionales. pages.title: Gout is on the rise – and excruciating. Why are sufferers still judged for it? | Health & wellbeing | The Guardian
pages.description: About 1.6 million people in the UK have this agonising condition, but it is often viewed as a comical malady brought on by overconsumption and idleness. What can be done to end the stigma?
pages.text: Gout is on the rise – and excruciating. Why are sufferers still judged for it? | Health & wellbeing | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation ‘People insinuate it’s self-inflicted, from drinking lots of red wine and eating red meat’ … Brett McAllister-Byrne, who suffered from gout in his early 30s. Photograph: Lily Renshaw/The Guardian View image in fullscreen ‘People insinuate it’s self-inflicted, from drinking lots of red wine and eating red meat’ … Brett McAllister-Byrne, who suffered from gout in his early 30s. Photograph: Lily Renshaw/The Guardian Health & wellbeing Gout is on the rise – and excruciating. Why are sufferers still judged for it? About 1.6 million people in the UK have this agonising condition, but it is often viewed as a comical malady brought on by overconsumption and idleness. What can be done to end the stigma? Tim Dowling Sun 15 Nov 2026 09.00 EST Last modified on Mon 16 Nov 2026 05.34 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google B rett McAllister-Byrne was in his early 30s when he first noticed a sharp ache in his ankle and big toe. “I felt it the night after playing football, and I thought I must have had a knock or something,” he says. “But then it just got worse and worse.” The next morning McAllister-Byrne, an urban planner, was in too much pain to go to work. When he described the episode to his family, they suggested it might be gout. “I was like, really?” he says. “Can you get that in your 30s?” Gout has been with us for as long as we know: in 1910 a case was diagnosed in a mummy found near a temple in Upper Egypt. It is the most common form of inflammatory arthritis – and, it is often said, the only curable one – resulting from raised levels of uric acid in the blood. Uric acid is produced when your metabolism breaks down molecules called purines, which are found in your body’s own cells and in certain foods you eat. Excess uric acid is normally processed by the kidneys and passed through urine, but persistently high urate levels can eventually lead to sharp crystals forming in the joints. The presence of these crystals can in turn trigger a profound immune response: inflammation, redness and pain. Eventually, hardened lumps of urate crystals called tophi can form under the skin. High urate levels can have many causes, but they are not, in themselves, the sole cause of gout. “Virtually all people with gout will have a raised urate level,” says consultant rheumatologist Prof Edward Roddy. “But most people with a raised urate level don’t get gout.” View image in fullscreen The majority of gout sufferers experience the first attack in their big toe. Photograph: jittawit.21/Getty Images The pain of a gout attack is so debilitating that it can be hard to describe: the 19th-century writer and clergyman Sydney Smith said it felt “like walking on my eyeballs”. “Sometimes people think they’ve broken a bone – that’s quite a common thing,” says Roddy. “There is some qualitative research showing that people compare the intensity of the pain to having a heart attack or a kidney stone, and that women with gout compare the intensity of the pain to childbirth.” It can also arrive, in the first instance, with little or no warning. “Often it comes on overnight,” says Roddy. “So somebody goes to bed pain-free, then they wake up and can’t put their foot to the floor.” In the UK, Europe and the US, gout afflicts 2%-4% of the population. In the UK that equates to about 1.6 million people. “That is an awful lot more people in this country, for example, than have rheumatoid arthritis,” says Lucy Donaldson, director of research at Arthritis UK. pages.description: Obtén más información sobre el rol, visión y resultados de la UNESCO. La UNESCO es la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Educación, la Ciencia y la Cultura. Nuestro objetivo es promover la paz y la seguridad a través de la cooperación internacional.
pages.text: UNESCO: Construyendo la Paz a través de la Educación, la Ciencia y la Cultura, la comunicación y la información Pasar al contenido principal Búsqueda Búsqueda Quicks links : Inteligencia Artificial Respuestas a emergencias Desafíos clave ©Ramon R/Shutterstock.com COP31: Proteger nuestras reservas de agua Mientras se celebra la COP31 en Antalya (Türkiye), del 9 al 20 de noviembre de 2026, bajo el tema de la resiliencia hídrica y oceánica, la UNESCO llama la atención sobre la criosfera, es decir, las regiones heladas de la Tierra: glaciares, mantos de hielo, nieve, hielo marino y permafrost. Estas reservas heladas contienen casi el 70% del agua dulce del planeta, pero se están derritiendo a un ritmo acelerado. Para protegerlas, la UNESCO promueve soluciones integradas que combinan la ciencia, la educación y los conocimientos de los pueblos indígenas y las comunidades locales. Ver más La UNESCO actúa en apoyo de las personas afectadas por crisis La cultura, la educación, la ciencia y la información son necesidades esenciales en tiempos de turbulencia y crisis. Son motores poderosos de cohesión social, resiliencia y esperanza en un futuro mejor. La UNESCO desempeña un papel vital en la protección de los fundamentos sociales y culturales que sustentan la estabilidad, la dignidad y la recuperación de las comunidades afectadas por crisis. Al proteger estos pilares, ayudamos a garantizar que las sociedades puedan reconstruir no solo la infraestructura, sino también la confianza, la identidad y la capacidad colectiva para avanzar. Leer más ©UNESCO Nuestro impacto en las comunidades Descubra cómo la UNESCO impulsa el cambio en todo el mundo. ¿Cuál es la magnitud de la brecha de género en el liderazgo educativo? La Organización ofrece servicios clave a sus Estados miembros, estableciendo normas y estándares globales, desarrollando herramientas para la cooperación internacional, generando conocimiento para las políticas públicas y construyendo redes globales de sitios e instituciones inscritas en sus listas. Descubrir Thumbnail play_arrow © UNESCO Nuestras áreas de competencia La UNESCO utiliza la educación, la ciencia, la cultura, la comunicación y la información para fomentar el entendimiento mutuo y el respeto por nuestro planeta. Nuestros objetivos estratégicos La estrategia de la UNESCO aborda los desafíos globales con objetivos en educación, medio ambiente, cohesión social y tecnología. Actuar en tiempos de emergencias La UNESCO apoya a las comunidades afectadas por los conflictos y catástrofes causadas por riesgos naturales, garantizando el acceso a una educación de calidad y la protección del patrimonio cultural. Construir un multilateralismo más fuerte La UNESCO se sitúa en primera línea de la cooperación internacional, en estrecha coordinación con los otros organismos del Sistema de Naciones Unidas.
