pages.title: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The fact the question of European security now features in discussions is viewed in Moscow as a victory, BBC Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg says.
pages.text: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Steve Rosenberg Russia Editor, Moscow EPA Putin sounded uncompromising and confident at his talks with the US envoys Russia's President Vladimir Putin says he wishes "eternal peace" for Ukraine. That is the same Russian president who ordered the full-scale invasion of Russia's neighbour nearly five years ago and who continues to reject the idea of a comprehensive ceasefire. And what, in Moscow's view, is a prerequisite for peace? The Kremlin spelt it out after talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner: "A new, long-term architecture of indivisible security and peace." Translated from Kremlin-speak, it means Moscow wants to change the security set-up of Europe in a way that benefits Russia. What Russia is pushing for is, potentially, the biggest change to European security arrangements since the end of the Cold War. The Kremlin has put back on the table its controversial proposal from December 2021 – the "draft treaties" with the US and Nato which would not only have put the brakes on the alliance's eastward enlargement by giving Moscow cast-iron guarantees that, for instance, Ukraine and Georgia would never be allowed to join, but also rolled back Nato military infrastructure from countries of central and eastern Europe which became Nato members following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. Western leaders dismissed such demands as an unacceptable Russian ultimatum. Two months later Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The "draft treaties" were put away. Now they are out of the geopolitical filing cabinet, and being quoted again by the Kremlin. What is more, Yuri Ushakov, Putin's foreign policy aide, has suggested that Moscow is about to "add certain new considerations" to its list of demands in light of Western efforts "to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia". That does not mean, of course, that Western governments will accept them. But the fact that the question of European security is featuring now in discussions on Ukraine is viewed here as a victory for Moscow. "In December 2021 Russia actively proposed that Nato rethink the security system in Europe," wrote newspaper Komsomolskaya Pravda earlier this week. "Our proposals were almost laughed at. "Having secured one victory by forcing the West to think about security, our diplomats need a second by making the West heed Russia's concerns about Nato enlargement." The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, has called Russia's demands for a new European security architecture a "trap" designed to "shift attention away from a ceasefire". "The sequencing of Ukraine-Russia talks is important," Kallas wrote on social media. "The priority should be securing a ceasefire, followed by a peace agreement. Only then can there be discussions on Europe's wider security architecture." Europe's problem is that, right now, it is not at the table. Moscow has had no desire to give it a chair. It has slammed European leaders for their military support for Kyiv and tough stance on Russia. This week's peace talks in Abu Dhabi involved Ukraine, Russia and the US. After his discussions in Moscow, Witkoff indicated that Putin had agreed to the idea of European representatives joining the next round of Ukraine peace talks. But on Friday the Kremlin indicated a final decision on European participation had not been taken. "Once we understand their true intentions and their readiness to facilitate the peace process, then it will be possible to take a decision about dialogue on Ukraine in a wider format," said Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov. pages.description: El Programa de voluntarios de ayuda con impuestos sobre los ingresos (VITA) y el Programa de asesoramiento tributario para ancianos (TCE) preparan declaraciones de impuestos gratuitamente para los contribuyentes que reúnen los requisitos.
pages.text: Preparación gratuita de la declaración de impuestos para contribuyentes calificados | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Preparación gratuita de la declaración de impuestos para contribuyentes calificados English Español 中文 (简体) 中文 (繁體) 한국어 Русский Tiếng Việt Kreyòl ayisyen Más en Presentar Individuos Quién debe presentar Pasos para presentar sus impuestos Presente su declaración de impuestos Free File Obtener una prórroga Enmendar la declaración Actualice mi información Acontecimientos de la vida (en inglés) Estudiantes Empleados Padres Militares Jubilados y Personas de edad avanzada Negocios y trabajadores por cuenta propia Organizaciones caritativas y sin fines de lucro Contribuyentes internacionales Enlaces gubernamentales (en inglés) Gobiernos federales, estatales y locales (en inglés) Gobiernos tribales indígenas (en inglés) Bonos exentos de impuestos (en inglés) Números de identificación del contribuyente (TIN) El Programa de Ayuda Voluntaria a los Contribuyentes del Impuesto sobre el Ingreso (VITA, por sus siglas en inglés) y el Programa de Asesoramiento Tributario para los Ancianos (TCE, por sus siglas en inglés) del IRS ofrecen ayuda tributaria básica gratuita a personas calificadas. El programa de VITA ha operado por más de 50 años. Aunque el IRS no establece un límite de ingreso para todo el programa, los centros VITA individuales pueden establecer sus propios límites. El programa generalmente se enfoca en servir a los contribuyentes que cumplen con las reglas de ingresos del Crédito tributario por ingreso del trabajo (EITC, por sus siglas en inglés). Muchos centros ofrecen ayuda tributaria gratuita a las personas que necesitan ayuda para preparar sus propias declaraciones de impuestos, incluyendo: Personas que generalmente ganan $70,244 o menos Personas con discapacidades Personas que tienen dominio limitado del inglés. Además del programa VITA, el programa de TCE ofrece ayuda tributaria gratuita, especialmente a personas de 60 años de edad o más, y se especializa en asuntos de pensiones y temas sobre la jubilación, asuntos que son para personas de edad avanzada. Aunque el IRS administra los programas de VITA y TCE, dichos centros son operados por socios del IRS y el personal consiste en voluntarios quienes desean hacer una diferencia en sus comunidades. Los voluntarios certificados por el IRS que proporcionan asesoramiento tributario usualmente son personas jubiladas asociadas con organizaciones sin fines de lucro que reciben subvenciones de parte del IRS. Los servicios de VITA y TCE no solamente son gratis, también son una fuente confiable para la preparación de declaraciones de impuestos. Todos los voluntarios de VITA y TCE que preparan declaraciones tienen que tomar y aprobar un adiestramiento sobre la ley tributaria que reúne o excede los estándares del IRS. Este adiestramiento incluye el mantener la privacidad y confidencialidad de toda la información de los contribuyentes. Además de requerir a los voluntarios que certifiquen su conocimiento sobre las leyes tributarias, el IRS requiere una verificación de calidad para cada declaración preparada en un centro de VITA y TCE antes de que se presenten. Cada temporada de presentación, decenas de miles de voluntarios dedicados de VITA y TCE preparan millones de declaraciones federales y estatales. Además, ellos asisten a los contribuyentes con la preparación de miles de declaraciones preparadas mediante la Autoayuda Facilitada. Antes de visitar Antes de visitar un centro VITA o TCE, vea la Publicación 3676-B (EN-SP) PDF para conocer los servicios que se ofrecen y revise los documentos e información que debe llevar , a fin de asegurar que tenga todos los documentos e información necesaria para que los voluntarios le puedan ayudar. pages.title: Iran was behind cyber-attack on French supermarket freezers, Paris says | France | The Guardian
pages.description: French foreign minister vows European sanctions against Tehran over ‘unprecedented’ hacks last month
pages.text: Iran was behind cyber-attack on French supermarket freezers, Paris says | France | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Perished food outside supermarkets hit by cyber-attacks targeting refrigeration systems in France. Photograph: Lucien Libert/Reuters View image in fullscreen Perished food outside supermarkets hit by cyber-attacks targeting refrigeration systems in France. Photograph: Lucien Libert/Reuters France Iran was behind cyber-attack on French supermarket freezers, Paris says French foreign minister vows European sanctions against Tehran over ‘unprecedented’ hacks last month Kim Willsher in Paris Mon 9 Nov 2026 12.54 EST First published on Mon 9 Nov 2026 11.53 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google France has said Iran was responsible for a massive cyber-attack on supermarket freezers and chiller cabinets that was described by its foreign minister as being an act of “unprecedented scale and unprecedented aggression”. Jean-Noël Barrot said “Europe-wide sanctions” would be imposed against those responsible, adding that the attacks – which took control of digital thermostats to push temperatures up to above 50C – constituted “a major violation of the nation’s interests”. At a press briefing during the G7 summit in Paris, he said: “Thanks to the remarkable efforts of government agencies, I am able to confirm that the Islamic Republic of Iran’s Revolutionary Guards are responsible for this attack.” He said the Iranian ambassador had been summoned “to protest in the strongest possible terms against this extremely serious act.” Swathes of French supermarkets were hit in the cyber-attacks on 11 and 12 October. Some were forced to throw away entire inventories of perishable food. Similar incidents have been reported since, including on supermarket fridges in other European countries last week and on a French blood bank. The Paris public prosecutor, Laure Beccuau, said on Monday that specialist investigators and government agencies had identified “a modus operandi” characteristic of the Iranian group Shahid Kaveh, a cyber warfare unit linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC). This included “the use of Farsi and IP addresses traced back to devices located in Iran”, she said. Beccuau said her office had opened an investigation against the head of Shahid Kaveh, his deputies and “others who will be identified” on charges of “fraudulent attacks on an automated data processing system committed as part of an organised crime ring and of causing damage dangerous to persons”. She said the offences were “aggravated by the fact they were committed to serve a foreign power – in this case Iran”. Gérôme Billois, a partner at the cybersecurity and technology company Wavestone, said Shahid Kaveh had been active since 2020 and was known to have carried out cyber-attacks mostly on water distribution systems in the US. “Two countries are known for this kind of attack: Iran and Russia. Given that recent cyber-attacks on supermarkets and the blood bank in France concerned freezers it is reasonable to think Iran is directly linked to both,” he said, “For the moment they are attacking easy equipment but as a state group that has the means, the determination and the time, we should be prepared to see attacks on other systems like water or electricity.” During the attack last month, hackers remotely overrode the temperature setting on thousands of freezers , fridges and chiller cabinets in as many as 700 supermarkets and shops across France, pushing them from as low as -27C (-16.6F) to well over 50C (122F) in some cases. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion Thousands of tons of food had to be dumped and in some stores the extreme temperature rise sparked fires, triggering sprinklers and water damage. Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks Related Links 1990-2023 DRAFT Inventory Report is available for public comment per federal register notice ( FRL- 9448-04-OAR, FR Doc. 2024-31058 ) . The draft report will be uploaded to public docket EPA-HQ-OAR-2024-0591 between January 15 and February 13, 2025. Comments were due by March 17, 2025. 1990-2022 Inventory Report and its Data Highlights Greenhouse Gas Inventory Data Explorer Natural Gas Systems Data in the Inventory Stakeholder Webinar: Waste Sector Data and Methodology in the Inventory Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) GHGRP and the U.S. Inventory of Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks USDA's USFS Resource Bulletin U.S. Greenhouse Gas Inventory Report Archives About the Inventory of Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks EPA develops an annual report called the Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks (Inventory), that tracks U.S. greenhouse gas emissions and sinks by source, economic sector, and greenhouse gas going back to 1990. EPA has prepared the Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks since the early 1990s. This annual report , provides a comprehensive accounting of total greenhouse gas emissions for all man-made sources in the United States, including carbon dioxide removal from the atmosphere by “sinks,” (e.g., through the uptake of carbon and storage in forests, vegetation, and soils) from management of lands in their current use or as lands are converted to other uses. The gases covered by the Inventory include carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulfur hexafluoride, and nitrogen trifluoride. The national greenhouse gas inventory is submitted to the United Nations in accordance with the Framework Convention on Climate Change . In preparing the annual emissions and sinks inventory report, EPA collaborates with hundreds of experts representing more than a dozen U.S. government agencies, academic institutions, industry associations, consultants and environmental organizations. EPA also collects greenhouse gas emissions data from individual facilities and suppliers of certain fossil fuels and industrial gases through the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program . Trends Overview of Greenhouse Gas Emissions Note: All emission estimates are sourced from the Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks: 1990–2022 . Land Use, Land-Use Change, and Forestry in the United States is a net sink and offsets 13% of these greenhouse gas emissions. This net sink is not shown in the above diagram. Key findings from the latest Inventory include: In 2022, U.S. greenhouse gas emissions totaled 6,343 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalents, and 5,489 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalents after accounting for sequestration from the land sector. Emissions increased in 2022 by 1 percent (after accounting for sequestration from the land sector) compared to the previous year. The increase in total greenhouse gas emissions was driven largely by an increase in CO 2 emissions from fossil fuel combustion. In 2022, CO 2 emissions from fossil fuel combustion increased by 1 percent relative to the previous year. This increase in fossil fuel consumption emissions was from increased energy use, due in part to the continued rebound in economic activity after the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. Greenhouse gas emissions in 2022 (after accounting for sequestration from the land sector) were 17 percent below 2005 levels. pages.title: How to Report Animal Drug and Device Side Effects and Product Problems | FDA
pages.description: Veterinarians and animal owners are encouraged to report adverse experiences and product failures to the government Agency that regulates the product.
pages.text: How to Report Animal Drug and Device Side Effects and Product Problems | FDA Skip to main content Skip to FDA Search Skip to in this section menu Skip to footer links Home Animal & Veterinary Safety & Health Report a Problem How to Report Animal Drug and Device Side Effects and Product Problems Report a Problem In this section Español What types of problems can I report? Which drugs and devices used in animals can I report to FDA? How do I report a problem? What information should I include? Contact Information Additional Information The FDA encourages veterinarians and animal owners to report adverse events associated with drugs or devices used in animals. We use the information from these reports to monitor the safety of products once they have reached the market. What types of problems can I report? Adverse events can include: Side effects in animals, such as vomiting, diarrhea, colic, seizures, and other symptoms. Side effects in people exposed to drugs and devices used in animals, such as needle stick injuries, rashes, or headache or nausea secondary to product contact. Product defects, such as broken product seals, leaking bottles, and other problems. Medication errors , such as giving the wrong drug or dose, giving a drug too frequently, and other scenarios. Lack of effectiveness, such as a product not working, a product that stops working, or a product that isn’t working as well as it did. Back to the top Which drugs and devices used in animals can I report to FDA? FDA-approved animal drugs have a six-digit New Animal Drug Application (NADA) number, or for generic animal drugs, an Abbreviated New Animal Drug Application (ANADA) number. Drug manufacturers are required to include the application number on most labeling components of currently approved and marketed animal drugs as part of the following statement: “Approved by FDA under NADA # XXX-XXX” or “Approved by FDA under ANADA # XXX-XXX.” This helps you clearly identify approved animal drugs and distinguish them from unapproved ones. Indexed animal drugs are drugs listed in FDA’s Index of Legally Marketed Unapproved New Animal Drugs for Minor Species, referred to simply as ‘the Index’. Animal drugs listed in the Index are unapproved but can be legally marketed for a specific use in certain minor species. All indexed drugs have a six-digit Minor Species Index File (MIF) number that begins with the number nine (for example, MIF 9XX-XXX). The six-digit MIF number is required on the drug’s label. Unapproved animal drugs include human drugs used in animals, compounded drugs , animal supplements, and other products. Medical devices include thermometers, glucose meters, and bandage materials. The information below explains how to report an event. Veterinary biologic products, including animal vaccines, and many flea and tick products are not regulated by FDA. Animal Drugs and Devices - see instructions below Animal Vaccines - contact the USDA APHIS Center for Veterinary Biologics at (800) 752-6255. Flea and Tick Products Some flea and tick products are regulated by FDA, and some are regulated by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). The label of the product can help you determine if the product is an FDA-approved or an EPA-registered flea and tick product or other pesticide: To report a problem with a flea or tick product that is FDA-approved, see instructions below. To identify an EPA-registered product, look for an EPA registration number on the back panel of the package, usually near the manufacturer’s address: “EPA Reg. No.” For EPA-registered products or other pesticides – contact the National Pesticide Information Center at 800-858-7378. Back to the top How Do I Report Adverse Events for Animal Drugs and Devices? You can report adverse drug events to FDA in one of the following ways: For an FDA-approved product or an Indexed product , we recommend calling the drug company to report the adverse drug events. The company responsible for the approved or Indexed drug

pages.title: Cómo elegir un profesional de impuestos | Internal Revenue Service
pages.description: Aprenda sobre cómo escoger a un preparador de declaraciones de impuestos calificado y acceder el directorio del IRS de preparadores de declaraciones de impuestos federales con credenciales y calificaciones particulares.
pages.text: Cómo elegir un profesional de impuestos | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Cómo elegir un profesional de impuestos English Español 中文 (简体) 中文 (繁體) 한국어 Русский Tiếng Việt Kreyòl ayisyen Más en Profesionales de impuestos Agentes inscritos (en inglés) Participantes del Programa anual de la temporada de presentación de impuestos Agentes inscritos de los planes de ahorros para la jubilación (en inglés) Organizaciones Certificadas de Empleadores Profesionales (CPEO, por sus siglas en inglés) (en inglés) Centro informativo sobre el crédito tributario por ingreso del trabajo (EITC, por sus siglas en inglés) (en inglés) Actuarios inscritos (en inglés) Proveedores de presentación electrónica (en inglés) Presentación electrónica modernizada (en inglés) Hay varios tipos de preparadores de declaraciones de impuestos, incluyendo contadores públicos autorizados, agentes registrados, abogados, y muchos otros que no tienen una credencial profesional. Usted espera que su preparador tenga las destrezas en preparación de impuestos y que presente su declaración de impuestos sobre los ingresos con precisión. Usted confía en él o ella con su información que es altamente confidencial. Ellos saben sobre su matrimonio, sus ingresos, hijos y sus números de Seguro Social, en fin, los detalles sobre su vida financiera. La mayoría de los preparadores de declaraciones de impuestos proporcionan servicio tributario de excelencia y profesional. Sin embargo, cada año, algunos contribuyentes sufren con sus finanzas debido a que escogen el preparador de declaraciones de impuestos incorrecto. Asegúrese de verificar nuestros consejos sobre cómo escoger a un preparador de impuestos y cómo evitar a preparadores de impuestos "fantasmas" que no tienen ética profesional . ¿Que clase de preparador de impuestos necesito? Cualquier persona puede ser un preparador de declaraciones de impuestos mientras tanto tenga un número de identificación tributaria del preparador remunerado (PTIN, por sus siglas en inglés) del IRS. Sin embargo, los preparadores de declaraciones de impuestos tienen destrezas, educación y experiencia en diferentes niveles. Aprenda sobre las credenciales y cualificaciones (en inglés) de los preparadores de impuestos. Vea Elija un preparador de impuestos con prudencia . Obtenga información sobre el Programa de Ayuda Voluntaria a los Contribuyentes con los Impuestos (VITA, por sus siglas en inglés) que ofrece preparación básica gratuita de declaraciones de impuestos para contribuyentes calificados. ¿Cómo puedo verificar las credenciales de un preparador de impuestos? Nuestro Directorio de preparadores de declaraciones de impuestos federales con credenciales y determinadas cualificaciones (en inglés) le puede ayudar a encontrar preparadores en su área quienes tienen credenciales profesionales en la actualidad reconocidas por el IRS, o quienes tienen un Registro de cumplimiento del programa anual de la temporada tributaria. Además, puede verificar las organizaciones profesionales (en inglés) a las cuales muchos preparadores de impuestos pertenecen. ¿Qué hago si tengo una queja sobre un preparador de impuestos? El fraude de preparadores de declaraciones de impuestos se encuentra en la lista de las estafas tributarias más comunes. El IRS proporciona consejos sobre cómo evitar a preparadores de impuestos inescrupulosos y también tiene el compromiso de investigar a los preparadores de declaraciones de impuestos pagados que actúan de manera inapropiada. Presente una queja si ha sido afectado financieramente por la mala conducta o por las prácticas inapropiadas en la preparación de impuestos de parte de un preparador de declaraciones de impuestos. pages.description: OpenStreetMap is a map of the world, created by people like you and free to use under an open license.
pages.text: erik_cycling's Diary | The route a real person takes | OpenStreetMap Select Language Loading... Close erik_cycling's Diary The route a real person takes Posted by erik_cycling on 4 November 2026 in English . Spent the morning with the Bicycle wiki page and a 300-post thread about access=dismount, and the same thing kept coming up: our cycling data is really good at describing the road, and a bit less good at describing the person on the bike. We tag the surface, the separation, the access. But the thing that decides whether I actually ride a route is rain, fatigue, and whether I trust the stretch where the cycle lane ends and the traffic doesn’t slow down. None of that is in the data, and it’s the part that matters on a Tuesday morning when it’s pouring. I keep coming back to the idea that the gap between “legal to ride” and “would actually ride” is where the interesting mapping is. Maybe that’s a project for a quieter evening. Location: Vestervold, Meatpacking District, Copenhagen, Copenhagen Municipality, Capital Region of Denmark, 1601, Denmark Discussion Comment from frederik_nlp on 4 November 2026 at 18:26 Same question keeps coming up for me in Aarhus. I ride long distances and the access tags tell me where I’m allowed, but not where I’d actually go on a Tuesday in November. The “would actually ride” layer is the one I miss most — it’s the difference between a technically legal route and one I’d trust with my commute. I’ve been thinking about whether a “comfort level” or “traffic confidence” tag could work, but I suspect it would be too subjective for the wiki. Maybe a community-sourced “frequently ridden” flag for routes people actually choose? Or even just a note in the changeset comments when someone maps a route they personally use regularly? Curious what the 300-post thread landed on. The “legal to ride” vs “would actually ride” framing is the right one — I think most cyclists feel this gap but haven’t had a name for it. Comment from erik_cycling on 5 November 2026 at 06:26 Hi Frederik — Aarhus, that’s a good test case. The access tags problem hits harder when you’re commuting 15km each way in November, I can tell. The 300-post thread: honestly, it didn’t land anywhere. It went through about four phases — first the legal/technical access question, then a long detour into how different countries handle dismount requirements, then someone brought up the whole “designated cycling infrastructure” vs “permissive” debate, and by the end it was mostly people arguing about whether a particular tag combination in a specific German city was correct. The “legal to ride” vs “would actually ride” gap was the thing everyone kept circling back to but nobody could pin down a solution for. Which is kind of the point, I think. Your “frequently ridden” idea is the most interesting thing I’ve seen proposed for this. The changeset note version is low-friction enough that it might actually happen — “mapped this because I ride it every day” is a sentence someone would actually type. The flag version is harder because you need a threshold and a process before it’s useful. One thing I’d add from Copenhagen: the rain factor is not a comfort level, it’s a binary. A route I ride in dry weather is not the same route I ride when it’s been pouring for three days and the canal-side paths are flooded. That’s not “I feel less safe” — that’s “the path is underwater.” If there’s a way to capture that, it’s not a comfort tag, it’s a seasonal accessibility tag. But I don’t know how you’d make that work in the data model. Good to have someone in Aarhus thinking about the same thing. Comment from Lejun on 6 November 2026 at 05:37 For argument’s sake: “I rush through this residential road everyday at 130 km/h, so I edited the maxspeed accordingly. Nevermind the designated speed the infrastructure has been built after or the legal speed limit. ‘cause that’s how I would actually drive and there’s no law enforcement”. Search for information on your state, county, or city. What is the U.S. Census? The U.S. Census Bureau provides data about the nation’s people and economy. Every 10 years, it conducts a census counting every resident in the United States. The most recent census was in 2020. Who must participate? By law, all U.S. residents are required to take part in the census. To protect people’s privacy, all personal information collected by the census is confidential for 72 years. pages.title: What is up with car door handles these days? | Dave Schilling | The Guardian double quotation mark
pages.description: Why is everything computerised, automated or impossible to turn off these days?
pages.text: What is up with car door handles these days? | Dave Schilling | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation ‘I contend that things do not have to be worse. In fact, allow me to be so bold as to suggest they could be better.’ Photograph: Tom Hudson/Zuma Press Wire/Rex/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen ‘I contend that things do not have to be worse. In fact, allow me to be so bold as to suggest they could be better.’ Photograph: Tom Hudson/Zuma Press Wire/Rex/Shutterstock Opinion Technology This article is more than 1 year old What is up with car door handles these days? This article is more than 1 year old Dave Schilling Why is everything computerised, automated or impossible to turn off these days? Sat 5 Apr 2025 07.00 EDT Last modified on Sat 5 Apr 2025 15.54 EDT Share I believe, deep in my soul, that car companies’ number one goal in life is to ruin the experience of driving. I don’t have any direct evidence of this conspiracy to rob us of the pleasure of the open road, other than the cacophony of beeps, blips, bloops and blops that greet us in the latest models. Oh, and the screens. Every year, they try to find a new place to glue a touchscreen in a car, like Pizza Hut hunting for more orifices to stuff cheese into one of their pies. Everything is computerized, automated or impossible to turn off. According to surveys of new-car buyers by the market research firm Strategic Vision, satisfaction with car controls plummeted by 23 percentage points in the last nine years. The whiz-bang gizmos foisted on the North American car buyer have devolved from the glorious, life-saving back-up camera to gesture controls that allow you to turn an invisible knob to crank up the volume on Espresso without touching a single thing in your vehicle. Elon Musk could be the Democrats’ best hope | Moira Donegan Read more Back in January of this year, BMW ditched gesture control in their cars after a decade-long run of forcing adults to poke and prod the air like a mime drunk on cheap wine. Gesture control was cheaper for the automaker because they could cut back on making actual knobs, plus it’s just funnier to watch while stuck in traffic. Here’s what you had to do to make your car work , according to the company: Turn the volume up: circle your finger in a clockwise direction. Turn the volume down: circle your finger in a counter-clockwise direction. Accept a call: point to the BMW iDrive touchscreen. Select navigation/custom setting: use two fingers to point to the touchscreen. Change rearview camera angle: draw a circle using your forefinger and thumb. Regret your life choices: look in the mirror for 10 seconds. When do I have time to learn this? You want me to draw a circle with not just one, but two of my fingers? What do I do if I lost a digit in a particularly gruesome lathe accident? Drive an Audi, that’s what. If carmakers aren’t trying to ruin driving, then I’m pretty sure they’re just bored. After decades of the industry claiming an electric car wasn’t commercially viable, the Toyota Prius came along and realigned our expectations of what could be under the hood of a car. The hybrid engine – part gas, part electric – was the first baby step toward the fleets of all-electric vehicles from Chevrolet, Volkswagen and that one used car you are desperately trying to sell but no one would dare drive in it any more . In an effort to solve problems that don’t exist, carmakers are creating more problems Car companies have solved the greatest problem in the history of automobiles: that these vehicles emit actual poison whenever you operate them. So the ennui has set in: “And Alexander wept, seeing as he had no more worlds to conquer.” Yes, but what if Alexander could remove some knobs from the console of your Mini Cooper? Perhaps a retractable door handle that you constantly have to be reminded how to use? Hey Alexander, quit weeping and start playing Cat Quest in your car . Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. U.S. Gridded Methane Emissions The gridded EPA U.S. methane greenhouse gas inventory (gridded methane GHGI) includes time series of annual methane emission maps with 0.1° x 0.1° (~ 10 x 10 km) spatial and monthly temporal resolution for the contiguous United States (CONUS). This gridded methane inventory is designed to be consistent with methane emissions from the U.S. EPA Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks (U.S. GHGI). The gridded methane GHGI dataset includes annual methane emission fluxes for over 25 inventory emission source categories, including those from agriculture, petroleum and natural gas systems, coal mining, and waste. Gridded methane emissions data are generated by allocating national annual U.S. GHGI methane emissions from individual source categories to a 0.1° x 0.1° CONUS grid, using a series of spatial and temporal 'proxy' datasets at the state, county, and grid levels. Where possible, proxy data are the same data used to develop the U.S. GHGI so that the gridded emissions can be, as closely as possible, a spatial and temporal representation of the national-level U.S. GHGI. Monthly scaling factors are also provided for a subset of emissions categories with strong temporal variation (e.g., manure management, petroleum and natural gas production, etc.). The gridded methane GHGI dataset can be used by researchers to better compare the national U.S. GHGI with emission estimates from more regional and local observations of atmospheric methane. Users of the gridded GHGI are asked to cite the original reference ( Maasakkers et al., 2023 ) in their publications. Error estimates are also described in that reference. Manuscripts describing the gridded GHGI have been peer-reviewed, but are not part of the same annual expert and public review processes as the U.S. EPA National and State-level Inventory. Data Version Details The gridded methane GHGI is continually updated to capture ongoing improvements and updates to the national U.S. GHGI. The gridded GHGI currently includes 2 versions, each of which reflect sectoral methane emissions that are consistent with different versions of the U.S. GHGI. Versions include: Current Version(s) Gridded methane GHGI Version 2 Published in 2023 Emission Year(s): 2012 – 2018 Resolution: 0.1°×0.1° spatial, annual & monthly temporal Consistent with the 2020 U.S. GHGI Reference: Maasakkers et al., 2023 Data Download Gridded methane GHGI Version 2 - Express Extension Published in 2023 Emission Year(s): 2012 – 2020 Resolution: 0.1°×0.1° spatial, annual temporal Consistent with the 2022 U.S. GHGI Reference: Maasakkers et al., 2023 Data Download Note: This dataset is not a full update to the main v2 gridded GHGI (above), and instead uses annual source-specific spatial patterns from the main product to allocate methane emissions from a more recent version of the U.S. GHGI, across an extended time series. This allows for publication of gridded emissions data that reflect more recent inventory data, in the interim, before a full update to v3 is complete. More information is available on the Data Download page. Previous Versions Gridded methane GHGI Version 1 Published in 2016 Emission Year(s): 2012 Resolution: 0.1°×0.1° spatial, annual & monthly temporal Consistent with the 2016 U.S. GHGI Reference: Maasakkers et al., 2016 Data Download External Resources This dataset will also be featured on the upcoming U.S. Greenhouse Gas Information Center. Visit the ‘ Explore Data ’ tab on the US GHG Center site to create and view custom maps of the gridded methane GHGI v2 – Express Extension dataset. pages.title: Aide to pro-Kremlin Ukrainian ex-PM badly hurt in Moscow car bomb British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Sergei Zavorotny, now a journalist and commentator, was previously an adviser to Ukrainian ex-prime minister Mykola Azarov.
pages.text: Aide to pro-Kremlin Ukrainian ex-PM badly hurt in Moscow car bomb Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Aide to fugitive Ukrainian ex-PM wounded in latest Moscow car bombing 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Dan Sales Reuters The site of a car explosion that wounded Sergei Zavorotny in Moscow A car bomb attack in Moscow has wounded a former adviser to Ukrainian ex-prime minister Mykola Azarov, Russia's Investigative Committee says. Sergei Zavorotny, now a journalist and commentator, was behind the wheel of his black Toyota when the explosion happened and Azarov told Russian TV his condition in hospital was "rather critical". The car bomb went off a day after a Russian colonel was killed in another explosion in St Petersburg, and both blasts are seen as part of a series of attacks on military and prominent figures linked to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Zavorotny, 72, worked as a press aide to Mykola Azarov in Kyiv until 2014. But when pro-Kremlin Ukrainian president Viktor Yanukovych was toppled from power, Azarov fled Kyiv for Russia and tried unsuccessfully to set up a government in exile. In a 2020 US Senate report on interference in the 2016 American presidential election, Zavorotny is described at the time as an SVR [Russian foreign intelligence] officer involved in influence operations. Russia's Investigative Committee said on Telegram on Friday: "Serhiy Zavorotny, a former adviser to the former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, was injured while driving a car. He was taken to one of the city hospitals, where he is receiving medical care." It added: "A set of necessary investigative actions is being carried out. A number of examinations will be appointed, including medical and explosives." According to several unconfirmed reports, Zavorotny suffered a number of serious injuries after an explosive device was detonated remotely. Russia said the car bombs are the latest in a series of attacks targeting pro-Kremlin figures. On Thursday a car bomb in the Pushkinsky District of St Petersburg killed a member of the Russian military, again after it was attached to the base of the car and detonated remotely. The man targeted in the attack is yet to be named officially, but reputable sources suggest he was a high-ranking figure in the 6th Guards Air and Air Defence Forces Army. Overnight into Friday, Ukraine and Russia exchanged attacks on each other's territories. Ukrainian authorities said a hospital had been targeted by Russian bombardment. They added that three people, including a 17-year-old boy, were also killed in attacks across southern Odesa and Zaporizhzhia. Russia said a Ukrainian strike on an industrial facility in the central Samara region killed four people. And in the southern Volgograd region another four died after an industrial zone was hit by drones. A further person died in the Bryansk border region, an area that is often fired upon. Ukraine said these were retaliatory attacks in response to Russia's persistent targeting of its cities. pages.title: Hot fridges, a fake nuclear alert and a $6bn heist: are we in the foothills of a hacking epidemic? | Hacking | The Guardian
pages.description: As AI exposes flaws in IT systems and geopolitics plays out on the cyber frontline, some experts say the events of recent weeks could soon be a common occurrence
pages.text: Hot fridges, a fake nuclear alert and a $6bn heist: are we in the foothills of a hacking epidemic? | Hacking | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Composite: Guardian Design/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Composite: Guardian Design/Getty Images The Sunday read Hacking Hot fridges, a fake nuclear alert and a $6bn heist: are we in the foothills of a hacking epidemic? As AI exposes flaws in IT systems and geopolitics plays out on the cyber frontline, some experts say the events of recent weeks could soon be a common occurrence Dan Milmo and Aisha Down Sun 8 Nov 2026 01.00 EST Last modified on Wed 11 Nov 2026 12.26 EST Share Alex Pearce was doing the morning rounds at his fruit and vegetable wholesale business in London on Monday last week when he noticed something odd. The defrost light on refrigeration unit 2 was on, and the panel reading was 150C. Unit 4 was the same. As he approached his biggest unit, its defrost light also blinked on. It was at this point that Pearce thought: is this a cyber-attack? He walked over to the box connecting the units to the internet and yanked out the cable. He was right. View image in fullscreen Alex Pearce unplugged the internet at his wholesale fruit and vegetable business after seeing the temperature of the refrigeration units shoot up. Photograph: Martin Godwin/The Guardian On the same day, retailers in Belgium , Estonia, Ireland, Finland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden reported similar problems, with refrigerators and freezers in some shops soaring to as high as 50C (122F). “If it had happened on a Saturday morning, when I don’t tend to be here, it could ultimately have led to a fire,” Pearce said. But it is not just Pearce and a disparate group of retailers, as well as French blood banks , that have been suffering. The hacking attack was one of three over a number of days. On 30 October, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, was robbed of $6.3bn (£4.7bn) in a record heist and on 1 November hackers targeted Ukraine’s emergency alert app, sending people in Kyiv a fake nuclear strike alert . View image in fullscreen Hackers targeted Ukraine’s emergency alert app this month to send warnings to people in Kyiv. Photograph: Roman Pilipey/AFP/Getty Images The official message after the fridge attacks is: expect more disruption. We are in the “foothills” of a new hacking landscape, the head of the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre said this week. Referring to flaws in IT systems that are being exposed by AI technology, the NCSC boss, Richard Horne, said: “There are so many vulnerabilities out there that … you could say are waiting to be exploited.” He added: “The most serious risk we face in the short term is just a huge rise in the volume of incidents … and I think you could probably point to the last few months and say we’ve started to see that.” Hacked fridges and other dangers lurking in the ‘internet of shit’ Read more Websites around the world were temporarily taken out of service as a precaution last month when AI technology from the ChatGPT developer OpenAI helped discover a flaw in PHP , a computer language used to build much of the world wide web. French supermarket fridges were also attacked last month in what could have been a trial run for the more expansive foray this week . View image in fullscreen Boxes of perished goods outside an Intermarché in Paris last month after a cyber-attack that could have been a trial run for this week’s foray. Photograph: Lucien Libert/Reuters To Azeem Azhar, a tech entrepreneur and commentator, the way AI models were discovering flaws that assailants could harness recalled China’s Covid ground zero. This was, he said, a “ Wuhan moment ”. Azar’s assertion headlined a Substack post that also quoted the cybersecurity executive Matthew Prince, who said last month: “We’re going to have a couple of years where every single week it’s going to feel like the sky is falling.” Not long afterwards, Pearce’s defrost l

Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office January 24, 2023 Estimated Read Time min Author: Dr. Lynn Wendt, Laboratory Relationship Manager, Idaho National Laboratory Read Lynn's bio ► Meet the other bloggers ► Return to Bioprose blog ► As the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) supports research, development, and demonstration to enable conversion of grasses, crop residue, and forest byproducts into alternative fuels and advanced manufacturing materials, year-to-year chemical changes caused by climate volatility have become a growing concern. Examining the differences in biomass samples from 2010, a normal year, and the drought year of 2012, researchers from Idaho National Laboratory (INL) have set out to identify what drought does to biomass chemistry and what adjustments might be needed in the processing and production of drought-impacted biomass. While it has always been known that drought can affect biomass yields and production costs, extreme swings and unpredictability in weather, especially in the American Midwest, are raising new questions. In the 2021 Regional Feedstock Partnership Biomass Quality Assessment Final Report , the INL-led team has produced an assessment of what effect variable environmental conditions can have on the chemical properties of Miscanthus, switchgrass, sorghum, energy cane, mixed perennial grasses, and short-rotation woody feedstocks such as shrub willow. A Wealth of Information DOE’s Bioenergy Technologies Office (BETO) announced its Billion Ton Vision in 2005, which provides a roadmap of how one billion tons of biomass might be produced for the bioenergy industry by 2030. The Regional Feedstock Partnership and subsequent Bioenergy Feedstock Library were created to help reach the Billion Ton Vision. For years, DOE’s Bioenergy Feedstock Library, hosted at INL, has been accumulating biomass samples. Today, the library stores and tracks metadata and analytical data on more than 70,000 samples, making it one of the largest bioenergy resource data repositories in the world. Year-to-year chemical changes in biomass came into sharp focus when the biomass data from 2012, the year drought affected 65% of the country, was compared to biomass data from the same locations in 2010, a non-drought year. Drought conditions at the end of October in 2010 and 2012 for Nebraska, Missouri, and Oklahoma. Credit Source: Frontiers in Energy Research, article authors: A. Hoover, et al. Three Species, Three Climates For each of the three species—Miscanthus grown in Nebraska, a tall fescue mixture harvested from Missouri, and switchgrass grown in Oklahoma—three aspects were considered to determine the location-specific drought conditions and the drought stress reactions for each of the biomass types. Precipitation and temperature trends during the growing season had to be considered, as plants that experience drought conditions can recover if favorable conditions return before harvest. Second, chemical changes, including multiple types of compatible solutes, structural components, and inorganic elements, were assessed. pages.title: What we lose when animals go extinct | National Geographic
pages.description: Animals are disappearing at hundreds of times the normal rate, primarily because of shrinking habitats. Their biggest threat: humans.
pages.text: What we lose when animals go extinct | National Geographic Photographs by Joel Sartore By Elizabeth Kolbert 20 min read This story appears in the October 2019 issue of National Geographic magazine. LIFE, BESIEGED Most of the animals shown here are among the more than 28,000 species of animals and plants that the International Union for Conservation of Nature says are threatened with extinction. That number actually understates the risk. Since 1964, when the IUCN established a “ red list ” of threatened species and began compiling data gathered worldwide, the list has become the preeminent global database of endangered life and an essential tool for conservation policy. Yet the IUCN has been able to assess only about 106,000 species of the more than 1.5 million species of animals and more than 300,000 plants that scientists have described and named—which they estimate is less than a quarter of what’s really out there. A recent intergovernmental report on the biodiversity crisis estimated that extinction threatens up to a million animal and plant species, known and unknown. The IUCN hopes to raise the number of species assessments to 160,000 by 2020. Next up on its agenda: a “ green list ” of conservation successes. It will be much shorter than the red one. The large yellow-footed tortoise, Chelonoidis denticulata (vulnerable), from South America and the Caribbean, is hunted for its meat, which is considered a delicacy. It also is captured and traded as a pet. Kansas City Zoo, Missouri THE BIGGEST THREAT: HUMANS Habitat loss—driven primarily by human expansion as we develop land for housing, agriculture, and commerce—is the biggest threat facing most animal species, followed by hunting and fishing. Even when habitat is not lost entirely, it may be changed so much that animals cannot adapt . Fences fragment a grassland or logging cuts through a forest , breaking up migration corridors; pollution renders a river toxic ; pesticides kill widely and indiscriminately. To those local threats one must increasingly add global ones: Trade, which spreads disease and invasive species from place to place, and climate change , which eventually will affect every species on Earth—starting with the animals that live on cool mountaintops or depend on polar ice . All of these threats lead, directly or indirectly, back to humans and our expanding footprint. Most species face multiple threats. Some can adapt to us; others will vanish. Humphead wrasse, Cheilinus undulatus (endangered) Dallas World Aquarium Arctic fox, Vulpes lagopus (least concern) Great Bend–Brit Spaugh Zoo, Kansas Lesser flamingo, Phoeniconaias minor (near threatened) Cleveland Metroparks Zoo 1 of 16 Red panda, Ailurus fulgens fulgens (endangered) Virginia Zoo - Photograph by Joel Sartore, National Geographic Photo Ark If we lived in an ordinary time— time here being understood in the long, unhurried sense of a geologic epoch—it would be nearly impossible to watch a species vanish. Such an event would occur too infrequently for a person to witness. In the case of mammals, the best-studied group of animals, the fossil record indicates that the “background” rate of extinction, the one that prevailed before humans entered the picture, is so low that over the course of a millennium, a single species should disappear. But of course we don’t live in an ordinary time. Everywhere we look, species are winking out. Just in the past decade, two mammal species have gone extinct: a bat known as the Christmas Island pipistrelle and a rat, the Bramble Cay melomys . The International Union for Conservation of Nature lists more than 200 mammal species and subspecies as critically endangered. In some cases, like the Sumatran rhino or the vaquita —a porpoise native to the Gulf of California—there are fewer than a hundred individuals left. Esto le permite presentar su declaración de impuestos sin multas hasta el 15 de octubre. Asegúrese de pagar cualquier impuesto que adeude para la fecha de presentación en abril. La prórroga es solo para presentar su declaración. Obtenga una prórroga Existen tres maneras de llegar hasta el 15 de octubre para presentar su declaración de impuestos. Pague en línea y marque la casilla Pague lo que adeude al utilizar una opción de pago en línea y marque la casilla que está pagando como parte de la presentación para una prórroga. No tiene que presentar un formulario de prórroga separado y recibirá un número de confirmación de su prórroga para sus registros. Utilice Free File (sin límite de ingresos para prórrogas) Utilice Free File del IRS para solicitar electrónicamente una prórroga automática de la declaración de impuestos. Solicite una prórroga por correo Presente el Formulario 4868 (SP), Solicitud de Prórroga Automática para Presentar la Declaración del Impuesto sobre el Ingreso Personal de los Estados Unidos . Puede presentar por correo, en línea con un socio de presentación electrónica del IRS o a través de un profesional de impuestos. Estime cuánto impuesto adeuda para el año en el formulario de prórroga: Reste los impuestos que ya pagó para el año de presentación. pages.description: OpenStreetMap is a map of the world, created by people like you and free to use under an open license.
pages.text: simon04's Diary | DinoData: a phone-first tag editor that explains every tag | OpenStreetMap Select Language Loading... Close simon04's Diary DinoData: a phone-first tag editor that explains every tag Posted by simon04 on 4 November 2026 in English . DinoData is a web-based tag editor for OpenStreetMap nodes, ways and relations, designed for phones first. Open an object, see what it is and what each tag means in your language, edit the tags with inputs suited to them, and save as a changeset . Geometry is not edited. It runs entirely in the browser and is hosted on Wikimedia Toolforge. It started as a Wikidata editor; the OpenStreetMap mode lives next to it in the same app. Finding an object Search for a place, or paste what you have: an openstreetmap.org URL (including edit and API URLs), an iD or JOSM remote control link, a short ID like n123 or way 123 , or coordinates. Other text is a place search with Photon and Nominatim . “Near me” lists the tagged objects around you via the Overpass API , handy while surveying. Understanding the tags What the object is (“Cafe”), from the translated presets of the iD tagging schema Every tag explained from the wiki’s data items : description in your language, status, image, links to the wiki page and the Wikidata concept Deprecated and discouraged tags marked A small map, the parent ways and relations, and the history: tags added, changed and removed per version, with user and changeset comment Editing Preset fields with matching inputs: chips for yes/no and other choices, a value picker with translated options and the most used values from taginfo , chips for multiple values like cuisine=pizza;pasta , toggles for diet:* , names per language, a search for wikidata=* , and number, phone and URL keyboards Issues with one-tap fixes: deprecated tags , values not matching the format documented on the wiki, tags not meant for the element type, incompatible tags Undo per field or tag; pending edits survive reloads and the login For power users, a text view shows all tags as key=value lines or as Level0 text. Paste tags with Ctrl+V anywhere: key=value lines, tab-separated lines, "key"="value" from taginfo or Overpass turbo , or Level0 text as is. key= removes a tag. Copied Level0 text contains the full object, so it can be pasted into Level0 . Saving Log in with your OpenStreetMap account (OAuth 2.0 in a popup, so pending edits are kept), review the changes, enter a comment and pick a source . Each save is one changeset with created_by=DinoData . If someone edited the object in the meantime, the tags are merged; only keys changed on both sides need a choice. Limitations No geometry editing, no creating or deleting objects, no editing of relation members, one object per changeset, no offline editing. The interface of the OpenStreetMap mode is available in English, German and Dutch. Try it Open dinodata.toolforge.org/#osm . DinoData is free software under GPL-3.0; the code is on GitHub , and bug reports and ideas are welcome in the issue tracker . pages.title: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.
pages.text: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks 4 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Harry Sekulich Getty Images US envoys Jared Kushner (left) and Steve Witkoff (right) met Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday evening Ukraine's president has welcomed a pledge from US envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, to include delegates from the European Union in the next round of peace talks with Russia. European leaders have expressed deepening security concerns this week, and Volodymyr Zelensky said bringing them into the talks would ensure the EU has a "voice" in negotiations. Kushner and Witkoff met Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday evening as part of a busy day of shuttle diplomacy - they met Vladimir Putin in Moscow earlier, who said that Russia's position on the war - and its demand for territory - has not changed. The meetings follow talks in Abu Dhabi last week that failed to reach a breakthrough in ending the war. But Thursday did see Russia and Ukraine agree to another prisoner exchange - the largest swap yet since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. Kushner said it would return "thousands of people to their families", but there were no further details over how many prisoners would be exchanged or when it would happen. US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow Europe's security 'fundamentally reshaped' by war in Ukraine Zelensky has for several years been calling for European delegates to be included in the peace talks, and says it makes sense because of Kyiv's longer-term ambition to join the European Union. On Thursday, Kushner said that the US has been "working very, very closely over the past several months with Europeans and I think that that's been very important." He added that he had stressed to Putin how important it was to have European delegates "at the table". "He's willing to give it a try," Kushner added. Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US government's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin. Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent. Earlier on Thursday, the EU's foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, told the BBC's Newshour the presence of a European delegate showed the Kremlin "now realised that Europe is a big player". Kallas also expressed doubts that there was Russian momentum towards a peace deal. Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) Micheál Martin told a host of European leaders gathered in Dublin on Thursday that he believed the security of the region had been "fundamentally reshaped" by Russia's war. "Many member states [of the EU] feel an existential threat because of what has happened in Ukraine and the potential, if Ukraine was to fall, for further aggression on the European continent," he told reporters. Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. Tensions between the US and Ukraine were on display on Thursday before Witkoff and Kushner's meeting with Zelensky. Earlier, the Ukrainian leader said that the military was facing more "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones. Starshield technology, which was developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX company for government and military use, has played a vital role in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line. on a healthy planet Skip to main content UNESCO , Artificial Intelligence Can We Trust AI on Climate? The short answer depends on how hard you push and which language you use. A new report by UNESCO and University College London, presented at COP31, finds that AI models answer 90% of climate questions correctly but quickly abandon scientific facts when challenged by users—a warning to policymakers and researchers considering AI for climate policy development. Accuracy also varies widely across 13 different languages, reflecting differences in available training data, with better outcomes in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese and lower marks in languages such as Hindi, Urdu and Swahili. Eight times out of 10, models pivoted at the very first sign that the user mildly disagreed, confirming alarming errors such as ‘Co2 is not the main driver of climate change. NIST promotes the development and deployment of advanced communications technologies by advancing the measurement science underlying wireless technologies. NIST provides measurement assurance through the development of quantitative analytical measurement tools to aid industry in the deployment of innovative biotechnologies and advanced biomaterials. NIST develops safety standards for construction. We also study ways to better protect buildings from dangers like earthquakes and windstorms. NIST develops the technology, measurement methods and standards to address the needs of the chemical industry. NIST develops cybersecurity and privacy standards, guidelines, best practices, and resources to meet the needs of U.S. industry, federal agencies, and the broader public. NIST provides the standards, develops the instruments and performs the calibrations necessary to keep both the smallest electronic components and the largest power grids running smoothly and safely. NIST develops testing methods, measurement science and reference materials to ensure the quality of energy-related products and services and ensure fairness in the marketplace. NIST is helping to advance measurements and tools for environmental science. NIST's fire research develops, verifies and utilizes measurements and predictive methods to quantify the behavior of fire and means to reduce its impact. Bringing together experts from the forensic, research, legal and law enforcement communities to strengthen forensic science and create a safer, more just society. NIST provides measurement assurance for biomedical stakeholders through the development of measurement tools for medical devices, clinical diagnostics, imaging tools and biotherapeutics. NIST advances the state-of-the-art in IT in such applications as cybersecurity and biometrics. NIST infrastructure research encompasses smart grids and smart cities, public safety, community resilience, communications, critical infrastructure security, buildings and construction codes. NIST provides technical support to the nation's manufacturing industry as it strives to out-innovate and outperform the competition. NIST develops testbeds, defines benchmarks and develops formability measurements and models for a variety of emerging materials. NIST researchers use the latest mathematics approaches and computational methods to help tackle some of the most difficult scientific, technical and engineering problems and tasks. Metrology is the science of measurement and its application. NIST's work in metrology focuses on advancing measurement science to enhance economic security and improve quality of life. NIST is at the forefront of basic research with neutrons, and the NIST Center for Neutron Research is a national resource for industry, universities and government agencies. The Baldrige Performance Excellence Program offers criteria, assessments, tools, training and a community for those dedicated to helping organizations improve. pages.text: How to File a Complaint | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content How to File a Complaint More in This Section Close How to File a Complaint Information You Need to File a Complaint Third-Party Complaints Local Offices Freedom of Information Act Spanish Version The Wage and Hour Division is responsible for enforcing some of the nation’s most comprehensive federal labor laws. The workers who are protected by these laws often want to know: How do we do what we do? Many investigations are initiated by complaints, which are confidential. The name of the complainant, the nature of the complaint, and whether a complaint exists may not be disclosed. An employer cannot retaliate against a worker for exercising their rights , filing a complaint or cooperating with an investigation. Complaint Process Gather Information Gather information you will need to file your complaint . While third-party complainants may not be able to provide all the information needed, the more information made available the better we can address concerns raised. How to File Call 1-866-487-9243, or for general questions reach out to us online . We Work with You We will work with you to answer your questions and determine whether an investigation is the best course of action. Gather information you will need to file your complaint with us. Learn More about Information You Need to File a Complaint Learn more about the investigation process and the laws we cover. Learn More about Visits to Employers Frequently asked questions and answers about filing a complaint with WHD. Learn More about FAQs In addition to complaints, we select certain types of businesses or industries for investigation. We target low-wage industries, for example, because of high rates of violations or egregious violations, the employment of vulnerable workers, or rapid changes in an industry, such as growth or decline. Here’s a breakdown of our typical investigation processes, regardless of whether the investigation starts from a complaint or an agency-initiated investigation: Investigation Process Initial Conference Our investigator holds an initial conference with the employer and/or the employer’s representative and tours the employer’s establishment. Conducting Interviews Our investigator interviews employees in private. Reviewing Records The WHD investigator reviews the employer’s records to determine compliance. Final Conference We hold a final conference with the employer and/or the employer’s representative to discuss any violations found and how to correct them. If back wages are owed to employees, the investigator will request payment of back wages. If you have questions or concerns, you can call us at 1-866-487-9243 or visit dol.gov/agencies/whd . You will be directed to the nearest WHD office for assistance. There are WHD offices throughout the country with trained professionals to help you.

pages.title: A bold plan to save Africa’s shrinking giraffe herds | National Geographic
pages.description: The mysterious, silent giants face increasing threats in Africa. Relocating animals to create new populations could bolster some species but poses new risks.
pages.text: A bold plan to save Africa’s shrinking giraffe herds | National Geographic By Joshua Foer Photographs by Ami Vitale 25 min read This story appears in the October 2019 issue of National Geographic magazine. Of all the large African mammals that wildlife veterinarian Pete Morkel has had to capture over his career—lions, forest elephants, white rhinos— giraffes are the most stressful. “With other animals, you’re trying to give just enough anesthetic to immobilize them, but with a giraffe, we use a total overdose to chemically knock them off their feet,” the sun-leathered 59-year-old tells me as I stalk him stalking a two-year-old female giraffe somewhere in the Nigerien bush, about 60 miles east of Niamey, Niger’s capital. He is wearing a camo hat and a pair of torn, purple-checkered boxers that he’s been wearing as shorts for the past several days. ( Giraffes Seen Feasting on Skeleton—Here's Why) Morkel has loaded his dart gun with a dose of etorphine, an opioid about 6,000 times more powerful than morphine. Once it penetrates the giraffe’s skin, he and his team will have just minutes to chase down the animal, tackle her, and inject her neck with an antidote to keep her from dying. If she can be successfully captured and survive a 500-mile translocation across Niger, she’ll become one of eight founding “Adams” and “Eves” of a new population of one of the world’s rarest wild mammals. An orphaned giraffe nuzzles a caregiver at Sarara Camp in northern Kenya. Samburu cattle herders found the abandoned calf and alerted Sarara—known for raising orphaned mammals and returning them to their habitat. The young giraffe now lives with a wild herd. Photograph by Ami Vitale The giraffes we have chased for a week are the descendants of some 50 animals that made their way to the West African country of Niger in the late 1980s, when drought and war pushed them from their habitat in neighboring Mali. They walked south-southeast across the Sahel, along the Niger River, and skirted Niamey before settling in the Koure region, on a dry and dusty plateau. A Fulani herder named Amadou Hama, 76, recalled what it was like decades ago when he first encountered one of these giraffes one evening while tending his cattle. “We thought it was the devil, because of that neck and those horns. People had told me about dangerous animals like lions, but nobody had ever told me about the giraffe. We were frightened. Even the cows were frightened.” These newly arrived giants were the last survivors of a once vast population of “white giraffes” whose range at the turn of the last century spanned all of West Africa, from the coast of Senegal to Nigeria. Framed against the Nairobi skyline, giraffes roam Nairobi National Park, four miles from the center of Kenya’s sprawling capital. More than 100 mammal species live in the 45-square-mile park, but Nairobi’s expansion threatens this habitat. Photograph by Paras Chandaria In 2016 a team of scientists came to an epiphany (if still contentious) about giraffes. Until then, the conventional view held that all giraffes belonged to a single species, Giraffa camelopardalis. But genetic analysis now suggests that giraffes are in fact four distinct species , actually more different from each other than the brown bear is from the polar bear. And those four species can be further classified into five subspecies, including the rare West African Giraffa camelopardalis peralta , the pale, spotted refugees now found only in the Koure region of Niger. Based on this new taxonomy , all but two subspecies would be considered vulnerable, endangered, or critically endangered, and across Africa, populations have declined by almost 40 percent over the past three decades, leaving an estimated 110,000 giraffes in the world. pages.title: US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: US envoy Steve Witkoff says President Putin has agreed to European negotiators joining the next round of Ukraine talks.
pages.text: US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow 4 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Laura Gozzi Sputnik / Pool via AFP Witkoff and Kushner's visit to Moscow was the latest of many trips the US envoys have made to see Vladimir Putin US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held a fresh round of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, a day after the latest discussions aimed at ending the war in Ukraine wrapped up in Abu Dhabi. The pair are now in Dublin to meet Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky, and Witkoff said a new round of trilateral talks had already been agreed with Putin. But in a sign of further tension, Zelensky said on Thursday morning that Ukraine's military was again facing "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones. The peace talks in the Emirates were framed as being centred around European security arrangements in a post-war scenario, although a resolution to the war sparked by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 still appears distant. Comments by both President Vladimir Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted, and that Moscow's demands for territory and neutrality continue to far exceed what Ukraine is prepared to consider. Witkoff said that Europeans would join the next round of talks. "They are our partners and it's important to us that they take part," Witkoff told Russian state TV after meeting Putin in the Kremlin. Prime Minister Andy Burnham had said that UK national security adviser Jonathan Powell would join Zelensky, Witkoff and Kushner for talks in Dublin, but Downing Street later said they had been delayed, meaning the national security adviser could no longer join. Earlier on Thursday, Zelensky said Ukraine was trying to clear up the Starlink situation with the American side but added "some things" were already clear: "If someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then this tells us where things are going." He did not elaborate further. Starshield was developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX company for government and military use. Along with Starlink, it has come to play a vital role in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line. A similar issue with connectivity affected the front line in late October and lasted about a week before it was fixed and it remained unclear who had ordered the temporary restrictions. Why is Ukraine so reliant on Starlink and can Europe plug the gap? Zelensky said the current disruption had been ongoing for several days and was "helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine". Meanwhile, some of the longstanding roadblocks in the peace process were addressed during the US-Russia talks in the Kremlin. The territorial issue continues to be a key point of contention, Putin said. "For us there is only one line of demarcation: the line of the state border. Because then it will be clear that we are here, and you are there. As soon as we start discussing 'grey zones'… arguments immediately start and any agreements become unstable. And there will be no lasting peace." He also suggested organising a humanitarian truce to allow for the evacuation of hundreds of civilians from a frontline area, on the model of last month's ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky. Putin suggested a similar five-day ceasefire for Kostyantynivka, a contested front-line Ukrainian city in the eastern region of Donetsk. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to this park navigation Skip to the main content Skip to this park information section Skip to the footer section National Park Service Katmai National Park & Preserve Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Katmai National Park & Preserve Contact Us Basic Information Physical Address Directions Operating Hours & Seasons Weather Fees & Passes Visitor Centers Internet & Cellular Access Internet & Cellular Access Details The purpose of Katmai National Park and Preserve is to protect, study, and interpret active volcanism surrounding the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes, extensive coastal resources, habitats supporting a high concentration of salmon and brown bears, and an ongoing story of humans integrated with a dynamic subarctic ecosystem. The park and preserve offer unique opportunities to explore vast wilderness and immense volcanoes, watch brown bears, fish for salmon and trout, and many other activities. Katmai is open year-round for you to enjoy. However, it is a remote park that cannot be accessed by car. There are few services in the park and preserve. The closest grocery store and post office are located outside of the park in King Salmon. Please, plan ahead and bring what you need to enjoy your visit. Browse the links below and Katmai’s frequently asked questions to help plan your visit.
