pages.description: NIST develops standards, methods, tools, and technology to advance the reliability of genomic measurements for
pages.text: Genomics | NIST Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/genomics Biotechnology Genomics Sign Up to Get NIST News GovDelivery Genome in a Bottle Consortium NIST Genome Editing Consortium NIST develops standards, methods, tools, and technology to advance the reliability of genomic measurements for use in biotechnology including genome editing, human genome sequencing, cancer genomics, and bioinformatics. NIST's programs in genomics are supported by our deep expertise in measurement science, molecular biology, cancer biology, and bioinformatics. For example, NIST scientists led the development of the world's first and only whole genome reference materials, authoritatively characterized by the NIST-led Genome in a Bottle Consortium ; these human genomes provide laboratories with the capability to accurately “map” DNA for genetic testing, benchmark sequencing technologies and bioinformatics, and develop new medical diagnostics and future customized drug therapies. The NIST-led Genome Editing Consortium aims to address the measurements and standards needed to increase confidence and lower the risk of utilizing genome editing technologies in research and commercial products. NIST's cancer biomarker reference materials help researchers and clinicians establish analytical validation of their measurement processes. News and Updates Release of RM 8043 - Forensic DNA Resource Samples Read more NIST Releases Trove of Genetic Data to Spur Cancer Research Read more NIST Releases Reference Material to Aid Gut Microbiome Research Read more Key Accomplishments The NIST Genome Editing Consortium Lexicon Working Group has developed a standard genome editing lexicon , with 42 defined terms. This lexicon was developed to provide a unified reference set of terms and technical definitions that standardizes their use and meaning, helping the biotechnology community have productive communications. NIST’s human genome reference material , the first of its kind in the world, generated data that is accurate enough to be used as a benchmarking tool for medical and research labs. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration used this resource to approve one of the first commercially available next-generation DNA sequencers for clinical use. NIST now offers four additional human genome reference materials to help test labs assess their ability to measure genetic links within families, and compare and contrast genes from people with different lineages. These additional materials increase the confidence of DNA sequencing labs in reporting results, improving genetic tests used for disease risk prediction, diagnosis, and progression tracking. These reference materials also give companies reliable data to guide innovation in hardware, software and clinical research. GIAB developed the first benchmark of large structural changes that occur in the human genome , which will enable clinical translation and technology development for detection of diseases associated with these difficult-to-detect changes; GIAB benchmarks helped demonstrate the performance of a new nanopore-based technology ; collaboration with PacBio to benchmark performance of a new highly accurate long DNA sequencing technology . NIST and GIAB continue to use new technologies to shed light on accuracy of more and more challenging DNA sequences. The method enables better use of taxpayers’ investment in science by helping to provide assurance that cell lines are as labelled. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Boise District Office The Boise District, located in southwest Idaho, manages approximately 4 million acres of public land stretching from the central Idaho mountains to the borders with Oregon and Nevada. The District has many challenges to face as it balances its mission of multiple use and sustainable yield to achieve a sustainable ecosystem. Some of the major activities occurring within the district include: livestock grazing, wildland fire suppression, as well as motorized and non-motorized recreation. The Boise District is divided into three geographic areas/field offices: Bruneau (1.4 million acres), Four Rivers (1.3 million acres) and Owyhee (1.2 million acres). The District also manages Idaho's only National Conservation Area, Morley Nelson Snake River Birds of Prey (487,000 acres), home to the greatest concentration of nesting birds of prey in North America – and perhaps, the world. Some 800 pairs of hawks, owls, eagles and falcons come each spring to mate and raise their young here. Directora de los CDC Inglés (English) Imprimir Related Pages Biografía del personal Erica Schwartz, MD, MPH, JD (RADM, USPHS, RET), es la directora de los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC) y la administradora de la Agencia para Sustancias Tóxicas y el Registro de Enfermedades. Función en los CDC Como directora de los CDC, la Dra. Schwartz lidera la agencia en su misión de proteger la salud y seguridad de las personas en los Estados Unidos mediante la orientación basada en la evidencia, la excelencia operativa y las soluciones basadas en colaboraciones para abordar los retos de salud pública en el siglo XXI. En este cargo, la Dra. Schwartz tiene como prioridad modernizar la infraestructura de datos de los CDC para la detección de amenazas en tiempo real; empoderar a los colaboradores estatales, tribales, territoriales y de las comunidades locales; y apoyar a la dedicada fuerza laboral de la agencia. Experiencia previa Antes de vincularse a los CDC, la Dra. Schwartz se desempeñó como subdirectora general de Servicios de Salud de los Estados Unidos. Durante su permanencia allí, cumplió un papel fundamental en la pandemia de COVID-19 con el diseño y puesta en marcha de sitios para la realización de pruebas desde el auto de carácter escalable en todos los 50 estados, Puerto Rico y el Distrito de Columbia. Este esfuerzo dio como resultado que casi 11.5 millones de personas en los Estados Unidos se realizaran pruebas y amplió el acceso a la atención médica al tiempo que se preservó la crítica capacidad hospitalaria. A principios de su carrera profesional, la Dra. Schwartz ejerció como médica ocupacional en la Marina de Guerra de los Estados Unidos. Sus funciones incluyeron su desempeño como jefa del Centro de Medicina Ocupacional y el Centro de Vacunación, así como fungir como jefa del Departamento de Medicina Preventiva del Centro Médico Naval en Annapolis, MD. Fungió también como médica ocupacional y epidemióloga clínica en el Centro de Salud Pública de la Marina de Guerra y el Cuerpo de Infantería de Marina en Portsmouth, VA. En el 2005, la Dra. Schwartz se transfirió de la Marina de Guerra al Servicio de Salud Pública de los Estados Unidos (USPHS) y fue asignada a la Guardia Costera de los Estados Unidos. Se enfocó en crear directrices para la protección de la salud del personal de respuesta durante crisis nacionales y globales importantes como los huracanes Katrina y Rita, la pandemia de H1N1 del 2009, el terremoto de Haití del 2010, el derrame de Deepwater Horizon y el brote de ébola en África Occidental. En el 2015, la Dra. Schwartz fue nombrada con el rango de contralmirante en el USPHS y pasó a ser la funcionaria médica principal de la Guardia Costera de los EE. UU, donde supervisó el sistema de atención médica, el programa de seguridad y las iniciativas de balance de trabajo y vida personal de la Guardia Costera. Estudios La Dra. Schwartz tiene un grado universitario en Ingeniería Biomédica y un título de doctor en Medicina de Brown University. También obtuvo una maestría en Salud Pública en Epidemiología de la Universidad de Ciencias de la Salud de los Servicios Uniformados y un doctorado en Derecho de la Universidad de Maryland. Su capacitación académica y profesional reflejan un compromiso de por vida con la salud pública, el rigor científico y la excelencia operativa. Energy Department Announces Actions to Secure American Critical Minerals and Materials Supply Chain The U.S. Department of Energy today announced its intent to issue notices of funding opportunities totaling nearly $1 billion to advance and scale mining, processing, and manufacturing technologies across key stages of the critical minerals and materials supply chains. Energy.gov August 13, 2025 Estimated Read Time min Proposed funding will accelerate the growth of the U.S. critical minerals and materials sector. WASHINGTON —The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced its intent to issue notices of funding opportunities (NOFO) totaling nearly $1 billion to advance and scale mining, processing, and manufacturing technologies across key stages of the critical minerals and materials supply chains. The funding announcements, issued in accordance with President Trump’s Executive Order Unleashing American Energy , will help ensure a more secure, predictable, and affordable supply of critical minerals and materials that are foundational to American energy dominance, national security, and industrial competitiveness. “For too long, the United States has relied on foreign actors to supply and process the critical materials that are essential to modern life and our national security,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright . “Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, the Energy Department will play a leading role in reshoring the processing of critical materials and expanding our domestic supply of these indispensable resources.” Proposed NOFOs announced today include: Critical Minerals and Materials Accelerator The Advanced Materials and Manufacturing Technologies Office expects to release a NOFO of up to $50 million early this fall through the Critical Minerals and Materials (CMM) Accelerator program. The CMM Accelerator promotes technology maturation that can unlock capital investments and facilitate domestic commercialization. The proposed NOFO addresses several areas of interest, including processes in the rare-earth magnet supply chain; processes to refine and alloy gallium, gallium nitride, germanium, and silicon carbide for use in semiconductors; cost-competitive technologies for direct lithium extraction and separation; and critical-material separation technologies that allow for the co-production of useful products from byproducts and scrap. Mines & Metals Capacity Expansion – Piloting Byproduct Critical Minerals and Materials Recovery at Domestic Industrial Facilities The Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management is announcing its intent to issue a NOFO to support approximately $250 million of financial assistance for American industrial facilities that have the potential to produce valuable mineral byproducts from existing industrial processes. To derisk the technical uncertainty and financial risk for commercial deployment, many technologies must be piloted at an industrial scale in an industrial facility where material feedstocks can be processed. The proposed NOFO addresses topic areas pertaining to both industry at large and the coal-based industry. Rare Earth Elements Demonstration Facility The Office of Manufacturing and Energy Supply Chains (MESC) is announcing its intent to issue a NOFO of up to $135 million to enhance domestic supply chains for rare earth elements (REEs). pages.title: The Artisans Trying to Bring Back Neolithic Fashion | National Geographic
pages.description: A growing community of craftspeople are trying to build knowledge of ancient clothing—by making it themselves.
pages.text: The Artisans Trying to Bring Back Neolithic Fashion | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE The Artisans Trying to Bring Back Neolithic Fashion A growing community of craftspeople are trying to build knowledge of ancient clothing—by making it themselves. Historical craft specialist Vasi Birchwood recreates fashion from the Neolithic period on her Youtube channel. This outfit is one of her creations. The jacket is made of deer skin, stitched with deer skin cord and a bone awl, and adorned with moose teeth. The shirt underneath the jacket is made of undyed linen, hand stitched with linen thread. The skirt is made of deer skin and decorated with braided hemp strings. Photo Illustration: NGM Staff; Source Photos for Illustration: Vasi Birchwood By Starre Vartan Published November 2, 2026 Around the fire, no one seems especially bothered by the rain. Some people duck beneath bark shelters to continue twisting cordage from plant fibers. Others cook foraged plants or work leather while steam rises from damp clothing. A few wander into the drizzle to gather more wood before returning to the warmth of the flames. Among them is historical craft specialist and YouTube educator Vasi Birchwood . For Birchwood, weather isn't an inconvenience so much as another participant in this meeting of experiential archeologists and craft experts in Northern Germany. That shift in perspective is just one of the many ways she does more than dress like a Neolithic person at these gatherings. The point is to inhabit, however briefly, a different relationship with the material world. "You sort of embrace it," Birchwood says about the weather. "When the rain eases, we'd go out and dance in it a little, then come back under the shelters and do crafts together again.” While it wasn't always pleasant, “it becomes a bonding experience." Around Northern and Southern Europe, a growing community of historical craftspeople, experimental archaeologists, and living-history practitioners are reconstructing ancient clothing—not simply to see what people wore, but to understand how some of the first technologies evolved. Archaeologists now increasingly collaborate with these specialists to test how ancient tools functioned or how long particular techniques might have taken. "When you read an academic paper," says UK archaeologist and heritage educator Sally Pointer , "it's often obvious whether the person writing it has actually worked with the materials they're describing." It's now commonplace, Pointer says, "for researchers to ask a specialist to reconstruct something to see if the archaeology makes sense." That’s exactly what Birchwood and her friends are doing in their gatherings; they’re live testing materials and techniques they’ve read about in scholarship to reality, which includes rain. The work experimental archaeologists do is now, most powerfully, changing how historians see ancient textiles. For decades, archaeology often treated textiles as a niche subject. Yet researchers increasingly argue that cloth deserves to sit alongside metallurgy, agriculture, and boat building as one of the defining technologies that shaped human civilization. "People forget just how clever our earlier selves were," Pointer says. "We live in a world where things happen almost by magic. The idea that a shirt could represent months of work is almost unthinkable." One reason textiles have remained so overlooked is simple: Ancient clothing almost never survives, except in rare cases they are preserved in unusually dry conditions, frozen, or subject to specific chemistry. “The evidence is incredibly limited. Sometimes you dip into the world of conjecture,” says Birchwood. That uncertainty is precisely what drew her deeper into experimental archaeology. Originally fascinated by Victorian-era clothing, Birchwood gradually worked backwards through medieval and Bronze Age garments before reaching the Neolithic, a period that date backs to about 4,000 years ago in Europe. pages.title: Food firms hope EU deal will end 'onerous' export process British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Businesses in the East of England are among those hoping for help with their post-Brexit trade.
pages.text: Food firms hope EU deal will end 'onerous' export process Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Food firms hope EU deal will end 'onerous' export process 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Andrew Sinclair East of England political editor Andrew Sinclair/BBC Since Brexit, businesses exporting products including sausages and shellfish to the EU must have every consignment approved by a vet A sausage manufacturer and a shellfish producer in the East of England say they hope a forthcoming EU summit will result in a deal to make it easier for them to sell to Europe. The government is hoping to finalise an agreement which would remove post-Brexit checks from food and agricultural exports, meaning less paperwork and no more expensive checks. Ministers say the deal could be worth as much as £5bn to the UK economy and could encourage businesses to grow. But an MP who played a leading role in the Leave campaign says the proposed deal would mean the UK following EU rules again, and the government should respect the result of the referendum. 'Red tape costs an extra £32,500 a year' Andrew Sinclair/BBC Abbie and Steven Williamson run Lynn Shellfish, which sends £7.5m-worth of produce to the EU every year In an office on the quayside at King's Lynn Docks, Abbie Williamson is preparing to do the paperwork for a shipment of cockles and whelks which will be leaving the next day for France. About two-thirds of the catch processed by Lynn Shellfish is sold to the EU. "Before Brexit, it was just one piece of paperwork. Now you're looking at 10 pieces, and they take anything up to four hours to fill in," she says. As part of the process, a vet has to inspect every pallet that's going on the lorry and fill out a 15-page health certificate. With lorries going to France every few days, she says the company is spending an extra £32,500 a year on vets and customs fees. Even then, there's no guarantee the shipment will get through. "We are still getting lorries rejected occasionally," she says. "We had one rejected last year because they didn't like the labels on the trays which we had been using for the last four years. The lorry had to come all the way back and we had to change the labels." Mark Dodd/BBC Shrimp being processed at Lynn Shellfish in Norfolk The EU says the paperwork and inspections are necessary because Britain is no longer part of its regulatory framework, and it needs to be sure our food is safe. Williamson says any deal which reduces paperwork "would make a big difference". "It would also give us the chance to enter the EU through different routes," she adds. "At the moment, we go through Boulogne because it normally works, but being able to use other ports like the Hook of Holland more easily could save time and costs." Her father Steven, who runs the company, says a deal is necessary to help his industry but he feels conflicted because he voted for Brexit and any deal with the EU will almost certainly involve having to accept its rules on food production. "That's not what I voted for, but we need a deal," he says. "It's what's needed for my industry to have a future. "Too many companies have suffered because of Brexit. We were promised the earth and were delivered nothing." 'I could employ more people' Andrew Sinclair/BBC Jonathan Edge says reduced paperwork could allow him to expand and employ more people Jonathan Edge runs Broad Oak Farm Sausage Company in Essex – a family business in Hatfield Broad Oak, near Bishop's Stortford, that employs 50 people. It sells about £130,000-worth of sausages to the EU every year, which is just 7% of its total produce. But the paperwork involved in getting them there takes up a large proportion of his staff's time. pages.title: UFC president Dana White stumps for Trump at Republican convention | UFC | The Guardian
pages.description: UFC president backs Trump for president in bombastic speech at Republican National Convention in Cleveland
pages.text: UFC president Dana White stumps for Trump at Republican convention | UFC | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation UFC president Dana White speaks during the Republican National Convention in Cleveland on Tuesday night. Photograph: Brian Snyder/Reuters View image in fullscreen UFC president Dana White speaks during the Republican National Convention in Cleveland on Tuesday night. Photograph: Brian Snyder/Reuters UFC This article is more than 10 years old UFC president Dana White stumps for Trump at Republican convention This article is more than 10 years old Outspoken UFC president delivers fighting words in support of Trump White: “For standing with us ... tonight I stand with Donald Trump” Guardian sport Tue 19 Jul 2016 22.52 EDT Last modified on Fri 9 Feb 2018 14.10 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google UFC president Dana White backed Donald Trump for president in a bombastic speech at the Republican national convention on Tuesday night in Cleveland. The remarks came nine days after White announced the sale of the Ultimate Fighting Championship – the mixed martial arts promotion that he and co-owners Lorenzo and Frank Fertitta purchased for $2m in 2001 – to a group led by Hollywood talent agency WME-IMG for approximately $4bn. It's official: Republican party nominates Donald Trump for president Read more White, who said he was “blown away and honored” by the invitation to speak, praised Trump for his support during the UFC’s early days, when MMA was branded as “human cockfighting” and outlawed in more than half of the United States. “In 2001, my partners [Lorenzo and Frank Fertitta] and I bought the UFC , and it was basically considered a bloodsport. State athletic commissions didn’t support us. Arenas around the world refused to host our events. Nobody took us seriously. Nobody. Except Donald Trump. Donald was the first guy that recognized the potential that we saw in the UFC, and encouraged us to build our business. “He hosted our first two events at [the Trump Taj Mahal], he dealt with us personally, he got in the trenches with us, and he made a deal that worked for everyone. On top of that, he showed up for the fight on Saturday night and sat in the front row. Yeah, he’s that guy. He shows up. “Donald championed the UFC before it was popular, before it grew into a successful business, and I will always be so grateful to him for standing with us in those early days, so tonight I stand with Donald Trump.” Dana White backed Donald Trump on Tuesday in Cleveland White went on to praise Trump’s business acumen, work ethic and steadfast friendship. Republican convention live: Chris Christie whips crowd into frenzy over 'guilty' Clinton Read more “Let me tell you three things that I respect about this man. First, Donald has great business instincts. He supports businesses of all sizes. He’ll make it possible for them to grow and succeed, which is the backbone of a strong economy. “Second, Donald is a hard worker. This guy is going to get up there, he’s going to roll up his sleeves. He will work with people and he will put in the time to get things done. “Third, for over 15 years, Donald Trump has been a loyal and supportive friend, and I know that if I needed Donald, he would be there for me, just like he was when I first met him. He’s one of these guys that sometimes he’ll pick up the phone and call me and say ‘Hey, good luck with the fights tonight. I’m going to be watching,’ or whatever it is that we might have going on.” Last year White said he was “not a political guy at all, not even a little bit” , but praised Trump for his unwavering loyalty. “Let me tell you something. I’ve been in the fight business my whole life. I know fighters. Ladies and gentlemen, Donald Trump is a fighter, and I know he will fight for this country.” Explore more on these topics UFC MMA US sports Republican national convention 2016 US politics Donald Trump Share Reuse this content Comments ( … ) Sign in or create your Guardian acco

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/glycomics Biotechnology Glycomics Sign Up to Get NIST News GovDelivery The field of glycomics defines the structures and functions of glycans, or sugars, in biological systems. Glycans perform many functions in cells and cell systems, from helping cells recognize invaders, to guiding cell growth, to enabling the folding of protein structures that affect health. In support of the biomanufacturing and protein therapeutics communities, NIST research underpins the characterization of glycans in three focus areas: development of glycan reference materials, development of mass spectral glycan reference data libraries, and administration of glycan measurement interlaboratory comparison studies. 76 Laboratories worldwide participated in the NIST Interlaboratory Study on Glycosylation Analysis of Monoclonal Antibodies This report describes the design of and results for the NIST Interlaboratory Study on the Glycosylation of NISTmAb, a Monoclonal Antibody Reference Material from 103 reports submitted by 76 laboratories. Two materials were used in the study, 1) the Primary Standard (PS) for NIST Reference Material 8671, NISTmAb, Humanized IgG1κ Monoclonal Antibody, and 2) a material derived from the PS by treatment with galactosidase. Read the report. Key Accomplishments Glycan reference standards: A glycan-based Standard Reference Material (SRM 3655) is being developed to support the biomanufacturing and protein therapeutics communities. The SRM will consist of a set of 13 individually-bottled, pure glycoforms including those most commonly observed as N-linked glycans on therapeutic monoclonal antibodies. This quantitative glycan material will enable accurate, SI-traceable quantification of antibody glycosylation, and can be used to assess quantity, identity, or stability between labs, between production lots, or over time. Mass spectral glycan reference data: The NIST Mass Spectral Reference Libraries are continuously increasing the number of glycan and oligosaccharide reference spectra included. Recent additions include glycan from NISTmAb, NIST Human Milk SRM 1953 and oligosaccharides from a variety of mammals, including samples shared with NIST from the National Zoo in Washington, DC . NIST Mass Spectrometry Data Center products relevant to glycomics include: NIST 17 Glycan 1.0 MS Library Library of Oligosaccharides in NIST Human Milk SRM 1953 Library of Free Oligosaccharides in Milk from a Variety of Mammals Glyco Mass Calculator Interlaboratory measurement comparison studies: NIST coordinated an interlaboratory study for laboratories that measure glycosylation in monoclonal antibodies. A published report describes the design of and results for the NIST Interlaboratory Study on the Glycosylation of NISTmAb, a Monoclonal Antibody Reference Material from 103 reports submitted by 76 laboratories. Reporting a TSCA Chemical Substantial Risk Notice CDX Electronic Communication for TSCA Substantial Risk Notices EPA is now able to electronically acknowledge receipt of substantial risk notices submitted via the Central Data Exchange (CDX). Learn more . On this page : Overview Read TSCA section 8(e) Frequent Questions. Who Must Report Substantial Risk Notifications to EPA under TSCA section 8(e)? What Types of Substantial Risk Notifications are Reportable under TSCA section 8(e)? How Soon do I have to Submit a Substantial Risk Notifications after I Obtain New Information? How do I File Substantial Risk Notifications and FYI Submissions under TSCA section 8(e) What is a “For Your Information (FYI)” submission? If I am Not a Chemical Manufacturer, Importer, Processor or Distributor, Can I Still Submit a Substantial Risk Notifications? Overview Section 8(e) of the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) requires that EPA be immediately notified when substances or mixtures present a substantial risk of injury to health or the environment. TSCA section 8(e) states that ‘‘Any person who manufactures, [imports,] processes, or distributes in commerce a chemical substance or mixture and who obtains information which reasonably supports the conclusion that such substance or mixture presents a substantial risk of injury to health or the environment shall immediately inform the [EPA] Administrator of such information unless such person has actual knowledge that the Administrator has been adequately informed of such information.’’ 15 U.S.C. 2607(e). EPA’s guidance states that Substantial Risk Notifications under TSCA section 8(e) should be submitted within 30 calendar days of obtaining substantial risk information. In addition, EPA established a classification system to distinguish voluntary “For Your Information” (FYI) submissions from Substantial Risk Notifications submitted formally to EPA under TSCA section 8(e), discussed above. The FYI classification was created by EPA to capture chemical risk submissions by persons or organizations not subject to the TSCA section 8(e) reporting requirements. Read TSCA section 8(e) requiring substantial risk notifications to EPA (15 U.S.C. 2607(e)). Read EPA’s guidance documents on Substantial Risk Notifications . Read TSCA section 8(e) Frequent Questions. View substantial risk notifications submitted to EPA in ChemView or CDAT Who Must Report to EPA under TSCA section 8(e)? Section 8(e) of TSCA requires manufacturers (including importers), processors, and distributors of chemicals to notify EPA immediately of information that reasonably supports the conclusion that their substances or mixtures present a substantial risk of injury to health of the environment. TSCA section 8(e) does not provide exemptions for small businesses, small production or importation volumes, or commercial activities such as manufacture for export only or research and development. EPA allows commercial establishments to assume responsibility for submitting substantial risk information obtained by individual employees and officials. EPA's TSCA section 8(e) policy statement explains that individual officers/employees are viewed as having discharged their individual TSCA section 8(e) responsibilities once they notify a designated supervisor or official in full about pertinent information, provided the employing entity has an established, internally publicized and affirmatively implemented procedure governing such Substantial Risk Notifications. Critical Minerals and Materials Accelerator Banner Color Light Text on a Dark Overlay (Default) Notice of Funding Opportunity: Critical Minerals and Materials Accelerator Funding amount: Up to $69,000,000 Background Information On April 7, 2026, the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI) Advanced Materials and Manufacturing Technologies Office (AMMTO), in partnership with the Office of Geothermal, announced a “Critical Minerals and Materials Accelerator” Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) of up to $69 million. The NOFO will focus investments on American, industry-led partnerships to prototype and pilot innovative critical materials processing technologies that are currently only proven at the bench scale to address challenges in high-impact areas. The program establishes a pipeline that will support technology maturation to ultimately unlock private capital investments. It will also leverage other DOE lab-based investments, such as the Critical Materials Innovation (CMI) Hub and the Minerals to Materials Supply Chain Research Facility (METALLIC). This NOFO will help ensure a more secure, predictable, and affordable supply of critical minerals and materials that are foundational to American energy dominance, national security, and industrial competitiveness. The NOFO includes the following topic areas: Topic Area 1 : Production and material efficiency for critical materials, including rare earth elements (REEs). Inclusive of the following sub-topics: 1A: Recovery and production from postindustrial manufacturing scrap 1B: Recovery and production from postconsumer scrap (with an emphasis on electronic waste and drivetrains) 1C: Recovery and production from blended feedstocks including mine tailings, postindustrial scrap, and postconsumer scrap Topic Area 2 : Processes to refine and alloy gallium, gallium nitride, germanium, and silicon carbide. Topic Area 3 : Cost-competitive direct lithium extraction, separation, and processing. Inclusive of the following sub-topics: 3A: Cost-competitive direct lithium extraction 3B: Advancing pre- and post- treatment and disposal technologies for direct lithium extraction 3C: Exploration and characterization of critical materials and REEs from volcanic-hosted geothermal systems This NOFO is one of several totaling nearly $1 billion that will advance and scale mining, processing, and manufacturing technologies across key stages of the critical minerals and materials supply chains. Webinar An informational webinar will be hosted on April 16, 2026, at 11:30 a.m. ET to discuss this funding opportunity as well as the application requirements. Register here Attending the informational webinar is not mandatory and will not positively or negatively impact the overall review of any applicant submissions. pages.title: Will the Bayeux Tapestry Finally Give Up Its Secrets? | National Geographic
pages.description: For centuries, scholars have puzzled over the hidden meanings within medieval Europe’s most enigmatic surviving artwork. Now a blockbuster exhibition in London is sparking fresh debate over the secrets in the stitches.
pages.text: Will the Bayeux Tapestry Finally Give Up Its Secrets? | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE Can a Moment in the Spotlight Help Unravel the Bayeux Tapestry’s Oldest Mysteries? For centuries, scholars have puzzled over the hidden meanings within medieval Europe’s most enigmatic surviving artwork. Now a blockbuster exhibition in London is sparking fresh debate over the secrets in the stitches. 0:11 National Geographic was at the British Museum this summer to document the Bayeux Tapestry’s historic (and secret) delivery and the elaborate installation process that followed. Once unpacked and unfolded, the tapestry was suspended from a truss and carefully raised, preparing it for placement in a precision-engineered display case. Video by Evie Milsom By Chris Heath Photographs by Zed Nelson Published November 11, 2026 Of all the wonders and mysteries that surround the 225-foot-long medieval artwork known as the Bayeux Tapestry, perhaps the greatest of all is its survival. There are so many ways for any fragile piece of fabric not to endure, whether by processes of nature (rot, heat, mold, pests, humidity, sunlight), by accident, or by the careless and destructive acts of humans. As the centuries pass, few such objects evade at least one of these fates. But the Bayeux Tapestry—not only a relic from a past almost inconceivably different from our own but also an incomparable window into that past—has done so for nearly a thousand years. It hasn’t come through unscathed. Its edges are scattered with pinholes where it was formerly exhibited using nails. It has been splattered by wax, likely while displayed in a cathedral in the northern French city of Bayeux. It is creased and frayed, in part from the winding and unwinding of a spool on which it was kept in the 19th century. In 1792, during the fervor of the French Revolution , it was once apparently taken as convenient material with which to cover a wagon, only to be saved by a citizen who valued its significance. The centuries of manhandling and entropy have taken a toll. A French conservation team, studying the tapestry in detail six years ago, documented 24,204 stains, 16,445 wrinkles, and 9,646 holes and gaps. An international team of conservators inspect the Bayeux Tapestry, attached to the paravent that helped fold it for transport. The fragile masterpiece, which chronicles the Norman invasion, had likely not left France since the Middle Ages. The Bayeux Tapestry, which is currently the subject of a headline-making exhibition at the British Museum, is not technically a tapestry at all but an embroidery: dyed wools stitched on bleached linen base cloth. Its embroidered scenes tell the story of the Norman Conquest of England , the 1066 invasion by William the Conqueror and an army from what’s now northern France, which ended Anglo-Saxon rule and reshaped England’s politics, culture, and language. It is broadly, though not universally, believed to have been created in the south of England in the late 11th century and brought to France soon after, and for as far back as it can be traced definitively—only to 1476—it has principally been kept in Bayeux. The current visit to London, most historians believe, is its first time out of France in roughly 950 years. The enduring fascination that surrounds it partly relates to how little about the tapestry we can say for certain. Discussion and exploration of exactly what it depicts, and what each image means and how each relates to the others, and of how the tapestry was made, and when, and by whom, and every other kind of particular, have filled hundreds of books and scholarly articles. Its central story concerns the Battle of Hastings , the bloody confrontation at which William’s forces defeated those of the English king Harold; generations of British schoolchildren have been taught that this is the moment at which the story of modern England begins. pages.title: What do Christmas market traders say about rising prices? British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: From £8 bratwursts to £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps, why is the cost of the markets rising year on year?
pages.text: What do Christmas market traders say about rising prices? Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live What do Christmas market traders say about rising prices? 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Haider Saleem and Lydia Flavell , North West, Manchester Christmas markets BBC Nils Borstel said his business was making less money despite more than doubling the price of a sausage Mention Christmas markets these days and the conversation often turns to rising prices – from £8 bratwursts, £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps and even £5 for a few marshmallow sticks. But what do the people behind the stalls think? Are they benefiting from the hikes or are their own profits being squeezed? Traders at Manchester's Christmas markets told the BBC they were feeling the pressure of increasing bills for staff, ingredients and energy, with some saying they were making less money despite charging more. One trader said it costs at least £4,000 a day to run each her four stalls, while another has cut prices to keep customers coming back. Nils Borstel, 25, helps run Bratwurst King, a family business which has operated at the markets since 1999. He said a sausage that previously cost £3.50 now sold for £8, with much of the increase taking place over the past five or six years. "But we don't earn more money," he said. Manchester Christmas market traders explain prices Borstel, whose family operates four stalls across the city centre, said rising costs for meat, electricity, staffing and accommodation had forced the business to increase prices. About 15 workers travel from Germany to help run the stalls, alongside staff recruited in the UK. He said that despite busy crowds and dry weather during the opening weekend, people appeared more cautious about spending than in previous years. For example, some customers were now buying one portion of food to share, rather than purchasing one each, he said. Borstel said he had seen a change in spending habits since 2019, when customers were more willing to buy food and drinks without worrying about the cost. He acknowledged that prices were high and did not want to increase them, but said the they were necessary to cover expenses. Poppy (left) and Neve questioned whether the portions they bought justified the prices Among those questioning the costs were Neve and Poppy, both 18. Neve, a student, said she had spent about £15 on one dish, while Poppy, who is taking a gap year, paid £11 for a Yorkshire pudding wrap. "I think it was pricey for what it was," Neve said. Poppy also felt she had not received much food for the money, although said it was tasty. Both said they enjoyed going into the city and looking around the markets, while Neve sympathised with traders, saying she thought the cost of renting space could force businesses to raise prices. Business pressures Charlotte Whittle, director of CT Catering, has been trading at the markets for 10 years and now operates four stalls. She said each stall cost at least £1,000 a day to run, bringing her total daily operating costs to at least £4,000. Whittle, who employs a range of staff, said customers often underestimated the work and expense involved. Before the markets opened, her business spent two weeks preparing its stalls, with another two weeks needed to dismantle them after Christmas. CT Catering director Charlotte Whittle says her business employs 57 people across four Manchester market sites She said the costs included staff wages, accommodation, deliveries, storage, packaging and card payment fees. Parking three vans in Manchester city centre could cost £100 a day alone, she said, with the vehicles needed to replenish stock throughout busy trading periods. pages.title: Why did UFC try to silence journalists and fighters as it returned to action? | UFC | The Guardian
pages.description: Saturday night saw a major live sports event staged in America for the first time in weeks. But Dana White wanted some details kept quiet
pages.text: Why did UFC try to silence journalists and fighters as it returned to action? | UFC | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Ryan Spann and Joe Rogan appear to contravene social distancing guidelines after a fight at UFC 249. Photograph: Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC View image in fullscreen Ryan Spann and Joe Rogan appear to contravene social distancing guidelines after a fight at UFC 249. Photograph: Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC UFC This article is more than 6 years old Why did UFC try to silence journalists and fighters as it returned to action? This article is more than 6 years old Saturday night saw a major live sports event staged in America for the first time in weeks. But Dana White wanted some details kept quiet Karim Zidan Mon 11 May 2020 04.00 EDT Last modified on Mon 11 May 2020 04.44 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google O n Saturday night, the Ultimate Fighting Championship became the first major organization to hold a live sports event in the US during the height of the Covid-19 pandemic. However, rather than being hailed as an entertaining night of cagefighting designed to distract sports fans in self-isolation, the focus has instead fallen on the UFC’s questionable protocols, and the lengths the promotion is willing to take to ensure that no one involved in the event can speak out. Justin Gaethje shocks Tony Ferguson with KO at controversial UFC 249 Read more On Friday night – less than 24 hours before the start of UFC 249 – reports emerged that Ronaldo Souza, had tested positive for Covid-19, along with his two cornermen. His bout with Uriah Hall was subsequently canceled , but at that point, the damage had been done. Souza had been spotted walking around the hotel and interacting with fighters over the previous days, and had even fist-bumped UFC president Dana White during the weigh-ins, albeit with gloves on. In an attempt to salvage the situation, the UFC released a statement confirming the positive tests and claiming that the organization’s “response to this development is indicative of the effectiveness of the health and safety measures UFC has put in place.” Yet, despite the spin, the glaring weaknesses in the UFC’s pandemic protocols would only become more prevalent come fight night. The UFC’s health and safety measures included testing everyone involved in the show – fighters, trainers, officials, and even media– for Covid-19. UFC also limited the arena to “essential” personnel, required athletes and staff to participate in medical screenings and temperature checks, and expected everyone involved to follow social distancing guidelines. However, social distancing was only used selectively during the event. While the commentators were seated at separate tables, they stood side-by-side at the start of the broadcast to introduce the show. None wore masks, including UFC color commentator Joe Rogan, who also conducted post-fight interviews with the fighters and even shook their hands. White was present in the front row, also without a mask. View image in fullscreen Henry Cejudo shakes hands with UFC president Dana White on Saturday after announcing his retirement in Florida. Photograph: Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC While the UFC’s protocols were loosely applied on fight night, the organization covered its bases and eliminated its own legal risk by making fighters and staff sign waivers that ban them from criticizing the coronavirus protocols in place for the event. If fighters violate this provision “whether relating to Covid-19 or otherwise,” the UFC reserves the right to “revoke all or any part of any prize monies or awards won by the Participant.” The news was first reported by Yahoo Sports , who obtained a copy of the legal waiver. When confronted with the clause, White played down its importance. The Last Dance: Is the Michael Jordan documentary a dressed-up puff piece? Filing a Significant New Use Notice (SNUN) under TSCA Overview Under section 5(a) of TSCA and 40 CFR part 721, if EPA promulgates a Significant New Use Rule (SNUR), a manufacturer or processor wishing to engage in a designated significant new use must submit a Significant New Use Notice (or "SNUN") to EPA at least 90 days before engaging in the new use. This notification provides EPA the opportunity to evaluate the new use and, if necessary, take action to prohibit or limit the activity. EPA recommends that submitters consult with the Agency prior to submitting a SNUN to discuss what data may be useful in evaluating a significant new use. Discussions with the Agency prior to submission can afford ample time to conduct any tests that might be helpful in evaluating risks posed by the substance. Speak to a specialist: TSCA Hotline ( tsca-hotline@epa.gov or 202/554-1404) Joint SNUN submissions Potential SNUN submitters should be aware of 40 CFR 721.25(b) , which authorizes joint SNUNs by two or more persons -- for example, a manufacturer and several processors. In many cases, EPA will need to respond to a SNUN by amending the SNUR to allow companies other than the SNUN submitter (such as the submitter's processor customers) to engage in the newly approved use(s). Note that before EPA amends the SNUR, even after a manufacturer submits a SNUN and the review period expires, processors (and other manufacturers) of the substance are still legally required to submit their own SNUN before engaging in the significant new use. Electronic submission SNUNs are reported using the standard e-PMN form and are subject to a 90-day review process similar to that for a PMN. When submitting a SNUN, the submitter should include a cover letter that provides the Code of Federal Regulations citation of the SNUR and identifies the specific significant new use(s) for which the SNUN is being submitted. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Idaho Falls District Office The Idaho Falls District, located in southeast Idaho, manages approximately 3.7 million acres of public land. The topography and terrain differ substantially throughout the area, ranging from sagebrush and desert to high-elevation forests. The District itself incorporates 16 counties, with Montana to the north and Utah to the south. The western edge borders the Craters of the Moon National Monument and Preserve, with the eastern edge extending to the beautiful Teton mountain range. With such a diverse geographic area, the Idaho Falls District has many challenges to face as it balances its mission of multiple use and sustainable yield to achieve a sustainable ecosystem. Some of the major activities occurring within the district include: grazing, recreation, mining, wildlife and fisheries, fire management, riparian and wetland management, realty and land use. The Idaho Falls District is divided into four geographic areas/field offices: Challis (799,000 acres), Salmon (493,000 acres), Upper Snake (1,854,000 acres) and Pocatello (557,000 acres). Funding Notice: Mines & Metals Capacity Expansion – Piloting By-Product Critical Minerals and Materials Recovery at Domestic Industrial Facilities NOFO number : DE-FOA-0003583 Download the full funding opportunity : NETL Exchange Funding Amount : $275,000,000 Background Information On November 14, 2025 , the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced up to $275 million in federal funding for American industrial facilities capable of producing valuable minerals from existing industrial and coal byproducts. These critical materials are essential for developing technology needed to support U.S. energy production, manufacturing, and transport and for our national defense. The Department announced in August its intent to invest $1 billion to advance and scale mining, processing, and manufacturing technologies, delivering on President Trump’s Executive Orders, Unleashing American Energy and Immediate Measures to Increase American Mineral Production . These actions will secure America’s critical material supply chain, increase domestic mineral production, reduce reliance on foreign sources, and strengthen U.S. energy independence. These pilots will demonstrate the feasibility of recovering critical minerals from existing American infrastructure and industrial activity, reducing waste while building new domestic supply chains for high-value materials. Eligibility Eligible applicants include institutions of higher education, for- and non-profit entities, state and local governments, and Indian Tribes. Topic Areas This funding opportunity has two topic areas for the design, construction, and operation of large pilot-scale facilities to produce critical materials: Topic Area 1 : Mines & Metals Pilots—Coal-Based Industry Topic Area 2 : Mines & Metals Pilots—All Industries Funding DOE expects to award up to $275 million in federal funding with a minimum of 20% cost-sharing from the awardees. Mines and Metals Capacity Expansion – Topic 1 Selections AMMPT announced $75 million across five selected projects that use coal and coal-based feedstocks to produce rare earth elements and other critical materials aiming to derisk the technical and financial uncertainties for commercial deployment of critical materials byproduct recovery technologies. Selected projects will reduce America’s dependence on foreign resources through large pilot-scale production under real-world conditions. pages.title: A New Discovery Offers a Glimpse Into the World of the Hittites—in Their Own Words | National Geographic
pages.description: A new cache of cuneiform tablets reveals the everyday lives of people in the Hittite Empire—from religious rituals to a princess who died in a plague.
pages.text: A New Discovery Offers a Glimpse Into the World of the Hittites—in Their Own Words | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE A New Discovery Offers a Glimpse Into the World of the Hittites—in Their Own Words A new cache of cuneiform tablets reveals the everyday lives of people in the Hittite Empire—from religious rituals to a princess who died in a plague. Thousands of cuneiform tablets like this fragment have been discovered in excavations across Turkey. Together, they are illuminating the lives of the Hittites—an ancient civilization that rivaled Egypt’s New Kingdom then seemingly vanished. Photo Illustration: NGM Staff. Source Photo for Illustration: Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures and Alamy By Sarah Bond Published October 26, 2026 Archaeologists working at the site of Kayalıpınar in central Turkey have announced the discovery of 131 cuneiform tablets written in Hittite and Hurrian and dating to the reign of the Hittite King Tudhaliya II circa 1400 BC. The new tablets advance our knowledge of the Hittite civilization beyond the confines of its well-excavated capital city, giving researchers better access to the lives of people who lived, fought, worshipped, and died in other areas of the vast empire—from priests who divined the future to an infant princess who fell ill from a previously unknown epidemic. Together with earlier findings, the discovery also allows us to learn about the lives of the Hittites in their own words, rather than relying on narratives in the Hebrew Bible or inscriptions left behind by Egyptian pharaohs. By deciphering these clay cuneiform tablets, archaeologists are finally revealing an important but fragmented history of an empire that emerged in modern-day Turkey and Syria during the Late Bronze Age, grew to rival the power of New Kingdom Egypt, and then seemingly vanished. The Hittites used an Indo-European language, and scribes adapted that language to a system of writing called cuneiform that uses signs for syllables and vowels. ( The Hittite Empire Transformed the World—and Then the World Forgot It .) However, most of the Hittite tablets that survive are not representative of the entire population: Around 30,000 tablets and fragments come from the royal capital of the Hittite Empire, Hattusa (modern-day Boğazkale), an archive that transmits largely elite and royal perspectives from the royal citadel. This means that the daily lives and rituals of those living within hundreds of other Hittite cities are less well known—until these excavations at Kayalıpınar. In antiquity, Kayalıpınar was the site of the ancient Hittite city of Šamuḫa , a religious and commercial center that became an important military capital during Tudhaliya’s reign. The site is being excavated by Çiğdem Maner, an associate professor from Koç University Department of Archaeology and History of Art. "When the cache of newly unearthed tablets is added to the 53 tablets discovered at the same site in 2025, 184 new documents tell us about the people within the city. “There are very few archives that we have found outside the capital city. The ones from Šamuḫa are some of the first,” says archaeologist and Bronze Age expert Eric Cline , who was not involved in the excavation. “They further confirm it was an important Hittite city.” HISTORY & CULTURE Vesuvius Revisited: A New Story of the Day the World Exploded HISTORY & CULTURE This ancient trading city had a surprising Greek influence HISTORY & CULTURE Did anyone survive Pompeii? The new tablets reveal Hittite religion, bureaucratic procedures, and administrative life connected to the state. They also point to mass upheaval. During the imperial period when the tablets were written, the mountainous Kaska tribes were attacking Hittite cities, including the capital. This made Šamuḫa an even more important military center for resisting the encroaching raiders during Tudhaliya’s reign. Bat Week is an annual celebration of bats and the many roles they play in our ecosystems. The international event is organized by a team of representatives across North America from conservation organizations and government departments. Bat Week strives to show the critical importance of bats and raise greater awareness of conservation efforts worldwide. Everyone can join in on the Bat Week fun! pages.description: الأمم المتحدة نفسها جزء من منظومة الأمم المتحدة. وإن التعاون بين الأمم المتحدة والكيانات الأخرى في المنظومة ضروري لتحقيق أهداف المنظمة المنصوص عليها في ميثاق الأمم المتحدة.
pages.text: تعريف بعملنا | الأمم المتحدة Skip to main content عملنا تنسق الأمم المتحدة عملها مع الصناديق والبرامج والوكالات المتخصصة والمنظمات الأخرى التابعة لمنظومة الأمم المتحدة . الأمم المتحدة نفسها جزء من منظومة الأمم المتحدة. والتعاون بين الأمم المتحدة والكيانات الأخرى في المنظومة ضروري لتحقيق أهداف المنظمة المنصوص عليها في ميثاق الأمم المتحدة . ومنذ صوغ ميثاق الأمم المتحدة، أُسندت إلى المنظمة مهام جديدة لم تكن متصورة وقت إنشائها. وحددت المنظمة أهدافا لبناء عالم أكثر استدامة ، واتفقت الدول على العمل الجماعي لإبطاء تغير المناخ . ومع تنامي المشكلات التي تواجه البشرية، اتسع نطاق عمل الأمم المتحدة كذلك. التقرير السنوي عن أعمال المنظمة فيديو تعريفي بماهية الأمم المتحدة "خطة عمل" الأمم المتحدة في مقر الأمم المتحدة في نيويورك، تصدر الجمعية العامة و مجلس الأمن و المجلس الاقتصادي والاجتماعي قرارات ترسم ما يمكن تسميته، على نحو غير رسمي، "خطة عمل" الأمم المتحدة. وتنفذ الأمانة العامة للأمم المتحدة هذا العمل بالتعاون مع كيانات منظومة الأمم المتحدة . الأمانة العامة للأمم المتحدة للأمانة العامة للأمم المتحدة، ومقرها مدينة نيويورك، مكاتب في جنيف و فيينا و نيروبي . وتشكل اللجان الاقتصادية الإقليمية في أديس أبابا و بانكوك و بيروت و جنيف و سانتياغو جزءا من الأمانة العامة للأمم المتحدة. منظومة الأمم المتحدة لكل صندوق وبرنامج ووكالة متخصصة وكيان آخر تابع لمنظومة الأمم المتحدة ميزانيته وولايته وقيادته ومقره. وتملك هذه الكيانات جميعا مكاتب إقليمية ومحلية في المناطق الجغرافية الرئيسة في العالم، شأنها شأن الأمم المتحدة. تعمل الأمم المتحدة ومنظومة الأمم المتحدة معا في خمسة مجالات يمكن أن تتداخل، وكثيرا ما تتداخل بالفعل. تعريف بعملنا يغطي عمل الأمم المتحدة خمسة مجالات رئيسة: pages.text: YouthRules | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content The Wage and Hour Division promotes positive and safe work experiences for teens by providing information on federal and state labor laws that apply to young workers. Child Labor Topics Learn about your rights as you make your way into the workforce. Learn More about Young Workers Ensure your child’s job does not jeopardize their health, well-being, or educational opportunities. Learn More as Parents Help educate young workers and their parents on child labor requirements. Learn More as Educators Understand if and how you can employ minors at your company. Learn More as Employers Child Labor 44 Seconds Where can I work? 18 Seconds What hours can I work? 16 Seconds How to File a Complaint 25 Seconds Common Questions What are the child labor laws that apply to workers in the restaurant industry? Are workers under 18 allowed to load, operate, or unload balers and compactors? Are workers under 18 allowed to operate meat slicers or bakery machines? Is an intern or student entitled to receive the minimum wage and overtime pay? Are workers under 18 allowed to clean or operate meat processing machinery? What are the child labor laws that apply to driving or delivering goods? Other Resources Our resources can help everyone better understand federal child labor laws . State Labor Laws Some state child labor laws are inconsistent with the federal child labor provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act, 29 U.S.C. 212(c), and its implementing regulations at 29 CFR Part 570. Where a state child labor law is less restrictive than the federal law, the federal law applies. Where a state child labor law is more restrictive than the federal law, the state law applies. Contact Us Many investigations are initiated by complaints, which are free and confidential. The name of the complainant, the nature of the complaint, and whether a complaint exists may not be disclosed. An employer cannot retaliate against a worker for exercising their rights , filing a complaint or cooperating with an investigation. pages.title: Bessent blames Lutnick's department for Nvidia chip sales to Megaspeed British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Scott Bessent told CNBC that several government agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".
pages.text: Bessent blames Lutnick's department for Nvidia chip sales to Megaspeed Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Pressure grows on Trump's Commerce Secretary Lutnick in fallout from Nvidia scandal 4 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Rachel Clun , business reporter, New York and Bernd Debusmann, Jr , White House reporter How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security? US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-spec AI chips, as the fallout from the Nvidia scandal widens to President Donald Trump's cabinet. Pressure is building on Lutnick from across the political spectrum to explain his department's actions. Jensen Huang was ousted as Nvidia CEO after revelations he had an affair with a businesswoman who was also allegedly a Chinese spy. Megaspeed, the firm she worked for, had been probed by US government agencies over suspicions it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China, reports said, but was not on a list of firms US companies are prevented from working with. Bessent told CNBC several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months". "But Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added. Bessent's comments come after Lutnick was called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over the Commerce Department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips. Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Huang. Bloomberg via Getty Images Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said some parts of the administration wanted more controls on trade with Megaspeed Bessent said he was "frustrated" by delays in putting the company on the export control list and reports of leakage of AI chips into China. "President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s, so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, because it gives the Chinese an advantage," he said. Last year, the Commerce Department had been investigating Megaspeed over suspicions it had been smuggling some of Nvidia's advanced AI chips into China, according to the New York Times. Megaspeed has been contacted for comment. There was also pressure on the Commerce Department to add it to the list, but the Financial Times separately reported that the department was delaying efforts to have the cloud computing firm included. However, Bessent also pointed the finger at Nvidia. "The story has been thus far of Jensen Huang's personal foibles," he told CNBC . "The real story here should be: did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies? "It's important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that." Bessent's pointed comments are a rare instance of internal debate within the Trump administration spilling out into the public view, although tensions have reportedly simmered between Bessent and Lutnick in the past. In 2024, the two reportedly jostled for the role of treasury secretary ahead of Trump's return to the White House, and last year the pair butted heads over the administration's tariff policy, according to US media. How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions Huang has been summoned to testify before the Senate Banking Committee about his alleged affair with the former Megaspeed executive, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. pages.title: Controversy and a corporate spectacle under the Claw: Trump’s birthday fight night at the White House | Donald Trump | The Guardian
pages.description: Despite a last-ditch legal bid to block the event, the White House spent the night as a marketing department for the private fighting company
pages.text: Controversy and a corporate spectacle under the Claw: Trump’s birthday fight night at the White House | Donald Trump | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Trump watches the heavyweight bout between Josh Hokit and Derrick Lewis. Photograph: Kent Nishimura/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Trump watches the heavyweight bout between Josh Hokit and Derrick Lewis. Photograph: Kent Nishimura/AFP/Getty Images America at 250 Donald Trump This article is more than 5 months old Controversy and a corporate spectacle under the Claw: Trump’s birthday fight night at the White House This article is more than 5 months old Despite a last-ditch legal bid to block the event, the White House spent the night as a marketing department for the private fighting company Joseph Gedeon in Washington Mon 15 Jun 2026 10.06 EDT Last modified on Thu 25 Jun 2026 13.40 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A warm Sunday night on the South Lawn – with bright lights, fireworks, a fighter plane flyover, thousands of spectators, and the first major professional sporting event ever staged at the White House – produced many memorable scenes. One might linger more than most. Justin Gaethje, the American interim lightweight champion, stood alone in the Oval Office in his fight shorts, draped in an American flag, studying a framed Declaration of Independence before he turned to walk out to the cage. It wasn’t the first time hand-to-hand combat had taken place on the grounds of 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue. Theodore Roosevelt boxed and wrestled there, sparring with aides, and a session with a young military officer detached the retina in his left eye, leaving him partially blind for the rest of his presidency. Roosevelt told almost no one, and it wasn’t disclosed publicly until he left office. Trump celebration marred by Michelle Obama smear But Sunday, or Donald Trump’s 80th birthday, inverted that mystique. The combat – inside an octagon, overshadowed by 92ft of steel called “the Claw” – was anything but hidden. This was the moment the American presidency, under Trump, completed its symbolic merger with a private fighting company: the Ultimate Fighting Championship, or UFC . View image in fullscreen Donald Trump and UFC CEO Dana White at the White House in Washington DC on 14 June 2026. Photograph: Kent Nishimura/AFP/Getty Images It was a spectacle intertwining in patriotism and history, packaged to feel completely real. Sincerity was the delivery mechanism to the viewers: the actions were secondary to how they are perceived. The UFC spent its early years banned in a majority of US states. Its CEO Dana White has spent the last few years telling the story of how one man – Trump – had been willing to stage what everyone else called a sideshow, or worse . On Sunday, this partnership led this one figure sport to the heart of the US federal government. Fighters walked through the White House, bathed in warm amber light in the dark night sky, and down a military honor-guard corridor of flags and rifles, with the south portico repurposed as a grand entrance. Trump and White made the walk together, cameras trailing, before reaching a balcony where the Zac Brown Band played and military aircraft passed low overhead, which Trump saluted. They walked a red carpet to their seats in the front row. Broadcasters including Joe Rogan and Daniel Cormier called the fights cageside, while other commentators worked a separate desk from the historic Green Room , traditionally used to receive foreign dignitaries. Rogan’s tie was several inches short, which amid all the choreography felt like the only unrehearsed thing on the lawn. Visually it fell into one palette – red, white and blue gloves, shorts, canvas and costume design – with ring-card girls dressed as versions of Wonder Woman, Supergirl and assorted other American-coded superheroines. Patriotism and licensed IP, side by side. Outside the perimeter, at the Ellipse, a small group of protesters built a cardboar

pages.text: How federal impeachment works | USAGov Skip to main content How federal impeachment works Impeachment is the process of bringing charges against a government official for wrongdoing. A trial may be held, and the official may be removed from office. The impeachment process The Constitution gives Congress the power to impeach federal officials. An official can be impeached for treason, bribery, and “other high crimes and misdemeanors.” The House of Representatives brings articles (charges) of impeachment against an official. Learn more about the House’s role in impeachment. If the House adopts the articles by a simple majority vote, the official has been impeached. The Senate holds an impeachment trial. In the case of a president, the U.S. Supreme Court chief justice presides. Learn more about the Senate’s role in the impeachment process . If found guilty, the official is removed from office. They may never be able to hold elected office again. If they are not found guilty, they may continue to serve in office. Learn more about impeachment , including its history and how the U.S. Constitution grants impeachment powers to Congress. Past impeachments of federal officials The House has initiated impeachment proceedings more than 60 times. But there have been only 21 impeachments. This includes three presidents, one cabinet secretary, and one senator. Of those who were impeached, only eight officials were found guilty by the Senate and removed from office. All eight were federal judges. The presidents impeached by the House were: Andrew Johnson in 1868 William Jefferson (Bill) Clinton in 1998 Donald John Trump in 2019 and 2021 Presidents Johnson, Clinton, and Trump remained in office following acquittals by the Senate on all charges. Former President Richard Nixon was not impeached. He resigned after Congress started the impeachment process against him in 1974. Impeachment of state and local officials A state legislature can impeach its governor and other state officials. Many local governments also have impeachment procedures. Find your state legislature’s website to learn more. LAST UPDATED: November 13, 2025 SHARE THIS PAGE: Have a question? Ask a real person any government-related question for free. pages.description: The National Institute of Standards and Technology is developing the expertise, tools, and reference material and data to support microbiome research and expedite the commercial and clinical availability of new treatments, technologies, and products to meet critical needs in health care, food safety
pages.text: Microbial measurements | NIST Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/microbial-measurements Biotechnology Microbial measurements Sign Up to Get NIST News GovDelivery Trillions of microorganisms, communities known as “microbiomes,” live on and inside us, in our homes and the air we breathe, and in soil and plants. Most microbiomes contribute to necessary functions within us and our environments, like digestion and plant growth. We are largely living in successful partnership with them. A better understanding of these complex microbial communities would help us harness them for applications to human and animal health, agriculture and food safety, water treatment, manufacturing, renewable energy, and the detection of biological threats. For microbiome research to more quickly deliver products to the clinic and market and make the best use of taxpayer funding, the field requires standardized protocols for sample collection, and reference materials and data. These standardized tools help the many organizations working on microbiome research reproduce each other’s work and build upon it. Standards also enable “comparability”: results obtained in different labs with different procedures can be meaningfully compared to one another with more certainty, which is particularly important when making decisions about treating patients. NIST develops standards, methods, tools, and technology to advance the reliability of microbial community measurements , pathogen detection and identification, and microbial cell quantification for use in various sectors of the bioeconomy. NIST's programs in microbial metrology are supported by our deep expertise in measurement science, microbiology, metabolomics, metagenomics, flow cytometry, and bioinformatics. The microbiome field has seen disruptive technological innovations over the last 2 decades, paving the way for new science. We are developing advanced measurements, documentary standards, and reference materials to improve confidence in microbial measurements. For example, NIST scientists led the development of RM 8376 , a Mixed Microbial Genomic DNA standard designed to assess the analytical performance of metagenomic next generation sequencing (NGS)-based pathogen detection. The team is now working towards the development of whole cell microbial reference materials including the generation of single strain and mixed multi-strain materials. NIST co-founded and leads the International Microbiome and Multi-Omics Standards Alliance (IMMSA) , an open consortium of microbiome-focused researchers from industry, academia, and government that exists for the mutual benefit of the entire microbiome scientific community. IMMSA currently has over 700 members and convenes recurring webinars that provide a platform for researchers to share ideas and discuss challenges related to microbiome measurement assurance. The NIST-led Rapid Microbial Testing Methods Consortium aims to support the use of rapid methods to detect microbial contaminants in regenerative medicine and advanced therapy products . Wastewater surveillance is a promising approach to monitor biological and chemical contaminants on a community level and has recently been shown effective for the early detection of SARS-CoV-2 outbreaks. While much has been learned during the COVID-19 pandemic response, much work remains to establish a wastewater surveillance capability poised to address new targets as they emerge. NIST is working with DHS and EPA to develop standards that help enable robust, comparable wastewater surveillance. NIST, in collaboration with the EPA, is also developing a DNA reference material to assess the analytical performance of EPA-developed water quality testi

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Twin Falls District Office The Twin Falls District, located in south-central Idaho, manages over 3.9 million acres of public lands that stretch north toward Redfish Lake, east to American Falls, west to the Bruneau River and south, dipping over the Nevada border. The office is located in Twin Falls, a city perched on the rim of the Snake River Canyon, and home to the dramatic Perrine Bridge, one of a handful of artificial structures where base-jumping is legal. Here on the Twin Falls District the responsibilities are as diverse as the landscape itself, and include livestock grazing, recreation and one of the most successful fuels treatment programs in the Nation. Each year, hundreds of thousands of acres are treated to restore or improve native vegetation for wildlife habitat, livestock grazing and to reduce the frequency of wildland fire on the landscape. This District is host to three field offices: Shoshone Field Office (1.7 million acres), Jarbidge Field Office (nearly 1.4 million acres) and Burley Field Office (834,700 acres). The District also manages Idaho's only National Monument, Craters of the Moon National Monument and Preserve (275,000 acres). Energy Secretary Chris Wright Visits Ames National Laboratory, Advancing U.S. Leadership in Critical Materials, Science, and Innovation Secretary Wright joined Senator Ernst, Representative Latta, Representative Miller-Meeks, Representative Hinson and Representative Westerman at the Ames National Laboratory highlighting the importance of unleashing American energy, science, and innovation Energy.gov August 14, 2025 Estimated Read Time min Secretary Wright joined Senator Ernst, Representative Latta, Representative Miller-Meeks, Representative Hinson and Representative Westerman at the Ames National Laboratory highlighting the importance of unleashing American energy, science, and innovation. WASHINGTON— U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright joined U.S. Senator Joni Ernst (R-IA), U.S. Representative Bob Latta (R-OH-05), U.S. Representative Bruce Westerman (R-AR-04), U.S. Representative Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA-01), and U.S. Representative Ashley Hinson (R-IA-02) at the Ames National Laboratory to see firsthand the lab’s cutting-edge research and its pivotal role in addressing national energy and materials engineering challenges. Secretary Wright’s visit included briefings and discussions with scientists and lab experts in key mission areas, including rare earth minerals, critical materials, AI, and next-generation energy technologies. Wright toured the Critical Materials Innovation Hub, a Department of Energy (DOE) Innovation Hub led by Ames, that is spearheading efforts to restore American energy dominance, secure domestic supply chains, reduce dependence on foreign actors, and strengthen the scientific capabilities essential to U.S. competitiveness. “Ames National Laboratory is leading the way in groundbreaking science and innovation that will strengthen America’s energy future,” said Secretary Wright . “By investing in critical minerals, advanced manufacturing, and AI, we are building more secure domestic supply chains—bolstering America’s national security and increasing access to affordable, reliable energy for all Americans. These bold steps position the U.S. not just to compete, but to lead, for generations to come.” “Secretary Wright is the fourth cabinet official to visit Iowa this week and it is an absolute breath of fresh air how accessible the Trump administration is compared to the previous four years,” said U.S. Senator Joni Ernst . “America's national labs are not just critical to technological advancement but also national security. The Ames National Lab is a hub of innovation and will help ensure that our nation has the energy and critical materials to power the AI revolution.” “As Chairman of the Energy Subcommittee on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, I appreciated the opportunity to visit Ames National Laboratory with U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, Senator Joni Ernst, Congressman Bruce Westerman, Chairman of the Natural Resources Committee, Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks, and Congresswoman Ashley Hinson to see their cutting-edge research in materials science to breakthroughs in critical materials and energy innovation,” said U.S. Representative Bob Latta, Energy Subcommittee Chair on Energy and Commerce Committee . “Our National Laboratories, like Ames, power American innovation and will play a key role in advancing President Trump’s agenda for American energy dominance and global competitiveness.
