pages.description: تعمل الدول الأعضاء الآن على تحقيق أهداف التنمية المستدامة للأمم المتحدة بحلول عام 2030. وفي الوقت نفسه تعمل الدول الأعضاء على تحقيق الأهداف المنصوص عليها في اتفاقية باريس للمناخ لعام 2015 لتقليل الانبعاثات، وكلاهما حيوي لرفاهية البشرية.
pages.text: دعم التنمية المستدامة والعمل المناخي | الأمم المتحدة Skip to main content دعم التنمية المستدامة والعمل المناخي في عام 2018، وفرت المياه من الآبار وضخها حتى مسافة 4 كيلومترات في منطقة مستوطنة كالوبيي في كينيا، ولتقليل تكاليف الوقود، استخدم المجلس النرويجي للاجئين (الشريك المنفذ لبرامج المياه والصرف الصحي والنظافة التابعة للمفوضية) مضخات تعمل بالطاقة الشمسية لمدة 6-7 ساعات يوميًا، مما يوفر تكاليف الوقود. ان الهدف السادس من أهداف التنمية المستدامة للأمم المتحدة هو "ضمان الوصول إلى المياه والصرف الصحي للجميع". الصورة: Patrick Kihara/ الأمم المتحدة للبيئة أطلقت الأمم المتحدة جدول أعمال التنمية المستدامة في عام 2015، مما يعكس الفهم المتزايد من قبل الدول الأعضاء بأن نموذج التنمية المستدام لهذه الأجيال والأجيال القادمة يوفر أفضل مسار للمضي قدمًا للحد من الفقر وتحسين حياة الناس في كل مكان في الوقت نفسه، وبدأ تغير المناخ في إحداث تأثير عميق على وعي البشرية. مع ذوبان القمم الجليدية القطبية، وارتفاع مستويات البحار العالمية، وتزايد ضراوة الظواهر الجوية الكارثية، ولا يوجد بلد في العالم في مأمن من آثار تغير المناخ. سيساعد بناء اقتصاد عالمي أكثر استدامة على تقليل انبعاثات غازات الاحتباس الحراري التي تسبب تغير المناخ. ولذلك، من الأهمية بمكان أن يفي المجتمع الدولي بأهداف التنمية المستدامة للأمم المتحدة ، وكذلك أهداف خفض الانبعاثات المنصوص عليها في اتفاقية باريس للمناخ لعام 2015. إن التنمية المستدامة والعمل المناخي مرتبطان، وكلاهما ضروري لرفاهية البشرية في الحاضر والمستقبل. رئيس الأمم المتحدة المعني بعقد العمل من أجل أهداف التنمية المستدامة هل تساءلت يومًا: ما هي "اتفاقية باريس" وكيف تعمل؟ يشرح هذا الفيديو الأساسيات. تقرير التنمية المستدامة العالمية المشتركة البيئية خطة التنمية المستدامة الأهداف الإنمائية للألفية - كان ما يقرب من 40 في المائة من سكان العالم النامي يعيشون في فقر مدقع قبل عقدين فقط. ومنذ ذلك الحين، نجح العالم في خفض مستوى الفقر المدقع إلى النصف، حيث ساهمت الأهداف الإنمائية للألفية التابعة للأمم المتحدة بشكل كبير في هذا التقدم. خطة التنمية المستدامة لعام 2030 - إدراكًا لنجاح الأهداف الإنمائية للألفية، والحاجة إلى إكمال مهمة القضاء على الفقر، تبنت الأمم المتحدة خطة التنمية المستدامة لعام 2030 ، والتي تتضمن إنهاء الفقر وانعدام الجوع والصحة الجيدة والرفاهية، وتعليم جيد والمساواة بين الجنسين والمياه النظيفة والصرف الصحي وطاقة نظيفة بأسعار معقولة، والعمل اللائق والنمو الاقتصادي، والصناعة والابتكار والبنية التحتية، وتقليل عدم المساواة، ومدن ومجتمعات مستدامة والاستهلاك والإنتاج المسؤولان والعمل المناخي، والحياة تحت الماء والحياة على الأرض والسلام والعدل والمؤسسات القوية، والشراكات لتحقيق الأهداف. اتفاقية باريس - أثناء صياغة هذه الأهداف والموافقة عليها، دعمت الأمم المتحدة مفاوضات تغير المناخ، التي أدت إلى اتفاقية باريس بشأن تغير المناخ في عام 2015. والهدف الرئيسي لاتفاق باريس هو تعزيز الاستجابة العالمية لتهديد تغير المناخ عن طريق الحفاظ على ارتفاع درجة الحرارة العالمية أقل بكثير من درجتين مئويتين فوق مستويات ما قبل الصناعة، أو حتى أقل من 1.5 درجة مئوية. بالإضافة إلى ذلك، تهدف اتفاقية باريس إلى تعزيز قدرة البلدان على التعامل مع آثار تغير المناخ. ولتحقيق هذه الأهداف، سيتم وضع التمويل والتكنولوجيا الجديدة وإطار بناء القدرات المعزز. كما تنص الاتفاقية على تعزيز شفافية العمل والدعم من خلال إطار الشفافية. قمتان رئيسيتان قمة التنمية المستدامة لعام 2023 انعقدت قمة أهداف التنمية المستدامة لعام 2023 في يومي 18 و 19 أيلول/سبتمبر 2023 في نيويورك. وكانت القمة بمثابة بداية مرحلة جديدة من التقدم المتسارع نحو تحقيق أهداف التنمية المستدامة مع توجيه سياسي رفيع المستوى بشأن الإجراءات التحويلية والمُعجلة حتى عام 2030. كما كانت القمة، التي عقدها رئيس الجمعية العامة، نقطة منتصف الطريق نحو الموعد الأقصى المحدد لتحقيق جدول أعمال 2030 وأهداف التنمية المستدامة. فضلا عن أنها مثلت كذلك تجاوبا لتأثير الأزمات المتعددة والمتشابكة التي يواجهها العالم، ومن المتوقع أن تعيد إشعال شمعة الأمل والتفاؤل والحماس لجدول أعمال 2030. وقال الأمين العام أنطونيو غوتيريش في كلمته التي ألقاها عند افتتاح المنتدى رفيع المستوى: “إن أهداف التنمية المستدامة ليست مجرد قائمة أهداف. إنها محامل لآمال ولأحلام ولحقوق ولتوقعات الناس في كل مكان." اعتمدت قمة أهداف التنمية المستدامة إعلانا سياسيا يدعو إلى الاستعداد لعقد من العمل وإلى تحقيق التنمية المستدامة. مؤتمر قمة الطموح المناخي نظرا أزمة المناخ الم

DOE Issues Final Non-FTA LNG Export Authorization for Additional Exports From the Venture Global Calcasieu Pass Project U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright today signed a final authorization for additional liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports to non-free trade agreement (non-FTA) countries from Venture Global’s Calcasieu Pass project in Cameron Parish, Louisiana. Energy.gov August 4, 2025 Estimated Read Time min WASHINGTON —U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright today signed a final authorization for additional liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports to non-free trade agreement (non-FTA) countries from Venture Global’s Calcasieu Pass project in Cameron Parish, Louisiana. This authorization allows Calcasieu Pass, an LNG export project that has been in operation since 2022, to export an additional 20 billion cubic feet of natural gas as LNG per year—an amount that could support approximately five additional cargos per year. “Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, the United States has made massive leaps in unleashing LNG dominance,” said Secretary Wright . “Today’s authorization is another reminder that this administration is committed to expanding the supply of abundant, affordable, and secure American energy. The data over the past 10 years of U.S. LNG exports clearly shows that we can lead the world in energy production while lowering energy costs here at home.” “With this decision, DOE is continuing to return to regular order on LNG exports,” said Tala Goudarzi, Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management . Venture Global’s Calcasieu Pass project has been exporting LNG to the global market since March 2022. Venture Global’s second LNG export project, Plaquemines, began exporting late in 2024 , and Venture Global recently announced a final investment decision on Phase 1 of its third LNG export project, CP2. On March 19, 2025, DOE issued a conditional non-FTA export authorization to CP2 that is ready for a final order now that FERC has concluded its review of the project. U.S. natural gas production and exports are currently at record highs, averaging 105.9 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) and 14.6 Bcf/d in 2025, respectively, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration’s latest Short-Term Energy Outlook . Thanks to President Trump’s bold energy agenda, U.S. LNG exports are on track to double around the end of this decade once all export projects under construction are completed. ### View Next Press Release Energy Secretary Marks 200th Day of Trump Administration at SRNL’s New Advanced Manufacturing Collaborative Center August 7, 2025 View Previous Press Release Energy Department Announces First Pilot Project for Advanced Nuclear Fuel Lines August 4, 2025 Explore more on these topics: Returning to Regular Order on LNG Exports Media Inquiries: (202) 586-4940 or DOENews@hq.doe.gov Read more at the energy.gov Newsroom

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Community, Fire, and Enforcement Jun 8, 2026 On June 3, 2025 at approximately 2 p.m., a member of the Salmon, Idaho community reported smoke in the West Fork of Wimpey Creek on Bureau of Land Management managed lands. Central Idaho Dispatch received the call and promptly mobilized firefighting forces. A US Wildland Fire Service fire engine responded, heading up the steep, rocky road toward the location of the smoke report. A United States Department of Agriculture Forest Service (USDA FS) helicopter launched to assist and located the smoke high on the ridgeline in topography difficult to navigate by ground crews. With the helicopter holding a hover, four heli-rappellers descended by rope to the scene of the fire and were joined by other US Wildland Fire personnel. The firefighters sized up the fire at approximately one-quarter acre, 30% active, and creeping on a 20-40% slope in timber, grass, and dead/downed timber with 3-5 mph south-southwest winds. Firefighters in the background cleaning up during the Wimpey Fire. (BLM photo) Firefighters dug hand line around the perimeter of the fire successfully halting forward progress. Seven hours after being reported, the Wimpey Fire was officially considered controlled at 9 p.m. on June 3, 2025. Since no lighting had occurred in the area for 24 hours, Central Idaho Dispatch requested a fire investigator to search for a cause. A BLM fire investigator, who is also a BLM Ranger, arrived on scene at approximately 7:30 p.m. to gather information and document initial observations of the fire directly from the firefighters. The investigator located evidence showing the fire burned uphill and identified the origin on the downslope perimeter. At the origin, remnants of a campfire were discovered, indicating it caused the fire. The investigator learned from a BLM Ranger that individuals cutting firewood had been in the area leading up to the start of the fire on June 3. The Ranger had received a citizen report expressing concern that wood cutters were in the area working through the night. The Ranger had previously contacted some wood cutters, advising them to pick up litter and validate wood tags. Since there was sign of wood cutting near the origin of the fire, this prior information provided a useful direction for the investigation. Smoldering ground with active flames during last year's Wimpey Fire. (BLM photo) The BLM fire investigator and USDA FS Law Enforcement Officer (LEO) interviewed the wood cutters and suspected they were responsible for the fire. The officers gathered additional information, including that the responsible party started fires in the West Fork of Wimpey Creek to clean up their slash. They admitted to covering the fires with dirt and rocks, but did not carry water to douse them. The BLM Ranger issued a Federal Violation Notice to the individual responsible for causing the fire. The USDA FS LEO informed the responsible party that per fuelwood permit stipulations, slash may be scattered and does not need to be piled, and it is not safe to burn. As we look back on the June 2025 Wimpey Fire, the takeaway is that the BLM does our best work with coordinated effort and all hands on deck. In this case, that effort started with community members who saw something that wasn’t right and appropriately reported it. Through diligent work by local fire and law enforcement staff, the Wimpey Fire was controlled at just one-quarter acre. Cuando caduca el período estatutorio, ya no podemos tasar o cobrar impuestos adicionales o permitir que usted reclame un reembolso. Fechas de vencimiento del estatuto La fecha de vencimiento de una ley de prescripción depende del: Plazo en que el IRS puede tasar los impuestos Plazo en que el IRS puede recaudar los impuestos Plazo en el que usted puede reclamar un crédito o un reembolso Cómo saber qué fecha de vencimiento del estatuto le aplica a usted Cuando le tasamos o recaudamos impuestos o cuando decidimos sobre su reclamación presentada para un crédito o un reembolso, le enviamos por correo un aviso o carta. El aviso o carta le informará sobre el año tributario, qué acciones estamos tomando y los próximos pasos a seguir. Para obtener más información, consulte Cómo entender su carta o aviso . pages.description: Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen says Trump administration has not properly invested existing funds
pages.text: Transportation secretary Sean Duffy blames prior presidents and Congress for flight stoppage | Trump administration | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation US transportation secretary Sean Duffy speaks during a press briefing at the Department of Transportation headquarters building in Washington DC, on Saturday. Photograph: Aaron Schwartz/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen US transportation secretary Sean Duffy speaks during a press briefing at the Department of Transportation headquarters building in Washington DC, on Saturday. Photograph: Aaron Schwartz/AFP/Getty Images Trump administration Transportation secretary Sean Duffy blames prior presidents and Congress for flight stoppage Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen says Trump administration has not properly invested existing funds Michael Sainato Sun 15 Nov 2026 11.18 EST Last modified on Sun 15 Nov 2026 19.05 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Donald Trump’s administration on Sunday blamed the travel chaos stemming from Friday’s four-hour nationwide flight stoppage on prior presidents as well as a lack of congressional funding – though a Democratic senator argued that the Trump administration hasn’t properly invested all of the funds it has already been given to implement needed air travel infrastructure upgrades. “I take responsibility for what was given to me by prior administrations,” the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, told CNN’s Dana Bash, a day after he said routine but necessary maintenance botched by a contractor had caused Friday’s Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop , leading to the delay or cancellation of thousands of flights throughout the weekend. Nearly 2,000 ​flights within, into or out of the US on Sunday were canceled and more than 8,600 were delayed, according to the aviation data site FlightAware . Meanwhile, Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland criticized how the Trump administration has managed existing funding allocated for the improvements coveted by Duffy. Two planes collide on taxiway at Miami airport one day after national grounding Read more “It’s really rich to hear the secretary pointing the fingers at Congress when Congress has given the administration what they asked for,” Van Hollen separately told CNN’s Bash on Sunday morning. “If they need more, they should come up and justify it. I will support what is necessary to have a safe system and a reliable system.” Duffy claimed the congressional funding that Van Hollen mentioned – $12.5bn – was limited in scope and not nearly enough. “I have no money in that $12.5bn that I can use for a new architecture for telecom,” said Duffy. “I can’t build new software to manage our airplanes in the airspace because it dates back to the 1990s, but there’s no money for that. There’s no money for towers. Our towers are old.” Duffy also spent part of the interview with CNN defending Trump, who waited until Sunday to remark on the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years. The president’s comments came in the form of social media posts blaming the Biden administration and describing himself as busy “in the White House having meetings on many subjects”. They came after he had posted about what he envisioned to be a bipartisan congressional initiative to revitalize the motion picture and television industries. “Before I even was sworn in, the president who loves the airspace was telling me we have to modernize,” Duffy said to Bash. “This is the first president we have who cares this much about modernizing the airspace.” When asked why Trump took two days to comment on the ground stop, Duffy claimed he was in constant behind-the-scene contact with the president. “He was fully engaged because this is important to him, and it’s important to America,” Duffy claimed. “The president is fully supportive, fully engaged, and was fully tracking what’s happening.” View image in fullscreen Airplane luggage from canceled flights piles up during a nationwide groun

La influenza y el embarazo 17 de sep. del 2024 English (US) Lo que debe saber La influenza (gripe) durante el embarazo tiene más probabilidades de causar una enfermedad que requiera hospitalización. Si está embarazada y tiene síntomas de influenza, llame a su proveedor de atención médica inmediatamente. Los CDC recomiendan un pronto tratamiento antiviral contra la influenza durante el embarazo para las personas con influenza confirmada o presunta. La influenza y el embarazo La influenza también podría ser dañina para el bebé en gestación durante el embarazo. (La fiebre es un síntoma común de la influenza que se ha asociado en algunos estudios a defectos del tubo neural y otros efectos adversos para un bebé en gestación). Recibir la vacuna contra la influenza durante el embarazo puede proteger contra la influenza y las hospitalizaciones relacionadas con la enfermedad. La vacunación contra la influenza durante el embarazo también puede proteger a los bebés contra la influenza durante varios meses después del nacimiento y de hospitalizaciones relacionadas con esta enfermedad, ya que la madre embarazada transmite anticuerpos al bebé en gestación durante el embarazo. Cuando usted recibe una vacuna contra la influenza durante el embarazo o la lactancia, su cuerpo produce anticuerpos contra la influenza que se comparten con su bebé a través de la leche materna. Condiciones médicas prexistentes Si está embarazada, no existe ninguna recomendación de que usted o las personas con condiciones médicas prexistentes necesiten obtener un permiso especial o consentimiento por escrito de su médico o profesional de atención médica para vacunarse contra la influenza si lo hace en su lugar de trabajo, una farmacia u otro lugar fuera del consultorio de su médico. No debe recibir la vacuna contra la influenza en atomizador nasal durante el embarazo. Seguir leyendo Ideas equivocadas acerca de la influenza estacional y las vacunas contra la influenza El mejor momento para la vacunación Para la mayoría de los adultos, septiembre y octubre son generalmente buenos meses para vacunarse cada año. También se puede considerar la vacunación en julio y agosto para quienes estén en el tercer trimestre de embarazo, ya que esto puede ayudar a proteger a sus bebés contra la influenza por varios meses después del nacimiento (cuando son demasiado pequeños para ser vacunados). La vacunación es la mejor manera de protegerse contra la influenza Recibir la vacuna contra la influenza es la primera y más importante medida que una persona puede tomar para protegerse contra la influenza y sus posibles complicaciones graves. Si está embarazada, debe recibir la vacuna contra la influenza inyectable y no en atomizador nasal. Un estudio en el 2013 mostró que durante las temporadas de influenza 2010-2011 y 2011-2012 la vacunación redujo el riesgo de influenza durante el embarazo en hasta la mitad. Estos resultados concuerdan con el rango general de efectividad de la vacuna contra la influenza estimada en adultos de 18 a 64 años. Un estudio en el 2018 mostró que recibir la vacuna contra la influenza durante el embarazo redujo el riesgo de hospitalización por influenza en un promedio del 40 %. pages.title: Tracking a Mystery: When and How the First Americans Arrived | National Geographic
pages.description: The first Americans weren't one group of people; they arrived at different times, and likely by different methods.
pages.text: Tracking a Mystery: When and How the First Americans Arrived | National Geographic The Oregon Coast, pictured here, may have been a byway for the first Americans as they followed the nutrient-rich coast southward on foot and by boat, says the new book, Atlas of a Lost World . Photograph by Ty Milford, Aurora BOOK TALK When, How Did the First Americans Arrive? It’s Complicated. The first Americans weren't one group of people; they arrived at different times, and likely by different methods. By Simon Worrall Published June 9, 2018 • 13 min read How did human beings first come to North America? Across the Bering Strait, on foot? Down the “kelp highway” by boat? Across the Atlantic via the polar ice cap? And when did they reach here? 10,000 years ago? 40,000? Or were they always here, as the Navajo and other Native American tribes believe? In his new book, Atlas Of A Lost World , author Craig Childs sets off to test these different theories on the ground, traveling from Alaska to Chile, Canada to Florida. What he finds, despite the best efforts of archaeologists and the latest technology , still remains in many ways a mystery. Speaking from his home in Colorado, he explains why many Native Americans reject the idea that their ancestors migrated from somewhere else; how an archaeologist nicknamed Dr. Poop believes he has identified the first human excrement in America ; and why diversity seems to have been built into America’s DNA. Photograph courtesy Random House Let’s cut straight to the chase: when did humans first arrive in North America? The first arrivals keep getting older and older because we’re finding more evidence as time goes on. Right now we can solidly say that people were across the Americas by 15,000 years ago. But that means people were probably already well in place by then; and there’s enough evidence to suggest humans were widespread 20,000 years ago. There’s some evidence of people as far back as 30,000 to 40,000 years ago, but the evidence gets thinner and thinner the further back you go . It appears there’s not a single arrival date. No doubt there was a first person walking in, but when that happened is well before 20,000 years ago. The solid dates of 15,000 are based on sites where you can find fire pits , burned bones and work stones that have been turned into scrapers and hammers and spear points. When you go back further, you’re finding mammoths that have been shattered open in a way that’s characteristic of humans. Then you start getting into these questions of what really counts as a sign of human presence, and what is just a trampled mammoth bone that happens to look like it was struck by a human with a rock. Equally thorny is the question of how humans got here. Give us a quick 101. [Laughs] The easiest way to get here is by foot. The Bering Land Bridge has been the longstanding theory because that’s the clearest connection between Asia and North America, up in the Arctic, and it only appears when ice is locked up on land and sea levels drop. It’s the only place where you could walk from one side to the other. I spent some time up on an island that is a remnant of the land bridge between the coast of Siberia and Alaska. There, you can see walking across. But when you got to the other side, you’d be facing 5 million square miles of ice; and that’s when you start looking at coastal migrations. People in the Ice Age were already moving up and down the coast of Japan, Kamchatka, and Korea, using boats, and the evidence is clear that they were getting out to places you can only reach with boats. It makes sense that you would keep following the coast around. The land bridge has a coast, which would bring you down Alaska and British Colombia, to Washington and Oregon. This is the more viable way into North America, because there’s what is called the kelp highway , a biotically rich region that follows the entire coast. Read the June 24, 2026 news release . EPA Advances Comprehensive PFAS Strategy with Legally Defensible, Practical, Scientifically Sound Drinking Water Protections In May 2026, EPA announced an holistic approach to tackle PFAS across its full lifecycle. EPA also concluded that the existing regulations provide the tools necessary to develop protective permit conditions without the need to modify the hazardous waste definition. Energy Secretary Marks 200th Day of Trump Administration at SRNL’s New Advanced Manufacturing Collaborative Center Secretary Wright joined Senator Graham, Representative Wilson, and state and local leaders for the opening of the new Advanced Manufacturing Collaborative, creating a new chapter for American innovation in South Carolina. Energy.gov August 7, 2025 Estimated Read Time min Advanced Manufacturing Collaborative in South Carolina Set to Lead on AI, Energy, and Manufacturing WASHINGTON —U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright joined U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham (R-SC), U.S. Representative Joe Wilson (R-SC-02) and state and local leaders for the opening of the new Advanced Manufacturing Collaborative , creating a new chapter for American innovation in South Carolina. Launched during the first Trump Administration and led by the Department of Energy’s Savannah River National Laboratory (SRNL), the new center enables DOE’s mission to support American manufacturing – serving as an economic driver, creating jobs, spurring innovation and maximizing the reach of industry in South Carolina. “The Advanced Manufacturing Collaborative will bring the expertise of the Department of Energy’s National Labs together with innovators from academia and the private sector with one shared goal: to unleash America’s energy potential,” said Energy Secretary Wright . “This mission was started by President Trump in his first term, and I am proud to be representing the Department of Energy 200 days into his second administration for the grand opening of this facility, completed in record time.” “The opening of the Advanced Manufacturing Collaborative on USC Aiken’s campus will greatly enhance the ability for the Savannah River National Laboratory and private sector, along with academia, to work together on critical initiatives," said U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham (R-SC) . "I was proud to secure federal funding for this facility because I believe this partnership will pay dividends for South Carolina and the rest of the nation. The opening of this facility will cement Aiken as a hub for innovation and advanced technology development for years to come. Finally, I would like to thank Secretary Wright and President Trump for recognizing the importance of South Carolina’s contribution to positioning America as a leader in manufacturing and innovation. I will continue to work with them to ensure the Palmetto State remains on the forefront in this effort." “The opening of this facility is a success story of how the government, private sector, and institutions of higher education can come together to drive meaningful innovation and opportunities for the community and nation,” said Congressman Joe Wilson (R-SC-02) . “I am grateful to represent the Savannah River Site and its workforce and will continue to work with President Trump, Energy Secretary Wright, Congress, and local leaders to reinvigorate the nuclear industrial base at the Site and support Peace Through Strength.” Located on the campus of the University of South Carolina-Aiken, the state-of-the-art 63,000-square-foot facility connects the best of American industry, academia and government to increase capabilities in areas such as additive manufacturing, AI-driven automation, and novel materials for fusion energy and energy resilience. pages.title: Libyan town of Derna rebuilt after floods becomes showcase for strongman Khalifa Haftar 's rule British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The remarkable reconstruction of Derna is being used as a showcase for the rest of Libya by Khalifa Haftar and his sons.
pages.text: Libyan town of Derna rebuilt after floods becomes showcase for strongman Khalifa Haftar 's rule Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Town rebuilt after devastating floods becomes showcase for Libyan strongman's rule 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Tim Whewell Derna AFP via Getty Images Whole areas of Derna have been entirely rebuilt "It was joy when I moved in. I could finally relax," says Abdulwahab Damdoum, surveying his luxurious new apartment overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, in the eastern Libyan city of Derna. Just three years ago he was clinging in terror to the roof of a house as the world's deadliest flood this century surged around him. Now the 27-year-old port worker, his wife and two young daughters have been given a new, free, 300-sq-m home in a showcase development commissioned by a son of Khalifa Haftar, the warlord who controls eastern Libya. It is part of a rapid $2bn (£1.5bn) rebuilding of Derna that the powerful Haftar family hope will serve as a model for development throughout Libya, increasing their influence across a country currently split between east and west, with rival governments in charge. The money comes from the state coffers of the oil-rich country, allocated by its parliament. But there are no published records of how it has been spent, raising questions about accountability and possible corruption. Damdoum, like many flood survivors, simply thanks the head of the Development and Reconstruction Fund, Belkacem Haftar, for what has been achieved since the early hours of 11 September 2023, when lashing rain from Storm Daniel burst two dams above Derna, sending a wall of water 7m (23 ft) high cascading down onto the sleeping city. The exact death toll will probably never be known. Some estimates have been as high as 6,000, though 4,000 now seems a more likely figure. Many bodies are still unidentified. Tim Whewell/BBC Abdulwahab Damdoum lost his father, brother and sister in the flood In a city of about 100,000 people, that means almost everybody lost someone they loved. The 14 relatives and neighbours on the roof with Damdoum – including his father, brother and sister - all drowned. He survived, but his home was destroyed, and he had to find temporary accommodation. "It was rent, rent, rent," he says. "Now, no-one can take this [new flat] from me. I thank Engineer Belkacem. God sent this person who picked the city up from disaster." Portraits of Belkacem, widely known simply as "the Engineer", his younger brother Saddam, a military chief also involved in reconstruction, and their father Khalifa are on hoardings all over Derna and the region. "Since 2011, Libya has not built big projects like this," says Hussein el-Mansory, project manager of the "2,000 Apartments" complex where Damdoum now lives. "I feel very happy and proud and I'll tell my children: 'I made this.'" The complex includes a new mosque, hospital, shopping mall and schools. New roads, bridges have also been built in Derna. But while many survivors have been rehoused, some are still waiting. Among them is Izz al-Nasr Ibzeou, a marine science lecturer at the university. His wife Salima, her mother Mouna, and all the couple's seven children, aged between one and 11, drowned. His family home was ruined, but the authorities have not yet fully restored it because Ibzeou also has an undamaged apartment in another part of town. He returns every day to his old house, now an empty shell, to see his children's possessions, which he has kept in dust-covered piles. "This is my son Moez's bike. He played with it every day. And this is my daughter Fawzia's dress. She wore it whenever she went to a wedding," Ibzeou says. "Even if I decide not to come to remember them, my feet will bring me here of their own accord." pages.text: Session 3: Methane Leaks Field Trip "Safari" | Climate Action Hands-On: Harnessing Science with Communities to Cut Carbon | MIT OpenCourseWare Browse Course Material Course Info Instructors David Damm-Luhr Rajesh Kasturirangan Zeyneb Magavi Chris Nidel Nathan Phillips Audrey Schulman Britta Voss Jeff Warren Ory Zik As Taught In January IAP 2017 Level Non-Credit Course Info Instructors David Damm-Luhr Rajesh Kasturirangan Zeyneb Magavi Chris Nidel Nathan Phillips Audrey Schulman Britta Voss Jeff Warren Ory Zik As Taught In January IAP 2017 Level Non-Credit Topics Energy Climate Fossil Fuels Engineering Environmental Engineering Environmental Management Social Science Public Administration Environmental Policy Topics Energy, Climate & Sustainability Climate Science Climate and Energy Policy Energy Engineering Environmental Engineering Science & Math Earth Science Social Sciences Policy and Administration Learning Resource Types collections Image Gallery notes Lecture Notes theaters Lecture Videos theaters Video Materials theaters Workshop Videos Download Course search search GIVE NOW about ocw help & faqs contact us RES.ENV-001 | January IAP 2017 | Non-Credit Climate Action Hands-On: Harnessing Science with Communities to Cut Carbon Menu More Info Summary Objective: Hands-on field activity collecting data on real-word methane leaks from natural gas infrastructure in Cambridge and Somerville MA. Familiarize two sets of 5–8 participants with the tools and methods. Session structure: Split participants into two groups. Each group has a 90 minute excursion in a 12-passenger van equipped with a Picarro gas leak monitor, GPS linked, connected to a laptop for real-time display of methane concentration as it drives. Outline for each group trip: Brief (5 minute) introduction to the equipment and methods. Drive along routes known to have methane leaks, discuss what’s observed as we go. At select locations of interest (e.g. larger methane concentrations), stop the van. Everyone gets out to take a closer look. Where is the likely leak source? Use handheld methane probe for more precise measurement. Discuss clues about natural gas infrastructure repairs (e.g. spray paint tags, manhole covers, pavement patches) and presence of leaks (e.g. tree damage). Instructors: Nathan Phillips (Boston University), Audrey Schulman ( HEET ) Safari Results This video shows some highlights of one group’s leak safari. pages.description: Use this checklist if you are considering claiming the credit or have already submitted a claim to the IRS.
pages.text: Employee Retention Credit Eligibility Checklist: Help understanding this complex credit | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Employee Retention Credit Eligibility Checklist: Help understanding this complex credit More In News Working Families Tax Cuts News releases Tax relief in disaster situations Topics in the news Fact sheets IRS statements and announcements IRS Tax Tips IRS guidance Media center Tax articles to share Posters to share On this page Part A: Check your eligibility Part B: Claim the ERC if you're eligible Part C: Resolve an incorrect ERC claim You can use this question-and-answer tool to see if you might be eligible for the Employee Retention Credit (ERC or ERTC) . Resolving an incorrect claim may help you avoid having to repay an incorrect credit, possibly with penalties and interest. The IRS continues to warn employers about unscrupulous ERC promoters who oversimplify and misrepresent eligibility rules and lure ineligible taxpayers to claim the credit. The IRS is committed to helping taxpayers who are eligible, while preventing incorrect ERC claims. Employee Retention Credit The ERC is a pandemic-era tax credit for employers that kept paying employees during the COVID-19 pandemic either: when they were shut down due to a government order, or when they had the required decline in gross receipts during certain eligibility periods in 2020 and 2021, or qualified as a recovery startup business for the third or fourth quarters of 2021. Part A: Check your eligibility Answer these questions in numerical order to see if you may be eligible for the ERC. ERC Eligibility Checklist Question 1 Did you 1) operate a trade, business or tax-exempt organization and 2) have employees and pay wages to them between March 13, 2020, and Dec. 31, 2021? For more info, see IRS.gov/ercqualified . Note – Household employers are not eligible for ERC. Yes No Ineligible If no, you aren't eligible to claim the ERC. If you improperly claimed ERC, see Part C . Question 2 Did your trade or business experience the required decline in gross receipts during the eligibility periods in 2020 or the first three calendar quarters (Jan. through Sept.) of 2021? For more info and examples, see IRS.gov/ercdecline Yes No Maybe Eligible If yes, you may be eligible for the ERC. You will need to confirm that your decline in receipts meets requirements. See IRS.gov/ercdecline . If you meet the requirements, skip to Part B . Question 3 Are you claiming the ERC because of supply chain issues? For more info, see IRS.gov/ercsupply and the IRS legal memo on supply chain disruptions (AM-2023-005) PDF , which includes examples. Yes No If Yes Be extremely cautious. A supply chain disruption by itself doesn’t qualify you for the ERC. Carefully review IRS.gov/ercsupply and the examples in the legal memo on supply chain disruptions (AM-2023-005) PDF PDF . Be sure your supplier’s government order meets the criteria in #4; then go to Part B . If you incorrectly claimed ERC, go to Part C . Question 4 Was the operation of your business or organization fully or partially suspended by a government order due to the COVID-19 pandemic during 2020 or the first three calendar quarters (Jan. through Sept.) of 2021? The order must be a government order , not guidance, a recommendation or a statement. The government order must be due to the COVID-19 pandemic and must have fully or partially suspended your operations . You can only claim ERC for periods the order was in effect and your operations were suspended. For more info, see IRS.gov/ercqualifying Yes No Maybe Eligible If yes, you may be eligible for the ERC. For more information and examples of government orders and full or partial suspension see IRS.gov/ercqualifying . pages.text: Union Resources | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Union Resources The Office of Labor-Management Standards (OLMS) administers provisions of the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act (LMRDA), which promotes labor-management transparency by making available reports showing unions’ financial condition and employer expenditures for their activities in persuading workers during union organizing campaigns. It also promotes labor union democracy and financial integrity through adopting and enforcing standards for union officer elections and union trusteeships and safeguards for union assets. OLMS also administers the standards of conduct provisions of the Civil Service Reform Act of 1978 ( CSRA ) and the Foreign Service Act of 1980, which extend comparable protections to Federal labor unions. A union that represents only employees of state, county, or municipal governments is not subject to the LMRDA or the CSRA. See 29 CFR Part 451 and the OLMS Interpretative Manual Definitions section for further information concerning labor organization coverage under the LMRDA. OLMS has the authority to enforce certain provisions of the LMRDA. However, some provisions of the LMRDA such as the Bill of Rights and the fiduciary standards for union officers can only be enforced by union members through a private suit in Federal district court. See the OLMS Interpretative Manual Enforcement section . The CSRA standards of conduct regulations also incorporate many of the LMRDA provisions. When administering the standards of conduct regulations for Federal sector unions, OLMS is guided by LMRDA policies and principles. Unlike the LMRDA, the CSRA standards of conduct regulations are enforced entirely through various administrative actions depending upon the violation. This generally involves the filing of a complaint by an OLMS District Director, a hearing before a Department of Labor administrative law judge, the judge's report and recommendations, and a decision and order by the Department’s Administrative Review Board. For further Union Resources Information, see the sections below, the OLMS Publications on the LMRDA and CSRA , the OLMS Interpretative Manual and related Questions and Answers , or contact OLMS . Also, for procedures on enforcement for the LMRDA and CSRA, including information on filing a complaint, please visit this page . To view union annual financial and other reports for the year 2000 and later, as well as order copies of earlier reports, visit the Online Public Disclosure Room . Union Democracy | Union Financial Integrity | Union Transparency | Compliance Assistance Sessions Voluntary Compliance Partnership Program Union Democracy The LMRDA and CSRA promote union democracy through standards for union officer elections and union trusteeships. Concerning union democracy, the LMRDA and CSRA establish democratic standards for conducting union officer elections, including frequency and method of election, right of members in good standing to be candidates, rights of candidates, and voting rights of members. OLMS investigates and supervises a number of elections to ensure adherence to these standards. An investigation will be conducted if OLMS receives a timely complaint. If the investigation determines that the election provisions have been violated, OLMS may negotiate a voluntary agreement to have the union rerun the election under OLMS supervision. Failing that, OLMS will take legal action seeking a new election. Where warranted, OLMS investigates criminal violations associated with elections including ballot fraud, false statements, and deprivation of rights under the LMRDA by violence. OLMS also conducts investigations to determine the validity of trusteeships imposed by national unions on subordinate bodies, in which the parent body suspends, partially or fully, the autonomy of the subordinate body. Tomar medidas para tener aire limpio y prevenir los virus respiratorios 18 de ago. del 2025 English (US) Lo que debe saber Los virus respiratorios se pueden propagar en el aire que respira, especialmente en espacios interiores y con mucha gente. Tomar medidas para tener aire limpio ayuda a reducir los microbios dañinos y los virus en el aire, lo que disminuye sus posibilidades de presentar una enfermedad respiratoria. Es una estrategia de prevención principal recomendada para todos para disminuir el riesgo de presentar enfermedades respiratorias. Recomendación Dentro de lo posible, tome medidas para tener aire limpio. Esto puede significar dejar entrar aire fresco del exterior, purificar el aire del interior o reunirse al aire libre. Las partículas de virus no se acumulan en el aire libre tanto como lo hacen en espacios interiores. Cómo funciona Algunos microbios se propagan por el aire entre las personas. Esto sucede más fácilmente en espacios interiores, con mucha gente y con poca circulación de aire. Para reducir el riesgo de exposición, es bueno mejorar la calidad del aire aumentando la circulación, limpiando el aire con purificadores o decidiendo reunirse al aire libre. Medidas que puede tomar Dejar entrar la mayor cantidad de aire fresco posible a su hogar al abrir puertas y ventanas o usar extractores de aire. Si su casa tiene un sistema central de calefacción, ventilación y aire acondicionado (HVAC, un sistema con conductos de aire que pasan por toda la casa) con filtro, configurar el ventilador en la posición de "encendido" en lugar de "automático" cuando tenga visitas, y usar filtros plisados. Cambiar su filtro cada tres meses o según las instrucciones del fabricante. Usar un purificador portátil de partículas en el aire de alta eficacia (HEPA, por sus siglas en inglés). Dentro de lo posible, hacer las actividades al aire libre, donde la circulación de aire es mejor. Medidas que pueden tomar las organizaciones Asegurarse de que los sistemas de calefacción, ventilación y aire acondicionado existentes cumplan con al menos el requisito mínimo de ventilación de aire exterior según los códigos de diseño de ventilación. Los códigos aplicables se basan en el año de construcción o de la última renovación de la edificación y en la ocupación prevista del edificio. Tener como meta hacer 5 o más cambios de aire por hora (ACH) de aire limpio. Esto puede lograrse mediante cualquier combinación de sistema de ventilación central, ventilación natural o dispositivos adicionales que proporcionen ACH equivalentes a su ventilación actual. Aviso Los CDC ofrecen directrices separadas y específicas para entornos de atención médica ( COVID-19 , influenza , y prevención y control de infecciones en general ). Las leyes federales de derechos civiles podrían requerir modificaciones razonables o adaptaciones razonables en distintas circunstancias. Nada de lo incluido en estas directrices tiene como objetivo restarle valor a esas leyes o remplazarlas. Aviso Los enlaces a sitios web pueden llevar a páginas en inglés o español. EPA’s First Ever PFAS TECH Strategy Spurs Innovation in Research and Technology to Address PFAS October 26, 2026 Contact Information EPA Press Office ( press@epa.gov ) DENVER, CO – Today, at an event in Commerce City, Colorado, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin launched the first ever agency-wide PFAS Technology, Evaluation, Coordination, and Harmonization (PFAS TECH) strategy. This new effort will help catapult technology innovation on PFAS while supporting practical tools, funding, and technical assistance to benefit communities addressing local PFAS challenges. “The Trump EPA is laser-focused on making America healthy again by developing real and tangible agency-wide strategies to protect Americans from exposure to PFAS,” said EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin. “Technology innovation is essential to accelerating our efforts to address these contaminants, and EPA’s new PFAS TECH strategy will advance scientific discovery, demonstrate the real-world feasibility of advanced technologies, and help reduce PFAS in the environment.” The PFAS TECH strategy prioritizes collaboration between EPA, federal partners, states, local leaders, and the private sector. EPA’s goals through this new strategy are to: Power innovation in research and development by accelerating new PFAS treatment and destruction technologies through funding, forming new partnerships, and supporting early-stage innovation. In keeping with the Trump EPA’s commitment to cooperative federalism, this effort includes working with federal partners, states, local businesses, universities, and water systems to test promising methods like foam fractionation, supercritical water oxidation, and other emerging treatment approaches. Demonstrate what’s possible through pilot-scale initiatives by conducting projects at Superfund sites, military facilities, wastewater treatment plants, and drinking water systems that will test performance under real conditions, lower technical risk, and show communities what PFAS cleanup options are practical and scalable. Translate progress into practical actions by creating user-friendly guidance, launching the Break the Bond Navigator, sharing updated technology information, and helping water systems access funding and technical assistance. “Partnerships are the key to unlocking innovation and next-generation technologies. To that end, EPA’s Office of Water is actively pursuing public-private partnerships to promote research, development, and scalable water treatment technologies for PFAS removal,” said EPA PFAS Lead and Assistant Administrator for the Office of Water Jess Kramer. “These partnerships will accelerate technology breakthroughs to reduce PFAS in water while also reducing the cost of treatment to save money.” In addition to developing partnerships, EPA intends to issue grant funding for research related to the destruction of PFAS. For example, funding will be available under the Science to Achieve Results (STAR) grant program and Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) grant program. "EPA is prioritizing research and development on PFAS and ensuring our science is gold standard and directly applicable to needs in local communities as they work to address PFAS pollution,” said Teresa Booeshaghi, Associate Administrator for the Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions. “One such study is conducting full scale pilot tests to optimize the performance of drinking water treatment methods being deployed all over the country.” To catalyze the development and use of new technologies for treatment of

Secretaries Wright, Burgum Join JERA and U.S. LNG Producers to Finalize Agreements Expected to Add over $200 Billion to U.S. GDP Secretary Wright and Secretary Burgum, vice-chair and chair of the National Energy Dominance Council respectively, announce the finalization of four 20-year agreements to purchase 5.5 million tons per year of American LNG. Energy.gov June 11, 2025 Estimated Read Time min WASHINGTON — U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright and Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum, vice-chair and chair of the National Energy Dominance Council (NEDC) respectively, today joined Yukio Kani, global CEO and chairman of JERA Co., Inc. and representatives from several U.S. LNG producers to announce the finalization of four 20-year agreements between JERA and U.S. companies to purchase up to 5.5 million tons per year of American LNG. The agreements, which are projected to support more than 50,000 U.S. jobs and add more than $200 billion to U.S. GDP according to S&P Global analysis, underscore President Trump’s efforts to unleash American LNG production and the significant role the U.S. LNG industry plays in strengthening the U.S. economy and bolstering global energy security. The agreements include sales and purchase agreements with NextDecade Corporation and Commonwealth LNG, and heads of agreements with Sempra Infrastructure and Cheniere Marketing LLC, to purchase LNG from America’s Gulf Coast. The announcement is yet another major milestone for President Trump’s commitment to increase investment in the U.S. and unleash American dominance. “Today’s announcement of investments in American energy that will unlock nearly a quarter trillion dollars in U.S. GDP is a massive milestone and a bold demonstration of President Trump’s leadership,” said Secretary Wright . “More than 50,000 jobs, tens of billions of dollars in new LNG export infrastructure, and a more secure energy future is just around the corner because we have a President who prioritizes our nation’s prosperity and energy security. This is another powerful example of the growth of the U.S. LNG export industry over the past decade, which is a boon to our allies around the world who seek to expand trade with the U.S. while supporting their own energy security.” “This investment is a message to the world that American LNG is back thanks to President Trump and we’re leading on the world stage,” said Secretary Burgum . “I am proud to join Secretary Wright and JERA CEO Yukio Kani to celebrate this commitment that will bring in almost a quarter trillion dollars to our nation’s economy and support over 50,000 American jobs for our country’s LNG industry. America is no longer begging for foreign energy – we’re producing it cleaner, smarter, better, and more reliably than the rest of the world.” “Today represents a true win-win and we want to thank President Trump for his leadership and commitment to unleash American energy – both of which were essential to completing these Agreements,” said Yukio Kani , Global CEO and Chairman of JERA Co., Inc. “They reflect a strong commercial partnership between the U.S. and Japan, strengthen Japan’s energy security and reaffirm the U.S.’s leading role in the global LNG market. We look forward to continuing our work with the President, Secretaries Burgum and Wright, and their teams, in partnership with the Government of Japan and the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, on shared energy goals moving forward.” BACKGROUND: President Trump and Secretary Wright have been hard at work to expand U.S.

pages.text: Información sobre el Foro Nacional de Impuestos del IRS | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Información sobre el Foro Nacional de Impuestos del IRS English Español Más en Profesionales de impuestos Agentes inscritos (en inglés) Participantes del Programa anual de la temporada de presentación de impuestos Agentes inscritos de los planes de ahorros para la jubilación (en inglés) Organizaciones Certificadas de Empleadores Profesionales (CPEO, por sus siglas en inglés) (en inglés) Centro informativo sobre el crédito tributario por ingreso del trabajo (EITC, por sus siglas en inglés) (en inglés) Actuarios inscritos (en inglés) Proveedores de presentación electrónica (en inglés) Presentación electrónica modernizada (en inglés) ¿Qué es el Foro Nacional de Impuestos del IRS? El Foro Nacional de Impuestos del IRS es el principal evento de divulgación del IRS para la comunidad de profesionales de impuestos. Cada uno de los cinco foros del IRS es un evento de tres días que brinda a los profesionales de impuestos la información más reciente sobre asuntos tributarios federales y estatales presentados por expertos del IRS y sus organizaciones asociadas a través de una variedad de seminarios y talleres de capacitación. Además de los seminarios, los foros también cuentan con una sala de exposiciones de dos días, programas especiales y más. Fechas del programa de 2026 e información de inscripción La inscripción para el Foro Nacional de Impuestos del IRS (en inglés) 2026 ya está abierta. Ubicaciones y fechas de 2026 Ciudad, estado Ubicación Fechas Chicago, IL Hyatt Regency Chicago 7 al 9 de julio de 2026 New Orleans, LA Hyatt Regency New Orleans 4 al 6 de agosto de 2026 New York, NY New York Hilton Midtown 18 al 20 de agosto de 2026 Orlando, FL Caribe Royale Orlando 1 al 3 de septiembre de 2026 San Diego, CA Town and Country Resort 15 al 17 de septiembre de 2026 Aspectos destacados del Foro Educación continua Los seminarios del Foro Nacional de Impuestos del IRS brindan créditos de educación continua (CE, por sus siglas en inglés) para agentes registrados (EA, por sus siglas en inglés), contadores públicos autorizados (CPA, por sus siglas en inglés), participantes del Programa de la temporada de presentación anual (AFSP, por sus siglas en inglés) y participantes del Consejo de Educación Tributaria de California (CTEC, por sus siglas en inglés). Los asistentes deben comprender y cumplir con los requisitos de la CE de su agencia de licencias correspondiente. Para recibir un crédito de CE se requiere la asistencia a la presentación por la totalidad de 50 minutos. Para el 2026, una selección de seminarios se ofrecerá durante dos sesiones consecutivas (100 minutos). Parta estos seminarios, se requiere asistir a los 100 minutos completos de la presentación para recibir los dos créditos de CE disponibles para esa sesión extendida. Sala de resolución de casos El programa de resolución de casos del TAS (Servicio del Defensor del Contribuyente) ofrece asistencia personalizada, disponible en persona solo con cita previa, para ayudarle con su caso más difícil relacionado con un asunto tributario del IRS. Representantes del IRS y del TAS con experiencia especializada estarán presentes para una conversación individual, realizar una investigación profunda de su caso e intentar de resolver rápidamente su asunto tributario. Sala de exposiciones del Foro Nacional de Impuestos (NTF, por sus siglas en inglés) Docenas de expositores muestran una amplia selección de productos y servicios que pueden ayudar a mejorar sus operaciones comerciales. El horario de la sala de exposiciones NTF es el martes de 11 a.m. a 6 p.m. y el miércoles de 10 a.m. a 2:30 p.m. Oportunidades de “networking” (interconexión) ¡Disfrute de buena comida y excelente compañía! pages.title: US officials say flight stoppage stemmed from ‘routine maintenance’ as travel chaos continues | Air transport | The Guardian
pages.description: Thousands of flights still canceled as officials blamed ageing air control system for nationwide grounding
pages.text: US officials say flight stoppage stemmed from ‘routine maintenance’ as travel chaos continues | Air transport | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Passengers wait to retrieve luggage from canceled flights at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Virginia, on 13 November 2026. Photograph: Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA View image in fullscreen Passengers wait to retrieve luggage from canceled flights at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Virginia, on 13 November 2026. Photograph: Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA Air transport US officials say flight stoppage stemmed from ‘routine maintenance’ as travel chaos continues Thousands of flights still canceled as officials blamed ageing air control system for nationwide grounding Anna Betts Sat 14 Nov 2026 12.11 EST First published on Sat 14 Nov 2026 10.03 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The Trump administration says Friday’s four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that delayed or canceled thousands of flight stemmed from routine maintenance. At a news briefing on Saturday, the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, said that the issues began when a contractor was performing “routine maintenance” at a remote FAA facility to “switch telecommunications lines” from copper wire to fiber optic cable. “What we’re working to determine is whether we had incompetence,” Duffy said, “or did they install a faulty router.” He added: “Once we were able to isolate the work that was being done at this remote location, all of our systems came back online,” and the ground stop was lifted. However, travel chaos continued across the US on Saturday. At the briefing, the FAA’s head, Bryan Bedford, apologized to passengers and said he believed that the worst of the disruption “is behind us”. “We will still have delays and cancellations today, but that will set us up for a full recovery tomorrow,” Bedford said. “Based on everything that we’re hearing from our airline partners, they believe that they’ll be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday.” “I want to reiterate: we see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related,” he continued. “So we want to be clear that we have a equipment issue, and we’re working through what this defective piece of equipment was.” Later on Saturday, L3Harris, the federal contractor that Duffy said had been updating air traffic control equipment before the ground stop, released a statement saying that it took the ground stop and its negative effects “on travelers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously”. The contractor said that it had completed more than 70% of the planned airspace communications conversion from legacy copper wires to a fiber optic system. “We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the [Friday] ground stop of our nation’s air travel,” the contractor said. On Saturday,airlines worked to recover from Friday’s four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that delayed or canceled thousands of flights. By of 11am ET on Saturday morning, more than 4,000 flights within, into or out of the US had already been canceled, according to FlightAware , adding to the more than 8,000 cancellations recorded on Friday. The disruption, which marked the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years, left passengers stranded at airports across the country and facing uncertainty about when they could reach their destinations. pages.description: Buenas estrategias de higiene, como lavarse las manos, puede ayudar a reducir su riesgo de presentar enfermedades respiratorias.

La higiene y prevención de virus respiratorios 18 de ago. del 2025 English (US) Lo que debe saber La higiene es un hábito o una práctica regular que mejora la limpieza. Practicar una buena higiene es una estrategia de prevención principal recomendada para todos para disminuir los riesgos de presentar enfermedades respiratorias. Recomendación Practique una buena higiene al cubrirse la nariz y la boca al toser y estornudar, lavarse o desinfectarse las manos con frecuencia, y limpiar las superficies que se tocan frecuentemente. Cómo funciona Cubrirse la nariz y la boca al toser y estornudar limita la propagación de microbios para proteger a los demás. Lavarse las manos con jabón elimina los microbios de las manos, lo que hace que sea menos probable que infecten el sistema respiratorio cuando se toca los ojos, la nariz o la boca. Si no hay agua y jabón disponibles, usar un desinfectante de manos con al menos un 60 por ciento de alcohol puede matar estos microbios. Para eliminar los microbios y la suciedad de las superficies, use limpiadores de uso doméstico que contengan jabón o detergente. Medidas que puede tomar Cubrirse la nariz y la boca con un pañuelo desechable al toser o estornudar . Botar los pañuelos desechables usados a la basura. Si no tiene un pañuelo desechable, cúbrase la nariz y la boca cuando tosa o estornude con la parte interior del codo, no con las manos. Aprender y usar la técnica correcta para lavarse las manos . Enseñarles a los niños la forma correcta de lavarse las manos. Limpiar de manera regular las superficies que se tocan frecuentemente, como los mesones, las barandas y las manijas de las puertas. Medidas que pueden tomar las organizaciones Imprimir afiches gratuitos y colocarlos en áreas muy visibles. Asegurarse de que los establecimientos estén equipados con jabón, agua y una forma de secarse las manos (por ejemplo, toallas de papel o secadores de manos). Colocar dispensadores de desinfectante de manos con al menos un 60 por ciento de alcohol cerca de las superficies que se tocan frecuentemente y en las áreas donde no se pueda acceder fácilmente a agua y jabón, como cerca de los ascensores, los equipos compartidos, y las entradas y salidas de los edificios. Limpiar de manera regular las superficies que se tocan frecuentemente, como los mesones, las barandas y las manijas de las puertas. Aviso Los CDC ofrecen directrices separadas y específicas para entornos de atención médica ( COVID-19 , influenza , y prevención y control de infecciones en general ). Las leyes federales de derechos civiles podrían requerir modificaciones razonables o adaptaciones razonables en distintas circunstancias. Nada de lo incluido en estas directrices tiene como objetivo restarle valor a esas leyes o remplazarlas. Aviso Los enlaces a sitios web pueden llevar a páginas en inglés o español. pages.text: Trump EPA Celebrates One Year of the Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions with 100 Gold Standard Science Wins | US EPA Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Trump EPA Celebrates One Year of the Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions with 100 Gold Standard Science Wins In Just One Year, OASES Turned Rigorous Science into Action to Combat PFAS Contamination, Make Sound Policy Decisions, Support American Businesses, and More October 20, 2026 Contact Information EPA Press Office ( press@epa.gov ) WASHINGTON — This week, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) marks the one-year anniversary of the Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions (OASES), celebrating the agency's historic structural modernization to better integrate science into agency actions and meet our statutory obligations. One year ago, EPA finalized a comprehensive set of organizational improvements that refocused its work on the agency’s core mission of providing clean air, land, and water for communities across the nation. These cross-agency shifts are expected to deliver more than $300 million annually for the American people. OASES has driven a pivotal transformation in how scientific research is conducted and applied within EPA. Since its inception, OASES has prioritized practical, solution-oriented projects that align directly with the immediate needs, goals, and requirements of EPA program and regional offices to respond effectively to emerging issues and regulatory needs. Over the past year, this structural alignment has allowed the agency to center its scientific enterprise on real-world solutions that protect human health and the environment while continuing to safely advance the American economy. “OASES’s actionable commitment to gold standard science is a foundation of our ongoing efforts to build a more efficient agency. Every day, Americans can see the real-world impact that this office has on their lives,” said EPA Deputy Administrator David Fotouhi. “Over the past year, this office energized our EPA labs across the country, produced cutting-edge science, and gave our state partners and stakeholders the technical assistance they need to help us grow our nation’s economy while ensuring that all Americans have clean air, clean water, and clean land.” Here are 100 gold standard science actions OASES has taken since October 2025: Completed groundbreaking work on PFAS emissions and destruction, providing the first demonstration that a municipal waste combustor may effectively destroy PFAS in municipal solid waste and directly supporting EPA’s PFAS disposal and destruction guidance. Used geospatial intelligence tools and Super Intelligence (SI) image processing tools from the Environmental Photographic Interpretation Center to review and analyze imagery focused on transboundary flow events of untreated wastewater, trash, and sediment into the Tijuana River watershed and Pacific Ocean. Operationalized a new lead service line identification test bed at the Edison, New Jersey laboratory to improve minimally invasive methods for locating and classifying lead service lines in communities, enabling utilities to make decisions on service line replacement. DOE Finalizes 2024 LNG Export Study, Paving Way for Stronger American Energy Exports The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today released its Response to Comments on the 2024 LNG Export Study, marking a critical step toward returning to regular order on liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports. Energy.gov May 19, 2025 Estimated Read Time min WASHINGTON— The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today released its Response to Comments on the 2024 LNG Export Study, marking a critical step toward returning to regular order on liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports. With this action, DOE has completed the final hurdles left over from the Biden administration’s reckless pause on LNG export permits, paving the way for the Trump Administration to fully unleash American LNG exports. “President Trump was given a mandate to unleash American energy dominance, and that includes U.S. LNG exports,” U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said. “The facts are clear: expanding America’s LNG exports is good for Americans and good for the world. Today, the Department of Energy is following the facts, closing the door on the Biden administration’s failed policies, and putting America’s energy future on stronger footing.” “The 2024 Study confirms what our nation always knew—LNG supports our economy, strengthens our allies, and enhances national security. Biden’s opposition defied reason and reality and hurt American progress. We are pleased to issue the Response to Comments on the 2024 LNG Export Study, which will allow DOE to close out this chapter and fully return to regular order on LNG exports,” said Tala Goudarzi, Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management . The 2024 LNG Study was released at the end of the Biden administration in December 2024 and had a public comment period through March 20 th of this year. Based on the record evidence from the 2024 LNG Export Study and the public comments received, DOE makes several key findings, including: the United States has a robust natural gas supply that is sufficient to meet growing levels of exports while minimizing impacts to domestic prices; growing LNG exports increases our gross domestic product and expands jobs while improving our trade balance; and increasing U.S. LNG exports enhances domestic and international global security with no discernable impact to global greenhouse gas emissions. In sum, DOE concludes that the complete record from the 2024 LNG Export Study, inclusive of the Study, the comments received, and this Response to Comments, supports the proposition that exports of LNG from the United States are in the best interest of the American public. With the public comments to the 2024 LNG Export Study now addressed, DOE will proceed with issuing final orders on pending applications to export U.S.-sourced natural gas as LNG to non-free trade agreement countries. A Notice of Availability of the Response to Comments will be published in the Federal Register in the coming days. In the meantime, the Response to Comments is available on DOE’s website here . ### View Next Press Release Energy Secretary Chris Wright Delivers Keynote Remarks on Completion of First B61-13 Production Unit at Pantex Plant May 19, 2025 View Previous Press Release Energy Department Announces Emergency Actions to Provide Overdue Relief to Puerto Rico Power Grid May 16, 2025 Media Inquiries: (202) 586-4940 or DOENews@hq.doe.gov Read more at the energy.gov Newsroom

pages.text: What to know about the rare nationwide ground stop issued by the FAA | Air transport | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Passengers look at departures and arrivals boards at Boston Logan international airport after the FAA issued a national ground stop ‘due to extraordinary circumstances and reasons for safety’ following the agency's earlier report of serious air traffic control communications issues. Photograph: Brian Snyder/Reuters View image in fullscreen Passengers look at departures and arrivals boards at Boston Logan international airport after the FAA issued a national ground stop ‘due to extraordinary circumstances and reasons for safety’ following the agency's earlier report of serious air traffic control communications issues. Photograph: Brian Snyder/Reuters Air transport Explainer What to know about the rare nationwide ground stop issued by the FAA The Federal Aviation Administration issued a ground stop for all planes due to take off in the US, delaying and canceling thousands of flights Robert Mackey Fri 13 Nov 2026 18.56 EST Last modified on Sat 14 Nov 2026 15.14 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The nationwide disruption to air travel in the United States began with a “ground stop” order issued by the US Federal ⁠Aviation Administration at 3:53pm ET on Friday due to “communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers”, the agency said . The order remained in effect, halting departures from all US airports and delaying landings, for more than four hours. Here is what we know about the rare nationwide ground stop issued by the FAA. Nationwide FAA ground stop: nearly 11,000 flights delayed or canceled at airports across the US Read more 1. What caused this? After the FAA lifted the ground stop at 8.15pm ET Friday, Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, and Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, appeared to suggest that the cause of Friday’s outage was that older technology became overwhelmed with data after new technology was introduced. The FAA announced three days ago that a new air traffic management tool, known as Smart, had been activated at all 22 air route traffic control centers in the US, but Duffy denied that the new system caused the outage. At a briefing on Saturday, Duffy said that the outage began after “a contractor was doing routine maintenance to switch telecommunication lines from old copper wire … to fiber” and a newly installed router “started flooding other routers in our air traffic control system”. The FAA, he said, was still working to determine whether the fault was “incompetence” by the contractor, or “a faulty router”. 2. How did the old technology cause this? In an initial briefing on Friday night, Mullin seemed to suggest that Duffy’s Department of Transportation was to blame, saying: “As secretary Duffy and FAA was going in and putting patches into the system, they were putting new equipment and new technology, and that new equipment, new technology, just wasn’t – it was overwhelming the older system, which is why secretary Duffy made it very clear the patchwork doesn’t work. We need one complete system. We need someone to come in and build the whole system. Doing it nickel-and-dime-ing it together does not work. This is what happens when that takes place. ” But Duffy denied that the new Smart system, which incorporates artificial intelligence and was rolled out this week, had caused the problem, pointing on Saturday to problems with the installation of new equipment. 3. How do we know this wasn’t a cyber-attack? Mullin said at the briefing on Friday: “We’ve seen zero evidence that this was a cyber-attack.” “Now, when we start looking at cyber threats, cyber-attacks, typically some people are going to raise their hand up and say: ‘Hey, we did that.’ There’s no chatter. Section 5333(b) Annual Certifications Public Transit Employee Protections 49 U.S.C. § 5333(b) The Law - 49 U.S.C. § 5333(b) The Guidelines - 29 CFR § 215 Protective Arrangements Unified Protective Arrangement - Updated January 3, 2011 Special Warranty - Updated January 3, 2011 Section 5311 Certification Process Information Section 5311 Grant Notifications Nonunion Protective Arrangement - Updated July 8, 2024 National (“Model”) Agreement - July 23, 1975 OLMS Transit Employee Protection Decisions Glossary For Transit Employee Protection Assistance: E-mail OLMS-Transit@dol.gov or call (202) 693-0123 OVERVIEW When federal funds are used to acquire, improve, or operate a mass transit system (public transportation), federal law requires arrangements to protect the interests of mass transit employees. 49 U.S.C. § 5333(b) (formerly Section 13(c) of the Urban Mass Transportation Act). Section 5333(b) specifies that these protective arrangements must provide for the preservation of rights and benefits of employees under existing collective bargaining agreements, the continuation of collective bargaining rights, the protection of individual employees against a worsening of their positions in relation to their employment, assurances of employment to employees of acquired transit systems, priority of reemployment, and paid training or retraining programs. 49 U.S.C. § 5333(b)(2). The Department of Labor (DOL) must certify that protective arrangements are in place and meet the above requirements for all grants of assistance under of the Federal Transit Law before the Department of Transportation’s Federal Transit Administration (FTA) can release funds. The FTA includes the terms and conditions of the certification and protective arrangements in its contract of assistance with the grant recipient. There is no basis for a waiver or exemption from the requirements of section 5333(b). A protective arrangement is not a collective bargaining agreement and does not create a collective bargaining relationship where one does not already exist. For further information on Mass Transit Employee Protections, see the sections below or contact OLMS at (202) 693-0123 or OLMS-Transit@dol.gov . Also, visit the transit employee protections decisions page to view landmark certifications and claims decisions. DOL’S PROCEDURES FOR CERTIFICATION OF PROTECTIVE ARRANGEMENTS ( 29 CFR § 215 ) Pursuant to its Procedural Guidelines, 29 CFR § 215, DOL refers the grant application and the proposed terms and conditions to: the recipient and any subrecipients of the funding, and any unions representing employees of the grantee, its contractors, and/or other service area providers. When protective arrangements have been previously negotiated and agreed to by the transit employees' union and the grant applicant, and the arrangements continue to meet the requirements of 5333(b), the Department will refer on the basis the previously certified protective arrangements. If there are no previous or existing arrangements that may be applied to the pending grant, DOL proposes to apply the terms and conditions of the January 3, 2011 Unified Protective Arrangement (UPA) 29 CFR § 215.3(b)(1) and (2). DOL may certify term and conditions without referral if the grant application falls under one of the following exceptions: 1) neither the grant recipient’s employees, nor those of any other transit provider in the service area are represented by a union, (in which case the Act’s protections are contained in a " Nonunion Protective Arrangement " developed by DOL); 2) the grant specifies that is only for routine repl

Estas medidas pueden ayudar a reducir el riesgo de infectar a personas que tienen mayor riesgo de enfermarse gravemente. Recomendación Si podría tener un virus respiratorio.... ‎ Quédese en casa y lejos de los demás (incluidas las personas con las que vive que no están enfermas) si tiene síntomas de un virus respiratorio que no se puedan explicar mejor con otra causa. Estos síntomas pueden incluir fiebre, escalofríos, fatiga, tos, moqueo y dolor de cabeza.* Puede retomar sus actividades habituales cuando, por al menos 24 horas, se cumplan estos dos criterios: Sus síntomas mejoran en general, y No ha tenido fiebre (sin estar tomando medicamentos antifebriles). Cuando regrese a sus actividades habituales, tome precauciones adicionales durante los 5 días siguientes, como tomar medidas para tener aire limpio , practicar buena higiene , ponerse una mascarilla que se ajuste bien a la cara , mantener distanciamiento físico o hacerse una prueba de detección para los momentos en los que estará alrededor de otras personas. Tomar precauciones es especialmente importante para proteger a las personas con factores que aumenten su riesgo de enfermarse gravemente a causa de virus respiratorios. Tenga en cuenta que aún podría propagar el virus que lo enfermó, incluso si se está sintiendo mejor. Es probable que sea menos contagioso después de que sus síntomas se resuelvan por completo, pero algunas personas, como aquellas con condiciones médicas que deprimen el sistema inmunitario, pueden excretar el virus por un largo tiempo. Si empieza a tener fiebre o a sentirse peor después de haber vuelto a sus actividades habituales, quédese de nuevo en casa y lejos de los demás. Si sus síntomas están mejorando en general, y no ha tenido fiebre ni tomado medicamentos para reducirla por al menos 24 horas, puede retomar sus actividades habituales de nuevo. Debería luego tomar precauciones adicionales durante los 5 días siguientes como se mencionó previamente. *Los síntomas podrían incluir, entre otros, molestia en el pecho, escalofríos, tos, apetito reducido, diarrea, fatiga (cansancio), fiebre o sentirse afiebrado, dolor de cabeza, en los músculos o en el cuerpo, pérdida reciente del gusto o del olfato, moqueo o congestión nasal, estornudos, dolor de garganta, vómitos, debilidad, sibilancias. Cómo funciona Cuando tiene una infección por un virus respiratorio, puede propagarla a otras personas. Por cuánto tiempo alguien puede propagar el virus depende de distintos factores, como qué tan enfermo está (gravedad), las condiciones médicas subyacentes (como tener el sistema inmunitario debilitado) y cuánto dura la enfermedad (duración). Esto no es igual para todas las personas. Cuando sus síntomas estén mejorando en general y no haya tenido fiebre (sin estar tomando medicamentos para reducirla) por al menos 24 horas, en general es menos contagioso, pero aun así le va a tomar más tiempo a su cuerpo deshacerse por completo del virus. Durante este tiempo, podría aún propagarle el virus a otras personas. Tomar precauciones por los 5 días siguientes puede ayudar a reducir el riesgo.
