pages.title: Lockerbie bombing accused Abu Agila Mas'ud al-Marimi loses bid to have case thrown out British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Abu Agila Mas'ud al-Marimi had claimed he was victim of an illegal rendition when he was transferred into US custody.
pages.text: Lockerbie bombing accused Abu Agila Mas'ud al-Marimi loses bid to have case thrown out Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Lockerbie bombing accused loses bid to have case thrown out 22 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google David Cowan Scotland home affairs correspondent Reuters Abu Agila Mas'ud Kheir Al-Marimi has been in custody since December 2022 A Libyan man accused of building the bomb that brought down an American airliner over Lockerbie nearly 38 years ago has lost his bid to have the case thrown out of court. Abu Agila Mas'ud al-Marimi had claimed he was the victim of an illegal rendition when he was transferred into US custody from Libya in 2022. A US district court judge has ruled that the manner of his removal should not prevent his trial going ahead in Washington in January. Marimi has denied playing a key role in the attack on Pan Am 103, which killed 270 people on 21 December 1988. Reuters Hundreds of people died when Pan Am Flight 103 exploded over Lockerbie in December 1988 His attempt to have the case dismissed was made public through documents lodged with the court in Washington. Marimi's lawyers said he was violently abducted from his home in Tripoli in 2022 by armed members of a militia, "in a cloak and dagger operation conducted in the middle of the night". They alleged that weeks later, after being held without access to lawyers in a detention centre, he was handed over to FBI agents at an airport in Misrata and flown to the United States. Marimi argued the case should be dismissed because the United States had invaded his constitutional rights and violated extradition agreements between the US and Libya. Court transcripts obtained by BBC Scotland News have revealed that trial judge Dabney Friedrich rejected the defence motion. She referred to a longstanding American legal doctrine, which stipulates that a court's right to hold a trial is not impaired if the suspect has been the subject of a forceful abduction. "This rule rests on the principle that due process of law is satisfied when one present in court is convicted of a crime after a fair trial and in accordance with constitutional procedural safeguards," said the judge. "Put differently, there's nothing in the Constitution that requires a court to permit a guilty person rightfully convicted to escape justice because he was brought to trial against his will." In her ruling, the judge said there were two exceptions to that doctrine. One would apply if Marimi had been brought before the court through the US government's "deliberate, unnecessary and unreasonable invasion" of his constitutional rights. For that exception to be triggered, the challenged conduct had to be carried out by, or at the direction of, US officials. The judge said Marimi's allegations "at best suggest that US government officials exerted pressure on Libyan officials to facilitate a rendition, not that US government officials directed or controlled the challenged conduct." The second exception to the doctrine would apply if the US government had violated an extradition agreement which was the only way a suspect could be transferred between the two countries. The judge said the US government had invoked two conventions to secure Marimi's appearance in a US court. "Neither the Montreal Convention nor the Terrorists Bombing Convention provides that it is the only way by which one country may gain custody of a national of another country for the purposes of prosecution," she said. "Accordingly, Libya was free to transfer Mr Al-Marimi to the United States using any method it chose." The defence and prosecution have fought a series of legal battles in the approach to Marimi's trial, which is now scheduled to get underway on 19 January after three postponements. pages.description: The Bureau of Land Management leased 20 parcels totaling 3,388 acres in Montana and North Dakota for $21,339,550 in total receipts during a quarterly oil and gas lease sale.
pages.text: BLM Oil and Gas Lease Sale in Montana and North Dakota Generates Over $21 Million in Revenue | Bureau of Land Management Skip to main navigation Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Press Releases BLM Oil and Gas Lease Sale in Montana and North Dakota Generates Over $21 Million in Revenue Organization: Bureau of Land Management BLM Office: Montana/Dakotas State Office Media Contact: BLM Montana Communications blm_mt_newsroom@blm.gov Oct 27, 2026 BLM photo BILLINGS, Mont. – The Bureau of Land Management leased 20 parcels totaling 3,388 acres in Montana and North Dakota for $21,339,550 in total receipts during a quarterly oil and gas lease sale. Combined lease bonus bids and rentals are distributed between the federal government and state where parcels are located. This lease sale was conducted under the Working Families Tax Cut Act , which resets the royalty rate for new federal onshore oil and gas production to a minimum of 12.5%, reversing the 16.67% rate set by the Inflation Reduction Act. By lowering the federal onshore royalty rate from 16.67% to 12.5%, the Working Families Tax Cut Act, also known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, reduces the cost of doing business on public lands, making oil and gas development more economically attractive to industry. This is expected to spur additional leasing and drilling activity, which in turn supports increased domestic energy production and strengthens U.S. energy security. Oil and gas lease sales support domestic energy production and American energy independence, while contributing to the nation’s economic and military security. Consistent with Executive Order 14154 , “Unleashing American Energy,” the BLM's lease sales help meet the energy needs of U.S. citizens and solidify the nation as a global energy leader long into the future. Leasing is the first step in the process to develop federal oil and gas resources. The BLM ensures oil and gas development meets the requirements set forth by the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 and other applicable legal authorities. Oil and gas leases are awarded for a term of 10 years and as long thereafter as there is production of oil and gas in paying quantities. Information on current and upcoming BLM leases is available through the National Fluid Lease Sale System . BLM lease sales are held online through Efficient Markets . Results are available on the National Fluid Lease Sale System . After navigating to the page, filter to the sale, and select the action “View Sale Documents” to view the sale results. The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.

Comparta información sensible sólo en sitios web oficiales y seguros. 21 mayo del 2024 English (US) Pruebas de diabetes Puntos clave Necesitará una prueba de azúcar en la sangre para averiguar si tiene prediabetes o diabetes. La prueba es sencilla y, por lo general, los resultados estarán disponibles rápidamente. Por qué hacerse la prueba La prediabetes y la diabetes tipo 2 generalmente no presentan ningún síntoma . (La diabetes tipo 1 es distinta; los síntomas pueden presentarse rápidamente y pueden ser graves). Es por eso que se insta a las personas con algún factor de riesgo a que le pregunten a su médico si deberían ser evaluadas. Ser evaluado significa hacerse la prueba cuando no tiene ningún síntoma. Detectar la prediabetes a tiempo puede ayudar a las personas a prevenir o retrasar la diabetes tipo 2. Descubrir si tienen diabetes tipo 2, y tomar medidas, puede ayudar a las personas a prevenir o retrasar complicaciones de salud graves. Hacerse la prueba es simple y rápido. Le sacarán una muestra de sangre en el consultorio o en un centro médico para que puedan medir el nivel de azúcar en ella. Por lo general, los resultados están disponibles rápidamente. Seguir leyendo: Factores de riesgo de la diabetes Cuándo hacerse la prueba Diabetes tipo 2 o prediabetes Consulte a su médico sobre hacerse la prueba de prediabetes o diabetes tipo 2 si tiene alguno de los factores de riesgo. Si le hicieron una prueba de azúcar en la sangre en una feria de salud o farmacia, haga un seguimiento con su médico. Su médico podría querer hacerle la prueba otra vez para asegurarse de que los resultados sean precisos. Diabetes tipo 1 Si su médico piensa que usted tiene diabetes tipo 1, puede que también le haga una prueba de sangre para la detección de anticuerpos autoinmunitarios. Estas sustancias muestran que su cuerpo se está atacando a sí mismo y a menudo se encuentran en las personas con diabetes tipo 1, pero no las que tienen diabetes tipo 2. Puede que le hagan una prueba de orina para la detección de cetonas. Se producen cetonas cuando su cuerpo quema grasa para obtener energía. Tener cetonas en la orina indica que tiene diabetes tipo 1 y no diabetes tipo 2. Diabetes gestacional La diabetes gestacional generalmente aparece alrededor de la semana 24 del embarazo. Probablemente le harán la prueba entre la semana 24 y 28. Si tiene mayor riesgo de presentar diabetes gestacional, el médico podría hacerle la prueba antes. Si sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre son más altos de lo normal durante el inicio de su embarazo, puede que no tenga diabetes gestacional. En su lugar, puede que tenga diabetes tipo 1 o tipo 2. Tipos de pruebas Pruebas para la diabetes tipo 1, diabetes tipo 2, prediabetes y diabetes gestacional Prueba de A1c La prueba de A1c mide sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre promedio durante los últimos 2 o 3 meses. Normal : menos de 5.7 % Prediabetes : 5.7-6.4 % Diabetes : 6.5 % o mayor Prueba de azúcar en la sangre en ayunas Esta prueba mide sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre después de ayunar (no comer) toda la noche. Normal : 99 mg/dL o menor Prediabetes : 100-125 mg/dL Diabetes : 126 mg/dL o mayor Prueba de tolerancia a la glucosa Esta prueba mide sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre antes y después de beber un líquido que contiene glucosa. Tendrá que ayunar (no comer) la noche anterior a la prueba y le extraerán sangre para medir sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre en ayunas. Luego, beberá el líquido y se le revisarán sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre. Estas revisiones generalmente suceden 1 hora, 2 horas y posiblemente 3

pages.title: Austrian and Swiss women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: The Swiss government told the BBC that the freed national was on her way back to Switzerland.
pages.text: Austrian and Swiss women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Two European women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya 22 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Basillioh Rukanga and Makuochi Okafor , BBC Africa Christoph Greztmacher Eva Greztmacher, 76, had spent many years in Niger as an aid worker Two women - a Swiss and an Austrian – have been freed after more than a year in captivity in Niger and handed over to authorities in the Libyan city of Benghazi. Austrian national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss Claudia Abbt, 69, were kidnapped separately in the northern Nigerien city of Agadez in January and April last year. No details have been given about who was holding them or their demands, although some reports have previously linked the kidnapping to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of their release were not disclosed. The Austrian and Swiss governments have both confirmed the release of their citizens. The Swiss government said Abbt was free and on her way back to Switzerland, while Austria said Gretzmacher had been released after "intensive diplomatic efforts". "We are all very relieved that Eva G. is free again after more than 21 months... For many months, we worked closely, discreetly, and in a spirit of trust with our regional, European, and international partners. These joint efforts have paid off," Foreign Minister Beate Meinl-Reisinger said in a statement. Kidnapping of foreigners soars in Africa's lawless Sahel region The Swiss foreign ministry said the country's federal administration officials had met Abbt in Benghazi and she had received medical care. "She is doing well under the circumstances and is currently on her way back to Switzerland," it added. Federal Councillor Ignazio Cassis thanked those involved in Abbt's release, adding that he was "relieved that [she] is free again after more than a year and a half". The government said it had established a task force - including the foreign affairs department, police and other agencies - after the kidnapping became known. It added that Switzerland had maintained regular contact with Austria from the outset. Earlier, Libyan officials were reported as saying the women would be handed over to authorities in their respective countries after necessary procedures were completed. Libya's al-Masar TV showed the two women entering what looks like an ambulance and later being attended to by a health worker. Speaking in French, the women thanked Khalifa Haftar, military commander of eastern Libya, and his son, Saddam Haftar, for their release. Gretzmacher was an aid worker who had lived for many years in Niger, while Abbt had spent several years living and working as a community worker in Agadez. A plane was expected to leave Benghazi on Thursday, first stopping in Vienna to transfer Gretzmacher to Austrian authorities before continuing to Switzerland with Abbt, privately owned Air Info Agadez news outlet reported. Libya has struggled to recover from the chaos that followed the 2011 Nato-backed uprising that toppled long-time ruler Muammar Gaddafi. It is split between two administrations - one in the east backed by Haftar, and the other in the west in the capital Tripoli, led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah. Under Gaddafi, many ethnic Tuaregs from Mali and Niger were recruited to join armed groups loyal to him in Libya. After he was killed, many went home. Analysts say this has been a major factor in the spread of instability in the Sahel region. Niger and its neighbours have faced years of jihadist violence, including kidnappings and deadly attacks, carried out by different groups linked to al-Qaeda and Islamic State. The country has been under military control since 2023 when Gen Abdourahmane Tchiani deposed the country's elected President, Mohamed

pages.description: On Bureau of Land Management public lands in central Montana, two newly installed wildlife-tracking towers are already helping researchers uncover the hidden movements of bats across the continent.

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Tracking Bats Across Big Skies: BLM Lands Help Expand Montana’s Motus Network Oct 28, 2026 On Bureau of Land Management public lands in central Montana, two newly installed wildlife-tracking towers are already helping researchers uncover the hidden movements of bats across the continent. “As a species, bats play an important role in our environment by controlling insect populations that may otherwise harm crops and forests, and transmit diseases,” said Rebecca Newton, wildlife program lead for the BLM Montana/Dakotas . “Currently, many bat species across the country are threatened by a fatal disease called White-Nose Syndrome. Because of their nocturnal behavior, small size, and roost preferences, bats are challenging to study – and challenging to help in the case of WNS. The more we can do help state wildlife managers ensure the survival of this important and beneficial animal, the better off we will be.” BLM Montana/Dakotas staff approved installation of Motus towers on BLM lands as part of a broader effort by Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks to build a statewide network of automated telemetry stations that detect and collect data on flying wildlife in their proximity. The most-recently installed towers were placed in the Upper Missouri River Breaks National Monument during late-summer: one in the Bullwhacker area and another near 8-Mile Bench. BLM and Montana FWP staff work together installing a Motus wildlife-tracking tower near 8-Mile Bench in the Upper Missouri River Breaks National Monument. The station is part of Montana’s growing network for detecting tagged bats, birds and other flying wildlife. Photo by Jesse Hankins, BLM Upper Missouri River Breaks National Monument wildlife biologist. The value of the BLM-supported network became clear almost immediately. Before the second tower was fully online, the Bullwhacker station detected a northern hoary bat during the night of Aug. 20 that had been tagged in Utah before traveling north and continuing toward the Midwest. The detection highlighted both the distances bats can travel and the importance of public lands in connecting wildlife-movement data across state boundaries. BLM Public Lands Help Fill Strategic Gaps Across Montana, multiple BLM field offices have supported the network by reviewing and approving tower locations on public lands, and even helping with tower installation as FWP expands the statewide system. Tower placement is focused along river corridors and other strategic locations where wildlife movements are likely to be detected. For BLM Montana/Dakotas, the new Motus station installations facilitated by the monument and the Miles City, Butte, Dillon, Lewistown, Glasgow, and Billings field offices demonstrate how public lands can support landscape-scale wildlife science. By providing locations for receiving stations, BLM-managed lands help researchers collect information that would otherwise be difficult or impossible to obtain. “The tracking devices that Motus towers are designed to detect can be much smaller than some satellite transmitters popular for tracking wildlife movements,” said Newton . “This means that small and lightweight species, like bats, small birds, and even large insects like monarch butterflies can now be tracked using this technology.” A Statewide Tracking Network FWP is building the Montana network as part of the international Motus Wildlife Tracking System and plans a network of 50 stations across the state, forming a “fence” of detection sites that can

pages.title: The most audacious thefts at the Louvre in the last century | National Geographic
pages.description: One of the most infamous heists in the cultural institution’s history was the 1911 theft of the Mona Lisa—when Pablo Picasso numbered among the suspects.
pages.text: The most audacious thefts at the Louvre in the last century | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE The Louvre has a wild history of being robbed in broad daylight One of the most infamous heists in the cultural institution’s history was the 1911 theft of the Mona Lisa—when Pablo Picasso numbered among the suspects. People gather around the Mona Lisa painting in Paris, three years after it was stolen from the Louvre by Vincenzo Peruggia in 1911. The theft is one of the most famous in the museum's history. Roger-Viollet, Getty Images By Erin Blakemore Published October 19, 2025 It took just seven minutes for a group of audacious thieves to pull off what may have been one of the most daring crimes in modern art: the theft of Napoleonic-era jewels from the Louvre in Paris on the morning of October 19. The heist, which took place while the museum was open to the public, involved a variety of jewels once owned by members of the French monarchy, including an emerald necklace and earrings that Napoleon gave his second wife Marie-Louise for their wedding. Now, questions are raging about how masked men could successfully evade security and nab priceless objets d’art from one of the most important art institutions in the world. It’s far from the first time. The museum has a longstanding history of shocking break-ins and unsolved thefts—despite being built precisely to protect the nation’s cultural heritage in the wake of a bloody revolution. French police officers seal off the entrance to the Louvre Museum after a jewelry heist on October 19, 2025, in Paris, France. It is being reported that thieves made of with historic jewels belonging to Napoleon and Empress Josephine. Kiran Ridley, Getty Images A French forensics officer examines the cut window and balcony of a gallery at the Louvre that was the scene of a robbery earlier in the day of October 19, 2025, in Paris. Kiran Ridley, Getty Images A basket lift used by thieves to steal the French crown jewels is seen at the Louvre on October 19, 2025, in Paris. Alexander Turnbull, AP Photo Though the Louvre palace dates back to the 13th century, the museum was founded during the French Revolution, a time of fervor for both egalitarian museums and political systems. In 1792, violent insurgents stormed Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette’s royal residences and declared a republic. Suddenly, the monarchy’s entire art collection belonged to the new state—and were under threat from looters who wanted to seize or smash all traces of the French monarchy. ( This is what happened the last time the French crown jewels were stolen .) The museum at the Louvre would safeguard state property amid the chaos of the revolution, as well as showcase a newly democratic France’s most prized treasures. But its cultural keepsakes have long proven tempting to would-be art thieves, and over the years the museum racked up a long list of security problems, and thefts. Here's the story of some of the museum’s most audacious crimes in the last century—nearly all of which have taken place during broad daylight. The Apollo Gallery at the Louvre, where the jewelry theft occured. Stephane De Sakutin, AFP via Getty Images The thieves reportedly took pieces of sapphire jewelry from the Louvre museum on Sunday. STEPHANE DE SAKUTIN, AFP via Getty Images The thieves also stole this emerald-and-diamond necklace, which Napoleon gave to his second wife Marie-Louise for their wedding. STEPHANE DE SAKUTIN, AFP via Getty Images The 1911 Mona Lisa heist The shocking theft of the “Mona Lisa”—then a lesser-known work by Leonardo da Vinci—occurred on the morning of August 21, 1911. It was a weekday, and Vincenzo Peruggia, an Italian immigrant who had briefly worked at the museum building frames and cases, dressed in his old work uniform and walked into the Louvre unchallenged . Lars Gotrich Producer, NPR Music and Series Editor, Tiny Desk Instagram Lars Gotrich is the editor of Tiny Desk and Tiny Desk Radio , a nationally broadcast program based on the beloved live concert series. He's produced performances at the Desk by Paramore, GWAR, Amy Grant, Turnstile, and Goo Goo Dolls. After years writing about music for zines and working in college radio, Gotrich started his career at NPR as an intern for the All Songs Considered podcast in 2006, where he's been a regular presence ever since. He's produced several different series for NPR Music, including First Listen, Song We Love, #NowPlaying and the Listening Party. While Gotrich covers all kinds of music, he is best known as the creator of roséwave, the pop-forward summer music series, and Viking's Choice , a curatorial free-for-all that emphasizes the loud and the weird. And, once upon a time, Gotrich hosted #WAXnEGGS , a live cooking show filmed in his home, featuring live sets by the likes of Waxahatchee and Speedy Ortiz. When he's not behind the mic or editing stories, Gotrich has appeared as a talking head in the music documentaries Welcome to Deathfest , Parallel Love: The Story of a Band Called Luxury, and No More Punk Time . He's also penned liner notes for vinyl releases by Sixpence None the Richer, Mary Halvorson, and Roadside Monument, among others. He is the world's okay-ist guitarist. pages.title: Lockerbie bombing suspect seized from Libya in 'cloak and dagger' operation British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Abu Agila Mohammad Mas'ud Kheir Al-Marimi claims he was unlawfully taken from Libya to stand trial over the bombing.
pages.text: Lockerbie bombing suspect seized from Libya in 'cloak and dagger' operation Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Lockerbie bombing suspect seized from Libya in 'cloak and dagger' operation 13 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google David Cowan Scotland home affairs correspondent Media outlet Libyan Review broadcast footage of Abu Agila Mas'ud Kheir Al-Marimi in a US prison A Lockerbie bombing suspect has claimed he was illegally removed from Libya to stand trial in the United States after "a cloak and dagger operation conducted in the dead of night". Abu Agila Mohammad Mas'ud Kheir Al-Marimi has alleged he was abducted by armed men and handed over "hooded and bound" to FBI agents, who had a plane waiting to fly him out of the country. Al-Marimi, also known as Mas'ud, has denied building and priming the bomb that brought down Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie on 21 December 1988, killing 270 people. The Libyan argues he was the victim of an unlawful rendition and has asked a judge in Washington DC to throw the case out of court. In response, the US Department of Justice said, under American law, the manner of his removal should not stop his thrice-postponed trial from finally getting underway in January. Al-Marimi's version of what happened is detailed for the first time in papers lodged with the court by his legal team. Lockerbie bombing trial date set as judge warns against further delay I thought the Lockerbie bombing was a closed case until I started asking questions The US government charged him with destroying the airliner in December 2020, and formally requested his "extradition, expulsion or otherwise lawful removal" from Libya to stand trial. At the time, Al-Marimi was in custody in Libya, serving a jail sentence for attacking rebel forces during the uprising against Col Muammar Gaddafi in 2011. According to Al-Marimi, he was released from prison on "compassionate grounds" on 30 September 2021 and returned to his family in Tripoli. About two weeks later, a group of armed men, many wearing masks, came to his house and rearrested him, without telling him why or who they were. Defence lawyers claim his "abduction" was reportedly carried out by a militia with "a reputation for brutality and disdain for human rights". They allege Al-Marimi was dragged across the floor "with no care for his health and mobility issues", that his son was beaten with a rifle, and that his wife and daughter were attacked. They said the grandfather was taken to a prison in the city of Misrata, about 116 miles (187km) east of Tripoli, where he was placed in solitary confinement for several days. On the morning of 11 December 2022, Al-Marimi said his captors gave him a sandwich and some tea and told him to pack his belongings. He expected to be released, but instead he was handed over to the FBI. Reuters Hundreds of people died when Pan Am Flight 103 exploded over Lockerbie in December 1988 A US government aircraft was waiting at Misrata airport when Al-Marimi arrived with a "loosely fitted cloth hood" over his head. His escorts asked the FBI to hurry up because onlookers were watching and he was placed on board the plane. The Libyan authorities handed over a plastic "trash bag" containing some of his belongings, including a Quran, a prayer rug, clothing, toiletries, and medicine. On the flight to the US, the FBI questioned Al-Marimi, performed a "head to toe medical examination" and provided him with clean clothes and blankets, his lawyers said. They claim the prime minister of the Tripoli-based Libyan government, Abdulhamid Dbeibah, later secured financial investment from the United States, including $16m (£12m) to secure Libya's transition to a democratic state and a contract with US oil giant Honeywell International. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn From Open Rangeland to Historic Battlefields Oct 21, 2026 CROW AGENCY, Mont. — The Bureau of Land Management Wild Horse and Burro Program manages and protects wild horses and burros on public rangelands across 10 Western states. These animals require active management because they have no natural predators and herds can quickly outgrow available water and forage. To maintain healthy horses on healthy rangelands, the BLM reduces herd sizes when they exceed what the land can support. These gathered animals are placed into private care through its national adoption and sales program. They get a second life as personal saddle horses, trail companions, —even historic reenactment mounts. June marked a major milestone in American history as descendants, historians, reenactors and equestrian enthusiasts gathered in Montana to commemorate the 150th anniversary of the Battle of the Little Bighorn. Over 19 tribal nations were represented, and the National Park Service was prepared to receive more than 10,000 visitors during three days of commemoration activities. The Little Bighorn National Battlefield waived standard fees and operated an off-site shuttle system from nearby parking areas to get visitors up to the yet-to-be-completed visitor’s center and the national cemetery. The U.S. Cavalry School camps on the bank of the Little Bighorn River each year across from the mouth of the historic Medicine Tail Coulee, a significant site in the battle’s story. The school offers hands-on experience, bringing together history lovers and horses to ride the battlefield and live a trooper’s life in the frontier Army. Among the mounts traversing the rolling hills and river crossings of the battlefield were former wild horses adopted through the BLM program. These mustangs proved that with proper gentling and training, wild-born horses can handle the heat, gunfire and close-order formation riding required of a cavalry mount from the Old West. Grace Thompson: Building Partnerships and Trust Grace Thompson is a full-time horse trainer who starts and gentles wild horses through her business, G.E.T. Horsemanship (Gentle, Effective, Thorough methods). Working with mustangs is a lifelong passion. From her farm in Chattanooga, Tenn., she has been directly involved in prepping these adoptees for new homes. Grace Thompson (center, white horse), a full-time horse trainer from Chattanooga, Tenn. starts and gentles wild horses through her business. Working with mustangs is her lifelong passion. (Photo by Sharon Moore, M.C. Lonesome Dove Western Photography.) "Wesley was my very first mustang. I adopted him in 2018 for my first Youth Extreme Mustang Makeover," Thompson said . "Pryor was my first adult mustang. I adopted him in 2019 for the Players’ Choice Extreme Mustang Makeover and purchased him at the end of the competition." Thompson has worked with Wesley since he was 10 months old, while Pryor was 3 years old when she acquired him. Both horses live on her farm. "Both of these guys are incredibly laid-back," Thompson said . "They handle pressure well and thrive on clear understanding and good leadership. Wesley is my primary bareback and bridle-less horse, while Pryor is my main mounted-shooting horse." At this year's 150th anniversary event, Thompson served as a corporal in the school. She said her primary training goal for the season was preparing both horses to serve as rental mounts for other participants. Pryor was assigned to Quartermaster Sgt. Comparta información sensible sólo en sitios web oficiales y seguros. el 19 abril del 2024 English (US) Factores de riesgo de la diabetes Puntos clave Algunos factores de riesgo de la diabetes se pueden manejar a través de cambios de comportamiento, como hacer más actividad física. Otros factores de riesgo no se pueden cambiar, como los antecedentes familiares y la edad. Averigüe su riesgo para cada tipo de diabetes. Diabetes tipo 1 Se cree que lo que causa la diabetes tipo 1 es una reacción autoinmunitaria (el cuerpo se ataca a sí mismo por error). Nadie sabe cómo prevenir la diabetes tipo 1. Los factores de riesgo que se conocen incluyen: Antecedentes familiares: uno de los padres o uno de los hermanos o hermanas tiene diabetes tipo 1. Edad: la diabetes tipo 1 puede producirse a cualquier edad, pero generalmente ocurre en niños, adolescentes o adultos jóvenes. En los Estados Unidos, las personas de raza blanca tienen más probabilidades de presentar diabetes tipo 1 que las afroamericanas y las hispanas o latinas. La prediabetes y la diabetes tipo 2 La prediabetes y la diabetes tipo 2 comparten casi todos los mismos factores de riesgo. Si ya tiene prediabetes, este es un factor de riesgo agregado que aumenta sus probabilidades de presentar diabetes tipo 2. Usted tiene riesgo de presentar prediabetes y diabetes tipo 2 si: Tiene sobrepeso u obesidad. Tiene 45 años o más. Uno de sus padres o hermanos tiene diabetes tipo 2. Hace actividad física menos de 3 veces a la semana. Tiene la enfermedad del hígado graso no alcohólico. Ha tenido alguna vez diabetes gestacional (diabetes durante el embarazo) o ha dado a luz a un bebé que pesó más de 9 libras. Es una persona afroamericana, hispana o latina, indígena de los EE. UU. o nativa de Alaska. Algunas personas nativas de las islas del Pacífico y algunas personas asiaticoamericanas también tienen mayor riesgo. Diabetes gestacional Usted está en riesgo de presentar diabetes gestacional (diabetes durante el embarazo) si: Tuvo diabetes gestacional en un embarazo anterior. Dio a luz a un bebé que pesó más de 9 libras. Tiene sobrepeso u obesidad. Tiene más de 25 años de edad. Tiene antecedentes familiares de diabetes tipo 2. Tiene un trastorno hormonal llamado síndrome del ovario poliquístico (PCOS, por sus siglas en inglés). Es una persona afroamericana, hispana o latina, indígena de los EE. UU., o nativa de Alaska, Hawái o de otras islas del Pacífico. La diabetes gestacional por lo general desaparece después de dar a luz. Pero tener antecedentes de diabetes gestacional aumenta su riesgo de presentar diabetes tipo 2. El bebé también tiene más probabilidades de tener obesidad cuando sea niño o adolescente, y de presentar diabetes tipo 2 más adelante en la vida. Reduzca su riesgo Algunos factores de riesgo, como la edad y los antecedentes médicos familiares, no se pueden evitar. Pero hay algunas cosas que puede hacer para reducir su riesgo de presentar prediabetes, diabetes tipo 2 o diabetes gestacional. Algunos cambios de comportamiento para reducir su riesgo incluyen: Aumentar la actividad física. Alimentarse saludablemente. Perder peso si tiene sobrepeso u obesidad. Cambios pequeños y graduales pueden hacer una gran diferencia para reducir su riesgo de prediabetes, diabetes tipo 2 o diabetes gestacional, y pueden mejorar su salud y bienestar general. Nunca es demasiado tarde ni temprano para empezar. Si tiene prediabetes y necesita apoyo adicional, hay ayuda disponible a través del programa de cambio de estilo de vida del Programa Nacional de Prevención de la Diabe

CIMC - How to Download Data This page explains how to download data from Cleanups in My Community (CIMC) Starting from the CIMC landing page or the CIMC Map View : Select: "Create a listing of cleanups or grants" from the CIMC landing page or Cleanups and Grants listing from the CIMC map view. On the "Cleanups in My Community Listing" page, select your geography (see " About the Data " page for more details on geography available in CIMC). Make sure you have chosen what you want to include in your download ("Cleanups" or "Brownfield Grants"). You may also use the "Cleanup" or "Brownfields Grants " tabbed menus to further refine the data you want to download. When you have made your data and geographic selections, choose "Apply". When the screen refreshes, scroll down to see your list at the bottom of the page. The initial view of the list may only show a portion of all the records that meet your criteria. You may view the additional pages by clicking the right arrow in the lower right corner of the page. You can choose to open or save the resulting list of cleanups or grants on the "Cleanups in My Community List Results" page to an Excel or CSV file format by clicking "Actions" and then "Download" from the Actions drop down menu. Your computer interface will walk you through the process of opening the file or saving the file to your computer. The download will include all the results records, even if they do not all appear on the results page. The Excel export will include working links to the profile pages. Additional Data may be Downloaded for Brownfields Properties: After following the previous steps for Downloading Data from CIMC, go to the bottom of the CIMC List Results page, and click on the button on the right called "Click for More Brownfields Info". On the "Advanced Brownfields Property Search" page, choose the additional categories of data you want, and then click on Submit. The results will display on the "Advanced Brownfields Property List Results" page. Only Brownfields properties will be shown in this view and will be available for download with these additional fields. Only the first 15 records will be shown initially. You may view the additional pages by clicking "Next" at the bottom of the page. On the "More Brownfields Information" page, go to the bottom left corner of the page and click on "Export to CSV". Your computer interface will walk you through the process of opening the file or saving the file to your computer. All the list results will be downloaded, for all the columns, whether they appear on the first page of list results or not. Note: Multiple lines for a property may appear if a property received multiple funding sources from EPA and/or reported multiple accomplishments at a particular property. DOE Issues Extension to Delfin LNG Project U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright today approved a liquefied natural gas export permit extension for Delfin LNG LLC, granting additional time to commence exports from the project proposed for offshore Louisiana. Energy.gov March 10, 2025 Estimated Read Time min WASHINGTON– U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright today approved a liquefied natural gas (LNG) export permit extension for Delfin LNG LLC (Delfin), granting additional time to commence exports from the project proposed for offshore Louisiana. The permit extension, which had been delayed by the Biden-Harris administration, was announced by Secretary Wright in his opening remarks at CERAWeek in Houston. “While the previous administration pursued a strategy of energy subtraction, I am proud to be working with President Trump to advance a strategy of energy addition – embracing all forms of energy that are affordable, reliable and secure,” said Secretary Wright . “The positive energy and renewed enthusiasm for U.S. leadership in energy exports from our allies and trading partners here at CERAWeek is palpable, and I am thrilled to sign this order to help another U.S. LNG project advance.” The issuance to Delfin marks the fourth LNG-related approval from DOE since President Trump took office, following an export approval to Commonwealth LNG on February 14 , an order on rehearing removing barriers for the use of LNG as bunkering fuel announced on February 28 , and an approval providing the Golden Pass LNG terminal more time to commence exports issued March 5. “With this decision, I am pleased to see DOE help this project progress after the regulatory setbacks it faced during the Biden administration,” said Tala Goudarzi, Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management. Delfin, majority-owned by Fairwood Peninsula, Talisman Global Alternative Master, L.P. and Talisman Global Capital Master, L.P., is seeking to reach a final investment decision later this year and have construction begin on its offshore floating liquefied natural gas vessel (FLNGV). Today’s order extends the commencement date for Delfin’s export authorization for exports of up to 1.8 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) of natural gas as LNG to non-free trade agreement countries to June 1, 2029. ### View Next Press Release Secretary of Energy Chris Wright Delivers Keynote Remarks at CERAWeek 2025 March 10, 2025 View Previous Press Release Secretary Wright to Deliver CERAWeek Keynote Address in Houston March 7, 2025 Media Inquiries: (202) 586-4940 or DOENews@hq.doe.gov Read more at the energy.gov Newsroom

pages.title: Edmonia Lewis confronted American slavery in her sculptures. Then history forgot her. | National Geographic
pages.description: A new exhibition of her masterworks is traveling the country and reclaiming her place in American history.
pages.text: Edmonia Lewis confronted American slavery in her sculptures. Then history forgot her. | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE Edmonia Lewis confronted American slavery in her sculptures. Then history forgot her. A new exhibition of her masterworks is traveling the country and reclaiming her place in American history. During her lifetime, Edmonia Lewis was America's most famous artists. Seen here, the biracial sculptor defied the odds and produced trailblazing work. Augustus Marshall, Courtesy Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture By Katy Kelleher Published June 15, 2026 Part celebrity, part anomaly, sculptor Edmonia Lewis captivated mid-19 th -century audiences with her luminous, large-scale marble sculptures that appeared nearly lifelike in their carefully rendered detail. For wealthy Americans on the Grand Tour, a stop at her studio was practically necessary. But visitors weren’t just there to follow in the footsteps of Pope Pius IX and President Ulysses S. Grant, both admirers of Lewis, they were there to obtain proof. They wanted to see with their own eyes that Lewis, a petite biracial woman, could render life from stone. For some, it beggared belief that her hands could have coaxed forth vivid expressions from blocks of Carrara marble. While she was able to delegate some of the brute work of carving to assistants, Lewis made a point of ensuring that the public saw her with a chisel in hand, an unusual choice for sculptors of the era. Even in the prime of her storied career, Lewis still needed to prove herself, to justify her talents, just as she had been doing her entire life. Although she was internationally famous during her heyday, Lewis has largely been forgotten. She lived during a time of artistic rupture, and towards the end of her life, her Neoclassical-style sculptures had fallen deeply out of fashion, dismissed by an art world enraptured by the provocations of modernism. Abstraction became more exciting than the sentimental realism preferred by the Victorians, and Lewis was nothing if not a realist. Now, a new exhibition is reviving Lewis’s reputation and reclaiming her place in America’s history. Spearheaded by Jeffrey Richmond-Moll, curator of American Art at the Peabody Essex Museum and Shawnya L. Harris, curator of African American and African Diasporic Art at the Georgia Museum of Art, “Edmonia Lewis: Said in Stone,” is a curatorial feat. The exhibition took over a decade to assemble, largely because Lewis’s impressive output had been scattered, forgotten, and in some cases, badly damaged. A view of some of the 115 objects included in the exhibition "Said in Stone," that revives Lewis's legacy. Kim Indresano, Courtesy Peabody Essex Museum “We are at a moment where, around the country, we’re asking questions about who should be a part of the stories we tell about our nation’s history and who has been left out,” says Richmond-Moll. “ Said in Stone, ” which will travel the United States through July 2027, includes 30 sculptures from throughout Lewis’s career, including early busts and later large-scale masterworks, plus dozens of additional objects—letters, photographs, examples of Indigenous crafts, and pieces by her contemporaries—that provide historical context and help fill the gaps left by works that remain missing. Together, these 115 items mark the first, long-overdue retrospective of the artist’s career, revealing the trailblazing sculptor behind the chisel. (A Raphael masterpiece is finally back in one piece.) From student to sculptor Likely born in upstate New York in 1844, Edmonia Lewis spent her childhood with the Mississauga Ojibwe tribe—“my mother’s people,” as she called them. A young Lewis watched as her mother and aunts practiced beadwork, weaving, and leatherwork, and she often traveled with them to markets around the state, where they sold their art. “It instilled in her a creative vision,” says Richmond-Moll. pages.title: Chris Van Hollen says he has path to win Senate leader over Chuck Schumer | US Senate | The Guardian
pages.description: Progressive US senator calling for more inclusion within Democratic caucus cites openness to change among peers
pages.text: Chris Van Hollen says he has path to win Senate leader over Chuck Schumer | US Senate | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Senator Chris Van Hollen speaks to the media after taking the stage at Democrats’ post-midterm election conference in Denver, Colorado, on Friday. Photograph: Kevin Mohatt/Reuters View image in fullscreen Senator Chris Van Hollen speaks to the media after taking the stage at Democrats’ post-midterm election conference in Denver, Colorado, on Friday. Photograph: Kevin Mohatt/Reuters US Senate Chris Van Hollen says he has path to win Senate leader over Chuck Schumer Progressive US senator calling for more inclusion within Democratic caucus cites openness to change among peers Marina Dunbar Sun 15 Nov 2026 13.46 EST Last modified on Sun 15 Nov 2026 14.12 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer , asserting that he has a path to victory amid a dedicated campaign that includes a series of television appearances. Van Hollen, a Maryland progressive, appeared on Sunday on CNN, ABC and Fox News as he continues to make his case for why his peers in the Senate should reject Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus for nearly a decade. On CNN’s State of the Union, he reaffirmed that he believes he has a path to victory, citing support and a widespread openness to change within the Senate Democratic caucus. “This really is a response to the call of the voters, who clearly rejected Donald Trump and his awful policies, but they haven’t fully hired the Democrats,” Van Hollen said, alluding to how the US president’s Republican party lost control of Congress during the 3 November midterm elections . “They’ve given us a chance, and I think we need to earn their trust. And I think that begins by not going back to business as usual.” Van Hollen criticized reports that Schumer’s team may move the Senate caucus leadership election date earlier than 1 December. He contended that the caucus should have a debate about the group’s direction as the Democrats assume control of Congress in January for the second half of Trump’s second presidency. What the choice between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen for Senate leader is all about | Bernie Sanders Read more Van Hollen also responded to a list that was reportedly leaked by Schumer’s team to the political news outlet the Hill that revealed the committed votes the New York senator claims to already have. Van Hollen said that some of those senators on the list have actually already pledged to vote for him instead of Schumer. He also called for more “inclusion and democracy” within the Democratic caucus, accusing Schumer of trying to exclude the more progressive members of the party. Van Hollen alluded to victories by Democratic senators-elect whose candidacies Schumer did not support – Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Troy Jackson of Maine – and said they “would not be there” if Schumer had his way. “He joined with Aipac and crypto to try to defeat them,” Van Hollen said, referring in part to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, which opposed El-Sayed and Jackson. Appearing on ABC News’s This Week, Van Hollen accused Schumer’s team of putting out misinformation by leaking the alleged list of supporters, equating it to an intimidation tactic. “They’re essentially trying to instill fear in people who may say that they’re going to support me as a new leader,” he said. “We just had a great day for our democracy around the country. How about a little democracy in the Senate Democratic caucus?” View image in fullscreen Chris Van Hollen addresses fired federal workers and their families at the Hart Senate office building on 24 June 2025 in Washington DC. Photograph: Jemal Countess/Getty Images for Tuesday Group Fired Feds On Fox News Sunday, Van Hollen responded more directly to the Hill’s report, calling it “a bunch of nonsense”.

pages.title: Libya oil refinery fire: Firefighters battle huge blaze after drone attack British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Monday's drone strike on the Zawiya refinery was the third such incident in two days.
pages.text: Libya oil refinery fire: Firefighters battle huge blaze after drone attack Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Libyan authorities battle big blaze at major oil refinery 11 August 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Basillioh Rukanga Watch: Huge blaze after attack on petrol tank in Libya Libyan emergency services have been battling to contain a huge blaze at a major oil plant after it was targeted by unknown attackers. The Zawiya refinery, west of the capital Tripoli, was hit in a drone strike on Monday evening - the third such incident in two days. The National Oil Corporation (NOC) said a tank containing about 4.5m litres of fuel was directly hit, triggering a huge fire that caused it to collapse. It said it was considering suspending operations if the attacks continued. There were no "serious injuries" from the fire, with most patients treated for smoke inhalation, Libya's Ambulance and Emergency Service said on Tuesday. The Zawiya refinery is the largest operational facility in Libya, with an output of 120,000 barrels per day. The NOC condemned similar attacks in past days in Zawiya, including two drone strikes on a naphtha reservoir and a water desalination plant. It called on the authorities to investigate who was behind the violence. The attacks have highlighted continuing instability in Libya, which has been split in two since a civil war broke out after the ousting of former leader Muammar Gaddafi. Colonel Gaddafi seized power in 1969 and ruled autocratically for four decades until he was toppled and killed in 2011 in a rebellion assisted by Western military intervention Since his fall, rival power centres, one based in the east backed by military commander Khalifa Haftar, and one in the west in Tripoli, led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah, have been jostling for political and military dominance. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn National Public Lands Day Volunteers Revitalize Dean S. Reservoir in Montana Oct 16, 2026 Twenty-four volunteers, including six youths, gathered at Dean S. Reservoir to mark National Public Lands Day by constructing kiosks, installing culverts, fixing fences and clearing trails. Dean S. Reservoir is located east of Miles City, Montana, accessed in part by the Baker Highway and situated on the south side of the Pine Hills subdivision on BLM-managed land. The site has recently been upgraded with additional campsites, vehicle pullouts, and areas built to accommodate campers and trailers. Volunteers, including six youths, gathered at Dean S. Reservoir in Custer County, Mont. to mark National Public Lands Day by constructing kiosks, installing culverts, fixing fences and clearing trails. The BLM Miles City Field Office has a lengthy relationship with National Public Lands Day stretching back more than two decades. National Public Lands Day is the largest single-day volunteer event for public lands in the United States, held annually on the fourth Saturday of September. The BLM Miles City Field Office has a lengthy relationship with National Public Lands Day stretching back more than two decades. BLM staff have organized and conducted NPLD work events, each held at a different BLM location in eastern Montana. According to Tamara Tollett, a park ranger with the BLM Montana/Dakotas Miles City Field Office, the event saw a new crop of locals turn out to give back to the lands that provide so much for the American people. "Each participant was an integral part of the work we accomplished for the betterment of our public lands," said Tollett. "Dean S. Reservoir is in much better shape because of them." Tollett noted that the younger participants made a notable impression on project leaders by taking on labor-intensive tasks and insisting on continuing their work after lunch. "The youngest of the kids started working on installing a culvert, and once that was done, they moved to working on the trail — hard work for such young people," said Tollett. “Not only did all of these kids show up to work voluntarily, but they also made sure that they got the job done before leaving. I’m proud to have had the opportunity to work with such dedicated individuals.” Coordinated by the National Environmental Education Foundation, National Public Lands Day brings together thousands of volunteers to restore, clean up, and care for America's shared natural and historic spaces. Additionally, the 2026 NPLD events reflect the BLM’s new "All Americans Outside" initiative. pages.description: Cómo y cuándo controlar los niveles de azúcar en sangre, controlar los altibajos y más.

Comparta información sensible sólo en sitios web oficiales y seguros. el 21 mayo del 2024 English (US) Manejo de los niveles de azúcar en la sangre Puntos clave Mantenga sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre dentro de sus valores deseados lo más posible. Esto lo ayudará a prevenir o retrasar problemas graves de salud. Hay medidas específicas que puede tomar para hacer que los niveles de azúcar en la sangre sean más fáciles de manejar. Revisión de los niveles de azúcar en la sangre ¿Cómo reviso mis niveles de azúcar en la sangre? Use un medidor de azúcar en la sangre (también llamado glucómetro) o un monitor continuo de glucosa (CGM, por sus siglas en inglés) para revisar sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre . Un medidor de azúcar en la sangre mide la cantidad de azúcar en una muestra pequeña de sangre, generalmente de la punta de un dedo. Un monitor continuo de glucosa usa un sensor que se coloca debajo de la piel para medir sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre cada tantos minutos. Si usa un monitor continuo de glucosa, aún así debe revisar sus niveles diariamente con un medidor de azúcar en la sangre. Esto ayudará a garantizar que los valores de su monitor sean precisos. ¿Cuándo debo revisar mis niveles de azúcar en la sangre? La frecuencia con la que debe revisar sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre depende del tipo de diabetes que tenga y si toma medicamentos para esta enfermedad. Los momentos típicos para revisar sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre son: Cuando recién se despierta, antes de comer o beber algo. Antes de una comida. Dos horas después de una comida. A la hora de acostarse. Si tiene diabetes tipo 1 , o tiene diabetes tipo 2 y se administra insulina, o tiene niveles bajos de azúcar en la sangre con frecuencia, su médico podría pedirle que se revise los niveles más frecuentemente, como antes y después de hacer actividad física. Sus valores deseados de azúcar en la sangre El valor deseado de azúcar en la sangre es el nivel que usted trata de alcanzar tanto como sea posible. Estos son valores típicos: Antes de una comida: de 80 a 130 mg/dL Dos horas después de comenzar a comer: menos de 180 mg/dL Sus valores deseados de azúcar en la sangre podrían ser distintos con base en su edad, problemas de salud adicionales que tenga y otros factores. Hable con su equipo de cuidados de la salud sobre cuáles valores son mejores para usted. ¿Qué causa niveles bajos de azúcar en la sangre? Los niveles de azúcar en la sangre de menos de 70 mg/dL se consideran bajos. Los niveles bajos de azúcar en la sangre (también llamados hipoglucemia) tienen muchas causas, entre ellas: Saltarse una comida Administrarse demasiada insulina Tomar otros medicamentos para la diabetes Hacer más actividad física que la habitual Consumir alcohol Seguir leyendo: Acerca de los niveles bajos de azúcar en la sangre (hipoglucemia) ¿Qué causa niveles altos de azúcar en la sangre? Muchas cosas pueden causar niveles altos de azúcar en la sangre (hiperglucemia), entre ellas: Estar enfermo Estar estresado Comer más de lo habitual No administrarse suficiente insulina Si está enfermo y sus niveles de azúcar en la sangre son de 240mg/dL o más, use una prueba de cetonas (que se compra sin receta) para detectar las cetonas. Llame a su médico si su nivel de cetonas es alto. Un nivel de cetonas alto puede ser un signo temprano de cetoacidosis diabética (DKA, por sus siglas en inglés). La cetoacidosis diabética es una emergencia médica y debe tratarse de inmediato. Seguir leyendo: Acerca de la cetoacidosis diabética Formas de manejar sus nivele

Cleanups in My Community - About the Data Background Current Scope of Sites Included in Cleanups In My Community Additional Information about Cleanups Other (Non-cleanup) Data Mappable in CIMC Cleanup Program or Status Brownfields RCRA Corrective Action Superfund Federal Facility Superfund Sites Removals/Responses Recovery Act Locations for Superfund and Brownfields Geography Census Geography Background Accidents, spills, leaks, and past improper disposal and handling of hazardous materials and wastes have resulted in tens of thousands of sites across our country that have contaminated our land, water (groundwater and surface water), and air (indoor and outdoor). EPA and its state, territory and tribal partners have developed a variety of cleanup programs to assess and, where necessary, clean up these contaminated sites. Cleanups in My Community is intended to provide information about sites that might need to be cleaned up, are being cleaned up, or have been cleaned up, in your community or anywhere in the United States. The information can help people understand what is happening in their community, what has happened, and, with the contextual information provided, what could happen if certain events take place. We provide what data are available, and those data are limited by what we can legally generate and collect. See legal notices page for more information on data limitations. CIMC is an ever-green application – always improving. We are open to new ideas on how CIMC can be improved, please contact us with your ideas. Current Scope of Sites Included in Cleanups in My Community Currently, CIMC only shows sites, facilities and properties for which EPA collects information by law, or voluntarily via grants. At present, this does not include state or locally funded cleanups. In addition, data in this system is updated according to certain update or refresh schedules which vary by application and may not yet reflect real changes at the locations covered here. Currently, CIMC only includes data for the following EPA cleanup programs: Brownfields Properties : Grantees may report information on Brownfield properties receiving federal grants. Data, which dates back as far as 1998, are collected from grantees via ACRES. These data are pulled into CIMC twice a month. Brownfields Grants Jurisdictions : Geographic areas covered by specific Brownfields grants. These data are collected through ACRES. These data are pulled into CIMC twice a month. RCRA Corrective Action : Facilities cleaned up under the corrective action program of the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA). These data, dating back to 1980, are collected from the states using RCRAInfo. Only facilities data which states designate as being on the 2020 Baseline for Corrective Action and for public access are included in CIMC. These data are pulled from the RCRAInfo web service twice a month. Superfund and RCRA Corrective Action Boundaries: We are working with EPA regions to provide Superfund site boundaries, RCRA Corrective Action boundaries and control area boundaries (operable units, institutional control areas, LUCs, AULs, etc.) through CIMC. These are not official boundaries and have no legal standing, but are provided as a public service. For more information, please see our Legal Notices . At present, boundaries for EPA Regions 1 and 3 are available in CIMC. Additional boundaries will be added as they become available to the CIMC team. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to this park navigation Skip to the main content Skip to this park information section Skip to the footer section National Park Service Bering Land Bridge National Preserve Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Bering Land Bridge National Preserve Contact Us Safety Carrying plenty of supplies and dressing in layers are essential tasks when traveling in the Alaska backcountry. NPS Photo Backcountry Safety What To Wear There may be very little information about current weather conditions in the preserve, and sunny 70-degree days can rapidly turn into bone-chilling 40-degree rains. It is important to pack rain gear as well as cold weather gear, even if the forecast in Nome is calling for clear skies and warm temperatures during your trip. Pack Extra Food In addition to proper clothing, you should pack at least 3 days of extra food for your backcountry trip. Due to rapid shifts in weather, pickup could be delayed several days. Rain, fog, and low clouds can remain near the Serpentine Hot Springs valley for several days, causing your trip to last longer than expected. Bring a Medical Kit It is important to realize you are more than 80 miles from the nearest hospital and 540 miles from the nearest major medical facility in Anchorage. If you get injured in optimal conditions, you are looking at a 3 to 4 hour wait. It is important to bring a well-stocked medical kit. If you require any daily medication, it is a good practice to pack enough to last a week longer than your expected stay. Communication Due to its remote location, there is no cell phone service in the preserve. The only means of communication is by personal satellite phone. For another way to be covered in case of medical emergency, take a satellite tracking device or an Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT). Leave an Itinerary Let friends and family know when and where you are going, how long you'll be gone, and some idea of your plans. Be sure to include your satellite phone number and the name of the pilot and tail number of the plane you are taking. Call when you arrive back from the backcountry so friends and family know you are okay. Rescue will be delayed if others don't know your planned route or when you are returning. Contact Us While no backcountry permit is needed to visit Bering Land Bridge National Preserve, it is a good idea to contact park staff for information on cabin conditions and weather hazards as well as information about the preserve's features. Wildlife Safety Brown bears , wolves, foxes, and wolverines live in and around the preserve. It's always a good idea to carry bear spray while traveling through brown bear country. If backpacking, use a bear-proof container and cook and store food 100 yards and upwind from your sleeping area. Willows provide shade and shelter for bears and can reduce visibility. To avoid surprising a bear, make noise. Talk, sing, or clap loudly while in dense brush, near rushing water, or on windy days. The noises you make are often enough to keep bears away. Never approach a cub or get between a mother and a cub. It is important to keep your distance from muskoxen and caribou as well. These animals can overheat if frightened. They can also decide to charge you. The powerful horns and antlers of muskoxen, moose, and caribou can be just as deadly as a predator when they feel threatened. Bear Safety All of Alaska is bear country. Respecting bears and learning proper behavior can help you avoid a human-bear conflict Plan Your Visit With proper planning and equipment, a trip into the preserve can be rewarding. Secretary Wright Signs Export Authorization for Venture Global CP2 LNG U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright today approved a liquefied natural gas export authorization to the Venture Global CP2 LNG export project proposed for Cameron Parish, Louisiana. Energy.gov March 19, 2025 Estimated Read Time min WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright today approved a liquefied natural gas (LNG) export authorization to the Venture Global CP2 LNG export project proposed for Cameron Parish, Louisiana. This action reflects another step in the Trump administration’s commitment to restoring American energy dominance. “The benefits of expanding U.S. LNG exports have never been more clear, and I am proud to be taking action to support the American people and our allies abroad with more affordable, reliable, secure American energy,” said Secretary Wright . “Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, we are cutting the red tape around projects like CP2, unleashing our energy potential and ensuring U.S. can continue to meet growing energy demand for decades to come.” The issuance to CP2 marks the fifth LNG-related approval from DOE since President Trump took office, following an export approval to Commonwealth LNG on February 14 , an order on rehearing removing barriers for the use of LNG as bunkering fuel announced on February 28 , an approval providing the Golden Pass LNG terminal more time to commence exports issued March 5, and approval granting the Delfin LNG project additional time to commence exports issued on March 10. Once constructed, CP2, owned by Venture Global, will be able to export up to 3.96 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) of LNG. “The CP2 project is another project that has been waiting too long for regulatory action at DOE, and I am glad to see that being corrected today” said Tala Goudarzi , Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management. “With Venture Global’s track record of getting projects constructed quickly, I look forward to seeing this project come to fruition before long.” Today’s authorization conditionally grants CP2 authorization to export LNG to non-free trade agreement countries from the proposed CP2 LNG project. In the order, DOE finds that LNG exports from CP2 LNG are likely to yield economic benefits to the United States, diversify global LNG supplies, and improve energy security for U.S. allies and trading partners over the course of the export term through 2050. DOE expects to issue a final order to CP2 LNG in the coming months. CP2 is the third LNG export project that has been developed by Venture Global, with the Calcasieu Pass project coming online in March 2022 and the Plaquemines LNG project beginning exports in late 2024. Accompanying the buildout of LNG export terminals is an increase of natural gas pipelines across the U.S., with approximately 8.5 Bcf/d of pipeline additions for delivery to LNG export terminals recently completed in Texas and Louisiana. ### View Next Press Release ICYMI: WSJ: Thanks to Trump Administration, We Now Know the Truth About LNG’s Benefits March 21, 2025 View Previous Press Release DOE Approves Loan Disbursement for Palisades Nuclear Plant March 17, 2025 Media Inquiries: (202) 586-4940 or DOENews@hq.doe.gov Read more at the energy.gov Newsroom

pages.title: One of the hardest colors to make is not just blue—it's actually cerulean | National Geographic
pages.description: The Devil Wears Prada made a cerulean sweater a moment in fashion history. But its scientific history is much older, and more fascinating.
pages.text: One of the hardest colors to make is not just blue—it's actually cerulean | National Geographic SCIENCE One of the hardest colors to make is not just blue—it's actually cerulean The Devil Wears Prada made a cerulean sweater a moment in fashion history. But its scientific history is much older, and more fascinating. In the 1860s, cerulean pigment became popular among painters, including impressionist Claude Monet who used it in The Gare St-Lazare . Alamy By Bethany Brookshire Last updated May 1, 2026 Listen to this story See more of our narrated audio articles here Audio Timeline Slider: Use the left or right arrow keys to decrease or increase the slider value. Play audio 15 15 Audio Unmuted. Mute Volume Slider: Use the left or right arrow keys to decrease or increase the slider value. 0:00 / 0:00 Sign in or subscribe to hear the full story Some people might see a deep sky-blue sweater and think that it is simply blue. But there are many kinds of blue, from navy to baby. And in the case of one specific sweater in The Devil Wears Prada , “it's actually cerulean.” In the famous scene, Meryl Streep’s character, Runway editor Miranda Priestly, proceeds to give the hapless, cerulean-clad assistant Andy an iconic fashion history rundown of her “clearance bin” sweater. But cerulean itself has far more than fashion history behind it. Blues—including cerulean—are some of the rarest colors in nature, and astonishingly difficult to create. And yet, throughout history, humans have tried, over and over again, to reflect the blue of a perfect sky. As The Devil Wears Prada 2 brings Miranda Priestly back to screens, it’s worth asking what it takes to create a color that’s not just turquoise or lapis, but cerulean. It turns out that to make the right blue, scientists need elements from blue-hued cobalt to potassium and magnesium. And in pursuit of color and cash, a new study shows that some paint-makers may have tried to keep their cerulean chemistry a secret. ( This is the oldest blue pigment ever found in Europe .) From Egyptian tombs to French canvas “Blue came along fairly late as something that you could color things with,” says Kai Kupferschmidt , a science journalist and author of the 2022 book Blue: The Science and Secrets of Nature’s Rarest Color . That’s in part because it is rare in nature. Humans have been painting in color for more than 60,000 years, but they often stuck with charcoal, red and yellow, Kupferschmidt writes. The first known blue pigments were ground up from the blue mineral azurite and used in graves in Turkey nearly 9,000 years ago. Egyptian pharaohs imported the lapis lazuli, a deep blue mineral-filled rock from the Hindu Kush mountains in Afghanistan, at fabulous expense, but they also set out to make their own—the world’s first synthetic pigment developed around 3000 B.C. “One of the earliest examples is Egyptian blue or calcium copper silicate,” says Mas Subramanian , a materials chemist at Oregon State University in Corvallis. The result was the brilliant blue glaze found on Egyptian grave goods and other pottery. The word cerulean originated from a Latin term, caeruleum, “used in ancient Rome for Egyptian blue pigment,” says Václava Antušková , a conservation scientist at the Chemical-Technological Laboratory in the National Gallery of Prague in the Czech Republic. People also produced blues from plants like woad and indigo, both sold at fabulous prices. By the Renaissance, ultramarine produced from lapis lazuli was worth its weight in gold. ( Barbie pink may be Earth’s oldest color .) What does blue signify? Because blue raw materials were rare, the ancient world often didn’t infuse it with a lot of symbolic meaning, writes historian Michel Pastoureau in his 2018 book Blue: The History of a Color . It’s hard to make a color a symbol of something when you don’t have a paint for it, after all. But as blue paints became available in antiquity, artists began to use blue symbolically. pages.title: Robyn's first post-parenthood album is a manifesto on sensuality : NPR
pages.description: As the trailblazing Swedish star returns with her first album since 2018, she talks through going on IVF and solo parenting, expressing sexuality, and the negotiation of being a self-aware pop star.
pages.text: Robyn's first post-parenthood album is a manifesto on sensuality : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Robyn's first post-parenthood album is a manifesto on sensuality As the trailblazing Swedish star returns with her first album since 2018, she talks through going on IVF and solo parenting, expressing sexuality, and the negotiation of being a self-aware pop star. Music Interviews Robyn's first post-parenthood album is a manifesto on sensuality March 27, 2026 5:00 AM ET Heard on Morning Edition By Hazel Cills Robyn on her trolling, playful new album ‘Sexistential’ Listen · 4:56 4:56 Transcript Toggle more options Download Embed Embed < iframe src="https://www.npr.org/player/embed/nx-s1-5645112/nx-s1-9705482" width="100%" height="290" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" title="NPR embedded audio player"> Transcript "I always felt like there's this drag aspect to performing a female role," Robyn says. "It was so claustrophobic for me when I was younger but now it feels interesting to play with." Marili Andre hide caption toggle caption i Marili Andre Who knew that what pop music really needed was a song about hornily perusing dating apps while doing IVF? That's what Robyn delivers on the funny title track of her ninth studio album Sexistential , out March 27, a song that chronicles her journey conceiving her son as a solo parent (joking with her doctor that her dream donor might be hunky actor Adam Driver) and scrolling the Internet in sweatpants, calling out for "some IRL" and "your ASL" in between impulse buying stuff on Etsy she doesn't need. "My body's a spaceship with the ovaries on hyperdrive," she raps, somehow of our mundane, smartphone world and yet also hovering above us, an alien recalculating her relationship to Earth. Sponsor Message For most of her career Robyn has sought to deconstruct the aims of a contemporary pop singer, wriggling her way out of a commercial teen idol career beginning in the 1990s with hits like "Show Me Love." In the mid 2000s, with the help of left-field Swedish groups like The Knife and Röyksopp, she remade herself into what would become the blueprint for so many stars in the decade following: a steely, self-proclaimed "fembot with feelings too" who could turn raw, human vulnerability into larger-than-life synthpop hits like "Be Mine" and "Call Your Girlfriend." YouTube But for the last decade, Robyn's been chipping away at her reputation for being so many millennials' resident dancefloor therapist. She ventured deeper into club music with her 2015 side project La Bagatelle Magique and 2018's long-teased Honey , which focused on slow-building grooves and sparse production that begged to be mixed into DJ sets rather than replicating the expected chorus and verse beats of a stereotypical hit. And now she's back, nearly eight years after her last full-length album with Sexistential , with a restless album that continues the humanizing ethos of Honey but revisits the punchy, dramatic electropop of her most enduring songs. Sexistential is about sex, a topic the artist says has only become more emboldened and complex in her work as she gets older. But it's also about Robyn's relationship to pleasure at this point in her life, following the breakup of a long relationship and the artist pursuing single parenthood, and, as she says, "all the contradictions before and burning down ideas that didn't fit the situation I was in." اجتماعاتها وفعالياتها والبيانات الصحفية ، بالإضافة إلى الأخبار والتحقيقات . وفضلًا عن الحزم التي تتيحها خدمة (يونيفيد) و البث المباشر للمذيعين ، نوفّر تغطية مباشرة على قناتنا الشبكية ، وعلى قناتنا في يوتيوب ، وفي مختلف وسائط التواصل الاجتماعي . ويمكن مشاهدة برامجنا المميزة، بما في ذلك المقابلات ومقاطع الفيديو الخاصة والأفلام الوثائقية، عبر الإنترنت . يمكنك العثور على أحدث القصص و البرامج الإذاعية
