Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/08/nist-national-construction-safety-team-advisory-committee-meeting-scheduled NEWS NIST National Construction Safety Team Advisory Committee Meeting Scheduled for Sept. 23 and 24, 2026 August 13, 2026 Share Facebook Linkedin X.com Email NCST investigators monitor the progress of a structural engineering test in June 2025 as part of the Champlain Towers South investigation. Credit: NIST The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) will provide updates on its building failure investigations and related activities during a virtual meeting of the National Construction Safety Team (NCST) Advisory Committee on Sept. 23 and 24, 2026. During this public meeting, NIST team members will highlight progress on their investigations into the impacts of Hurricane Maria on Puerto Rico and the partial collapse of the Champlain Towers South building in Surfside, Florida. They will also provide an update on NIST’s Disaster and Failure Studies Program and detail their responses to the advisory committee’s 2025 recommendations. Anyone wishing to attend the virtual meeting must register by 5 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. Registered attendees who wish to speak during the public comment period may sign up to do so by selecting “yes” to the public comment question on the registration form. Additional details are available in the Federal Register notice . The full meeting agenda is available on the NIST website . In June 2026, NIST released a video detailing its technical findings on the cause of the Champlain Towers South collapse. All other previously released materials relating to these investigations are available on the Hurricane Maria and Champlain Towers South websites. pages.title: Incoming Democratic senators don’t want Chuck Schumer as majority leader | Chuck Schumer | The Guardian
pages.description: New lawmakers from Annie Andrews and Adam Hamilton to Abdul El-Sayed indicate they will not support him
pages.text: Incoming Democratic senators don’t want Chuck Schumer as majority leader | Chuck Schumer | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Chuck Schumer in Washington DC on 4 November 2026. Photograph: Douliery Olivier/Abaca/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Chuck Schumer in Washington DC on 4 November 2026. Photograph: Douliery Olivier/Abaca/Shutterstock Chuck Schumer Incoming Democratic senators don’t want Chuck Schumer as majority leader New lawmakers from Annie Andrews and Adam Hamilton to Abdul El-Sayed indicate they will not support him Ariana Baio in Washington Fri 6 Nov 2026 14.37 EST Last modified on Mon 9 Nov 2026 10.01 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Incoming Democratic senators want someone other than Chuck Schumer to become the next majority leader in the US Senate, although Schumer likely still has enough votes in his caucus to remain the top Democrat. Annie Andrews , the Democratic senator-elect from South Carolina, told Fox News’s Bret Baier on Thursday that the Democratic party needs new leadership. When asked whether she would support Schumer’s leadership bid, she replied: “I still very much believe it’s time for generational change on both sides of the aisle.” Adam Hamilton , the senator-elect from Kansas, told CNN on the campaign trail that he would not support Schumer as the party’s leader. Hamilton, the first Democrat to win a Kansas Senate seat in 94 years, had pitched himself as independent from the Democratic party. Abdul El-Sayed, the senator-elect from Michigan, again declined to support Schumer as the majority leader on CNN on Thursday and said he wanted to consider other options. Other incoming Democrats have also declined to support Schumer, including James Talarico, the senator-elect from Texas; Juliana Stratton , the senator-elect of Illinois; Chris Pappas , the senator-elect of New Hampshire; Peggy Flanagan , the senator-elect of Minnesota; and Troy Jackson , the senator-elect of Maine. Democratic voters have indicated they want newer and younger leadership in the party. Over the last two years, progressive Democrats have scored major victories in local and state elections. It’s led some lawmakers to push for similar changes in decade-old leadership. Schumer, 75, has served as the Democrats’ leader in the Senate since 2017. But Schumer did not appear worried about his bid for Senate majority leader, telling reporters on Wednesday : “I’ll be re-elected as majority leader.” Schumer likely has enough votes within his party to become the next majority leader. He’s also running uncontested as of Friday afternoon – no other Senate Democrat has officially thrown their hat into the ring. But the longtime Democrat has also encouraged members of his party to rally around one another. “The issue is not me … the issue is focusing on the American people and what they want,” Schumer told reporters. After securing a comfortable majority in both the House and Senate, Democrats will head into a new Congress with the ability to push back on Donald Trump’s administration and pass legislation they promised to voters. pages.title: What, Exactly, Is a Turtle? | National Geographic
pages.description: Paleontologists have resolved a decades-old debate over turtle evolution in a new study of 210-million-year-old skull fossils.
pages.text: What, Exactly, Is a Turtle? | National Geographic SCIENCE What, Exactly, Is a Turtle? Paleontologists have resolved a decades-old debate over turtle evolution in a new study of 210-million-year-old skull fossils. Researchers have found that turtles, like this Yellow-spotted River Turtle sunbathing on a log in the Napo River, are closely related to the reptile group known as the archosaurs, which include crocodiles and birds. Thomas P. Peschak, National Geographic Image Collection By Asher Elbein Published August 14, 2026 For decades, paleontologists, herpetologists, and geneticists have all struggled with a surprisingly tricky question: what, precisely, is a turtle? You might think the answer is easy: turtles are reptiles with a bony carapace formed from their ribs and spine, which they can pull their head and legs into whenever they hobble into trouble. But while fossil evidence makes it relatively easy to trace the origins of other reptile families through the great tree of life, turtles have remained a stubborn enigma. Their anatomy—from their shells to their skulls—is so strange and singular that for decades, nobody was sure where they belonged. “It's an incredibly great thing that turtles aren't an extinct reptile lineage because then they would just be this weird mystery that nobody really cared about,” says Brandon Peecook , a National Geographic Explorer and paleontologist previously from the Idaho Museum of Natural History and now at the Denmark Natural History Museum. “But because they're alive, it's so important to figure out what they are.” Now, turtles are coming out of their shell, thanks in part to a study released earlier this summer in the journal Current Biology . In it, Peecook and his colleagues united fossil evidence with pre-existing genetic clues to lock down turtles’ closest relatives: crocodiles and birds, not lizards and snakes. ( Fossilized egg from prehistoric giant turtle reveals baby inside ) That means they are most closely related to the large reptile family known as archosaurs, which also includes dinosaurs and pterosaurs, rather than lepidosaurs, which include lizards, snakes, and the tuatara. The finding helps solve a longstanding fossil mystery and helps researchers better understand how turtles evolved. “I was fist pumping when I saw this,” says James Parham, a paleontologist at California State Fullerton who was not involved in the study. Parham specializes in turtle evolution and even coined the name “Archelosauria” for the combined family of turtles and archosaurs back in 2015, but wasn’t sure he’d live to see the fossil evidence and genetic data line up. “Archosaurs are always the sexiest group, and turtles were always kind of weird and out there. And now it’s like ‘Ah, we’re right next to you, buddy.’” A fossil of Eunotosaurus, a broad-ribbed early reptile that dates back 260 million years. Jonah Choiniere, University of the Witwatersrand The Genetic Clues Since the late 1800s, one of the oldest known turtles was Proganochelys, a 210-million-year-old species from Germany that already had recognizable turtle anatomy, says Xavier Jenkins, a paleontologist at the American Museum of Natural History in New York and lead author of the study. But figuring out who its ancestors were was tricky. Turtle shells—formed out of ribs and vertebrae that have thickened into a surrounding box—are unlike anything else in the fossil record. And while most other reptile groups have two holes at the back of their skull, turtles have none—a trait that they share only with much older reptile groups from the Permian, some 260 million years ago. The obvious answer, many paleontologists concluded, was that turtles’ ancestors were likely much more primitive than those of other reptiles. But nobody could agree on which group of extinct reptiles those ancestors might be, leading some researchers to tentatively place them closer to the lizard and snake side of the reptile family tree. pages.description: حملة "اعملوا الآن" هي حملة الأمم المتحدة للعمل الفردي بشأن تغير المناخ والاستدامة.يمكن لكل فرد منا المساعدة في الحد من ظاهرة الاحتباس الحراري والعناية بكوكبنا، من خلال تغيير عاداتنا واتخاذ خيارات ذات تأثيرات أقل ضررًا على البيئة، ولدينا القدرة على مواجهة تحديات المناخ وبناء عالم أكثر استدامة.
pages.text: اعملوا الآن | الأمم المتحدة Skip to main content Photo: العمل من أجل مستقبلنا المشترك تبنّى الممكن هذا هو نداء أهداف التنمية المستدامة السبعة عشر، وهي مخطط لعالم أفضل. لا يتعين علينا انتظار المستقبل الذي نصبو اليه - يمكننا صنعه الآن. يمكن للجميع الانضمام إلى الحركة العالمية من أجل التغيير. "اعملوا الآن" (ActNow) هي حملة الأمم المتحدة لإلهام الناس للعمل لتحقيق أهداف التنمية المستدامة. يمكن للأهداف تحسين حياة كل فرد منا. هواء أنظف. مدن أكثر أمانًا. المساواة. وظائف أفضل. هذه القضايا تهم الجميع. لكن التقدم بطيء للغاية. علينا أن نتصرف بشكل عاجل لتسريع التغييرات التي تساهم في حياة أفضل على كوكب أكثر صحة. ماذا يحدث عندما يعمل الملايين من الناس معًا من أجل مستقبلنا المشترك؟ الكثير. انضم إلى الحملة لمعرفة المزيد - والقيام بالمزيد. الإجراءات المتخذة في كل أرجاء العالم من خلال تطبيق المحمول وروبوت الدردشة تصور التآزر بين المناخ وأهداف التنمية المستدامة تعرف على الترابطات بين تغير المناخ وثلاثة مواضيع رئيسية من أهداف التنمية المستدامة - المساواة بين الجنسين ، والطاقة المستدامة ، والسلام والأمن - من خلال شرحنا المرئي الجديد. تعد هذه القصص المتعددة الوسائط جزءًا من تعاون ActNow مع Google Arts & Culture وEarthrise ولصالح مشروع Mother Nature ، الذي يستكشف حياة النساء المتأثرات بتغير المناخ في جميع أنحاء العالم. ساحة تايمز سكوير في نيويورك تضاء من أجل السلام في عشية اليوم العالمي للسلام (21 سبتمبر)، أضاءت لوحات إعلانية متعددة في ساحة تايمز سكوير في مدينة نيويورك الليل من أجل السلام. وقد تم تنفيذ هذا النشاط بالتعاون مع شركة OUTFRONT Media ومنظمة الصحة العالمية لدعم حملة ActNow التابعة للأمم المتحدة، حيث شارك في نشر رسائل الأمل والعمل لبناء عالم يسوده السلام معًا. اختر قضيتك قم بإحداث تأثير يتيح لك تطبيق "AWorld" لهاتف المحمول - نظرًا لعدم وجود "كوكب باء" - اختيار وتتبع الإجراءات لتحقيق أهداف التنمية المستدامة. يمكنك أن تطلع على التأثير الذي تحدثه من حيث عدد الإجراءات المتخذة وكذلك المقاييس البيئية مثل ثاني أكسيد الكربون والمياه والكهرباء التي يتم توفيرها. يمكنك أيضًا القيام برحلات تعليمية والمشاركة في تحديات جماعية والحصول على النصائح وإجراء الاختبارات القصيرة، كل ذلك للعمل من أجل مستقبلنا المشترك. تعرفوا بالمزيد نصائح بشأن الطاقة في منزلك لا تزال الكهرباء والتدفئة في منازلنا تُنتج باستخدام الفحم والنفط والغاز كيف يمكنك تقليل بصمة منزلك الكربونية؟ تعرف ذلك هنا. كيف تجعل سفرك صديقًا للبيئة تعمل الطائرات والسيارات في الغالب بالوقود الأحفوري الملوث. تعرف على خيارات النقل المستدامة التي يمكن أن تقلل من تأثيرك على المناخ. أفكار غذائية من أجل كوكب أكثر صحة يساهم إنتاج الأغذية ونقلها والتخلص منها في انبعاثات غازات الدفيئة تعرفوا على الخيارات المفيدة لكم وللكوكب. الفيديو فيديوهات من داعمو حملة "اعملوا الآن" في كل أرجاء العالم الشاهد المغني روني جونز يمكن أن تساعدنا الموسيقى في خلق عالم أكثر استدامة. يؤكد الموسيقار روني جونز على قوة العمل الفردي من خلال أغنيته "المعجزة". https://vimeo.com/466740743 المؤلف كونور فرانتا يتحدث المؤلف كونور فرانتا عن العمل المناخي وتناول وجبات نباتية المصدر. https://vimeo.com/470768963 الممثلة إيلا قرووس تدعوكم الممثلة إيلا قرووس للإنضمام إلى حملة اعملوا الآن! فالتوقيت مناسب الآن للبدء بالعمل.

pages.text: Where to file phone company complaints | USAGov Skip to main content Where to file phone company complaints Learn where to complain about your home phone or cell phone company. Complain to your phone company If you have issues with your phone company's products, services, or billing, begin by contacting the phone company directly. If calling the phone company does not resolve the problem, you may want to write a complaint letter or email. Use this sample complaint letter as a guide to help you explain the problem to your phone company and what you want them to do to resolve it. Complain to the government about your phone company If you are not satisfied with your phone company’s response, contact your state government or the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). Contact your state consumer protection office for help resolving a phone company complaint. Contact the FCC to learn about types of phone company problems and to file a complaint using their online form. LAST UPDATED: November 13, 2025 SHARE THIS PAGE: Have a question? Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Public Input & Actions BLM Christmas Tree Permits Available in Carson City District Starting Nov. 16 Nevada Carson City DO Sierra Front FO Media Contact BLM Nevada Communications BLM_NV_NVSO_Web_mail@blm.gov BLM Office: Sierra Front Field Office November 9, 2026 CARSON CITY, Nev. – The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) Carson City District will begin selling Christmas tree permits on Monday, Nov. 16, online and in-person. The permit is valid from the date of purchase through December 25. To purchase a Christmas tree permit online, visit forestproducts.blm.gov and search for Nevada, Carson City District Office. The cost per Christmas tree permit is $5.00. Upon purchase, a map and permit stipulations will be provided. No more than ten permits may be purchased by one individual; the permits are for individual use only. The permit allows the purchaser to cut only a pinyon pine or juniper tree. Cutting of all other tree species is prohibited. Pinyon pine trees may only be harvested in the Clan Alpine and Desatoya Mountains east of Fallon, and the Excelsior Mountains southeast of Hawthorne. Pinyon pine trees may not be harvested within the Pine Nut Mountains or the Virginia Range due to past fires and habitat conservation. Juniper trees may be harvested on all BLM-administered lands within the Carson City District, except for within Wilderness or Wilderness Study Areas. People should also avoid cutting Christmas trees near city / residential areas. CDC A(H5N1) Bird Flu Response Update February 26, 2025 Feb. 26, 2025 At a glance CDC provides an update on recent developments in the multistate outbreak of avian influenza A(H5N1) virus, or "H5N1 bird flu," in dairy cows, poultry, and other animals in the United States. What to Know In this spotlight, CDC provides an update on recent human infections associated with the ongoing U.S. H5N1 bird flu outbreak in animals. These updates include information on the specific animal exposures and the genetic sequence analysis of the viruses detected from three recently confirmed cases in Nevada, Ohio, and Wyoming. Situation Update February 26, 2025 – CDC continues to respond to the public health challenge posed by a multistate outbreak of avian influenza A(H5N1) virus, or "H5N1 bird flu," in dairy cows, poultry, and other animals in the United States. CDC is working in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR), state public health and animal health officials, and other partners using a One Health approach . Public risk remains low Since April 2024, working with state public health departments, CDC has confirmed H5 bird flu in 70 people in the United States. To date, person-to-person spread of H5 bird flu has not been identified. CDC believes the immediate risk to the general public from H5 bird flu remains low but this risk assessment could change as influenza viruses constantly change. CDC is taking actions to be ready in case the current risk for the public changes. People with dairy cow or poultry exposures remain at greater risk of infection People with job- or recreation-related exposures to infected animals are at increased risk of infection. Most (67 of 70) confirmed human infections in the United States have had exposure to infected or presumed to be infected dairy cows or poultry (the source of exposure could not be determined for three cases). Epidemiology Updates As of February 24, CDC has confirmed three human cases of H5 bird flu in people who became ill in 2025: a dairy worker with exposure to infected dairy cows ( Nevada ), a poultry worker with exposure to infected commercial poultry ( Ohio ), and the owner of an infected backyard poultry flock ( Wyoming ). These are all considered higher-risk exposures . While the dairy worker was not hospitalized, both people with poultry exposures experienced severe illness and were hospitalized. Both hospitalized cases were confirmed positive from lower respiratory specimens, including a bronchoalveolar lavage and sputum. To date, there has been no evidence of onward spread from any of these people to anyone else. The dairy worker in Nevada had conjunctivitis (eye redness and irritation) and has recovered. Most infections associated with U.S. dairy cows to date have involved mild respiratory symptoms or conjunctivitis. This person was exposed to infected dairy cows and tested positive for avian influenza A(H5N1) virus. The poultry worker in Ohio had respiratory symptoms and is home and recovering. This person participated in culling activities on a farm with infected poultry. The initial upper respiratory specimens could not be confirmed as positive for avian influenza A(H5) virus at CDC, so CDC initially reported this as a probable case; a subsequent specimen from the person was confirmed positive for avian influenza A(H5) virus at CDC. pages.title: Brìghde Chaimbeul: Tiny Desk Concert : NPR
pages.description: Brìghde Chaimbeul expands the language of the Scottish smallpipes behind the Desk with a quiet, yet demonstrative presence.
pages.text: Brìghde Chaimbeul: Tiny Desk Concert : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Brìghde Chaimbeul: Tiny Desk Concert Brìghde Chaimbeul expands the language of the Scottish smallpipes behind the Desk with a quiet, yet demonstrative presence. Brìghde Chaimbeul: Tiny Desk Concert October 23, 2026 5:00 AM ET Lars Gotrich Credit: Photo: Vanessa Castilllo/NPR A folk revival only goes so far as an artist's understanding — and adaptation — of tradition. What themes and melodies spoke to the past can easily echo into the present, but come alive through the personality of its interpreter. Brìghde Chaimbeul expands the language of the Scottish smallpipes behind the Desk with a quiet, yet demonstrative presence. Chaimbeul grew up on the Isle of Skye, Scotland, speaking Gaelic and learning the Highland pipes before falling in love with the bellows-blown bagpipe she plays today. Drones are forever with this instrument, but Chaimbeul amplifies, manipulates and darkens the harmonics and frequencies of these pipe drones with effects pedals and contact mics that capture her percussive tapping on the chanter. The effect is mystic and ancient … completely transfixing. Sponsor Message The rhythm of language permeates the songs chosen here — deeply knitting untranslatable wordplay into the drones and melodies. Chaimbeul explains that the opening title, when said in Gaelic — which roughly means "sound of drones beginning to be tuned and sound of drones almost tuned" — sounds like "the rhythm of the words sound like the pulse of drones tuning." "She Went Astray," a song found by Scottish folklorist Peigi MacRae in 1934, is awash with a tonal cluster of tidal chords by Shahzad Ismaily , who, on synths, is naturally attuned to Chaimbeul's pipes throughout this performance. When she sings on "Pìobaireachd Nan Eun," it's to mimic the sounds of birds and swans — and in concert with drones that buzz and trill, it's a musical reminder of just how sublime and unknown the animal kingdom can be. For Chaimbeul, tradition is transformative. And that's none more apparent than in this version of "Bog an Lochan." The Scottish reel has several names and a long history, yet in her ecstatic repetition and ethereal ambience, Chaimbeul opens a gateway to another dimension. pages.title: Adam Hamilton wins in Kansas to become state’s first Democrat in Senate since 1932 | US midterm elections 2026 | The Guardian
pages.description: Pastor clinches victory over incumbent Roger Marshall in state that emerged as unexpected battleground this year
pages.text: Adam Hamilton wins in Kansas to become state’s first Democrat in Senate since 1932 | US midterm elections 2026 | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Adam Hamilton, who has beaten Roger Marshall in Kansas. Composite: The Guardian/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Adam Hamilton, who has beaten Roger Marshall in Kansas. Composite: The Guardian/Getty Images US midterm elections 2026 Adam Hamilton wins in Kansas to become state’s first Democrat in Senate since 1932 Pastor clinches victory over incumbent Roger Marshall in state that emerged as unexpected battleground this year Track results from all 50 states Gaya Gupta in Overland Park, Kansas, and Rachel Leingang Wed 4 Nov 2026 02.45 EST First published on Tue 3 Nov 2026 23.29 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Adam Hamilton has clinched a historic victory in the US Senate race in Kansas, fueling the country’s Democratic takeover of Congress as voters in key battleground states expressed frustration with Donald Trump. It’s the first time a Democrat has been elected to represent Kansas in the Senate since 1932. With his victory speech, Hamilton, a longtime pastor, transformed a crowded hotel ballroom into his own congregation, his podium into a pulpit. Speaking at a hotel in Overland Park, he recited Bible passages and the parable of the Good Samaritan in his address. “Do unto others as you’d have them do unto you,” he said, citing Matthew 7:12 in the Bible that’s more commonly known as “the golden rule”. “What does it look like in Washington if they actually did that? How would our policies and our politics change if we treated people this way?” Hamilton defeated the Republican incumbent, Roger Marshall, 66, who served as US senator for the state since 2021 and was elected to the US House of Representatives for two terms. But it was Marshall’s work as an obstetrician that factored heavily into his re-election campaign, after the New York Times reported that he had sued hundreds of his patients for unpaid bills, including dozens who were arrested after missing their court dates. Kansas emerged as an unexpected battleground this year. The closely watched Cook Political Report rated the race as a toss-up, noting it was one of several agriculture-heavy areas to be hit hard by high fuel and fertilizer prices because of Trump’s war on Iran. Hamilton ultimately won over Marshall with 51.1% of the vote, according to the AP’s tally as of early Wednesday morning. Democratic pastor Hamilton, 62, leads the largest United Methodist congregation in the country, United Methodist Church of the Resurrection based in the Kansas City area. He calls himself an “independent-minded Democrat” and had argued Kansas would benefit from having one US senator from each party. The state’s other seat is held by Republican Jerry Moran. Hamilton, who has frequently said that decency was on the ballot, pledged to become “Jerry Moran’s best friend” and bring members of both parties together to “solve problems, like it used to be”. “In deeply red Kansas, the heart of America, I want us to model what it looks like when thoughtful people actually work together to solve problems, instead of slinging mud at each other,” he said. Trump won Kansas handily in 2024, and sought to inspire Republican turnout by hosting rallies in the state leading up to election day. But Marshall’s liabilities, particularly the medical billing scandal, and Hamilton’s attempt at a pragmatic bipartisan appeal helped tighten the race this year. Several of the counties Marshall won in 2020 flipped for Hamilton this year, according to AP election data, and even the counties he did win were by much narrower margins than in his last election. Hamilton, who branded himself as a centrist with the slogan, “leading from the middle”, joined several other “prairie populists” this year to win over Republican strongholds by leaning on populist messaging and vowing to stand up to corruption and corporate interests. pages.title: The ‘Blessed Lizard’ That Inherited the Earth After Its Worst Apocalypse | National Geographic
pages.description: Shakajlura riojanensis, a newly discovered Triassic apex predator, ruled the land millions of years before the rise of giant dinosaurs.
pages.text: The ‘Blessed Lizard’ That Inherited the Earth After Its Worst Apocalypse | National Geographic SCIENCE The ‘Blessed Lizard’ That Inherited the Earth After Its Worst Apocalypse Shakajlura riojanensis , a newly discovered Triassic apex predator, ruled the land millions of years before the rise of giant dinosaurs. Emerging from the ashes of the planet’s worst mass extinction, Shakajlura riojanensis was an ancient crocodile cousin that reigned over the Triassic before large dinosaurs appeared. By Joshua Rapp Learn Published August 12, 2026 Paleontologists in Argentina have discovered a deadly prehistoric crocodile with “blade-like serrated” teeth that triumphed over the Triassic some 237 million years ago, before large dinosaurs arrived and usurped the throne. “We consider these as the apex predators of the Triassic,” says Ariel Cardillo, a doctoral candidate in vertebrate paleontology at Argentina’s National Scientific and Technical Research Council (CONICET) and lead author of the study. “They were really large animals compared to the rest of the ecosystem.” From snarling snout to tail, the new species Shakajlura riojanensis would have been nearly 20 feet long. “This may not look like much, but in the Triassic, most of the fauna is pretty small,” Cardillo says. Shakajlura ’s bite was likely as powerful as modern-day crocs, and every tooth was “like a knife pointing out of the mouth,” he adds. Cardillo and his colleagues published their discovery earlier this summer in the journal Papers in Palaeontology . ( Did this ancient croc hunt dinosaurs on land? ) Shakajlura also provides paleontologists with insight into a poorly understood period in Earth’s history when wildlife bounced back from “The Great Dying.” This cataclysmic event ended the Permian some 252 million years ago and is perhaps the largest mass extinction the planet has ever experienced. “Terrestrial ecosystems are really starting to get back into where they were before the big extinction,” says Keegan Melstrom , a paleontologist at the University of Central Oklahoma who was not involved in the work. “If you survived this mass extinction, you basically get to inherit the Earth.” A ‘Blessed Lizard’ In 2017, Cardillo’s colleagues were excavating a Late Triassic fossil deposit in the Chañares Formation in Argentina’s La Rioja province when they noticed part of an upper jawbone sticking out of the rock. They extracted it along with several more fossils and sent them to the La Plata Museum . In total, the team had found skull bones, parts of the upper and lower jaws, a backbone, limb fragments, and an almost complete hip bone. Together, the fossils clued the team in that they had uncovered a paracrocodylomorph, an ancient cousin of crocodiles. They chose the name Shakajlura riojanensis because it refers, in part, to the La Rioja province where the fossil was found. “Shakajlura” is a translation from Kakán, a language spoken by the Diaguita Indigenous people who live in the region, that means “blessed lizard.” The name references the rarity of the find—the last fossil from this group discovered in Argentina was described in 1997, nearly three decades ago. ( This ancient croc was bigger than most dinosaurs ) SCIENCE New megaraptor discovered—with its final meal still in its mouth SCIENCE Is Ichthyotitan the largest marine reptile yet known? SCIENCE The 11 most astonishing scientific discoveries of 2023 Shakajlura likely used its dagger-filled jaws to chow on prey such as dicynodonts, large herbivores that were ungulate-like precursors of mammals. Since Shakajlura likely wasn’t aquatic—it took millions of years before crocodilians adapted to a more marine lifestyle— it may have used its legs and upright posture to chase down prey rather than relying on ambushing like its modern-day relative, says Cardillo. pages.text: About Us | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content About Us Mission The U.S. Department of Labor established the Center for Faith in response to the historic Executive Order that recognized the essential role of faith-based organizations in supporting our communities. The Center for Faith engages with faith-based organizations to maximize their participation in grant funding opportunities and minimize regulatory burdens. Our goal is engaging faith organizations to defend religious liberty and lift up individuals through the dignity of work and self-sufficiency; and to combat anti-Christian, anti-Semitic bias, as well as all forms of religious discrimination. pages.description: Las infecciones urinarias (IU) son infecciones comunes y generalmente requieren de antibióticos para su tratamiento.

Los sitios web seguros .gov usan HTTPS Un candado ( ) o https:// significa que usted se conectó de forma segura a un sitio web .gov. Comparta información sensible sólo en sitios web oficiales y seguros. el 17 abril del 2024 English (US) Información básica sobre las infecciones urinarias Puntos clave ¿Siente dolor o ardor al orinar? Podría tener una infección urinaria (IU). Los antibióticos tratan las infecciones urinarias. Su proveedor de atención médica puede determinar si tiene una infección urinaria y qué antibiótico necesita. Información general El aparato urinario incluye la vejiga, la uretra y los riñones (ver figura). Las infecciones urinarias son infecciones comunes que ocurren cuando entran bacterias a la uretra, generalmente de la piel o el recto, e infectan el aparato urinario. Aparato urinario de la mujer, incluidas la vejiga y la uretra. Esta imagen muestra cómo las bacterias en la piel o el recto pueden subir por la uretra y causar una infección de vejiga. Show More Tipos y cepas Infección de la vejiga (más común, también conocida como cistitis). Infección de los riñones (menos común pero más grave, también conocida como pielonefritis). Infórmese más: Infecciones de las vías urinarias relacionadas con el uso de sondas Signos y síntomas Los síntomas de una infección de la vejiga pueden incluir: Dolor o ardor al orinar Orinar con frecuencia Sentir la necesidad de orinar a pesar de que la vejiga esté vacía Sangre en la orina Presión o calambres en la ingle o la parte inferior del abdomen Los síntomas de una infección de los riñones pueden incluir: Fiebre Escalofríos Dolor en la parte baja de la espalda o en el costado Náuseas o vómitos Los niños más pequeños probablemente no puedan decirle los síntomas de infección urinaria que tienen. Aunque la fiebre es el signo de infección urinaria más común en los bebés y los niños pequeños, la mayoría de los niños que tienen fiebre no tienen una infección urinaria. Factores de riesgo Las infecciones urinarias son más comunes en las mujeres porque la uretra de las mujeres es más corta y está más cerca del recto. Esto facilita la entrada de bacterias al aparato urinario. Otros factores de riesgo: Una infección urinaria anterior. Actividad sexual reciente. Cambios en las bacterias que viven dentro de la vagina o en la flora vaginal. Por ejemplo, la menopausia o el uso de espermicidas pueden causar estos cambios. Embarazo. Edad (los adultos mayores y los niños pequeños tienen más probabilidades de contraer infecciones urinarias). Problemas estructurales en el aparato urinario, como agrandamiento de la próstata. Mala higiene, por ejemplo, en los niños que están aprendiendo a ir al baño. Prevención Orinar después de la actividad sexual Mantenerse bien hidratado Ducharse en vez de tomar un baño Minimizar el uso de duchas vaginales, aerosoles o talcos en el área genital Enseñarles a las niñas que estén aprendiendo a ir al baño a limpiarse desde adelante hacia atrás Cuándo buscar atención médica Si usted o su hijo/a tienen síntomas de infección urinaria o cualquier síntoma intenso o preocupante. Hable con su proveedor de atención médica de inmediato‎ Si su hijo/a tiene menos de 3 meses de vida y fiebre de 100.4 °F (38 °C) o más. Diagnóstico Para determinar si usted tiene una infección urinaria, su proveedor de atención médica hará lo siguiente: Preguntarle sobre los síntomas Un examen físico Ordenar análisis de orina, de ser necesario Recetarle un antibiótico para tratar la infección urinaria, de ser necesario Tratamiento La mayoría de las infecciones urinarias se pueden tratar en la casa con antibióticos recetados por un proveedor de atención médica. ICYMI: DOE National Lab and Nuclear Weapons Directors Voice Support for Commonsense Permitting Reforms U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright received strong support from the Department of Energy’s (DOE) National Lab and nuclear weapons assembly plant directors after he announced expedited permitting reforms for construction projects on Energy Department lands. Energy.gov April 3, 2025 Estimated Read Time min GOLDEN, COLORADO— U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright received strong support from the Department of Energy’s (DOE) National Lab and nuclear weapons assembly plant directors after he announced expedited permitting reforms for construction projects on Energy Department lands. These common sense reforms will save at least hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars and rapidly accelerate project completion dates, helping better unleash American innovation, restore energy dominance, and modernize America’s nuclear stockpiles. What America’s National Lab Directors Are Saying: "The recent guidance issued by the Department of Energy related to how the Laboratory executes our construction activities is intended to provide new tools to improve our operations and increase our effectiveness. This guidance will have positive impacts on our construction scheduling, budgeting, work execution and safety. We believe this guidance will have a net positive impact on most of our construction activities now costing less than $300,000,000 including, Energetic Materials Characterization modular facilities and Pajarito Corridor Office Complexes (PCOCs). The new guidance will save the federal government tens of millions of dollars on projects at LANL like these by reducing costs and avoiding overruns due to delays. In addition, allowing the Laboratory to better utilize existing Occupational Health and Safety Administration standards (OHSA) will increase the number of construction companies that can bid on work at LANL and provide a more competitive bidding process that will assist in lowing the costs of construction." — Los Alamos National Laboratory Director Thom Mason "I appreciate Secretary Wright’s bold action to empower the National Laboratories to more efficiently deliver transformative scientific and technological outcomes that will benefit American taxpayers. This is the most substantive and quickest change in improving lab operations that I have seen in my many years with DOE.” — Pacific Northwest National Laboratory Director Dr. Steven Ashby "Secretary Wright's decisive actions in easing permitting rules and regulations for construction projects at the Department of Energy's National Labs are welcome progress. These reforms are a significant step forward in accelerating critical infrastructure improvements, ensuring that our National Labs can continue their vital work. Ames National Laboratory is soon to launch several major infrastructure improvement projects across its campus, projects that are necessary to continue to meet our scientific mission and the mission of the Department of Energy. These reforms will expedite our ability to meet the needs of our researchers and engineers, and continue our pursuit of delivering critical materials solutions to the nation." — Ames National Laboratory Director Adam Schwartz "Sandia National Laboratories welcomes the Department of Energy’s move to simplify permitting for critical infrastructure upgrades. pages.title: Democrat Annie Andrews flips South Carolina Senate seat held by Republicans since 1998 | US midterm elections 2026 | The Guardian double quotation mark double quotation mark
pages.description: Andrews ran a campaign on healthcare affordability and beat Darline Graham, sister of Lindsey Graham to win the race
pages.text: Democrat Annie Andrews flips South Carolina Senate seat held by Republicans since 1998 | US midterm elections 2026 | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Annie Andrews had faced an uphill battle. Illustration: Guardian Design / Getty Images View image in fullscreen Annie Andrews had faced an uphill battle. Illustration: Guardian Design / Getty Images US midterm elections 2026 Democrat Annie Andrews flips South Carolina Senate seat held by Republicans since 1998 Andrews ran a campaign on healthcare affordability and beat Darline Graham, sister of Lindsey Graham to win Track results from all 50 states Lois Beckett and George Chidi Wed 4 Nov 2026 07.51 EST First published on Tue 3 Nov 2026 22.16 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Democrat Annie Andrews , a pediatrician who campaigned on healthcare affordability, has won the race for US Senate in South Carolina , making her the first Democrat to represent the state in the Senate for over a quarter century. Andrews had faced an uphill battle in what has been seen as a reliably Republican state against Darline Graham, the sister of the late Republican powerbroker Lindsey Graham. “I think we just made some history,” Andrews said to exuberant supporters in Charleston on Tuesday night at her victory party. “South Carolina, you have shown the nation what is possible. You have shown the nation that in this era of partisan divides, of vitriol and name calling, in a politics dominated by billionaires and special interest groups and insiders in Washington DC, that we will not bow down, that we will not back down, and we will chart our own course.” Andrews called her candidacy a defense of South Carolina against external forces. “Tonight we here in South Carolina sent a clear message that this Senate seat does not belong to one family, one party, or to Washington DC” The 62-year-old Graham, who had been appointed by South Carolina’s governor to serve out the remainder of her brother’s term after he died in July aged 71, had been publicly urged to run for office by Donald Trump, who enthusiastically campaigned for her and denigrated her Democratic opponent, including referring to Andrews using a transphobic slur. But Graham’s lack of national political experience – she admitted she was “not that informed on national security” when asked about US policy on Taiwan during a debate in August – is believed to have made the race more competitive. The last time South Carolina elected a Democrat to the Senate was in 1998, but a New York Times/Siena poll the week before the election had the two candidates neck and neck, both polling at 48%. Graham had stayed close to Trump in her platform, including saying she fully trusted Trump on tariffs and the war with Iran, which is deeply unpopular with a majority of Americans . Andrews, in contrast, had called the war with Iran “illegal” and criticized its effect on gas prices. Andrews said in September she wanted to “find our way out of this illegal, unconstitutional billion-dollar-a-day war overseas”. Andrews had tried to separate herself from other Democrats on several issues, and faced criticism from LGBTQ+ advocates for an ad she aired in the final month of the campaign, in which she referred to trans women as “biological men” and said she did not “support and haven’t ever performed gender surgery for minors”. In 2022, Andrews had referred to South Carolina’s Save Women’s Sports Act as “actively harmful”, and wrote on X , “I will always support trans youth.” The election marks the first time South Carolina has elected a woman to the Senate, nearly a century after Hattie Caraway of Arkansas became the first female US senator, in 1932. As of October, 15 US states still have never had a woman as a US senator , including several liberal north-eastern states, including Pennsylvania, Connecticut, New Jersey and Vermont. pages.title: This UK seaside town is a fossil hunter's paradise | National Geographic
pages.description: Famed for its excellent fossil-hunting beaches, this Georgian town on Dorset’s Jurassic Coast offers plenty of seaside distractions, from paleontology walks to seafood feasts with a view.
pages.text: This UK seaside town is a fossil hunter's paradise | National Geographic TRAVEL Why the U.K.'s fossil capital is the perfect seaside getaway Famed for its excellent fossil-hunting beaches, this Georgian town on Dorset’s Jurassic Coast offers plenty of seaside distractions, from paleontology walks to seafood feasts with a view. The harbour wall of Lyme Regis is also known as The Cobb. Thomas Faull, Getty Images By Jessica Prupas Published August 1, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Were you to dig below Lyme Regis’ bunting-slung streets, you’d hit a geological marvel: the Blue Lias. This vast sequence of limestone and shale layers, formed during the Mesozoic era some 200 million years ago, reveals fossils as it erodes, making the town one of Europe’s most important paleontological centres. It’s a badge locals wear proudly: you’ll find a weather-beaten statue of celebrated fossil hunter Mary Anning overlooking Church Cliff Beach. In 1823, while wandering Lyme Regis’s coastline, she unearthed the world’s first complete skeleton of a Plesiosaurus and, nearly two centuries after her death, the town remains a magnet for excavators. Lyme Regis' seafront is a walkable promenade best discovered at dusk. Graham Custance, Getty Images Where should I begin? The main strip is Front Beach, which fringes the promenade with its wash of pastel huts. On its western end, you’ll find Shoreline Sauna , whose wood-fired, Nordic-style saunas sit right on the sand. Close by is the Cobb: a man-made harbour featured in the novel Persuasion by Lyme Regis habitué Jane Austen. It leads off Monmouth Beach, a quieter, pebbled stretch popular among fossil hunters scouring for ammonites — those distinctive, spiralled molluscs that have become a symbol of the town. You can learn more about Lyme Regis’s prehistoric residents at the Dinosaurland Fossil Museum , home to a collection of more than 30,000 specimens, including a dolphin-like ichthyosaur unearthed nearby and the skull of a vast, carnivorous mosasaur. The museum also organises fossil walks run by local palaeontologists, with the chance to collect fossilised bullet-shaped belemnites — the shells of squid-like creatures that once swam the oceans. Did you know? Lyme Regis local Mary Anning was just 12 years old when she discovered the famous ichthyosaur skeleton now housed in London’s Natural History Museum. What else is there beyond the fossils? The Cobb is the launch point for Lyme Rib Rides , whose sightseeing cruises zip along the coast. Choose between the exhilarating, 20-minute ‘Lyme dash’ or the hour-long cruise that passes towering cliffs and secret coves. Otherwise, head up the stairs linking Monmouth Beach with the South West Coast Path — a 630-mile trail tracing this wave-lashed corner of England. Walk west for an hour and you hit the Axmouth to Lyme Regis Undercliffs National Nature Reserve. The distinctive character of this seven-mile stretch of coastline was formed by a succession of landslides, yielding undulating bluffs and diverse woodland. Back in Lyme Regis, visit the Town Mill : the site dates back to 1340 and its 17th-century watermill has been painstakingly restored by volunteers. It’s become a home to local businesses including art studios, a vintage-inspired boutique and a potter’s workshop, plus Lyme Regis Brewery , whose craft beers go down a treat in the courtyard. A boat ride is an exhilarating way to see Lyme Regis’s coastline. Lyme Bay Rib Rides At Rockfish, TV chef Mitch Tonks serves sustainable seafood with views over Lyme Bay. Ed Ovenden Where’s good for food? Start your day at Kiosk , on Front Beach, serving sausage- or halloumi-stuffed breakfast bagels that are best enjoyed while reclining on a sunlounger on the shingle. For lunch or dinner, there’s Sandro’s , a dinky, family-run operation masterminded by ex-River Cottage chef Alessandro Strillozzi. pages.title: Democrat Chris Pappas wins New Hampshire Senate race to become first out gay male senator | US midterm elections 2026 | The Guardian double quotation mark
pages.description: Pappas focused campaign against Republican John Sununu on serving as a bulwark against Trump administration
pages.text: Democrat Chris Pappas wins New Hampshire Senate race to become first out gay male senator | US midterm elections 2026 | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Chris Pappas meets supporters as he arrives to vote in Manchester, New Hampshire. Photograph: Kylie Cooper/Reuters View image in fullscreen Chris Pappas meets supporters as he arrives to vote in Manchester, New Hampshire. Photograph: Kylie Cooper/Reuters US midterm elections 2026 Democrat Chris Pappas wins New Hampshire Senate race to become first out gay male senator Pappas focused campaign against Republican John Sununu on serving as a bulwark against Trump administration US midterm elections – live updates Track live results from all 50 states Shrai Popat and Lex McMenamin in Manchester, New Hampshire Wed 4 Nov 2026 01.57 EST First published on Tue 3 Nov 2026 20.22 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Chris Pappas , the four-term Democratic congressman, has won New Hampshire ’s US Senate race, making him the first out gay man to serve in the upper chamber. Pappas, 46, is a centrist voice in the US House who has at times broken with his party on major legislation. He focused his Senate campaign on serving as a bulwark against the Trump administration, which is unpopular in the Granite state, and defeated the former senator John Sununu in a closely fought contest. With 20% of the vote in, Sununu officially conceded to Pappas. As screens at Pappas’s election night watch party in Manchester switched to Sununu’s concession speech, the room erupted into screams, with the crowd chanting: “Let’s go Pappas!” The race had become a late source of anxiety for Democrats, with Pappas, a moderate, locked in a neck-and-neck battle with Sununu to succeed Jeanne Shaheen, the retiring Democratic senator. On Tuesday evening, Pappas thanked Sununu for a “very gracious” call to concede. “Tonight’s results are a wake-up call for corporate special interests and billionaires who have been rigging the economy, for the cowards in Congress who have enabled healthcare cuts, tariffs and war – and for the incompetent president who can’t even be bothered to care how people are being hurt,” Pappas said to the crowd. “Tonight, voters in New Hampshire , and all across the country, simply have had enough and are demanding a change in direction. I am ready to fight with everything I’ve got to deliver the change that we need.” Republicans were hoping to flip this New Hampshire Senate seat – will Trump get in the way? Read more Though Pappas, a longtime Granite state elected official, was the establishment Democratic candidate, his victory speech echoed much of the rhetoric of the populist candidates who have seen success this cycle – from Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan to James Talarico in Texas – and the crowd ate it up. With his husband Vann Bentley beside him, Pappas pledged to fight for reproductive freedom and, to even louder cheers, against the creation of datacenters and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention facilities. “This was a hard-fought victory tonight,” said Pappas. “It was made even harder by the tens and tens of millions of dollars that poured into New Hampshire from Donald Trump, Elon Musk and corporate special interests who are just fine with the way things are going right now. “They threw money, attack ads, and outright lies at us every day for months,” added Pappas, addressing the gathered campaign staffers, volunteers, supporters, and local Democratic officials. “But we beat them anyway, didn’t we?” Pappas secured endorsements from several prominent Democrats and portrayed Sununu, who once called Donald Trump a “ loser ”, as a faux moderate who would ultimately rubber-stamp the president’s agenda. Pappas sought to capitalize on the Trump administration’s low approval ratings, highlighting a range of unpopular policies on the campaign trail, from the war against Iran to Medicaid cuts included in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Scorpions Shine During Popular Night Hikes at Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area in Nevada Nov 6, 2026 A group of participants explores a desert trail at night using ultraviolet flashlights during a guided hike. (Photo courtesy of TJ Lopez, volunteer) As the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) marks 80 years of stewardship , Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area continues to create memorable experiences that inspire curiosity, learning, and a deeper connection to public lands. The conservation area is inspiring appreciation for one of the Mojave Desert's most misunderstood residents through its increasingly popular Scorpion Search Night Hikes. Led by BLM rangers, these evening programs invite participants to explore the desert after sunset and discover the fascinating world of nocturnal wildlife. Using ultraviolet blacklights, visitors can observe scorpions glowing bright green as they emerge from their daytime shelters to hunt and forage across the desert landscape. Along the way, rangers share information about scorpion biology, behavior, and their important role in maintaining healthy desert ecosystems. The hikes have quickly become one of Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area's most sought-after interpretive programs. Interest has grown significantly in recent years as word has spread about the unique experience. Participants travel from across the Las Vegas Valley and beyond for the opportunity to experience Red Rock Canyon after dark while learning about wildlife that many visitors rarely encounter. Under ultraviolet light, a desert hairy scorpion glows bright green along a trail in Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area. The unique fluorescence helps participants locate scorpions during guided Scorpion Search Night Hikes. (Photo courtesy of TJ Lopez, volunteer) Beyond showcasing scorpions, the hikes support broader efforts to connect the public with the nighttime environment of Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area. The programs are made possible through collaboration between the BLM and community partners working to promote night sky stewardship, public education, and responsible outdoor recreation. These efforts also support Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area 's pursuit of Urban Night Sky Place designation through DarkSky International . The guided hikes provide an opportunity to educate visitors about responsible nighttime recreation. Participants learn how artificial light affects wildlife, why darkness is an important natural resource, and how nocturnal species have adapted to thrive in the Mojave Desert. Many attendees leave with a greater understanding of the ecological importance of preserving natural darkness and protecting the habitats that support diverse desert wildlife. Participants guided by Parker Ranger Sydney Tuiofea gather on a trail during a Scorpion Search Night Hike. (Photo courtesy of TJ Lopez, volunteer) Scorpion Search Night Hikes continue to be offered seasonally throughout the warmer months and remain a valuable tool for engaging new audiences with public lands. By combining hands-on discovery, outdoor recreation, and environmental education, the program helps visitors develop a deeper appreciation for the unique resources that make Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area a special place both day and night. pages.title: The Odyssey is fiction. But its monsters and magic may have been based on real science. | National Geographic
pages.description: Odysseus faced the cyclops, his men turned into pigs, and he sailed between a six-headed monster and a whirlpool. Each of these, it turns out, have potential real-life explanations.
pages.text: The Odyssey is fiction. But its monsters and magic may have been based on real science. | National Geographic Premium SCIENCE The Odyssey is fiction. But its monsters and magic may have been based on real science. Odysseus faced the cyclops, his men turned into pigs, and he sailed between a six-headed monster and a whirlpool. Each of these, it turns out, have potential real-life explanations. In Homer's epic poem, Odysseus blinded the cyclops Polyphemus. Researchers have suggested that ancient people might have encountered fossils that could have resembled a giant, one-eyed creature. Alfredo Dagli Orti, Art Resource, NY By Bethany Brookshire Published July 17, 2026 The Odyssey is a myth. It’s doubtful that a man took a literal decade to make it from Troy on the coast of modern-day Turkey to the Greek island of Ithaca after the Trojan War, cursed to make love to witches, journey to Hades, and pick fights with a cyclops. Or at least, if he did take that long, his curse probably involved not asking for directions. But the tale of Odysseus’ extra-long journey home contains hints of things that people might have encountered in the ancient world, from a real-life cyclops to killer whirlpools and hallucinogenic plants. As Matt Damon steps into the famous wanderer’s sandals in The Odyssey on July 17, here are some of the scientific realities behind his legendary side quests. ( How do we know what ancient Greek warriors wore in battle? ) The cyclops In the story, the cyclops Polyphemus—a giant with a taste for human flesh, and of course, only one eye in the center of his head—traps Odysseus’ crew and munches a few for lunch. Odysseus blinds Polyphemus with a heated spear, and the men make their escape, tied to the bellies of Polyphemus’ sheep. One hypothesis for the origin of this mythical one-eyed giant lies in the fossils of Deinotherium giganteum , an elephant relative that roamed Europe, Asia and Africa between 23 and 8 million years ago . Paleontologists have unearthed its bones on the island of Crete, where the ancient Greeks could have come across them as well. Elephant skulls have relatively small eye holes, with a massive hole in the center. That hole is for the trunk. But as the elephants stood 15 feet (4.6 meters) tall at the shoulder, the huge skull might have been mistaken for the head of a huge, one-eyed person. But the Greeks could also have been familiar with cyclopia , a rare and deadly congenital defect where the eye sockets and brain don’t properly divide as the human embryo develops. Instead of a nose, the fetus grows a tubular appendage, which usually appears above a single eye. Cyclopia occurs in only one out of every 100,000 human births. Sadly, 39 percent are stillborn, and those that survive birth do not survive longer than 13 hours. While it is a very rare condition, scientists have estimated that at the time of The Odyssey , about 53 cases of human cyclopia would have been born around the world every year. In addition, other species can also exhibit cyclopia, including sheep, cattle and goats, especially if the mothers eat plants like hellebore. The monster and the whirlpool Odysseus made a clever escape from Polyphemus, but trapped between the six-headed sea monster Scylla and the mighty whirlpool Charybdis, he wasn’t so lucky. He loses his crew in a mighty storm, and morning finds Odysseus swept between the two. The dangerous passage has its basis in a real place—the Strait of Messina, a narrow channel that runs between Calabria in Italy and the island of Sicily. In the strait, the Ionian Sea meets the Tyrrhenian Sea, and the two bodies of water have opposing tides—high tide in the Ionian is low tide in the Tyrrhenian, and vice versa, says Sergio Longhitano , a sedimentologist at the University of Basilicata in Italy, who published a 2018 paper on the strait ’s tricky waters. pages.title: Faith Organizations Tips for Programs/Grants | U.S. Department of Labor
pages.text: Faith Organizations Tips for Programs/Grants | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Faith Organizations Tips for Programs/Grants On February 7, 2025, President Trump established the White House Faith Office via Executive Order 14205 , building on his efforts to ensure faith organizations can compete fairly for federal funds to provide essential social services. The executive order called for each federal agency to have a Center for Faith, and the Department of Labor quickly instituted an office staffed by Administration appointees to complete this important work. The President directed the White House Faith Office to lead ten initiatives for policy development ( White House FO Fact Sheet ). These initiatives reaffirm that faith organizations enjoy constitutional and Federal statutory protections for religious liberty and should have the opportunity to fully and actively participate in addressing critical issues like poverty, substance use disorder recovery, and community revitalization. This guidance reflects the Administration's commitment to protecting religious liberty, promoting economic opportunities, and fostering partnerships that build upon the documented successes of faith groups in serving Americans in need. Across the United States, millions of Americans face challenges including homelessness ( NCH: Homelessness in the US ), substance use disorder ( Addiction Statistics ), unemployment ( Civilian Unemployment Rate ), and family instability ( UT PRC: Children's Household Instability ). Faith organizations have long been instrumental in providing compassionate care, often filling gaps left by government programs. The Trump Administration recognizes these groups are most effective when they have equal opportunity to compete for federal resources, provided they adhere to constitutional and legal guidelines. The Center for Faith at the Department of Labor is tasked with ensuring that qualified faith organizations can partner with the Department to deliver critical employment and training services, particularly in areas such as job training, apprenticeship programs, and reemployment services for underserved populations. This guidance aligns with the Administration's focus on economic recovery, workforce empowerment and reducing regulatory barriers. Core Principles for the Department of Labor's Center for Faith: Equal Opportunity : Faith-based organizations must be eligible, on the same basis as any other organizations, to seek DOL support or participate in DOL programs for which they are otherwise eligible, and DOL must not discriminate on the basis of an organization's religious character, motives, or affiliation. Religious Liberty : Faith-based organizations that are DOL Service Providers retain their autonomy, right of expression, religious character, and ability to practice their religious beliefs, provided that they do not use direct Federal funds to support or engage in any explicitly religious activities. Service to All : Department of Labor funds must be used to provide services to all eligible individuals, regardless of their religious beliefs, and cannot support explicitly religious activities. Focus on Workforce Outcomes : The Department of Labor prioritizes programs that align with the Administration's economic goals, such as job creation, apprenticeship expansion, and reemployment, particularly for communities impacted by economic downturns or the opioid crisis. Accessing the Department of Labor's Federal Grants The federal government offers two primary types of grants which may be relevant to faith-based and community organizations: Discretionary Grants : Often directly awarded by federal agencies. Formula Grants : Funds distributed primarily to states, cities, or counties, which may then allocate resources to local organizations – including faith-based organizations. The Department of Labor offers a range of funding opportunities through discretionary grants and formula grants. Faith organizations

DOE Identifies 16 Federal Sites Across the Country for Data Center and AI Infrastructure Development Energy Secretary Chris Wright acts to strengthen America’s energy dominance and leadership in artificial intelligence by leveraging federal land and assets Energy.gov April 3, 2025 Estimated Read Time min GOLDEN, COLORADO —The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced plans to help ensure America leads the world in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and lower energy costs by co-locating data centers and new energy infrastructure on DOE lands. DOE has released a Request for Information (RFI) to inform possible use of DOE land for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure development to support growing demand for data centers. DOE has identified 16 potential sites uniquely positioned for rapid data center construction, including in-place energy infrastructure with the ability to fast-track permitting for new energy generation such as nuclear. In accordance with President Trump‘s Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence and Unleashing American Energy Executive Orders, DOE is exploring opportunities to accelerate AI and energy infrastructure development across the country, prioritizing public-private partnerships to advance the use of innovative technologies and strategies. “The global race for AI dominance is the next Manhattan project, and with President Trump’s leadership and the innovation of our National Labs, the United States can and will win,” Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said . “With today’s action, the Department of Energy is taking important steps to leverage our domestic resources to power the AI revolution, while continuing to deliver affordable, reliable and secure energy to the American people.” “President Trump is committed to ensuring American leadership in artificial intelligence and Secretary Wright is delivering,” said White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios . “The Trump Administration will unleash Federal resources to build out the data resources needed for an AI-powered future.” The Department is seeking input from data center developers, energy developers, and the broader public to further advance this partnership. The information collected will be used to inform development, encourage private-public partnerships and enable the construction of AI infrastructure at select DOE sites with a target of commencing operation by the end of 2027. The sites also offer the industry a chance to partner with DOE’s world-class research facilities co-located on the sites, furthering advancements in both the power systems design needed to run the centers and developing next-generation data center hardware. Publicly available information about each site, including location, available acreage, and other characteristics is provided in appendices to the RFI. Additionally, the RFI aims to gather information on potential development approaches, technology solutions, operational models, and economic considerations associated with establishing AI infrastructure. The national preserve designation enables the land to be federally protected, but also allows for public hunting, trapping, fishing, oil and gas exploration, and subsistence use (although state permits for some of these activities are still required). pages.title: مؤتمر القمة المعني بالمستقبل | الأمم المتحدة
pages.description: مؤتمر القمة المعني بالمستقبل: حلول متعددة الأطراف من أجل غد أفضل. 22 و23 أيلول/سبتمبر 2024. مؤتمر القمة حدث رفيع المستوى، يجتمع فيه قادة العالم للتوصل إلى توافق دولي جديد في الآراء بشأن كيفية تحقيق حاضر أفضل مع حماية المستقبل. وهذه الفرصة التي لا تتكرر أكثر من مرة في الجيل الواحد هي بمثابة لحظة لترميم ما تآكل من الثقة، ولإثبات قدرة التعاون الدولي على التصدي بفعالية لتحديات الحاضر، وكذلك لما نشأ من تحديات في السنوات الأخيرة، أو ما كان منها في حكم الممكن الكامن في ثنايا المستقبل.
pages.text: مؤتمر القمة المعني بالمستقبل | الأمم المتحدة Skip to main content نيويورك، 2024 مؤتمر القمة المعني بالمستقبل 21-20 أيلول/سبتمبر — يوما العمل التمهيديان 23-22 أيلول/سبتمبر — القمة وثائق قمة المستقبل اعتمد زعماء العالم ميثاقا للمستقبل يتضمن ميثاقا رقميا عالميا وإعلانا بشأن الأجيال المقبلة.لقد صدرمشروع قرار الجمعية العامة المعنون ’’ميثاق المستقبل‘‘ في الوثيقة A/79/L.2 وهو يضم التعاهد الرقمي العالمي وإعلان الأجيال المقبلة. ويغطي الميثاق مجموعة واسعة من الموضوعات بما في ذلك السلام والأمن والتنمية المستدامة وتغير المناخ والتعاون الرقمي وحقوق الإنسان والجنس والشباب والأجيال القادمة وتحويل الحوكمة العالمية. الموقع الشبكي المخصص للميثاق (E) ميثاق المستقبل بيان صحافي (E) | بيانات (E) | استعراض مؤتمر القمة وثيقة تعريفية شاملة بالميثاق القمة والفعاليات ذات الصلة أيام العمل روابط للبث المباشر المسجل حفل الافتتاح مستقبل رقمي للجميع: جلسة صباحية | جلسة بعد الظهر مستقبل سلمي للجميع: جلسة صباحية | جلسة بعد الظهر مستقبل مستدام للجميع: جلسة صباحية | جلسة بعد الظهر حفل الختام فيديو ملخص لفعاليات أيام العمل مقر الأمم المتحدة، نيويورك 20-21 سبتمبر 2024 قمة المستقبل روابط للبث المباشر المسجل الجزء قبل الافتتاح فقرة الافتتاح والجلسة العامة تسجيلات إضافية، بما في ذلك الحوارات التفاعلية مقر الأمم المتحدة، نيويورك 22 - 23 سبتمبر 2024 يوما العمل التمهيديان لمؤتمر القمة المعني بالمستقبل نجحت قمة أيام العمل المستقبلية، التي عقدت يومي 20 و21 سبتمبر/أيلول، في جمع آلاف من أصحاب المصلحة المختلفين، بما في ذلك ممثلون من الدول الأعضاء، والمجتمع المدني، والقطاع الخاص، والأوساط الأكاديمية، والسلطات المحلية والإقليمية، والشباب. الموقع الإلكتروني نحو ميثاق من أجل المستقبل تعرف على بعض الموضوعات الرئيسية لميثاق المستقبل وملاحقه؛ الميثاق الرقمي العالمي وإعلان الأجيال القادمة. الموقع الشبكي وثيقة تعريفية شاملة بالميثاق الأخبار والإعلام تعريف بقمة المستقبل هل هناك طريقة أفضل لتشكيل عالمنا؟ وكيف يمكننا تحقيق مستقبل أكثر عدالة في مواجهة كل هذا الحجم من الاضطرابات والصراعات العالمية؟ تفاصيل أوفى يجب علينا أن نتحرك الآن من أجل تشكيل #مستقبلنا المشترك نعيش لحظة محورية في التاريخ. فالخيارات التي نتخذها اليوم سيكون لها الأثر العميق على الأجيال الحالية والمستقبلية. وهذه هي فرصتنا التي تحدث مرة واحدة في كل جيل من أجل توحيد صفوفنا ونبني مستقبلاً يستحق أن نعيش من أجله. فيديوهات قمة المستقبل- إصلاحات ودعوات للوفاء بالوعود لجعل العالم أفضل للجميع 22 أيلول/سبتمبر 2024، نيويورك - في افتتاح قمة المستقبل بمقر الأمم المتحدة، اعتمدت الجمعية العامة- بالإجماع وبدون تصويت- قرارا يتضمن اتفاقا رئيسيا يُعرف بـ "ميثاق المستقبل" الذي يوصف بأنه دعوة للعمل والإصلاح لوضع العالم على مسار أفضل يعود بالخير على الجميع في كل مكان. المزيد التخطيط للمستقبل: خمسة أشياء يجب معرفتها عن قمة المستقبل التاريخية التي تستضيفها الأمم المتحدة قمة المستقبل، حدث تحتضنه الأمم المتحدة في أيلول/سبتمبر 2024 ويعد فرصة تحدث مرة واحدة في الجيل للمجتمع الدولي من أجل رسم طريق جديد لصالح الجميع. ومن المقرر أن تنعقد القمة يومي 22 و23 أيلول/سبتمبر. ولكن ما أهمية قمة المستقبل ومن أين أتت فكرتها؟ وما هي أبرز القضايا المطروحة على طاولة النقاش في القمة؟ أبرز خمسة أشياء يجب معرفتها عن قمة المستقبل . موقع أخبار الامم المتحدة تحركوا الآن من أجل مستقبلنا المشترك لقد تجاوزنا هدفنا المتمثل في تحقيق مليون إجراء قبل انعقاد قمة المستقبل في سبتمبر. استمروا في هذا الزخم وانضموا إلى التحدي! تحركوا الآن لقد فعلناها! مليون عمل من أجل مستقبلنا المشترك زعماء العالم: حان الوقت للسماح للشباب بالقيادة وقّع على الرسالة المفتوحة، الموجهة للشباب والحلفاء على حد سواء. تعرف على المزيد عبر الموقع الإلكتروني المخصص. اسمحوا للشباب بالقيادة "لا يمكننا بناء مستقبل لأحفادنا بنظام تم بناؤه لأجدادنا". أنطونيو غوتيريش، الأمين العام للأمم المتحدة تعريف بمؤتمر القمة المعني بالمستقبل قمة المستقبل هي حدث رفيع المستوى يعقد في مقر الأمم المتحدة في نيويورك يومي 22 و23 سبتمبر/أيلول 2024. وركزت القمة على صياغة إجماع دولي جديد بشأن تقديم حاضر أفضل وحماية المستقبل. إن التعاون العالمي الفعال أصبح يشكل أهمية متزايدة لبقائنا، ولكن من الصعب تحقيقه في ظل أجواء من عدم الثقة، واستخدام هياكل عفا عليها الزمن ولم تعد تعكس الحقائق السياسية والاقتصادية اليوم. وتهدف هذه الفرصة التي تأتي مرة واحدة في كل جيل إلى إصلاح الثقة المتآكلة وإثبات أن التعاون الدولي قادر على تحقيق الأهداف المتفق عليها

pages.title: Laser Focused: How Light Reflections Could Revolutionize 3D Printing of Metals | NIST Lock
pages.description: A NIST researcher is working to better understand 3D metal printing — in hopes that the technology could make more consistent parts.
pages.text: Laser Focused: How Light Reflections Could Revolutionize 3D Printing of Metals | NIST Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/blogs/taking-measure/laser-focused-how-light-reflections-could-revolutionize-3d-printing-metals Taking Measure Just a Standard Blog Laser Focused: How Light Reflections Could Revolutionize 3D Printing of Metals September 10, 2025 By: Brian Gutierrez Share Facebook Linkedin X.com Email David Deisenroth, a mechanical engineer at NIST, researches ways to improve metal 3D printing. Credit: M. King/NIST Even if you’ve never heard of “light caustics,” you’ve probably seen them. They’re the ethereal patterns of light that coat the bottoms of swimming pools and break up the shadows of glass. Anywhere light is bent or reflected by a curved surface, caustics can appear. This trick of the light is turning out to be an important tool for 3D-printing metal, a process in which high-powered lasers melt metal powder one layer at a time. NIST scientists have found that caustic reflections from those lasers contain clues about the metal’s microscopic shape. This research will give us never-before-seen, real-time insights into metal 3D printing. What’s Metal 3D Printing? Most metal 3D printers work by laying down a thin layer of metal powder, using a laser to melt that powder together into a solid shape, then laying down a new layer of powder and repeating the process. Humans have been making things out of metal for thousands of years and have come up with ways to make metal into a specific shape: forging, stamping, bending and many others. 3D printing won’t replace them, but it has a few unique advantages that can change the way we think about what’s possible to make with metals. First, 3D printing makes the inside and the outside of a part simultaneously. This enables 3D printing to make complicated shapes that aren’t possible with other methods. That means you can 3D-print a single part that otherwise would have required making several pieces bolted together. 3D printing of metals can make complex shapes that aren’t possible to make with other methods. But we need to learn more about this process, and that’s what NIST researcher David Deisenroth does in his lab at NIST. Credit: D. Deisenroth/NIST Another big advantage is flexibility. Most metal manufacturing techniques are designed for mass production. They require expensive molds, dies or tools for each new part you want to build. Essentially, you need to customize the factory for each new part you want to build. That’s fine if you plan to make many identical copies of a part. But sometimes you only want to make one of something, such as a medical implant that’s shaped to fit a specific person, a unique replacement part for a nuclear reactor , or a prototype for a new invention to work out the kinks before committing to mass production. But 3D-printed metal is a new technology, and the results don’t come out perfectly every time. Sometimes the printing process creates small defects that make the part weaker. Finding and correcting those defects while the print is happening is one of the biggest challenges for metal 3D printers. Part of NIST’s mission is to strengthen American manufacturing through research. So, our scientists have been studying metal 3D printing up close to search for defects. Solving this problem could make metal 3D printers more consistent and reliable. But getting a very close look at metal 3D printing isn’t easy; it’s next to impossible to see what’s going on inside the machine. pages.title: ‘Seismic shift’: Native American women made significant gains in US midterms | Native Americans | The Guardian
pages.description: Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary candidates in Tuesday’s elections, report says
pages.text: ‘Seismic shift’: Native American women made significant gains in US midterms | Native Americans | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Peggy Flanagan, a member of the White Earth band of Ojibwe and Minnesota lt governor, will represent her state in the US Senate. Photograph: Steven Garcia/NurPhoto/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Peggy Flanagan, a member of the White Earth band of Ojibwe and Minnesota lt governor, will represent her state in the US Senate. Photograph: Steven Garcia/NurPhoto/Shutterstock Native Americans ‘Seismic shift’: Native American women made significant gains in US midterms Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary candidates in Tuesday’s elections, report says Cecilia Nowell Sun 8 Nov 2026 16.04 EST Last modified on Thu 12 Nov 2026 04.43 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The US midterm elections saw voters elect a slew of historic representatives – from the country’s first Muslim senator to the first Black female governor – but among the most significant gains were those for Native American women. On Tuesday, voters elected the first Native American woman governor, senator and leaders of two tribal nations. Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary and Two Spirit candidates in the November midterms, according to Advance Native Political Leadership and the news site ICT . Deb Haaland, a citizen of Laguna Pueblo and Joe Biden’s former interior secretary, will lead the state of New Mexico . Peggy Flanagan, a member of the White Earth band of Ojibwe and current Minnesota lt governor, will represent her state in the US Senate. Crystalyne Curley will become the first woman to lead the Navajo Nation, one of the country’s largest tribes. And Tina Abrams will lead the Seneca Nation of Indians in western New York, also the first woman leader in the modern history of the state’s largest tribe. Mary Peltola, who is Yup’ik, could join Flanagan as another first Native woman in the US Senate pending the results of her still undecided race in Alaska. “This is a seismic shift that is happening in our communities,” Jordan James Harvill, a citizen of the Cherokee Nation and strategist with Advance Native Political Leadership, told the Associated Press. Although Native Americans have made significant gains in political power in recent years, it has been a long road to get here. Native Americans have only been allowed to vote across the entire United States since the 1960s . In 1985, Wilma Mankiller became the first woman elected to serve as principal chief of the Cherokee Nation. In 2018, Haaland and Sharice Davids, a member of the Ho-Chunk Nation, became the first women elected to Congress when they both won seats in the House of Representatives alongside a wave of progressive freshmen lawmakers, including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Ilhan Omar and Rashida Tlaib. Davids was easily re-elected last week in Kansas to a fifth term in Congress. “The first thing that made [running for office] feel really possible was seeing Deb Haaland, was seeing Sharice Davids on a national level,” New Mexico state senator Angel Charley, who is Laguna/Zuni/Diné, told the Guardian about her decision to enter state politics in 2024. In 2020, after an outpouring of voters from the Navajo and Hopi reservations in Arizona saw the long-red state vote for Biden, he named Haaland to lead the interior department, making her the first Indigenous cabinet secretary. The same year, Yvette Herrell, who is Cherokee, became the first Republican Native woman elected to Congress. She served from 2021 to 2023. This election cycle, a record-setting 363 Indigenous candidates ran for office in local, state and federal elections across the country – with at least 180 of them winning their races. Among them were Claire Valdez, a citizen of Ysleta del Sur Pueblo and Democrat from New York, who will join Davids in the US House of Representatives.
