Close christopheCD22's Diary Mise à jour des N° de route et de leurs propiétaires Posted by christopheCD22 on 28 July 2026 in French (Français) . Bonjour, Je travaille à l’exploitation des routes départementales au Conseil Départemental des Côtes d’Armor. Afin de mener à bien nos missions, nous utilisons des application informatique dont la carto est basée sur OSM. Nous constatons de nombreuses erreur d’affectation de route. En effet de nombreux déclassement de route de route départementale vers route communale n’apparaissent pas. Nos données carto sont en open data et utilisés par l’iGN qui met donc ses cartes à jour régulièrement. Comment faire pour les cartes OSM soient le plus à jour possible. Merci Discussion Comment from Lejun on 29 July 2026 at 04:48 (Je parle d’expérience) Pas de solution miracle. OSM est une base de données indépendante, et il faut prendre le temps d’aller modifier la clé ref section par section. Je suis dispo par message privé si nécessaire. Par curiosité, c’est quelles applications ? De tête j’ai Inforoute ? Ivoir ? Comment from Vétérini on 29 July 2026 at 07:03 La première étape si ça n’est pas déjà fait, c’est de publier le jeu de données de vos routes en open data ! 😇 Ça permettra de comparer facilement (et légalement, sans problème de licence) les données et mettre à jour là où c’est nécessaire, c’est ce qu’on a utilisé à Tours pour requalifier les portions de routes départementales en métropolitaines. Et comme OpenStreetMap est une carte collaborative, vous avez la main pour corriger vous-même les manques ! Un petit tuto est disponible ici : https://learnosm.org/fr/beginner/ N’hésitez pas non plus à poster un message sur https://forum.openstreetmap.fr pour présenter le sujet ou poser des questions, ça reste le support le plus répandu par la communauté française. Comment from christopheCD22 on 29 July 2026 at 13:47 Bonjour Vétérini, les données sont en open data. J’ai moi même fait des modifications après un petit apprentissage. C’est un travail très long à faire tronçon/tronçon. Comment from Vétérini on 29 July 2026 at 20:51 Bonjour Christophe, Est-ce bien ce jeu de données ? https://datarmor.cotesdarmor.fr/datasets/routes-departementales-des-cotes-darmor À partir de vos données, serait-il possible d’identifier facilement toutes les portions de routes qui ont été déclassées ? J’ai l’impression que le jeu de données contient certaines voies communales (dans la catégorie “VC”), mais certaines routes déclassées ne semblent pas du tout présentes dans le jeu de données, donc difficile de savoir facilement quoi mettre à jour dans OpenStreetMap. Avec des outils plus avancés (éditeur JOSM, requêtes Overpass), l’édition et la vérification des données OSM est plus efficace pour ce type d’opérations “lourdes”, mais c’est aussi plus difficile à prendre en main. Si vous avez les données précises des sections de routes déclassées, ça permettrait d’estimer l’effort nécessaire pour remettre OSM à jour. Au passage, j’en ai profité pour déclasser certains bouts de routes qui avaient été oubliées dans vos précédentes éditions ! Comment from christopheCD22 on 30 July 2026 at 08:30 Bonjour, C’est bien ce jeu de données. Je ne suis pas sur qu’il soit aisé d’identifier les portions de routes déclassées. Je vais essayé d’avoir des informations précises sur les routes déclassées ces dernières années. La personnes en charge de la carto est en congés pour le moment, je n’aurait pas toute les informations tout de suite. Merci pour votre aide précieuse. pages.title: Thawing Permafrost May Have Created a New Type of Landslide, Which Could Become More Common as the World Warms
pages.description: Scientists call the events permafrost detachment slides. Instead of thawing from the top down, these landslides seem to originate from a weakened base
pages.text: Thawing Permafrost May Have Created a New Type of Landslide, Which Could Become More Common as the World Warms Skip to main content A scar left by the 2018 Redstone River permafrost landslide, one of the two events investigated in the new study. Adapted from J. M. Young et al., Geophysical Research Letters , 2026 In 2017 and 2018, a pair of strange landslides moved huge masses of rock and dirt in Canada’s Northwest Territories. The events occurred in the central Mackenzie Valley, and one of them even dammed a river and created a lake . The two natural disasters are part of a new class of landslides scientists are calling “permafrost detachment slides” in a study published in the journal Geophysical Research Letters in September. They may have been partially triggered by severe wildfires that occurred in 1995, which destabilized the ground and allowed the base of the permafrost to thaw. What’s more, these events may become more common as the planet continues to warm. “It’s a very dramatic manifestation of the changing climate,” says study co-author Joseph Young , a geoscientist who conducted the work at the University of Alberta in Canada, to Matt Simon at Grist . “They’ve only started happening in the last 10, 15 years, and it’s a very drastic and abrupt change in the landscape.” Young and his colleagues began the study after seeing something strange in the Northwest Territories in 2019. While conducting field research, they spotted large landslide scars in valleys that they knew were stable permafrost , or permanently frozen earth, reports Stephanie Pappas for Live Science . To better understand what happened, the team homed in on two major events: the Johnson River slide in August 2017 that moved about 4.5 million cubic meters of dirt and rock, and the Redstone River slide in August 2018 that sent roughly 18 million cubic meters of debris tumbling down. Satellite imagery captured between 1980 and 2020 and field studies revealed some odd characteristics, the team found. “Typically with permafrost, everything just thaws and melts in a slurry and moves like a mud downslope,” Young tells Live Science . “But with these large landslides, we found blocks of frozen material in the debris.” The team monitored the temperature near the 1995 burn area near the slides and, for comparison, undisturbed forest from September 2020 to August 2022. Their data went into computer simulations, which allowed the researchers to investigate how the wildfires decades earlier may have affected the region. Quick fact: Permafrost The Northern Hemisphere’s permafrost regions cover an area equal to nearly 2.5 times that of the contiguous United States . Their resulting hypothesis? The fires that swept through the landscape burned off the vegetation that usually keeps the permafrost cool on sunny days. “After about 20 years or so, that thermal signature from the burned forest can reach the base of permafrost,” Young tells Grist . “It’s slight, but it’s there.” As the frozen ground warmed, it weakened and formed cracks, allowing water to seep in. That allowed the permafrost to thaw even more, destabilizing its bottom layers. Eventually, that caused the ground to detach and created the two landslides at the center of the study. They’re among more than 150 permafrost landslides in the area that happened around two decades after the severe wildfires, meaning the newly proposed mechanism could have contributed to many of these catastrophic events. The findings suggest scientists need to better study what’s happening below the surface of permafrost regions, says Dmitry Nicolsky , a geophysicist at the University of Alaska Fairbanks who wasn’t involved in the work, to Nikk Ogasa at Science News . “We don’t know how [the ground] will move—it might go slowly or it might go catastrophically.” Thankfully, Young says experts can look out for signs of an impending permafrost detachment slide and predict when it’s going to happen. “That’s kind of the silver lining,” he

While you may ﬁnd it useful to discuss broad conceptual issues and general solution procedures with others, the ﬁnal product that you turn in must be done individually. What you turn in must be your own product, written in your own handwriting, or in a computer ﬁle of which you are the sole author. Copying another’s work or electronic ﬁle is not acceptable. Although you may discuss your work with other students, what you turn in must represent your own work. Final Project For the ﬁnal project each team of 2 needs to submit a one-page proposal that outlines a plan to apply analytical methods to a problem you identify using some of the concepts and tools discussed in the course. The proposal should include a description of: (1) the problem, (2) the data that you have or plan to collect to solve the problem, (3) which analytic techniques you plan to use, and (4) the impact or overall goal of the project (if you could build a perfect model, what would it be able to do?). Each project team will set up a meeting with a member of the teaching team to show your progress in applying the analytical methods to your project topic. This meeting is intended to help you make progress on your project. The ﬁnal project submission will consist of a written report of at most 4 pages (not including appendices) that describes your analysis, as well as a 15 minute presentation (in powerpoint or pdf format) of your project. pages.description: Worksheets and activities for history lesson plans, for kindergarten through high school. Resources based on real census data, to increase statistical literacy.
pages.text: History Worksheets History Worksheets Skip Navigation History Worksheets Census data can give students a deeper understanding of historic events like the Missouri Compromise and social studies topics like women in the workforce. Use the grade-range tabs below to explore all the options. Corresponding teachers' guides are available for each activity. All Grades Grades K-5 Grades 6-8 Grades 9-12 All Grades All Grades Grades K-5 Grades 6-8 Grades 9-12 All Grades "I Have a Dream" – Learning About Martin Luther King Jr. Analyze census data and graphs that demonstrate how lives of African-Americans were changed by Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech. 19th Century Immigration - Causes & Effects Students will examine and interpret a population chart published in 1898 as well as an 1893 political cartoon about immigration. Adopting an Entrepreneurial Mindset - Using Census Data for Business Students will use the Census Business Builder data access tool to gather and analyze information that entrepreneurs may consider when opening a business. America Then and Now - Interpreting Changes in Demographic Data Students will review a series of infographics to learn how America’s demographics have changed between 1940 and 2024. Antebellum Economy - Understanding Employment in 1850 Students will examine a table of 1850 Census data on employment to understand the professions of free men across the United States at the time. Authorizing the First Census - The Significance of Population Data Students will analyze excerpts from the 1790 legislation that allowed for the administration of the first decennial census. Examining Changes in Data Students will analyze and compare census data on the education levels of African-Americans in 1850 and in 1880. Exploring 19th Century Population Growth through Interactive Maps Students will use two data visualization tools to explore U.S. population growth between 1790 and 1890. Exploring 19th-Century Child Labor Laws in the United States Examine historical photographs and a data table related to 19th-century industrialization and child labor. Exploring the Great Migration – 1910-1970 Consider the causes and effects of waves of migration and compare the historical data with more recent data on migration overall. Geographic Mobility in the United States - 1920-1950 Students will examine maps to explore changes in population density in the United States during three decades. Maps and Graphs - Exploring the U.S. Island Territories Students will examine data from the 1990–2010 censuses on population changes in the U.S. island territories. Median Income Patterns in the United States Students will examine, and make comparisons using, a data visualization of median household incomes by U.S. county. Missouri Compromise – Free vs. Slave States Introduces students to the Missouri Compromise and the issues associated with the expansion of slavery. Native American Dwellings Look at historical images to learn about three types of Native American dwellings. Population Expansion and Distribution in the United States: 1790-2010 Students will use a data visualization tool to understand shifts in the U.S. population distribution from 1790 to 2010. Population Profile of Our New Nation Refer to the 1790 and 1800 Censuses to compare the total population with the population of enslaved people, drawing conclusions from the data. Post-Civil War: Regional Shifts in U.S. Population by Age and Sex Students will examine population pyramids of 1850–1870 census data for different races/ethnicities and for the states and territories. Post-World War II Globalization - U.S. Citizens Living Overseas Students will analyze the 1950 Census form for Americans living overseas and 1910–1990. Slavery, Geography, and Politics Students will analyze multiple resources to learn how President Abraham Lincoln and Union forces used a 19th century population density map. ICYMI: Trump Administration Adds Two DOE Lithium Processing Projects to Federal Permitting Dashboard The Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council announced increased transparency and accountability for the federal permitting of two Department of Energy (DOE) lithium processing projects. Energy.gov June 3, 2025 Estimated Read Time min ICYMI— The Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council (Permitting Council) announced increased transparency and accountability for the federal permitting of two Department of Energy (DOE) lithium processing projects, advancing President Trump’s commitment to bolster domestic production of minerals and support American jobs. The projects — Kings Mountain and Liberty Owl — increase lithium processing in the United States. Currently, the Peoples Republic of China (PRC) controls 70% of the market, with lithium as a key component in many energy storage and defense applications. Once completed, these projects will help to develop more secure domestic supply chains, strengthening our national security and our economic security. The Kings Mountain, NC Project is owned by Albemarle Corporation, a leading provider in lithium that has established extensive capabilities in chemical manufacturing. The Kings Mountain Lithium Material Processing Plant is receiving a $150 million federal award through DOE’s Office of Manufacturing and Energy Supply Chains (MESC). This project supports the construction of a new, commercial scale processing facility that will have the capacity to produce 350,000 tons per year of lithium oxide concentrate. The Liberty Owl Project in the Texarkana region is owned by TerraVolta, a US-based critical minerals and resources company. This project is receiving a $225 million award through MESC for the construction of a commercial scale lithium extraction and refining facility to produce battery grade lithium from domestic brine resources from the Smackover region. These additions to the Federal Permitting Dashboard reflect the Trump Administration’s commitment to strengthen domestic supply chains for critical minerals and materials, reduce dependence on foreign sources and advance President Trump’s bold agenda for American energy dominance through a more secure, affordable and reliable U.S. energy system. The Department looks forward to working with federal partners, project sponsors, and developers to ensure these projects move forward with increased transparency, clear project timelines, expedited reviews, and the support needed to strengthen domestic supply chains, drive economic growth and deliver on President Trump's commitment to unleashing American energy and economic security. ### View Next Press Release ICYMI: Energy Secretary Wright, EPA Administrator Zeldin, and Interior Secretary Burgum Visit Alaska to Advance Unleashing American Energy June 6, 2025 View Previous Press Release Secretary Wright Announces Termination of 24 Projects, Generating Over $3 Billion in Taxpayer Savings May 30, 2025 Media Inquiries: (202) 586-4940 or DOENews@hq.doe.gov Read more at the energy.gov Newsroom

Disaster recovery Explore SBA’s low‑interest disaster loans designed to help businesses of all sizes, homeowners, renters, and private nonprofit organizations recover from declared disasters. Repair existing damage, reduce future risks, or get help with financial obligations when essential employees are called to serve. Apply for disaster loans Find your declaration Schedule Recovery Center appointments Declared disasters SBA is currently offering loans to support recovery from multiple declared disasters. Verify your eligibility and start the application process . You can find additional assistance and the latest federal updates for Presidential Declarations at fema.gov . You can search to see if your county is eligible for other disaster assistance or find options for bypassing permitting delays . Hawaii severe storms Check your eligibility for Hawaii severe storms Alaska floods Check your eligibility for Alaska floods California wildfires Check your eligibility for California wildfires Who is eligible to apply for a loan? Businesses of all sizes Homeowners Renters Private nonprofit organizations SBA disaster loans can be used for Disaster losses not fully covered by insurance or other sources. Business operating expenses which could have been met had the disaster not occurred Use the SBA Loan Portal to check your application status and manage your loan. Disaster loan types Explore SBA’s disaster loans Get help Explore help options Types of available disaster loans See which of SBA’s loans is best for you. Learn about disaster loan types. Physical damage loans Repair or replace disaster-damaged property. Homeowners, Renters, private nonprofit organizations , and businesses of all sizes are eligible. Home and personal property loans + If your home or personal property has been damaged in a declared disaster area you may be eligible for low-interest financial assistance from SBA. As a homeowner or renter, you may apply to SBA for a loan to help you recover from the disaster. Eligibility These loans cover disaster losses not fully covered by insurance or other sources. Proceeds from insurance coverage on home or property may be deducted from the eligible loan amount. Homeowners may apply for up to $500,000 to replace or repair their primary residence. Renters and homeowners may borrow up to $100,000 to replace or repair personal property — such as clothing, furniture, cars, and appliances — damaged or destroyed in a disaster. Use of proceeds You may not use the funds to upgrade homes or make additions, unless required by the local building code. Proceeds may not be used to replace profits. You may be eligible for a loan amount of 20% of total damages, as verified by SBA. SBA can refinance all or part of a previous mortgage in some cases, when the applicant does not have credit available elsewhere and has suffered substantial disaster damage. Terms First payment deferred for 12 months No interest accrual for the first 12 months For applicants unable to obtain credit elsewhere: The fixed interest rate will not exceed 4% SBA will determine whether an applicant can obtain credit elsewhere Maturity Up to 30 years No pre-payment penalty or fees Collateral requirements Collateral is required to the extent possible for physical damage loans over $50,000 in Presidential declarations and $14,000 in SBA Administrative declarations. Real estate is the preferred form of collateral, even if the equity is insufficient to secure the full loan amount. SBA will ask the applicant for available collateral, but will not decline a loan for lack of collateral. How to apply Apply

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn < All Public Input & Actions BLM and USWFS Launch Prescribed Burn Season in the Albuquerque District Office New Mexico Albuquerque DO Media Contact Wendy Brown winifred_brown@ios.doi.gov 720-830-6012 BLM Office: Albuquerque District Office October 20, 2026 ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. — The Bureau of Land Management and the U.S. Wildland Fire Service will begin prescribed fire operations throughout Catron, Cibola, Sandoval and Socorro counties as weather, fuel and air quality become favorable. Operations will continue throughout the fall and winter. These treatments are carefully planned to reduce hazardous fuels, protect nearby communities and restore native ecosystems. Information about specific upcoming and active burns is available on the BLM New Mexico Prescribed Fire website . “Prescribed fire is one of the most effective tools for reducing wildfire risk and improving habitat,” said BLM Socorro Field Manager Matt Atencio. “We carefully plan and execute these burns with the U.S. Wildland Fire Service to help protect communities and strengthen the health of our public lands.” Techniques range from broadcast burning, which is the application of fire to an entire area, to hand and machine pile ignitions. These burns focus on increasing safety in the wildland-urban interface and restoring ecological function to the landscape. Targeting built-up fuels and residual materials from previous thinning operations decreases the load of dead trees, branches, and underbrush that pose significant wildfire risks. “Every acre we treat is an investment in safer communities and stronger landscape resilience,” said USWFS Prescribed Fire and Fuels Specialist Lino Baca . “When we apply low-intensity fire to the landscape, we’re not just reducing risk, we’re leading with grit, stewardship, and the determination to leave the landscape better for those who follow.” What the public should know: During prescribed burns, smoke may settle in low-lying areas overnight. Residents are encouraged to close windows at night to avoid smoke impacts. When driving in smoky areas, drivers should slow down and turn on headlights. People with heart or lung disease, asthma, or other chronic conditions should ask their doctors about protecting themselves from smoke and should monitor their local air quality map. All burns are carried out when weather, fuel conditions, and air quality are within specific parameters. Firefighters use a combination of natural features and constructed control lines to keep the fire contained, with protocols in place to minimize smoke impacts on nearby communities. For more information, contact the BLM Albuquerque District Office or Baca at lbaca@blm.gov or (575) 838-3024. Related Files map-albuquerque -pile-burn-blm-nm-2026 (PDF / 2.1 MB) The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/itl/executive-orders/strengthening-and-promoting-innovation-nations-cybersecurity Information Technology Laboratory Connect with us GovDelivery X (Twitter) Executive Order 14306 -– Sustaining Select Efforts to Strengthen the Nation’s Cybersecurity and Amending Executive Order 13694 and Executive Order 14144 NIST’s Responsibilities Under Executive Order 14306 overview The President’s Executive Order (EO) on Sustaining Select Efforts to Strengthen the Nation’s Cybersecurity and Amending Executive Order 13694 and Executive Order 14144 issued on June 6, 2025, charges multiple agencies – including NIST – to strengthen the nation’s cybersecurity by focusing on critical protections against foreign cyber threats and enhancing secure technology practices. NIST is directly responsible for several actions in the EO, summarized below: Operationalizing Transparency and Security in Third-Party Software Supply Chains Develop and publish an update to the Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF). Establish a consortium with industry to develop guidance that demonstrates the implementation of secure software development, security, and operations practices based on the SSDF. Update NIST SP 800-53 to provide guidance on how to securely and reliably deploy patches and updates ( draft available for public comment until August 5, 2025) . Securing Federal Communications Develop guidelines for the secure management of access tokens and cryptographic keys used by cloud service providers. Promoting Security with and in Artificial Intelligence Ensure that existing datasets for cyber defense research have been made accessible to the broader academic research community. Aligning Policy to Practice Establish a pilot program of a rules-as-code approach for machine-readable versions of policy and guidance that OMB, NIST, and CISA publish and manage regarding cybersecurity. pages.title: Archaeologists in England Discovered 8,000 Roman-Era Frog Bones in a Single Ditch. They Just Solved the Mystery of How the Amphibians Ended Up There
pages.description: New research suggests that medium-sized birds of prey such as short-eared owls feasted on the frogs during a "short, intensive predation event" some 1,700 years ago
pages.text: Archaeologists in England Discovered 8,000 Roman-Era Frog Bones in a Single Ditch. They Just Solved the Mystery of How the Amphibians Ended Up There Skip to main content An aerial view of the Bar Hill archaeological site, where excavations uncovered some 8,000 frog bones between 2016 and 2018 © MOLA Headland Infrastructure Between 2016 and 2022, archaeologists conducting excavations along a planned stretch of England’s A14 highway unearthed an array of astonishing discoveries , including a Roman amulet carved to resemble the mythical Gorgon Medusa , the earliest physical evidence of beer production in Britain and an Iron Age comb crafted from a human skull. Comprising more than 280,000 artifacts, the finds—uncovered between modern-day Cambridge and Huntingdon —shed light on life in the region over roughly 12,000 years. But some discoveries raised more questions than answers: Why, for example, did a single ditch at the Bar Hill site in rural Cambridgeshire contain some 8,000 amphibian bones ? As Vicki Ewens , a senior zooarchaeologist at the Museum of London Archaeology (MOLA), told the Observer ’s Dalya Alberge in 2022, “In my experience, mainly working on sites from London, we don’t get that many frogs . To have so many bones coming from one ditch is extraordinary.” Frog bones found at Bar Hill © MOLA / Andy Chopping Ewens and her colleagues outlined several possible explanations for the unusual cache. Perhaps the amphibians fell into the ditch (also described as a gully) and found themselves trapped. Or maybe they succumbed to extreme cold during their wintertime hibernation . Alternatively, they could have served as the centerpiece of a meal—or several—enjoyed by Iron Age humans, although the absence of cut marks on the bones rendered this scenario unlikely. Four years after MOLA first announced the find, experts have finally solved the mystery of the ancient animal cemetery. Based on a groundbreaking analysis of amphibian arm bones, researchers led by Ewens and Paul Clarkson , an archaeologist at England’s Bournemouth University, concluded that most of the frogs whose remains were found in the ditch died young, eaten by birds of prey such as short-eared owls and hen harriers in the second or third century C.E., during Britain’s Roman era . A combination of environmental factors and human activity produced ideal conditions for this avian feast to unfold over a relatively short timeframe. As the authors write in the journal Environmental Archaeology , water levels in the Fens —the marshy wetland that houses the gully—retreated during the Roman period, enabling frogs in drying-out ponds to reproduce at a faster rate. When birds in search of their next meal arrived, they had no trouble spotting their prey: Locals had felled the trees in the area to make way for grazing livestock, leaving the amphibians with limited woodland protection from aerial predators. Did you know? Frogs and toads All toads are frogs , but not all frogs are toads. Both animals belong to the Anura order, meaning they are amphibians that lack tails. According to the University of Michigan’s Animal Diversity Web database, “There is no scientific distinction between ‘frogs’ and ‘toads,’ although most anurans are usually referred to as one or the other.” “We don’t often get an owl’s eye view of what it was like in the past from archaeological sites,” Clarkson says in a statement . “These bones not only tell us about life for people living near the Roman Fens , but they also give insights into the natural world—what wild animals were getting up to in the past, and what life was like for them.” The majority of the bones belonged to frogs and toads (specifically common frogs ), but shrews, voles and mice were also present in the assemblage. The remains represented no fewer than 469 individual animals. pages.text: Exempt organization types | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Exempt organization types More In File Individuals Businesses and self-employed Charities and nonprofits Exempt organization types Charitable organizations Churches and religious organizations Private foundations Political organizations Other nonprofits Lifecycle of an exempt organization Annual filing and forms Charitable contributions Search for charities Education sessions Stay Exempt International taxpayers Governmental liaisons Federal, state and local governments Indian tribal governments Tax exempt bonds Taxpayer identification numbers (TIN) Charitable organizations Organizations organized and operated exclusively for religious, charitable, scientific, testing for public safety, literary, educational, or other specified purposes and that meet certain other requirements are tax exempt under Internal Revenue Code Section 501(c)(3). Churches and religious organizations Churches and religious organizations, like many other charitable organizations, may qualify for exemption from federal income tax under Section 501(c)(3). Private foundations Every organization that qualifies for tax-exempt status under Section 501(c)(3) is classified as a private foundation unless it meets one of the exceptions listed in Section 509(a). Private foundations typically have a single major source of funding (usually gifts from one family or corporation rather than funding from many sources) and most have as their primary activity the making of grants to other charitable organizations and to individuals, rather than the direct operation of charitable programs. Political organizations A political organization subject to Section 527 is a party, committee, association, fund or other organization (whether or not incorporated) organized and operated primarily for the purpose of directly or indirectly accepting contributions or making expenditures, or both, for an exempt function. Other nonprofits Organizations that meet specified requirements may qualify for exemption under subsections other than 501(c)(3). These include social welfare organizations, civic leagues, social clubs, labor organizations and business leagues. The size of the world stock market is now estimated to be in the trillions. The largest stock market in the world is the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), located in New York City. About 2,800 companies are listed on the NSYE. In this problem, we’ll look at the monthly stock prices of five of these companies: IBM , General Electric (GE) , Procter and Gamble , Coca Cola , and Boeing . The data used in this problem comes from Infochimps . Download and read the following files into R, using the read.csv function: IBMStock (CSV) , GEStock (CSV) , ProcterGambleStock (CSV) , CocaColaStock (CSV) , and BoeingStock (CSV) . (Do not open these files in any spreadsheet software before completing this problem because it might change the format of the Date field.) Call the data frames “IBM”, “GE”, “ProcterGamble”, “CocaCola”, and “Boeing”, respectively. Each data frame has two variables, described as follows: Date : the date of the stock price, always given as the first of the month. StockPrice : the average stock price of the company in the given month. In this problem, we’ll take a look at how the stock dynamics of these companies have changed over time. Problem 1.1 - Summary Statistics Before working with these data sets, we need to convert the dates into a format that R can understand. Take a look at the structure of one of the datasets using the str function. Right now, the date variable is stored as a factor. We can convert this to a “Date” object in R by using the following five commands (one for each data set): IBM$Date = as.Date(IBM$Date, “%m/%d/%y”) GE$Date = as.Date(GE$Date, “%m/%d/%y”) CocaCola$Date = as.Date(CocaCola$Date, “%m/%d/%y”) ProcterGamble$Date = as.Date(ProcterGamble$Date, “%m/%d/%y”) Boeing$Date = as.Date(Boeing$Date, “%m/%d/%y”) The first argument to the as.Date function is the variable we want to convert, and the second argument is the format of the Date variable. We can just overwrite the original Date variable values with the output of this function. Now, answer the following questions using the str and summary functions. Our five datasets all have the same number of observations. How many observations are there in each data set? Problem 1.2 - Summary Statistics What is the earliest year in our datasets? pages.title: Texas puts to death man who beheaded three children, hours after Oklahoma execution | Capital punishment | The Guardian
pages.description: Oklahoma man, 73, executed for killing ex’s estranged husband, as US nears 40 executions for second straight year
pages.text: Texas puts to death man who beheaded three children, hours after Oklahoma execution | Capital punishment | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation John Allen Rubio, 46, was executed by lethal injection on Thursday at the state prison in Huntsville, Texas. Photograph: Jerry Cabluck View image in fullscreen John Allen Rubio, 46, was executed by lethal injection on Thursday at the state prison in Huntsville, Texas. Photograph: Jerry Cabluck Capital punishment Texas puts to death man who beheaded three children, hours after Oklahoma execution Oklahoma man, 73, executed for killing ex’s estranged husband, as US nears 40 executions for second straight year Associated Press Sun 15 Nov 2026 14.27 EST Last modified on Mon 16 Nov 2026 16.43 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Texas man convicted of fatally stabbing and beheading his three young children in a squalid, windowless apartment in 2003 was recently executed. John Allen Rubio, 46, was pronounced dead at 6.47pm on Thursday after a lethal injection at the state prison in Huntsville, Texas. His killings of his baby girl and two toddlers so rocked the city of Brownsville on the US border with Mexico that the apartment building was later demolished – and the land turned into a park and community garden. After a spiritual adviser prayed over him briefly, Rubio thanked friends and family for their “love and understanding” and said he was “not the same person I once was”. He thanked prison staff for teaching him how to find God and also expressed love for Angela Camacho, his common-law wife who is serving life in prison for her role in the slayings. “I want to say I’m sorry to my wife’s family,” he said. “I can’t change the past but I can tell you my life is going to be over. But that’s not going to make you happy.” Former death row prisoners call Byron Donalds to halt future Florida executions Read more “I’m going to be with my kids in a little bit,” he added. “I’m ready to go to heaven to be with my lord and savior.” As the lethal dose of the sedative pentobarbital began taking effect, Rubio took three breaths and began what sounded like snoring. All movement ceased after, and a physician pronounced him dead 21 minutes after the injection began. Also on Thursday, 73-year-old James Pavatt received a lethal injection at an Oklahoma prison for the fatal shooting of his girlfriend’s estranged husband in 2001. The victim was killed as he arrived to pick up his two young children before Thanksgiving. Thursday’s executions were the 36th and 37th this year, with the US on track to surpass 40 executions for a second consecutive year – a pace driven by Florida . The death penalty has drawn renewed attention since the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee in September. And on 5 November, California’s governor, Gavin Newsom, announced he would commute hundreds of death sentences before leaving office in January – what experts say would be the largest mass clemency in American history. In Texas , Rubio and Camacho were accused of killing three-year-old Julissa Quesada, 14-month-old John E Rubio and two-month-old Mary Jane Rubio in the apartment they shared in Brownsville. Camacho received a life sentence after pleading guilty. An appeals court overturned Rubio’s first capital murder conviction, ruling Camacho’s statements were improperly admitted as evidence in his trial. At his second trial, Rubio again pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity but again was convicted and sentenced to death. According to court records, Rubio wasn’t the biological father of the two older children but raised them as his own. At various points, Rubio claimed the children were possessed and that he was the “chosen one” intended to save the world. Unfortunately, the last administration especially and many before them sought to shut down Alaska in the name of climate nonsense. Those days are over. The Trump Administration is fully committed to restoring the rights and liberties of Alaskans, because when Alaska is unleashed, the entire country and world benefits.” Click here to watch a highlight video of the trip and here to download and view photos from the visit. Home » Disaster recovery » Options to bypass permitting delays Options to bypass permitting delays New option to accelerate rebuilding thanks to President Trump. In response to ongoing challenges with widespread permitting delays that have stalled recovery and rebuilding efforts in states like California, President Donald J. Trump has empowered the SBA to implement new regulations through a new executive order . These regulatory changes will enable SBA disaster borrowers to bypass certain state and local permitting requirements if the borrower has been unable to obtain requisite approvals after an extended period of time. The new regulations will allow for the timely use of approved SBA disaster loans and rapid rebuilding. Eligibility: If you have applied for a local permit more than 60 days ago, but still haven’t received approval, you may qualify for this self-certification option. Next Steps to Use the Builder Self-Certification Option Discuss with your contractor/builder: Review your situation with your contractor to confirm you meet the eligibility criteria. Access and complete the required forms via the links below: Disaster Loan Modification (Builder Certification) This form must be signed by you (the borrower). This form allows SBA to move forward with the builder-certification process. Builder Certification This form must be signed by your builder/contractor. It certifies that the planned repairs/reconstruction comply with applicable building codes, safety measures, and other substantive requirements and that your builder will continue to follow all applicable state and local rules other than the permitting or other approval requirements the regulatory changes allow them to bypass. If you do not have a builder/contractor, and you are the one overseeing repairs and getting permits or other approvals and you meet the requirements in the new regulations, you may sign the certification. Important Document Requirement: Ensure necessary signatures, address, and the loan number match loan documents exactly to prevent delays in processing. Upload the completed signed forms: Log back into your SBA Loan Portal, upload both signed forms, and submit your request. SBA will review the submission. A case manager will contact you with next steps or any additional requirements. If Your Loan Was Cancelled: If your loan was previously cancelled, you may be eligible to have it reinstated. Please send a secure message through your SBA Loan Portal to request reinstatement and discuss your options. If reinstated, you may then qualify for the builder self-certification process described above. These steps are designed to reduce unnecessary barriers, speed up rebuilding, and support your community’s full recovery. SBA continues to work closely with federal partners to ensure smooth implementation. If you need assistance, please visit sba.gov/disaster , call the SBA Disaster Assistance Customer Service Center at (800) 659-2955 (TTY: 711), or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov . SBA is currently offering loans to assist in recovery from the declared disasters below. Verify your eligibility and start the application process . You can also find additional help or read up on the latest federal updates at fema.gov .

pages.description: Celebrating National Public Lands Day, 25 volunteers and BLM staff spent a beautiful Saturday morning at El Malpais National Conservation Area giving back to the public lands they cherish.
pages.text: One day, one goal: caring for El Malpais National Conservation Area | Bureau of Land Management Skip to main navigation Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn One day, one goal: caring for El Malpais National Conservation Area Oct 22, 2026 The Narrow's Rim Trail within El Malpais National Conservation Area. BLM Photo. How did you celebrate Sept. 26, 2026—National Public Lands Day (NPLD)? As part of the largest single-day volunteer event dedicated to public lands in the country, 25 volunteers and BLM staff spent a beautiful Saturday morning at El Malpais National Conservation Area (NCA) giving back to the public lands they cherish. Narrows Rim Trail Restoration A team of 25 volunteers and BLM staff completed restoration work along the Narrows Rim Trail system, hiking the full eight-mile roundtrip from the Narrows Picnic Area. Carrying in hand tools, sun protection, and snacks, the crew worked their way along the dramatic sandstone rim, which rises approximately 500 feet above the surrounding landscape. Throughout the day, participants cleared weeds and downed timber from the trail corridor, and rebuilt rock cairn route markers to improve wayfinding for visitors. These efforts helped maintain safe, enjoyable access to the area while protecting natural resources and enhancing the recreation experience for the public. Most volunteers performed trail maintenance along the Narrows Rim Trail, an eight-mile roundtrip hike that climbs to the top of a 500-foot sandstone mesa, featuring spectacular scenic overlooks. BLM Photo. Restoration work included clearing obstacles such as weeds and downed timber along the Narrows Rim Trail, and rebuilding rock cairn route markers. BLM Photo. Cebolla Canyon Fence Repairs A smaller group of volunteers and BLM staff drove three government vehicles to remote Cebolla Canyon. En route to the project site, the crew gathered downed timber from along the roadway and used it to construct natural barrier fencing at a non-motorized trailhead. Placed along both sides of the entrance, the timber quickly stacked up high enough to create an effective barrier and discourage unauthorized travel. After a short hike farther into the wilderness, the team then turned their attention to repairing sections of a historic homestead fence that had fallen into disrepair. As they arrived at the site, the volunteers were pleased to discover a sign which indicated that the fence had originally been built by members of the same organization, New Mexico Volunteers for the Outdoors (NMVFO). The moment was a meaningful reminder of the group's longstanding commitment to public lands stewardship and the lasting impact of volunteer service. To protect wilderness from unauthorized vehicular access, volunteers gathered and placed downed timber along the sides of a narrow trail entrance. BLM Photo. A small group of volunteers joined BLM staff to repair historic homestead fencing, which was originally placed with the help of New Mexico Volunteers for the Outdoors in 1992. BLM Photo. A National Public Lands Day to Remember “National Public Lands Day at El Malpais National Conservation Area was a wonderful reminder of how special these places are,” said Evie Forster, El Malpais NCA Park Ranger. “Working alongside our volunteers to restore trails and fences helped us connect with this incredible landscape and give something back. We are truly grateful to everyone who shared their time, hard work, and commitment to caring for these public lands.” Twenty-five volunteers and BLM staff helped to make El Malpais National Public Lands Day in 2026 a big success. BLM Photo. Thank you to everyone who helped make National Public Lands Day

Solopreneur? NIST Has a Cybersecurity Guide Just for You November 2, 2026 Share Facebook Linkedin X.com Email A new NIST guide can help solo business owners — also called “solopreneurs” — grasp the basics of cybersecurity and craft a strategy that can help reduce their cybersecurity risk. The guide is designed to help solopreneurs prioritize and implement a selection of actions from the NIST Cybersecurity Framework that would best help their businesses. The publication is written in lay language and assumes no prior cybersecurity knowledge. Credit: Asian Isolated/Shutterstock If you work for yourself, as millions of Americans do, protecting your business from cyberattack is one of many responsibilities that falls entirely on your shoulders. Don’t feel daunted: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has just released a guide with your needs — and busy life — in mind. Small Business Cybersecurity: Non-Employer Firms (NIST Cybersecurity White Paper 50) is a lay-language resource offering cybersecurity basics tailored expressly to the “solopreneur” — a term referring to anyone who is a business’s sole paid employee. More than 28 million small businesses in the U.S. fall into the solopreneur category, existing in every industry and forming a substantial part of the economy. The publication is written to introduce solopreneurs to the fundamentals of a small-business cybersecurity program and provide an actionable approach to implementing it. “Because solopreneurs may not have cybersecurity expertise, we wanted to create a resource designed for them,” said NIST’s Daniel Eliot, one of the publication’s authors. “They can implement many of these actions on their own with limited technical knowledge or with minimal financial investment.” The publication is an update to what was previously titled Small Business Information Security: The Fundamentals ( NISTIR 7621 ). While that publication was aimed at small businesses of varying sizes and covered the broader topic of information security, the revision is narrower in scope and concentrates on protecting digital systems from malicious attack. The updated publication draws its guidelines from the well-known NIST Cybersecurity Framework ( CSF 2.0 ), though the new publication is written with the novice in mind. “This publication assumes the reader has no familiarity with cybersecurity or the NIST CSF,” Eliot said. “We want to educate people about what cybersecurity is and how it fits in with a successful business plan. We know solopreneurs are often very busy people, so any time we introduce a topic or throw out jargony terms, we try to provide context and definitions for the lay reader.” The publication’s opening section, which includes the introduction and a chapter on the NIST CSF, is essentially a primer on cybersecurity and how it can support a solopreneur’s business. “In addition to the general context, we highlight a set of actionable best practices that significantly reduce cybersecurity risks. These include regular data backups and maintaining updated software,” Eliot said. “They are a good set of first steps a small business might take.” The central section offers specific actions from the CSF that can be implemented in a solo business. For each of these actions, the guide includes the rationale for performing it, how the business can get started, and options for what to do later as the business grows. pages.title: This Four-Person NASA Crew Spent Over a Year on 'Mars.' Here's What They Did for 378 Days in a Simulated Martian Habitat
pages.description: An intense selection process and long preparation helped set the crew up for cohabitation in a 3D-printed replication of the Red Planet's environment in Houston. There, they practiced Marswalks, disrupted communications with people on Earth and food cultivation
pages.text: This Four-Person NASA Crew Spent Over a Year on 'Mars.' Here's What They Did for 378 Days in a Simulated Martian Habitat Skip to main content Four individuals participated in NASA's second Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) mission. NASA / James Blair On October 31, four NASA crewmembers returned from “Mars.” Not the actual Red Planet, of course, but a 3D-printed Mars habitat in Houston where the three men and one woman lived for 378 days. Now, the Mars analog astronauts— Ross Elder , Ellen Ellis , James Spicer and Matthew Montgomery —have started telling the world what took place after they disappeared into NASA’s Mars Dune Alpha habitat at the Johnson Space Center on October 19, 2025, for the agency’s second Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) mission. The mission aimed to test the kinds of physical and mental conditions that a team of Mars explorers would endure on the Red Planet, including long-term isolation, disrupted communication with people on Earth and food cultivation. The habitat includes both a base and a mock outdoor environment , so the crew could practice Marswalks. “For more than a year, they have lived in an isolated environment, conducting critical research and helping us better understand what it will take to send humans to Mars,” Vanessa Wyche , director of NASA’s Johnson Space Center, said during a livestream , just before the crew emerged. “Inside just 1,700 square feet, they managed to live with limited resources. They maintained their habitat. They grew crops, and they carried out simulated Mars operations.” After the speech, NASA astronaut Jack Hathaway , who had just completed a mission at the International Space Station, knocked on the door to the Mars habitat, called out “trick or treat” and opened it to reveal the crew’s smiling faces. Since then, the analog astronauts have been participating in post-mission evaluations and debriefs that, along with the data collected during their year in the simulated environment, will help inform future missions to Mars and those closer to home, per a NASA statement . Simulated Mars Habitat in Houston - Take a quick tour! Watch on So, what did they do for all that time? “Most days, we had things that were scheduled, from maintenance and science and engineering activities and some operational activities. So, we often do extravehicular activities, also known as EVAs or spacewalks,” Elder, who was the mission’s commander and test pilot, tells CNN News Central . “We would do drone and rover operations where we control certain equipment outside of the habitat, and we would practice additional data collection for both human health and behavioral sciences.” Each team member brought unique expertise to the mission. Elder was an experimental test pilot at the U.S. Air Force. Ellis, the mission’s medical officer and tactical thinker, is a U.S. Space Force officer. Spicer was the flight engineer and systems specialist, and he has experience in satellite communications and spacecraft development. Montgomery’s diverse background in hardware engineering, robotics, technology startups and independent films made him the “Swiss Army knife of crewmates;” he served as the mission’s science officer and versatile engineer. Quick fact: When was the first CHAPEA mission? The first mission of this kind also lasted 378 days, during which crewmembers Kelly Haston, Ross Brockwell, Nathan Jones and Anca Selariu entered the Mars Dune Alpha habitat on June 25, 2023 , and emerged on July 6, 2024 . Elder tells Fox News that combining their skills created “magic.” But that didn’t happen by accident; the selection process lasted about a year and a half and included personality evaluations by NASA psychologists, Montgomery tells the outlet. What’s more, they got to practice before entering the habitat. “The crew spent a lot of time together prior to the mission, so we got to work on our teamwork and build relationships,” Montgomery tells Nature ’s Kaia Gli

pages.text: Life Cycle of an Exempt Organization | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Life Cycle of an Exempt Organization More In File Individuals Businesses and self-employed Charities and nonprofits Exempt organization types Lifecycle of an exempt organization Before applying for tax-exempt status Applying for tax exempt status How to stay exempt Revocation of exemption Audits Annual filing and forms Charitable contributions Search for charities Education sessions Stay Exempt International taxpayers Governmental liaisons Federal, state and local governments Indian tribal governments Tax exempt bonds Taxpayer identification numbers (TIN) Organizations that meet the requirements of Internal Revenue Code section 501(a) are exempt from federal income taxation. In addition, charitable contributions made to some section 501(a) organizations by individuals and corporations are deductible under Code section 170. This website provides information about points of intersection between organizations and the IRS. The content includes explanatory information, and links to forms that an organization may need to file with the IRS. The materials cover five stages in an organization's life cycle: Starting Out : Creating an organization under state law, acquiring an employer identification number, and identifying the appropriate federal tax classification. Applying for Exemption : Acquiring, completing, and submitting application forms; how the IRS processes applications; and getting help from the IRS during the application process. Required Filings : Annual exempt organization returns, unrelated business income tax filings, Form 8976 – Notice of Intent to Operate Under Section 501(c)(4) , and other returns, reports and notices that an organization may have to file. Ongoing Compliance : How an organization can avoid jeopardizing its tax-exempt status, disclosure requirements, employment taxes, and other ongoing compliance issues. Significant Events : Audits, private letter rulings, and termination procedures. Lifecycle pages — including requirements for exemption — are available for the following types of organizations: Charitable organizations (Code section 501(c)(3)) Public charities Private foundations Social welfare organizations (section 501(c)(4)) Agricultural/horticultural organizations (section 501(c)(5)) Labor organizations (section 501(c)(5)) Business leagues (trade associations) (section 501(c)(6)) Charities and nonprofits topics A-Z Index Educational resources and guidance Publications Audit process Contact IRS exempt organizations About us Page Last Reviewed or Updated: 28-Jun-2026 Share Facebook Twitter Linkedin Print

pages.text: 1.5 Assignment 1 | The Analytics Edge | Sloan School of Management | MIT OpenCourseWare Browse Course Material Course Info Instructor Prof. Dimitris Bertsimas Departments Sloan School of Management As Taught In Spring 2017 Level Graduate Course Info Instructor Prof. Dimitris Bertsimas Departments Sloan School of Management As Taught In Spring 2017 Level Graduate Topics Business Management Operations Management Mathematics Probability and Statistics Topics Business & Management Management Operations Science & Math Mathematics Learning Resource Types notes Lecture Notes theaters Lecture Videos assignment_turned_in Problem Set Solutions assignment Problem Sets Download Course search search GIVE NOW about ocw help & faqs contact us 15.071 | Spring 2017 | Graduate The Analytics Edge Menu More Info Demographics and Employment in the United States In the wake of the Great Recession of 2009, there has been a good deal of focus on employment statistics, one of the most important metrics policymakers use to gauge the overall strength of the economy. In the United States, the government measures unemployment using the Current Population Survey (CPS) , which collects demographic and employment information from a wide range of Americans each month. In this exercise, we will employ the topics reviewed in the lectures as well as a few new techniques using the September 2013 version of this rich, nationally representative dataset. The observations in the dataset represent people surveyed in the September 2013 CPS who actually completed a survey. While the full dataset has 385 variables, in this exercise we will use a more compact version of the dataset, CPSData (CSV) , which has the following variables: PeopleInHousehold : The number of people in the interviewee’s household. Region : The census region where the interviewee lives. State : The state where the interviewee lives. MetroAreaCode : A code that identifies the metropolitan area in which the interviewee lives (missing if the interviewee does not live in a metropolitan area). The mapping from codes to names of metropolitan areas is provided in the file MetroAreaCodes (CSV) . Age : The age, in years, of the interviewee. 80 represents people aged 80-84, and 85 represents people aged 85 and higher. Married : The marriage status of the interviewee. Sex : The sex of the interviewee. Education : The maximum level of education obtained by the interviewee. Race : The race of the interviewee. Hispanic : Whether the interviewee is of Hispanic ethnicity. CountryOfBirthCode : A code identifying the country of birth of the interviewee. The mapping from codes to names of countries is provided in the file CountryCodes (CSV) . Citizenship : The United States citizenship status of the interviewee. EmploymentStatus : The status of employment of the interviewee. Industry : The industry of employment of the interviewee (only available if they are employed). Problem 1.1 - Loading and Summarizing the Dataset Load the dataset from CPSData (CSV) into a data frame called CPS, and view the dataset with the summary() and str() commands. How many interviewees are in the dataset? Problem 1.2 - Loading and Summarizing the Dataset Among the interviewees with a value reported for the Industry variable, what is the most common industry of employment? Please enter the name exactly how you see it. Problem 1.3 - Loading and Summarizing the Dataset Recall from the homework assignment “The Analytical Detective” that you can call the sort() function on the output of the table() function to obtain a sorted breakdown of a variable. For instance, sort(table(CPS$Region)) sorts the regions by the number of interviewees from that region. Which state has the fewest interviewees? Which state has the largest number of interviewees? pages.description: Not many bands can pull off an eight-minute rocker at the Tiny Desk. Chicago's finest lean into its excellent guitar playing, poignant lyrics and a sturdy, Midwestern sensibility.
pages.text: Ratboys: Tiny Desk Concert : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Ratboys: Tiny Desk Concert Not many bands can pull off an eight-minute rocker at the Tiny Desk. Chicago's finest lean into its excellent guitar playing, poignant lyrics and a sturdy, Midwestern sensibility. Ratboys: Tiny Desk Concert September 8, 2026 5:00 AM ET Elle Mannion Credit: Photo: Michael Zamora/NPR Not many bands can pull off an eight-minute rocker at the Tiny Desk. For more than 15 years, the members of Ratboys have honed their craft and earned the space to stretch out. "We've been watching these Tiny Desk concerts since back in the family desktop computer days," Julia Steiner says between songs. With excellent guitar playing, Steiner's sweet voice, poignant lyrics and a sturdy, Midwestern sensibility, Ratboys has become an indie-rock mainstay. While this set draws on this year's Singin' to an Empty Chair and 2023's The Window , there's a deep catalog of exceptional albums to explore. Sponsor Message "This one's for the chillers," Steiner says before playing that miniature epic. The twangy "Black Earth, WI" begins with a midtempo groove, but builds to a headbanging riff that explodes. Across its hard-won career, this is the kind of emotional thrill you come to expect in every Ratboys song. SET LIST "Penny in the Lake" "What's Right?" pages.description: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
pages.text: Universal Declaration of Human Rights | الأمم المتحدة مرحباً بكم في الأمم المتحدة Toggle navigation اختر اللغة الصفحة الرئيسية الإعلان العالمي لحقوق الإنسان الإعلان العالمي لحقوق الإنسان الإعلان العالمي لحقوق الإنسان الإعلان العالمي لحقوق الإنسان الإعلان العالمي لحقوق الإنسان—وثيقة تاريخية هامة في تاريخ حقوق الإنسان—صاغه ممثلون من مختلف الخلفيات القانونية والثقافية من جميع أنحاء العالم، واعتمدت الجمعية العامة الإعلان العالمي لحقوق الإنسان في باريس في 10 كانوان الأول/ ديسمبر 1948 بموجب القرار 217 ألف بوصفه أنه المعيار المشترك الذي ينبغي أن تستهدفه كافة الشعوب والأمم. وهو يحدد،و للمرة الأولى، حقوق الإنسان الأساسية التي يتعين حمايتها عالميا. وترجمت تلك الحقوق إلى 500 لغة من لغات العالم. تحميل الوثيقة الديباجة لما كان الاعتراف بالكرامة المتأصلة في جميع أعضاء الأسرة البشرية وبحقوقهم المتساوية الثابتة هو أساس الحرية والعدل والسلام في العالم. ولما كان تناسي حقوق الإنسان وازدراؤها قد أفضيا إلى أعمال همجية آذت الضمير الإنساني، وكان غاية ما يرنو إليه عامة البشر انبثاق عالم يتمتع فيه الفرد بحرية القول والعقيدة ويتحرر من الفزع والفاقة. ولما كان من الضروري أن يتولى القانون حماية حقوق الإنسان لكيلا يضطر المرء آخر الأمر إلى التمرد على الاستبداد والظلم. ولما كان من الجوهري تعزيز تنمية العلاقات الودية بين الدول، ولما كانت شعوب الأمم المتحدة قد أكدت في الميثاق من جديد إيمانها بحقوق الإنسان الأساسية وبكرامة الفرد وقدره وبما للرجال والنساء من حقوق متساوية وحزمت أمرها على أن تدفع بالرقي الاجتماعي قدماً وأن ترفع مستوى الحياة في جو من الحرية أفسح. ولما كانت الدول الأعضاء قد تعهدت بالتعاون مع الأمم المتحدة على ضمان اطراد مراعاة حقوق الإنسان والحريات الأساسية واحترامها. ولما كان للإدراك العام لهذه الحقوق والحريات الأهمية الكبرى للوفاء التام بهذا التعهد. فإن الجمعية العامة تنادي بهذا الإعلان العالمي لحقوق الإنسان على أنه المستوى المشترك الذي ينبغي أن تستهدفه كافة الشعوب والأمم حتى يسعى كل فرد وهيئة في المجتمع، واضعين على الدوام هذا الإعلان نصب أعينهم، إلى توطيد احترام هذه الحقوق والحريات عن طريق التعليم والتربية واتخاذ إجراءات مطردة، قومية وعالمية، لضمان الاعتراف بها ومراعاتها بصورة عالمية فعالة بين الدول الأعضاء ذاتها وشعوب البقاع الخاضعة لسلطانها. المادة 1. يولد جميع الناس أحراراً ومتساوين في الكرامة والحقوق. وهم قد وهبوا العقل والوجدان وعليهم أن يعاملوا بعضهم بعضاً بروح الإخاء. المادة 2. لكلِّ إنسان حقُّ التمتُّع بجميع الحقوق والحرِّيات المذكورة في هذا الإعلان، دونما تمييز من أيِّ نوع، ولا سيما التمييز بسبب العنصر، أو اللون، أو الجنس، أو اللغة، أو الدِّين، أو الرأي سياسيًّا وغير سياسي، أو الأصل الوطني أو الاجتماعي، أو الثروة، أو المولد، أو أيِّ وضع آخر. وفضلاً عن ذلك لا يجوز التمييزُ علي أساس الوضع السياسي أو القانوني أو الدولي للبلد أو الإقليم الذي ينتمي إليه الشخص، سواء أكان مستقلاًّ أو موضوعًا تحت الوصاية أو غير متمتِّع بالحكم الذاتي أم خاضعًا لأيِّ قيد آخر على سيادته. المادة 3. لكلِّ فرد الحقُّ في الحياة والحرِّية وفي الأمان على شخصه. المادة 4. لا يجوز استرقاقُ أحد أو استعبادُه، ويُحظر الرق والاتجار بالرقيق بجميع صورهما. المادة 5. لا يجوز إخضاعُ أحد للتعذيب ولا للمعاملة أو العقوبة القاسية أو اللاإنسانية أو الحاطَّة بالكرامة. المادة 6. لكلِّ إنسان، في كلِّ مكان، الحقُّ بأن يُعترَف له بالشخصية القانونية. المادة 7. الناسُ جميعًا سواءٌ أمام القانون، وهم يتساوون في حقِّ التمتُّع بحماية القانون دونما تمييز، كما يتساوون في حقِّ التمتُّع بالحماية من أيِّ تمييز ينتهك هذا الإعلانَ ومن أيِّ تحريض على مثل هذا التمييز. المادة 8. لكلِّ شخص حقُّ اللجوء إلى المحاكم الوطنية المختصَّة لإنصافه الفعلي من أيَّة أعمال تَنتهك الحقوقَ الأساسيةَ التي يمنحها إيَّاه الدستورُ أو القانونُ. المادة 9. لا يجوز اعتقالُ أيِّ إنسان أو حجزُه أو نفيُه تعسُّفًا. المادة 10. لكلِّ إنسان، على قدم المساواة التامة مع الآخرين، الحقُّ في أن تَنظر قضيتَه محكمةٌ مستقلَّةٌ ومحايدةٌ، نظرًا مُنصفًا وعلنيًّا، للفصل في حقوقه والتزاماته وفى أيَّة تهمة جزائية تُوجَّه إليه. المادة 11. ( 1 ) كلُّ شخص متَّهم بجريمة يُعتبَر بريئًا إلى أن يثبت ارتكابُه لها قانونًا في محاكمة علنية تكون قد وُفِّرت له فيها جميعُ الضمانات اللازمة للدفاع عن نفسه. ( 2 ) لا يُدان أيُّ شخص بجريمة بسبب أيِّ عمل أو امتناع عن عمل لم يكن في حينه يشكِّل جُرمًا بمقتضى القانون الوطني أو الدولي، كما لا تُوقَع عليه أيَّةُ عقوبة أشدَّ من

pages.title: BLM National Public Lands Day tradition continues in Roswell, New Mexico | Bureau of Land Management Lock
pages.description: In Roswell, it wouldn’t be National Public Lands Day without the members of Girl Scout Troop 18044.
pages.text: BLM National Public Lands Day tradition continues in Roswell, New Mexico | Bureau of Land Management Skip to main navigation Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn BLM National Public Lands Day tradition continues in Roswell, New Mexico Oct 7, 2026 The Oxbow Day Use Area’s beach next to the Pecos River. Photo BLM. In Roswell, it wouldn’t be National Public Lands Day without the members of Girl Scout Troop 18044. They have shown up consistently for more than 25 years to help the Bureau of Land Management with a variety of cleanup events. This year they helped the BLM on Sept. 12 at the Oxbow Day Use Area, where they filled the beds of two pickup trucks with trash. Members of Girl Scouts Troop 18044 try to pull a large piece of trash from under a tree during a National Public Lands Day cleanup event at the Bureau of Land Management Roswell Field Office’s Oxbow Day Use Area on Sept. 12. BLM Photo. Michael McGee, a hydrologist for the BLM’s Roswell Field Office, has helped organize the annual National Public Lands Day cleanup event for about 20 years. He invites Troop 18044 every year, he said, because the event is a good way for troop leaders to teach the importance of keeping public lands clean. Cheryl Martinez, troop leader of Girl Scouts of the Desert Southwest Troop 18044, said she has lost count of how many times the troop has participated in the event, but it is more than 25 times. Members of Girl Scouts Troop 18044 and a parent pick up trash during a National Public Lands Day cleanup event at the Bureau of Land Management Roswell Field Office’s Oxbow Day Use Area on Sept. 12. BLM Photo. “It’s an amazing way for the girls to learn that they need to take care of the area around them and participate in as much community service as they possibly can as kids, so as adults they’ll do it too,” Martinez said. Blake Ingram, an outdoor recreation planner for the BLM’s Roswell Field Office, has helped with the events for 10 years. As an outdoor recreation planner, he is familiar with the importance of teaching Leave No Trace principles. Members of Girl Scouts Troop 18044 and their parents pick up trash during a National Public Lands Day cleanup event at the Bureau of Land Management Roswell Field Office’s Oxbow Day Use Area on Sept. 12. BLM Photo. “It is always important to follow Leave No Trace guidelines when visiting your public lands,” Ingram said. “The philosophy of ‘take only pictures and/or memories, leave only footprints’ goes a long way in protecting your natural resources.” The group of 14 Girl Scouts, parents and troop leaders concentrated on picking up a part of the day-use area next to the Pecos River. Blake Ingram, left, an outdoor recreation planner for the Bureau of Land Management Roswell Field Office, and a Girl Scout Troop 18044 parent pick up trash during a National Public Lands Day cleanup event at the Bureau of Land Management Roswell Field Office’s Oxbow Day Use Area on Sept. 12. BLM Photo. “What a hidden gem,” Helen Cheromiah, assistant troop leader, said in amazement when she saw the beach area next to the river. A line of trees and other vegetation hides most of it from view until visitors are right on top of it. The Roswell Field Office acquired the 240-acre parcel of land next to the river about a year ago and is in the process of developing it for a variety of recreation uses that include fishing, kayaking, and bird watching. Cheryl Martinez, troop leader of Girl Scouts of the Desert Southwest Troop 18044, places trash in the back of a pickup truck during a National Public Lands Day cleanup event at the Bureau of Land Management Roswell Field Office’s Oxbow Day Use Area on Sept. 12. BLM Photo

Close oldnab's Diary Ma rencontre avec Panoramax Posted by oldnab on 26 July 2026 in French (Français) . RETEX : Questions existentielles sur ma rencontre avec panoramax à suivre peut-être : entrée de journal (à venir) : Cartographier mon village entrée de journal (à venir) : Simple model 3D dans OSM Je rappelle que ces entrées de journal ne sont ni des pages de WIKI, ni des conseils d’expert … . Ce sont juste des comptes-rendus d’expérience vécue ou des questionnements en cours mis ici pour servir à toute personne intéressée. A l’origine : mon trekking urbain recyclage (voir entrée de journal trekking urbain ) Lorsqu’il est apparu, en juin 2025, que j’allais passer devant les 1600 (que je pensais alors être 284) points d’apport de mon territoire, un contributeur m’a demandé de penser à tous les photographier et de verser les photos dans Panoramax, ce que j’ai accepté aussitôt. Et me voilà parti avec mon smartphone à la main pour photographier chaque point d’apport (en fait une photo par conteneur et une photo pour le point d’apport constitué par le groupe de conteneurs). J’ai aussi à l’occasion pris des photos de quelques points notables (notamment des oeuvres de street art croisées au bord des chemins). Comme je répondais à une demande sans avoir vraiment réfléchi à l’objectif, je ne me suis posé que peu de questions. J’ai rapidement compris qu’il y avait plusieurs instances de Panoramax avec un répertoire commun (références coordonnées entre les instances) et ai choisi l’ instance OpenStreetMap simplement parceque je répondais à une demande OSM et visais principalement à mettre l’attribut panoramax=xxxxx sur mes conteneurs. Rapidement une question : pourquoi ces photos? Au bout de 800 photos versées (j’ai peut-être l’esprit un peu lent), je me suis interrogé sur l’intérêt de ces versements. J’y voyais deux objectifs possibles : mettre à disposition des photos de terrain pour permettre à d’autres contributeurs de cartographier eux-mêmes à partir de ces photos les éléments qui les intéressent, sans nécessirement avoir à se déplacer. Mais cet objectif me paraissait plutôt faible car d’une part le cartographe, c’était moi et d’autre part je pensais avoir tiré des photos toutes les informations pertinentes pour la base OSM. Il faut comprendre qu’il s’agissait de photos plates (pas 360 degrés) centrées et zoomées sur les conteneurs et ne fournissant que très peu d’informations d’environnement utiles pour d’autres sujets. Je me disais que après mon usage, les photos n’avaient que peu d’intérêt pour les autres. Dès lors, pourquoi les publier et ne pas simplement les consulter localement (sur mon PC) pour mes sessions de cartographie mettre à disposition des photos pour faire connaître les paysages (cartographions nos territoires, autres usages non pressentis par moi ?, marketing touristique ?). Mais là, je me suis rapidement rendu compte que les photos de points d’apport volontaires n’étaient pas très “marketing” : beaucoup de conteneurs sales, beaucoup de conteneurs débordants, beaucoup d’incivilités de riverains déposant des déchets au sol à côté des conteneurs eux-mêmes, … . Lorsque j’ai essayé de partager ces interrogations sur le forum, j’ai essentiellement eu comme réponse : “toutes ces raisons sont valables, et tu fais comme tu le sens …”. Je sentais que ce travail était inutile et j’aurais volontiers arrêté si je ne m’étais pas engagé auprès du contributeur initial. J’ai donc fini mon trekking urbain avec publication dans panoramax de toutes les photos, mais sans grande conviction. Mais plus tard … Un peu plus tard, deux événements m’ont considérablement fait changer d’avis : un contributeur, sur le forum France, a demandé de l’aide pour configurer le code couleur des points d’apport volontaire de sa commune.
