Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/10/nist-report-provides-guidelines-transition-post-quantum-cryptography NEWS NIST Report Provides Guidelines for Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards October 27, 2026 Share Facebook Linkedin X.com Email A finalized report will help organizations transition to NIST’s post-quantum standards, which are necessary to withstand attacks by future quantum computers. The report identifies existing quantum-vulnerable cryptographic standards and the quantum-resistant standards that are designed to replace them. This report describes the timelines and migration activities for federal agencies, and it can serve as a key resource for technology providers and organizations that are developing their quantum-readiness road maps. Credit: J. Wang/NIST and Shutterstock In August 2024, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) released post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards made to withstand the assault of a future quantum computer. Now, the agency has released its high-level road map to help organizations switch to these standards. The report, Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards (NISTIR 8547) , outlines NIST’s official approach and timelines for transitioning away from quantum-vulnerable algorithms to quantum-resistant standards. It is the core technical document meant to inform federal agencies, industry partners and standards organizations about what needs to change and when during the migration to PQC standards — a cryptographic modernization with details that will vary by organization but timelines that apply broadly. “The report describes different use cases and says why one migration might take longer than another,” said NIST mathematician Dustin Moody, who heads the PQC standardization project. “We understand there’s not one strategy that fits all use cases, and we want to help people handle their migration while staying abreast of what’s changing.” While quantum computers are still in development, a sufficiently powerful device — known as a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer — would threaten the encryption methods that protect our confidential electronic information, from email messages to financial statements. Even though the transition to PQC is beginning before such a device appears, today’s encrypted data is already at risk from the “harvest now, decrypt later” threat, where adversaries collect sensitive data now with the intention of decrypting it when quantum technology matures. This threat is one of the main reasons why the transition to PQC is urgent, driving the need to make changes on a well-considered schedule. National Security Memorandum 10 established the year 2035 as the primary target for completing the migration to PQC across federal systems. Executive Order 14412 accelerated this timeline, requiring federal high-value assets and high-impact systems to migrate by 2030 for key establishment and 2031 for digital signatures. NISTIR 8547 supports these migration timelines. While the memorandum applies specifically to federal systems, many organizations that work with the federal government will be affected as well. The NIST report identifies quantum-vulnerable algorithms among NIST’s existing cryptographic standards. The report then provides the transition plan for the quantum-vulnerable algorithms in these standards, referencing the post-quantum algorithm standards NIST published in 2024. “We lay out how certain encryption algorithms people are using today will get phased out,” Moody said. “It’s important to know how a given algorithm might be

pages.title: German Renaissance Master Albrecht Altdorfer Pioneered Landscape Painting. A Work Previously Unknown to Scholars Just Emerged After 70 Years in a Private Collection
pages.description: Painted around 1520, the newly identified painting is one of only three pure landscapes painted in oil by the artist. It depicts a lush forest scene with castle ruins and a rainbow emerging from stormy skies
pages.text: German Renaissance Master Albrecht Altdorfer Pioneered Landscape Painting. A Work Previously Unknown to Scholars Just Emerged After 70 Years in a Private Collection Skip to main content The painting does not appear in Altdorfer’s catalogue raisonné and was only identified earlier this year. Sotheby’s / Rayan Bamhayan For nearly seven decades, a small 16th-century painting of a forest hung in a private collection in Switzerland, unbeknownst to art historians. Now, the 500-year-old work has emerged into the limelight, newly attributed to Albrecht Altdorfer , a German Renaissance artist who pioneered landscape painting. Measuring roughly nine inches long by eight inches wide and dating from around 1520, A Thickly Wooded Landscape With a Rainbow Behind the Trees and a Distant Outcrop to the Right Beneath a Cloud-Laden Sky will head to auction at Sotheby’s in London on December 9. “Every inch of this intimate picture is imbued with an intense mood that transcends its scale … It somehow still feels as modern and immediate as it would have appeared to those seeing it when it was first painted,” George Gordon , co-chair of Sotheby’s Old Masters department, says in a statement . “To add to the known body of work of one of the great masters of the Northern Renaissance is one of the most exciting discoveries imaginable in our field.” The painting, which does not appear in Altdorfer’s catalogue raisonné and was only identified earlier this year, is expected to sell for up to $6.6 million. “We don’t really know what it’s worth because it’s many decades since an Altdorfer last came to the market,” Gordon tells the Art Newspaper ’s Catherine Hickley. “It could fetch more than our estimate.” Until its discovery, scholars knew of just two oil landscapes by Altdorfer, both held in major European museums: Landscape With a Footbridge at London’s National Gallery and Landscape of the Danube Near Regensburg at Munich’s Alte Pinakothek . No Altdorfer painting has appeared on the market since 1980, when the National Gallery acquired Christ Taking Leave of His Mother . Painted in oil on vellum, A Thickly Wooded Landscape is the smallest and most densely forested of Altdorfer’s surviving landscapes in any medium, including engravings, etchings and drawings. In the foreground, tangled evergreens and mossy undergrowth rise without a single human figure in sight, while a distant castle perches atop a rocky outcrop on the right. Overhead, heavy clouds part just enough to reveal a faint glow from the sun, whose light catches a delicate rainbow arching behind the trees. Albrecht Altdorfer, A Thickly Wooded Landscape With a Rainbow Behind the Trees and a Distant Outcrop to the Right Beneath a Cloud-Laden Sky , c. 1520 Sotheby’s / Rayan Bamhayan Together, Altdorfer’s three known oil landscapes form a study in shifting weather and light. While Landscape With a Footbridge unfolds in blue daylight and the Landscape of the Danube canvas glows in warm evening light, the newly surfaced work captures the hushed atmosphere immediately after a rainstorm. “There is a sun, but the sun is really struggling to make its presence felt, and then you have a rainbow which has caught light from the sun,” Gordon tells the Guardian ’s Miatta Mbriwa. Before Altdorfer, European painters tended to treat nature as decorative scenery behind biblical or mythological narratives. “The first independent landscapes in the history of European art were painted by Albrecht Altdorfer,” art historian Christopher S. Wood writes in Albrecht Altdorfer and the Origins of Landscape . “These pictures tell no stories. They are physically detached from any possible explanatory context … They are complete pictures, finished and framed, which nevertheless make a powerful impression of incompleteness and silence.” As art historian Simon Schama observes in Landscape and Memory , “it was the outstanding achievement of Albrecht Altdorfer, in particular, to make the forest itself the natural protagonist.” Did

To measure the degree to which people are concerned about hot-button issues like Internet privacy, social scientists conduct polls in which they interview a large number of people about the topic. In this assignment, we will analyze data from a July 2013 Pew Internet and American Life Project poll on Internet anonymity and privacy , which involved interviews across the United States. While the full polling data can be found on the Pew Research Center’s website , we will use a more limited version of the results, available in AnonymityPoll (CSV) . The dataset has the following fields (all Internet use-related fields were only collected from interviewees who either use the Internet or have a smartphone): Internet.Use : A binary variable indicating if the interviewee uses the Internet, at least occasionally (equals 1 if the interviewee uses the Internet, and equals 0 if the interviewee does not use the Internet). Smartphone : A binary variable indicating if the interviewee has a smartphone (equals 1 if they do have a smartphone, and equals 0 if they don’t have a smartphone). Sex : Male or Female. Age : Age in years. State : State of residence of the interviewee. Region : Census region of the interviewee (Midwest, Northeast, South, or West). Conservativeness : Self-described level of conservativeness of interviewee, from 1 (very liberal) to 5 (very conservative). Info.On.Internet : Number of the following items this interviewee believes to be available on the Internet for others to see: (1) Their email address; (2) Their home address; (3) Their home phone number; (4) Their cell phone number; (5) The employer/company they work for; (6) Their political party or political affiliation; (7) Things they’ve written that have their name on it; (8) A photo of them; (9) A video of them; (10) Which groups or organizations they belong to; and (11) Their birth date. Worry.About.Info : A binary variable indicating if the interviewee worries about how much information is available about them on the Internet (equals 1 if they worry, and equals 0 if they don’t worry). Privacy.Importance : A score from 0 (privacy is not too important) to 100 (privacy is very important), which combines the degree to which they find privacy important in the following: (1) The websites they browse; (2) Knowledge of the place they are located when they use the Internet; (3) The content and files they download; (4) The times of day they are online; (5) The applications or programs they use; (6) The searches they perform; (7) The content of their email; (8) The people they exchange email with; and (9) The content of their online chats or hangouts with others. Anonymity.Possible : A binary variable indicating if the interviewee thinks it’s possible to use the Internet anonymously, meaning in such a way that online activities can’t be traced back to them (equals 1 if he/she believes you can, and equals 0 if he/she believes you can’t). pages.text: Discrimination, harassment, and retaliation | USAGov Skip to main content Discrimination, harassment, and retaliation Federal and state laws protect you from unfair and unwelcome treatment at work. The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) and states enforce discrimination and harassment laws. Workplace discrimination Discrimination happens when an employer treats an employee or job applicant unfairly because of their race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age (40 or older), disability, or genetic information. EEOC laws do not cover all employers. Coverage is often based on the number of employees. Verify if your employer is required to follow the EEOC's rules. Report workplace discrimination Report discrimination to the EEOC. Use the EEOC's public portal to follow the complaint process. Submit an online inquiry. Schedule an interview with someone from the EEOC. Submit a charge of discrimination. Ensure that you meet the time limits for reporting discrimination. In most cases, you must file a charge within 180 calendar days. Learn more about what to expect when you report discrimination. Report discrimination to your local government States and local governments also have anti-discrimination laws. Report discrimination to a local Fair Employment Practices Agency (FEPA). If the discrimination breaks both a state and federal law, the FEPA will also send your complaint to the EEOC. Use the EEOC's directory of field offices to find the FEPA near you. Report discrimination in employment for federal employees and contractors Federal employees and job applicants - report discrimination to the Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) office at the agency where it happened. Follow the EEO’s complaint process within 45 calendar days. Federal contractors - submit pre-complaint inquiries and complaints through the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP). File a discrimination lawsuit You can sue an employer for discrimination. If the lawsuit is based on a federal law, you must file a complaint with the EEOC first. After you file a report with the EEOC, learn how to get legal aid or find a lawyer . Workplace harassment Workplace harassment is unwelcome conduct based on a person’s race, color, religion, sex, national origin, older age, disability, or genetic information. Harassment includes: Offensive jokes, objects, or pictures Name-calling Physical assaults and threats Intimidation Harassment is unlawful when: Enduring the conduct is required to continue employment. It creates a work environment that is intimidating, hostile, or abusive. Sexual harassment Sexual harassment includes unwelcome sexual advances or requests for sexual favors. It can also include offensive comments about someone’s sex. Sexual harassment is unlawful when: It is so frequent and severe that it creates a hostile or intimidating work environment. It results in an adverse employment decision (ex: the person is demoted, denied promotion, suspended, or fired). Report harassment Follow these steps if you experienced harassment at work. If someone at work retaliated against you for reporting harassment, you can file a lawsuit. After you file a report with the EEOC, learn how to get legal aid or find a lawyer . Retaliation Retaliation happens when an employer treats someone poorly because they engaged in a protected activity. Protected activities include: Filing or being a witness in an EEOC charge or investigation Talking to a supervisor or manager about discrimination or harassment Refusing to follow orders that would result in discrimination Resisting sexual advances or intervening to protect others Common retaliation methods include: Firing Demotion Denying benefits Denying promotions Intimidation or threats Report retaliation Use the EEOC's public portal to report retaliation related to discrimination or harassment. You also have the right to file a lawsuit if someone at work retaliated against you. After you file a report with the EEOC, learn

Energy Department Slashes 47 Burdensome and Costly Regulations, Delivering First Milestone in America’s Biggest Deregulatory Effort The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced the first step in the Energy Department’s largest deregulatory effort in history, proposing the elimination or reduction of 47 regulations. Energy.gov May 12, 2025 Estimated Read Time min WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced the first step in the Energy Department’s largest deregulatory effort in history, proposing the elimination or reduction of 47 regulations that are driving up costs and lowering quality of life for the American people. Once finalized, these actions will save the American people an estimated $11 billion and cut more than 125,000 words from the Code of Federal Regulations. These actions, in accordance with President Donald Trump’s Executive Order, “Zero-Based Regulation to Unleash American Energy,” advance President Trump’s promise to restore consumer freedom, lower costs, and unleash American energy dominance. “While it would normally take years for the Department of Energy to remove just a handful of regulations, the Trump Administration assembled a team working around the clock to reduce costs and deliver results for the American people in just over 110 days,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright . “Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, we are bringing back common sense -- slashing regulations meant to appease Green New Deal fantasies, restrict consumer choice and increase costs for the American people. Promises made, promises kept.” The 47 actions include the proposed elimination or modification to dozens of consumer appliance standards, regulations limiting building and energy production and unscientific DEI requirements for grant recipients. pages.title: Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: Protesters say the move will stifle media freedom, while the government insists broadcasters need to cut costs.
pages.text: Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Rachel Flynn Getty Images Organisers said around 400,000 people took part on Sunday Thousands of people have gathered in central Prague to protest against the Czech government's plans to scrap the licence fee and use the state budget to fund public media. Critics say the plans would allow politicians to stifle media freedom. The coalition government - which consists of the populist ANO party and two right-wing Eurosceptic parties - insists the change will not affect editorial independence, but wants broadcasters to cut costs. Parliament passed the first draft of the proposal late last month. Since then, thousands of Czechs have taken part in protests. Czech households currently pay ⁠205 crowns ($9.44; £7.06) a month for public TV and radio. Sunday's protest was organised by the Million Moments for Democracy association which said "roughly 400,000" people had attended. "I know that our entire Czech Television is a guarantee of truth and objectivity," pensioner Milana Rudolfova, 72, told Reuters news agency. "If we do not have public television and radio then unfortunately we will not be able to believe anything anymore." EPA The protesters say the planned changes could allow politicians to stifle media freedom Prime Minister Andrej Babis has insisted the government does not want to control public media. "The funding system is changing, no one wants to control public media, no one wants to dictate to them what they should say and do, no one wants to nationalise them," Babis told the Czech News Agency. "We are doing this because the system is already outdated and most of Europe is going the same way today and others are joining in," he added. Some European countries, including France and Norway, have moved away from the public licence fee model in the last few years. France removed it in 2022 and its public media, which also carries advertising, is now funded by a portion of the income from VAT. Norway abolished its license fee in 2020 and moved its public broadcaster's funding into the national budget. Reuters said the proposal would amount to a 15% cut in funding for the public broadcasters Czech TV and Czech Radio. EPA These protesters held a sign depicting the animated character Vecernicek and saying "We stand with Czech TV" Some protesters wore pointed hats folded out of newspapers as a tribute to an animated character, Vecernicek, who has introduced Czech Television's nightly children's bedtime stories for decades. Critics have compared the government's media bill to changes in Hungary under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who tightly controlled state media when he was in power. Prime Minister Andrej Babis was appointed in December in 2025, and has faced criticism over his coalition's attacks on Czech media. "Political attacks against private and public media have become one of the hallmarks of Andrej Babis' premiership," said Pavol Szalai, Prague Bureau director of international press freedom organisation Reporters Without Borders, in June. pages.title: Scientists discover ‘dragon prince’ dinosaur, the T. Rex's missing ancestor | National Geographic
pages.description: Khankhuuluu mongoliensis was slender with features like no other member of the tyrannosaur family tree.
pages.text: Scientists discover ‘dragon prince’ dinosaur, the T. Rex's missing ancestor | National Geographic SCIENCE Scientists discover ‘dragon prince’ dinosaur, the T. Rex's missing ancestor Khankhuuluu mongoliensis was slender with features like no other member of the tyrannosaur family tree. This illustration depicts how the slender Khankhuuluu mongoliensis may have appeared as it roamed Mongolia during the Cretaceous period. The newest addition to the tyrannosaur family, the discovery of this "dragon prince from Mongolia" sheds light on the origins of Tyrannosaurus rex . Illustration by Julius Csotonyi By Riley Black Published June 12, 2025 Tyrannosaurus rex is a carnivorous icon. Exceeding 40 feet in length and nine tons, the bone-crushing giant stands out as the largest and last of its meat-eating family. Now a new and far smaller tyrannosaur is filling in the famous dinosaur’s evolutionary backstory. ( Meet 'Hellboy': New Spiky-Headed Dinosaur Found) The newest addition to the tyrannosaur family tree is named Khankhuuluu mongoliensis , which translates to “dragon prince from Mongolia.” Described this week in the journal Nature , the dinosaur has been identified for the first time from two partial skeletons that include skull bones, vertebrae, part of the hips, and limb bones. ( Deinocheirus Exposed: Meet The Body Behind the Terrible Hand) Altogether, the pieces reveal a slender tyrannosaur that roamed Cretaceous Mongolia about 86 million years ago and was about 13 feet long—or about the size of juvenile T. rex that would stalk North America 20 million years later. In fact, Khankhuuluu even looked like a juvenile of later, larger tyrannosaurs, with round eye sockets, blade-like teeth, and long, shallow jaws better suited to biting fast rather than hard. (​ T. rex had lips, upending its enduring pop culture image .) Khankhuuluu does more than simply add another dinosaur to the ever-growing roster of dinosaurs. “ Khankhuuluu gives us the origin story of tyrannosaurs,” says University of Calgary paleontologist and study co-author Darla Zelenitsky. Comparing the fossils of mature Khankhuuluu (a, d, g) with fossils of mature Gorgosaurus (c, f, i) and juvenile Gorgosaurus (b, e, h) provides new insights into the evolutionary lineage between the smaller-bodied tyrannosauroids, such as Khankhuuluu , and the larger eutyrannosaurians like Gorgosaurus and Tyrannosaurus . Silhouettes compare the sizes of Khankhuuluu (left) with a juvenile (right) and adult (middle) Gorgosaurus . Scale bars, 5 cm (individual elements) and 1 m (silhouette). Illustration by Voris et al. (2025), Nature Discovering a new tyrannosaur In the early 1970s, Mongolian paleontologist Altangerel Perle found a pair of partial tyrannosaur skeletons in the eastern part of the country. The bones seemed similar to a small tyrannosaur that had been named before, Alectrosaurus . But when University of Calgary paleontologist and study co-author Jared Voris studied the bones during a research trip to Mongolia in 2023, he soon realized that the bones did not belong to Alectrosaurus at all. ( Time to Slay the T. rex Scavenger “Debate”) The bones from the two skeletons belonged to a new form of tyrannosaur that had been waiting to be discovered in collections for half a century. “It had features like a hollow air chamber in side its nasal bone, which no other tyrannosaur species has,” Voris says. The fossils deserved a new name and have been recategorized as Khankhuuluu . Voris has found tyrannosaurs hiding in plain sight before. In 2020, Voris and colleagues named the 80 million-year-old tyrannosaur Thanatotheristes from bones assigned to another species found in Alberta. SCIENCE Why Everything We Thought We Knew About T. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Volunteer sees cycle of stewardship through her work on historic cave Apr 24, 2026 Cavers are a special breed. They like exploring tight dark places, undeterred by mud and whatever may be lurking. Give a caver a task to do, while down in a cave’s depths, and they will stay underground for hours and come back again a few weeks later to do it again. As it turns out, these are the same unique qualities found in some of the Bureau of Land Management’s most remarkable volunteers. The Bureau recently recognized one, in particular, with this year’s BLM Outstanding Volunteer Achievement Award. Carrin Rich from Carnuel, New Mexico, led cave restoration work at the Fort Stanton-Snowy River Cave National Conservation Area, along with a team of more than two-dozen volunteer cavers from New Mexico and Texas. The cavers were from local chapters of the National Speleological Society and included a handful of high school students, as well. “There is a ready supply of prepared and willing active cavers in New Mexico and West Texas,” Rich said. “Cavers love getting their hands dirty and doing work.” The work is physically and mentally demanding. Not everyone can spend that amount of time underground. Often, Rich will lead a team of four to five cavers for 12- to 15-hour expeditions. The team will stay overnight on the surface before and after the expedition to prep the gear and later to clean the gear. “The work consists of washing cave formations – stalactites, stalagmites, and walls of flow stone,” she said. “We’re literally washing the cave with sprayers, washers, and sponges.” Carrin Rich leads volunteers into an expedition at the Fort Stanton-Snowy River Cave National Conservation Area. Photo courtesy of Carrin Rich. The team is removing muddy boot prints, handprints, and marks from packs brushing against the walls during years of people roaming the caves. The marks, debris, and mud left behind don’t just change the appearance of the cave but can also alter the environment for species that depend on that environment. The Fort Stanton Cave has more than 56 miles of passages mapped, making it the second longest cave in New Mexico, the seventh longest cave in the U.S., the 32nd longest in the world, and the largest cave the BLM manages. Evidence shows that humans have used the Fort Stanton-Snowy River Cave for hundreds of years for various purposes, but probably never as a dwelling. The U.S. Army established Fort Stanton in 1855, to facilitate settlement of east central New Mexico, representing the first opportunity for non-indigenous visitors to explore the cave. “There’s all sorts of evidence of their visitation, like historic signatures carved in the rock and markings from torches,” Rich said. “We also do trail maintenance… we’re restoring a trail through the main section of the cave.” The goal of their work is to allow the public to someday be able to visit. The cave is closed to visitors due to white-nose syndrome, a fast-spreading disease that is sharply reducing bat populations nationwide. Even for scientists, researchers, and restorers, the cave is closed half the year to protect bat hibernation. The short six-month caving season is a challenge for the volunteers. Over that period, Rich will run four to six expeditions into the cave. Another challenge is water, which can be logistically difficult getting to the worksite since it’s heavy and they need to haul it manually. High school students will often help with supplying water. Close oldnab Mapper since: April 25, 2025 Last map edit: November 17, 2026 Home location Villennes sur Seine Company Retraité après une longue carrière dans les réseaux et la sécurité informatiques Link towards english version Je suis retraité depuis 2020 après une longue carrière dans les réseaux et la sécurité informatiques. Depuis, je consacre mon temps à marcher (sans prétentions de difficultés : pas de montagne, mais quand même de l’ordre de 2000 km par an) et à faire des maths (c’est un passe-temps depuis toujours, principalement en algèbre autour des équations fonctionnelles). J’ai découvert OSM très récemment (printemps 2025) à l’occasion de mon passage de Windows à Linux MINT et de mes premiers essais de smartphone avec un LineageOS (Android déGafamisé). ce qui suit n’engage bien sûr que moi J’ai d’abord considéré qu’il s’agissait d’une application de cartes éditables librement avant de découvrir qu’il s’agit en fait : d’une base de données cartographique mondiale, avec contributions libres, et surtout ne répertoriant et n’exposant que des données libres de droit, sous licences le plus libre possible. d’un considérable écosystème applicatif open-source exploitant cette base de données cartographique pour des utilisations très diverses pour contribuer ou exploiter de façon intelligente et efficace, voire ludique. Pour ceux que j’ai regardés et utilisés : Id, JOSM, OsmTracker, Osmose, StreetComplete, taginfo, overpass, panoramax, NSI Pour ceux que je n’ai fait que survoler pour l’instant : MapRoulette, Mon Commerce OSM, Libre Charge Map, H.O.T. pour exploiter la base de données à des fins diverses visant des publics variés Celle qui m’a amené à OSM : OsmAnd, puis leaflet et uMap Mais aussi cartes.app, un paquet d’applications pour randonnées pédestres, pour circulation cycliste, … que j’ai à peine entrevues. et bien sûr d’un ensemble d’applicatons propriétaires s’appuyant sur la base cartographique OSM (pas toujours avec les marques contributives, d’ailleurs) J’ai donc créé un compte, rejoint OpenStreetMapFrance (pas obligatoire) et essayé de comprendre suffisamment les principes, limites, recommandations pour pouvoir contribuer de façon efficace. Je suis donc un assidu lecteur du WIKI et du forum (même si parfois des conversations entières m’échappent - comme les échanges sur les relations pour les chemins de randonnée, linéaire ou en réseau,..-) Je suis passé rapidement de Id à JOSM et me suis rendu compte qu’il y avait (au moins) deux mondes dans la contribution : la contribution personnelle “de proximité” où chacun peut améliorer la cartographie de son environnement (StreetComplete est un bon exemple pour l’amélioration des tags mais il y a aussi les ajouts d’équipements qui ne sont pas encore dans OSM, des modifications de voirie assez récentes, etc). Ces contributions sont satisfaisantes et incitatives mais restent contraintes par le nombre de contributeurs sur le terrain concerné. Ces contraintes peuvent être combattues par les challenges (je n’ai ni participé ni créé mais le concept me parait passionnant) la contribution de masse qui consiste à partir d’une source disponible et à injecter dans OSM le résultat d’un traitement sur cette sourve. Bien sûr, il y a plusieurs contraintes dans ce cas : la source disponible doit être acceptable, en particulier : elle doit être disponible dans des contraintes de licence compatibles avec celles de OSM (libres mais aussi permettant la rediffusion sous la licence utlisée par OSM). pages.title: More Than 3,000 Tarantulas Were Found Hidden in Socks During a Major Wildlife Trafficking Bust at an Airport in Lima, Peru
pages.description: According to Peruvian officials, the three European travelers—including one who's been identified as a "renowned tarantula researcher"—could have made around $1.68 million from the creepy-crawly loot
pages.text: More Than 3,000 Tarantulas Were Found Hidden in Socks During a Major Wildlife Trafficking Bust at an Airport in Lima, Peru Skip to main content Officials found thousands of eggs, hatchlings and adult spiders. SERFOR Authorities in Peru say they have foiled a plot to smuggle more than 3,000 tarantulas—including species not yet described in scientific publications—out of the country. After receiving an anonymous tip , officials intercepted three travelers—two German citizens and one Polish citizen—at Jorge Chávez International Airport in Lima as they were checking in at the boarding area. When they searched the travelers’ luggage, they found thousands of eggs, hatchlings and adult spiders hidden in socks, according to a November 4 statement from the National Forest and Wildlife Service of Peru (SERFOR). “We noticed that some of them were moving,” Cora Suárez , a SERFOR forest and wildlife control technician who works at the airport, tells the Agence France-Presse . “There were small ones and large ones.” Workers used slender wooden sticks to gently brush the spiders into clear plastic containers. Once officials are done investigating them, the tarantulas will be taken to an authorized breeding center. Authorities are still trying to identify all the species. SERFOR The travelers were trying to fly to Germany. Instead, they were detained by the Peruvian National Police’s environmental crimes unit and now face criminal charges. Officials have not released the names of the individuals. However, one of the travelers was a “renowned tarantula researcher,” according to the statement, per a translation by the New York Times ’ Amanda Holpuch. Authorities suspect the individuals were smuggling the spiders for private collections, research and the exotic pet trade. Suárez tells the AFP that one tarantula can sell for roughly $560 in Europe, meaning the smugglers could have made around $1.68 million from the more than 3,000 tarantulas they had hidden in their suitcases. The spiders originated from several different parts of Peru, including the cities of Cajamarca, Cusco and Junín, and the regions of La Libertad and Loreto. Officials are still trying to pinpoint all the species in the loot but said it included several brightly colored creatures. Did you know? Wildlife trafficking Wildlife trafficking is the world’s fourth-largest form of organized crime, with an estimated annual value of up to $20 billion . So far, officials have identified Thrixopelma lagunas , also known as the Peruvian blue zebra or the blue birdeater. Authorities also found members of the Pamphobeteus genus, which are among the largest tarantulas in the world. One species was P. antinous , which is considered a vulnerable, legally protected threatened wildlife species in Peru. These arachnids are commonly known as Bolivian blue-leg birdeaters or steely blue legs. Some of the spiders are species that scientists haven’t formally described, including members of the Antikuna and Avicularia genera. “The traffickers made a meticulous selection to include different species,” Suárez says in the statement, per a translation by the Times . #LoÚltimo. El Serfor y Aduanas incautaron en el Aeropuerto Internacional Jorge Chávez más de 3000 tarántulas que eran transportadas de manera oculta dentro de equipajes de ciudadanos extranjeros, quienes tenían previsto viajar a Alemania. Los infractores fueron detenidos por la Policía Nacional del Perú (PNP) y se les abrirá un proceso administrativo sancionador. #NoTeCompresUnDelito 🔗 Más información en: https://t.co/XhEKaixkZ1 — Serfor Perú (@SerforPeru) November 5, 2026 According to Mongabay ’s Spoorthy Raman, trafficking these spiders to the European Union is a relatively low-risk, high-reward pursuit. This test provides a quantitative way to compare the performance of students from different parts of the world. In this homework assignment, we will predict the reading scores of students from the United States of America on the 2009 PISA exam. The datasets pisa2009train (CSV) and pisa2009test (CSV) contain information about the demographics and schools for American students taking the exam, derived from 2009 PISA Public-Use Data Files distributed by the United States National Center for Education Statistics (NCES). While the datasets are not supposed to contain identifying information about students taking the test, by using the data you are bound by the NCES data use agreement , which prohibits any attempt to determine the identity of any student in the datasets. Each row in the datasets pisa2009train.csv and pisa2009test.csv represents one student taking the exam. pages.description: Donalds is governor-elect in state that leads the US in the number of executions, with its 20th this year taking place next week
pages.text: Former death row prisoners call Byron Donalds to halt future Florida executions | Florida | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Florida governor-elect Byron Donalds speaks during Nasa's Max Power event at the Kennedy Space Center, in Merritt Island, Florida on 6 November. Photograph: Joe Skipper/Reuters View image in fullscreen Florida governor-elect Byron Donalds speaks during Nasa's Max Power event at the Kennedy Space Center, in Merritt Island, Florida on 6 November. Photograph: Joe Skipper/Reuters Florida Former death row prisoners call Byron Donalds to halt future Florida executions Donalds is governor-elect in state that leads the US in the number of executions, with its 20th this year taking place next week Richard Luscombe in Miami Thu 12 Nov 2026 13.58 EST Last modified on Thu 12 Nov 2026 14.00 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Three exonerated former death row prisoners in Florida have called on incoming governor Byron Donalds to halt the state’s record run of executions and review the cases of all 235 prisoners who are now condemned. At a press conference in Tallahassee on Thursday hosted by the advocacy group Floridians for Alternatives to the Death Penalty (FADP), the men said they were seeking a roundtable discussion with Donalds, a Republican, as well as the state’s new legislative leaders in pursuit of a moratorium. Florida leads the country in both executions and exonerations, and next Thursday’s scheduled execution of convicted murderer Thomas Overton will be the state’s 20th this year, one more than the record of 19 set in 2025. Herman Lindsey, who was exonerated in 2009 after spending three years on death row after his wrongful conviction for the 1994 killing of a pawn shop owner, said he hoped Donalds would be more sympathetic than termed-out governor Ron DeSantis, who will have signed 50 death warrants by the time he leaves office. All but two of those death sentences were carried out during DeSantis’ second term, which will end in January. “Mr Byron, you don’t look like you are a person that is barbaric,” said Lindsey, who is also executive director of Witness to Innocence, an organization that supports death row exonerees. “I hope that you consider re-evaluating the death penalty before you use it, and investigate. “It’s not about him ending the death penalty, but I want to give him the knowledge and assist him to learn anything that he needed about the death penalty so he can make valid, right decisions.” Lindsey’s call was backed by Joaquín José Martínez and Seth Penalver, other Witness to Innocence advocates who were also among the 30 condemned prisoners exonerated in Florida since the death penalty was reintroduced nationwide in 1976. “Thirty men were convicted and sentenced to die, and those convictions were wrong,” said Penalver, who was in prison for 18 years, 13 on death row, for a triple homicide in 1994 for which he was later acquitted. “Each of us had to find a way to get someone to listen and look again. When you are the person facing execution, you cannot afford for everyone to assume that somebody else has already checked everything. “You need someone who is willing to examine the evidence and take your questions seriously.” Martínez was sentenced to death in 1997 for a double murder and exonerated in 2001 when a court heard that some evidence against him was fabricated by one of the victim’s relatives, who worked at the investigating sheriff’s office, and that several informants were promised rewards for false testimony. “It’s easier to believe that a person that’s exonerated, who is taken out of death row, got out because he was lucky than it is to believe that our system is failing,” he said. “It’s time to evolve; it’s time to change. Energy.gov May 13, 2025 Estimated Read Time min RIYADH, SAUDI ARABIA — U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on energy cooperation and a Memorandum of Cooperation (MOC) on critical minerals with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s Minister of Energy H.R.H. Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud and H.E. Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources Bandar Alkhorayef, respectively. Secretary Wright signed the documents as a member of the United States delegation led by President Donald J. Trump. The intention to sign the MOU was announced during Secretary Wright’s trip to Saudi Arabia in April of this year. The signings coincided with President Trump’s announcement that he secured a $600 billion investment commitment from Saudi Arabia. “President Trump and I are excited to unveil two historic deals between the United States and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, advancing our shared vision of global energy addition by better developing our energy resources, growing our energy infrastructure, enhancing our research relationships, and more,” Secretary Wright said . “These deals on energy and critical minerals as well as the historic investment commitments made earlier today, forge powerful partnerships that will ensure President Trump’s vision of prosperity at home and peace abroad is fully realized.” “I’d like to express my sincere thank you to H.R.H. Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman and H.E. Bandar Alkhorayef for weeks of productive dialogue that have made this significant milestone possible. Together, we’re building a future of affordable, reliable, and secure energy for the United States, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and our allies around the world.” Background: The MOU for energy cooperation, signed by Secretary Wright and Saudi Arabia’s Minister of Energy, H.R.H. Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud, explores the potential for innovation, development, deployment of energy infrastructure in the two countries, and providing access to clean cooking solutions in developing countries. The MOU also highlights the intent to collaborate in various fields including petroleum refining and refined products trading, electricity generation technologies and energy storage systems, and artificial intelligence projects to accelerate deployment of energy-driven innovations. The two sides also outlined areas for cooperation on civil nuclear energy, including safety, security, and nonproliferation programs; vocational training and workforce development; U.S. Generation III+ advanced large reactor technologies and small modular reactors; uranium exploration, mining, and milling; and safe and secure nuclear waste disposal. The United States and Saudi Arabia also signed a MOC creating a framework for cooperation to strengthen and secure supply chains for critical minerals mining and processing. The two intend to explore joint ventures and investment opportunities, including in refining and processing facilities, and in workforce and research institutions that will ensure continued innovation related to mineral exploration, extraction, and processing. pages.title: Meet 'Hellboy': New Spiky-Headed Dinosaur Found | National Geographic
pages.description: A Triceratops cousin unearthed in Canada is so elaborately adorned "it blows your mind," one paleontologist says.
pages.text: Meet 'Hellboy': New Spiky-Headed Dinosaur Found | National Geographic Stubby horns over the eyes of Regaliceratops peterhewsi (pictured in an artist's imagining) reminded its discoverers of the comic book character Hellboy. Art by Julius T. Csotonyi. Courtesy of Royal Tyrrell Museum, Drumheller, Alberta. WEIRD & WILD Meet 'Hellboy': New Spiky-Headed Dinosaur Found A Triceratops cousin unearthed in Canada is so elaborately adorned "it blows your mind," one paleontologist says. By Devin Powell Published June 4, 2015 • 4 min read Triceratops has a new cousin with a devilishly good nickname: "Hellboy." Paleontologists who excavated the fossil skull of the horned beast from a steep cliff in Canada had a hell of time chipping the 600-pound (270-kilogram) specimen from the hard rock—hence its pet name. Only after freeing the fossil did the crew discover the moniker's pop culture connection. "There are these really stubby horns over the eyes that match up with the comic book character Hellboy ," says study leader Caleb Brown , a paleontologist at the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology in Alberta, Canada. Though it had much smaller horns on its brow than its iconic cousin, the newfound dinosaur boasted a sizable horn on its snout and a fabulous frill on its head. (Also see " New Big-Nosed Horned Dinosaur Found in Utah .") The frill, or bony head protrusion, of Regaliceratops is so elaborate it "blows your mind," one scientist says. Photograph by Sue Sabrowski, Courtesy Royal Tyrrell That crown of triangular bone spikes inspired its Latin scientific name : Regaliceratops peterhewski, the first word of which translates to "royal horned face," according to the study, published June 4 in the journal Current Biology . The second word is the name of the geologist who first spotted the fossil about a decade ago, Peter Hews. ( See more bizarre dinosaurs .) "The size of these frill ornamentations blows your mind," says David Evans , a paleontologist at the Royal Ontario Museum in Canada who wasn't involved in the study. "If you found them by themselves, you'd almost think they were stegosaur plates." Fancy Headgear This latest addition to the clan of horned herbivores known as chasmosaurs lived about 68 million years ago during the Cretaceous period —just before the dinosaurs went extinct. Regaliceratops was especially showy for its time: Triceratops and other chasmosaurs from the same age tended to be conservative critters with smooth, unadorned frills. (See " New Horned Dinosaur Had a Funky Frill .") But fancy frills had been the fashion in a different lineage of horned dinosaurs that died out millions of years before Regaliceratops , the centrosaurs. Regaliceratops acquired its retro look thanks to convergent evolution, a process in which distantly related organisms independently evolve similar traits under similar conditions—such as the streamlined body shapes of ocean-dwelling sharks and dolphins. Expect the Unexpected Hellboy wasn't the first chasmosaur with extravagant headgear, either. Recent finds have turned up funky older relatives that lived alongside the centrosaurs, including the 76-million-year old Kosmoceratops . Every time you think you've seen it all some new, weird ceratopsian shows up. Nick Longrich , Paleontologist, University of Bath Dubbed the horniest dino in the world, Kosmoceratops boasted 15 horns and spikes on its head, including some on its forehead that curled downward like bangs. As with the tiny horn nubbins over Regaliceratops ' eyes, these curly protrusions would have offered little protection against predators and instead may have been used, like peacock feathers, to attract mates. (See "' Large-Nosed Horned Face' Nasutoceratops Debuts.") As the family tree of the horned dinosaurs (the ceratopsians) continues to expand, paleontologists have learned to expect the unexpected. Mac Ayres: Tiny Desk Concert September 3, 2026 5:00 AM ET Ashley Pointer Credit: Photo: Zayrha Rodriguez/NPR It's so easy to fall in love with the music of Mac Ayres . His hands-on approach to R&B is such a refreshing departure from the mainstream. Behind the Desk, Ayres brings a stunning band — including longtime collaborator, bassist and music director Declan Miers — and a selection of tunes from across his catalog. Tiny Desk Mac Ayres: Tiny Desk (Home) Concert This set is profoundly satisfying, tastefully arranged and always in the pocket. Opening with "Sunny & 62," Ayres builds lush harmonies with vocalists Brandon Lee Harris and Jess Schnieder before keyboardist Daniel Abraham Jr. cues the unmistakable motif of "Calvin's Joint." Ayres debuts "Please Come Home," an unreleased song co-written with Tiny Desk alum Carrtoons , leaning into '70s soul as guitarist Josh Porter creates a cinematic backdrop. "Where U Goin' Tonight" brings a subtle disco vibe and lets Ayres flex his stunning vocal range; the grooves, anchored by drummer Brian Richburg, are completely undeniable. Sponsor Message "This song changed my life," he tells the crowd before the set ends. Nearly a decade ago, "Easy" turned so many of us onto his music; it's also how Ayres ended his Tiny Desk (home) concert . And now the crowd joins in a sing-along, bringing everything full circle. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Oklahoma Field Office celebrates the certifications of five Petroleum Engineering Technicians Apr 16, 2026 Students gain knowledge in the field of a drill rig's mud circulating system during PET Module 2 Drilling. BLM Oklahoma Field Office employees Micheal Balliet and Ashley Babb served as instructors at Module 4 of the Petroleum Engineer Technician (PET) certification course in Oklahoma City in June. In addition to the instructors, the Oklahoma Field Office had four petroleum engineering technicians in the training. Students at PET Module 5 Gas Measurement are demonstrating Bernoulli's Principal. By blowing out of the mask, the tongues on the mask stick out. All newly hired PETs must first complete a formal mathematics course, preferably at a local community college, before attending the 3100-01 Oil and Gas Compliance Certification School modules. Each module is two weeks long and the course consist of six modules over a year’s time. The total duration for the series of modules encompassing formal training is usually followed by a period of on-the-job training and preparation for certification. Students visit a Blowout Preventer Equipment Supplier during PET Module 2 Drilling. The students are learning about the internal component of an annular preventer which is used to close in the wellbore during drilling. A BLM PET’s job involves balancing industry needs with regulatory requirements. Essentially, PETs ensure compliance with Federal regulations and policies related to oil and gas operations either on public lands or Federal sub-surface minerals. PETs evaluate applications for permit to drill, perform site inspections and monitor operations to prevent spills, contamination, and other environmental hazards. They also advise industry operators, landowners, and stakeholders on Federal oil and gas regulations. In addition, they maintain detailed records of well production, drilling activity, and compliance status to support industry operations and Federal decision-making. Students at PET Module 4 Oil Measurement gauge an oil storage tank to determine the quantity and quality of the oil in the tank. “It was awesome to see the representation from the Oklahoma Field Office at the training. Ashley and Micheal both did a great job presenting, and it was nice to have four students in the module,” said acting BLM Oklahoma Field Manager Evelyn Rodriguez. The Oklahoma Field Office currently has 12 PETs who conduct inspections across Oklahoma, Kansas and Texas, as well as provide oversight to Indian mineral owners. pages.text: Freedom of Information Act | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Freedom of Information Act The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) provides that any person has the right to request access to federal agency records or information. Like all federal agencies, the U.S. Department of Labor (DOL), is required to disclose records requested in writing by any person. However, agencies may withhold information pursuant to nine exemptions and three exclusions contained in the statute. FOIA applies only to federal agencies and does not create a right of access to records held by Congress, the courts, or by state or local government agencies . Under the statute, all federal agencies are required to respond to a FOIA request within 20 business days excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays. This period does not begin until the request is received by the FOIA office that maintains the records sought. Please use the link(s) below to learn how to make a FOIA Request. We encourage the public to explore VETS’ and DOL’s websites or use our search option to see if the information you seek is already available on our website. How to make a FOIA request DOL Guide for Requesting FOIA Records FOIA Appeal and Judicial Review How to Submit a FOIA Request FOIA requests can be submitted to the VETS' appropriate national or regional office by mail, email, or fax. The request as well as the envelope itself should be clearly marked "Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Request" with as much information as possible describing the record(s) being sought. By Email You may submit a FOIA request by sending an email to foiarequests@dol.gov . FOIA requests sent to any other DOL email addresses will not be accepted as a properly submitted request. By Mail You may mail a FOIA request to VETS national office or a regional office . If you cannot determine the proper agency to which your FOIA request should be addressed, you may mail a direct request (with as much information as possible describing the records sought) to the: Office of the Solicitor Division of Management and Administrative Legal Services 200 Constitution Ave NW Room N-2420 Washington, DC 20210 By Fax You may fax a FOIA request to "VETS FOIA Staff" at 202-693-4755 or "Solicitor FOIA Staff" at 202-693-5389. Additional Contacts VETS Service Center Contacts FOIA requesters seeking information concerning their submitted FOIA request; or to obtain general information on our agency’s FOIA practices and resources may contact the VETS' national service center contact or their regional service center contact. DOL FOIA Service Center Contacts Within the Labor Department, each agency processes its own FOIA requests. Therefore, a request will receive the fastest possible response if it is addressed directly to the agency the requester believes has the records. Send email to: foiarequests@dol.gov Once your FOIA request has been assigned a FOIA tracking number, you can also find out the status of your submitted FOIA requests using DOL's FOIA tracking system . FOIA Information The 2007 FOIA amendments created the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) to offer mediation services to resolve disputes between FOIA requesters and federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation. Using OGIS services does not affect your right to pursue litigation. You may contact OGIS in any of the following ways: 8601 Adelphi Road - OGIS College Park, MD 20740-6001 Email: ogis@nara.gov Web: https://www.archives.gov/ogis It is important to note that the services offered by OGIS, are not an alternative to filing an administrative FOIA appeal. Questions concerning this guidance can be addressed to the DOL's FOIA Public Liaison, Mr. Thomas Hicks. He can be reached by email at hicks.thomas@dol.gov or by phone at 202-693-5427. pages.text: How Do I Create a Good Password? | NIST Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/cybersecurity-and-privacy/how-do-i-create-good-password Information technology Cybersecurity and privacy How Do I Create a Good Password? And what else can I do to secure my online accounts? Passwords are one of the least secure ways of protecting your online information. Credit: JMiks/Shutterstock You may have come to the NIST website looking for tips on how to make a more secure password — and you will find that in this article. But experts have long considered passwords to be insecure. Even the longest, most complex passwords can be guessed, stolen or otherwise compromised. As new ways to verify your identity have emerged, cybersecurity experts at NIST encourage you to avoid relying on passwords whenever possible. But passwords seem inescapable. What should you do when you are required to create one? NIST maintains digital identity guidelines . These widely used guidelines include a ton of useful advice for IT professionals on how to protect and verify the identity of the users of their website or application. But if you are not an IT pro, and you just want some advice on how to make your online accounts more secure, read on. In this article, we’ll explain why passwords are inherently insecure. If you must use one, we’ll give you some tips to make your passwords easier to use and harder to steal. We’ll also explain how you can increase your account security by using tools such as multifactor authentication. How do hackers steal passwords? One of the most common ways that hackers steal a password is by tricking you into giving it to them. This is called phishing. For example, an attacker might send you a link to a website that looks identical to a website you trust. Even if you’re careful and knowledgeable, it can be difficult to detect a fake website. In a phishing attack, the fake website is actually controlled by an attacker. It will ask you to log in, just like the real website, and when you do, you will have unknowingly given away your username and password. That’s just one example of the many ways that someone, anywhere in the world, might get you to send them your password. It doesn’t matter how long or complicated your password is if an attacker is able to trick you into sending it to them. But I’ve never been phished. Are my passwords safe to use? Even without phishing, many passwords can be easily guessed. In general, people are bad at choosing unique passwords. “The worst password I can think of is ‘password’ or ‘12345,’” says Ryan Galluzzo , who leads NIST’s Digital Identity Program. “Those are at the top of an attacker’s list for potential attacks.” They are also two of the most common passwords. You might think your password isn’t that bad — that someone who was trying to log into your account wouldn’t get enough tries to guess it exactly. That’s right to some extent; login pages for most websites only let you guess a handful of wrong passwords before you are locked out. But attackers don’t usually guess passwords through the public login page. The guessing starts after a website has had a data leak and the attacker gets their hands on a copy of all the encrypted passwords. The passwords can be decrypted by guessing them correctly. And once an attacker has an offline copy of the encrypted passwords, they can make as many guesses as they like. With a modern PC, an attacker can attempt to decrypt 100 billion passwords per second. That’s a lot of guesses! If you printed out 100 billion passwords on single-spaced, double-sided pieces of paper, the sheets would fill about four semitrucks. But even with all those guesses, hackers will want to be as efficient as p

pages.title: Florida Is Facing Its Worst Dengue Outbreak in Decades, With at Least 524 Locally Acquired Cases. Here's What to Know
pages.description: Most dengue infections cause mild flu-like symptoms or no symptoms at all. But at least one person has died from this year’s outbreak in Florida, where health experts worry the disease will become more common in the future
pages.text: Florida Is Facing Its Worst Dengue Outbreak in Decades, With at Least 524 Locally Acquired Cases. Here's What to Know Skip to main content Dengue is a viral disease transmitted by mosquitoes. Joao Paulo Burini via Getty Images This year, the Florida Department of Health has recorded a staggering 524 locally acquired cases of dengue , a mosquito-borne viral disease, as of October 31. That’s the highest number recorded there since the disease returned to the state in 2009 , according to Forbes ’ John Drake. For context, only 62 locally acquired cases were documented in 2025. Most infected people either do not show symptoms or experience only mild illness . But in early September, a Tampa-area woman named Gay Rabb Small died of dengue on her 80th birthday, after developing a tremor and going to the emergency room, per the New York Times ’ Anemona Hartocollis. Later that month, three counties in Florida declared local emergencies over the illness, and in October, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued a national emergency response to dengue. “It is very unusual to have transmission in the United States,” Eva Harris , an infectious diseases expert at the University of California, Berkeley, tells the Times . “This is so very much of an eye-opener.” Here’s what to know about dengue. What is dengue? Dengue is a viral disease spread by mosquitoes, mainly the species Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus , which are both present in Florida , among other places. The disease is more common in tropical and subtropical regions , where these biting insects thrive, than in temperate climates. Around three in four infected people are asymptomatic or have mild flu-like symptoms, such as fever, headache, nausea and rash. Muscle and joint pain is another common symptom, which is why the disease is sometimes called “breakbone fever.” Symptoms usually appear within two weeks of being bitten by an infected mosquito and clear up after a week or two. However, one in four dengue cases becomes severe. Those symptoms include extreme abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, rapid breathing and blood in vomit or stool, and anyone experiencing them should seek medical care. These signs often appear after the fever goes away, and people who have previously been infected are at a greater risk of severe dengue. Individuals who recover from dengue can continue feeling fatigued for several weeks. Can you prevent or treat it? Although dengue vaccines exist , none are currently approved for use in the United States. They’re authorized in nations where the disease is more common, such as Argentina, Brazil, Indonesia and Thailand. Vaccines are also challenging to develop, because dengue has four distinct but closely related virus types , called 1, 2, 3 and 4. When infected with one type, the body builds up pathogen-fighting antibodies against it, and immunity lasts for life, reports the Associated Press ’ Mike Stobbe. But if later infected with a different type of dengue, the antibodies might fail to attack that virus and even help the pathogen enter immune cells and make copies of itself. Experts say the best way to protect yourself is to avoid mosquito bites. Cover up with loose-fitting long sleeves and pants, apply insect repellent with DEET and control for mosquitoes in and around your home, such as by removing stagnant water—where young mosquitoes live —and treating your yard with insecticide. Additionally, there are no specific treatments for dengue. For those with mild symptoms, physicians recommend drinking plenty of fluids and resting. Ill individuals can take acetaminophen to alleviate fever and pain, but they should avoid nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), such as ibuprofen and aspirin, because they can increase the risk of bleeding. People with severe dengue might need oral or intravenous fluids or even blood transfusions. Why is dengue so bad in Florida this year? La entidad puede recibir el valor total del crédito porque el IRS trata la cantidad del pago electivo como un pago de impuestos. Luego lo contamos como pago en exceso en la declaración y lo reembolsamos a la entidad. Nota: El pago electivo a veces también se conoce como "pago directo", que no debe confundirse con el método de pago del IRS . La transferibilidad permite a las entidades que no pueden utilizar el pago electivo pero califican para un crédito tributario elegible, transferir todo o una parte del crédito a un comprador tercero a cambio de efectivo. El comprador y el vendedor negociarían y aceptarían las condiciones y los precios. pages.title: Wilderness Character - Wilderness (U.S. National Park Service) Lock
pages.description: The Wilderness Act mandates the NPS to preserve wilderness character - comprised intangible and tangible qualities.
pages.text: Wilderness Character - Wilderness (U.S. National Park Service) Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you've safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to the main content Skip to the footer section National Park Service Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Contact Us Wilderness Character Bear Creek runs unimpeded through the Hain Wilderness in Pinnacles National Park, demonstrating its Natural, Untrammeled, and Undeveloped Qualities of wilderness character. Photo Credit: NPS/Gavin Emmons The term " wilderness character " was first referenced in the 1964 Wilderness Act . The Act states that federal agencies, like the NPS, are responsible for preserving the wilderness character of wilderness areas. Wilderness character is a holistic concept based on the interaction of (1) biophysical environments primarily free from modern human manipulation and impact, (2) personal experiences in natural environments relatively free from the encumbrances and signs of modern society, and (3) symbolic meanings of humility, restraint, and interdependence that inspire human connection with nature. This includes intangible qualities like developing a connection with nature, inspiration, relaxation, or a sense of adventure. Wilderness character also includes five tangible qualities associated with the biophysical environment: Great Sand Dunes Wilderness Photo Credit: NPS/Patrick Myers Natural Quality Ecological systems are substantially free from the effects of modern civilization. This quality recognizes the importance of healthy, intact ecosystems and challenges us to limit our negative effects on the functionality of these systems. Haleakala Wilderness Photo Credit: Ken Simpson Untrammeled Quality Wilderness is essentially unhindered and free from the intentional actions of modern human control or manipulation. This quality recognizes the importance of people co-existing with our planet, where people practice humility and are very selective and thoughtful about actions we take that might interfere with the rest of the natural world. Shenandoah Wilderness Photo Credit: NPS/Katy Cain Undeveloped Quality Wilderness is essentially without permanent improvements or the sights and sounds of modern human occupation. This quality recognizes that while developments, like structures or use of motorized equipment, are very important and appropriate in many places, wilderness gives us a chance to consider more traditional ways of interacting with the rest of the natural world. Marjory Stoneman Douglas Wilderness in Everglades National Park NPS Photo Opportunities for Solitude or Primitive and Unconfined Recreation Quality Wilderness provides opportunities for solitude or a primitive and unconfined type of recreation. This quality recognizes many recreational activities are appropriate and compatible with wilderness, especially those that rely on human power and give us a chance to 'unplug.' Bridge Canyon Wilderness in Lake Mead National Recreation Area Photo Credit: Peter Landres Other Features of Value Quality Wilderness may also contain ecological, geological, or other features of scientific, educational, scenic, or historical value. This quality recognizes the centuries-old and rich cultural traditions of indigenous people and other residents to lands now managed as wilderness. These important cultural and historical connections can be explored in this quality, along with the values we place on things like scenery, science, and education. pages.text: 2.5 Assignment 2 | The Analytics Edge | Sloan School of Management | MIT OpenCourseWare Browse Course Material Course Info Instructor Prof. Dimitris Bertsimas Departments Sloan School of Management As Taught In Spring 2017 Level Graduate Course Info Instructor Prof. Dimitris Bertsimas Departments Sloan School of Management As Taught In Spring 2017 Level Graduate Topics Business Management Operations Management Mathematics Probability and Statistics Topics Business & Management Management Operations Science & Math Mathematics Learning Resource Types notes Lecture Notes theaters Lecture Videos assignment_turned_in Problem Set Solutions assignment Problem Sets Download Course search search GIVE NOW about ocw help & faqs contact us 15.071 | Spring 2017 | Graduate The Analytics Edge Menu More Info Detecting Flu Epidemics via Search Engine Query Data Flu epidemics constitute a major public health concern causing respiratory illnesses, hospitalizations, and deaths. According to the National Vital Statistics Reports published in October 2012, influenza ranked as the eighth leading cause of death in 2011 in the United States. Each year, 250,000 to 500,000 deaths are attributed to influenza related diseases throughout the world. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the European Influenza Surveillance Scheme (EISS) detect influenza activity through virologic and clinical data, including Influenza-like Illness (ILI) physician visits. Reporting national and regional data, however, are published with a 1-2 week lag. The Google Flu Trends project was initiated to see if faster reporting can be made possible by considering flu-related online search queries – data that is available almost immediately. Problem 1.1 - Understanding the Data We would like to estimate influenza-like illness (ILI) activity using Google web search logs. Fortunately, one can easily access this data online: ILI Data - The CDC publishes on its website the official regional and state-level percentage of patient visits to healthcare providers for ILI purposes on a weekly basis. Google Search Queries - Google Trends allows public retrieval of weekly counts for every query searched by users around the world. For each location, the counts are normalized by dividing the count for each query in a particular week by the total number of online search queries submitted in that location during the week. Then, the values are adjusted to be between 0 and 1. The csv file FluTrain (CSV) aggregates this data from January 1, 2004 until December 31, 2011 as follows: “Week” - The range of dates represented by this observation, in year/month/day format. “ILI” - This column lists the percentage of ILI-related physician visits for the corresponding week. “Queries” - This column lists the fraction of queries that are ILI-related for the corresponding week, adjusted to be between 0 and 1 (higher values correspond to more ILI-related search queries). Before applying analytics tools on the training set, we first need to understand the data at hand. Load “FluTrain.csv” into a data frame called FluTrain. Looking at the time period 2004-2011, which week corresponds to the highest percentage of ILI-related physician visits? Which week corresponds to the highest percentage of ILI-related query fraction? Problem 1.2 - Understanding the Data Let us now understand the data at an aggregate level. Plot the histogram of the dependent variable, ILI. What best describes the distribution of values of ILI? A. Most of the ILI values are small, with a relatively small number of much larger values (in statistics, this sort of data is called “skew right”). B. The ILI values are balanced, with equal numbers of unusually large and unusually small values. C. Most of the ILI values are large, with a relatively small number of much smaller values (in statistics, this sort of data is called “skew left”). pages.text: CodentGIS's Diary | Flow of the River Ilagan | OpenStreetMap Select Language Loading... Close CodentGIS's Diary Flow of the River Ilagan Posted by CodentGIS on 15 November 2026 in English . It’s been two months since I started to edit the Ilagan River again. While I had done so in the past, way before these two months, this period turned out to be a great adventure that I’m still hiking. It was a time after Project CaCau . When I put it to an end, I felt not only disappointed, but ambitious. Why exactly? Well, I don’t know, but the roaring engine I had used to keep me going through that project was still on, and I couldn’t just stop it. So, I had to redirect it somewhere. For a bit, I had just redirected it to OSM. I experimented with multiple things and tried to pick up my old stuff. But one in particular caught my attention. A while ago, I was editing the river area of the Ilagan River. I never picked it up again until then. Despite that, it just stuck. Starting in the 15th of September, I got into the flow of the edits, and I never stopped. I didn’t just do the main river either. I had also started doing its tributaries because my satisfaction didn’t get put with just that. Then, suddenly, the Bintacan River got finished, then the Nanaguan, and then I was suddenly speeding through the headwaters of the Abuan. I was now pushing 2K-3K edits a day, with the little free time I had. My satisfaction didn’t stop; I had also started mapping the landslide areas. Now, at that point, I was satisfied. I had forgotten Project CaCau and its shadow that burdened me. Then, I realized: why not make this run official? Make it a project? So, I did. Enter, Project KarayanIlagan . It meant “Ilagan River” in Ilocano: Karayan as River, and Ilagan as itself. Nothing changed in my workflow; just that I finally had a name to keep it going and back it up, putting hashtag comments for it as #KarayanIlagan (and later on with #ChasingWaterways for my fellow mappers’ initiative), and to give it a history and recognition. Now, we place it here, right now. By the time I made this diary, I had gotten to 2nd in most map changes in the whole Philippines . I am still going, editing the waters of the River Abuan to contribute to my own project, ChasingWaterways, OpenStreetMap, and the Philippines itself. Eventually, I will finish, but for now, I will keep going. To the people who see this, please hope for me to succeed. God bless, and Mabuhay! Location: Bangag, Ilagan, Isabela, Cagayan Valley, Philippines Discussion Comment from GOwin on 16 November 2026 at 02:02 What an interesting journey — congratulations on all the progress you’ve made! It’s lovely to see you finding your way out of the muck after the “muddy experience” you shared in your diary last time. And thanks for the shout-out to our #ChasingWaterways initiative. You might find our FAQs and pointers useful as you continue your work: https://hackmd.io/@osmph/H1ZB1J9Tle If you happen to come across open MapRoulette tasks in your area that you’ve already resolved, would you be up for updating their status? It could save other contributors valuable time and effort. As the FAQ entry explains, a “virtual challenge”¹ can help you, with your friends, focus on tasks near an area you’re interested in. Here’s one for tasks across all open challenges in Isabela as an example: https://maproulette.org/browse/virtual/6895 . It’s also easy to create your own virtual challenge, either visually or using a GeoJSON file to define an area. These links are temporary and, as far as I know, currently last only 24 hours. ¹ Hard to say whether this will be supported in MapRoulette v4, which is in active development and intended to replace the current interface. As an alternative, especially if you work alone, consider “multi-tasking mode” instead. Leave a comment Log in to leave a comment

حقوق متساوية، وأن نبيّن الأحوال التي يمكن في ظلها تحقيق العدالة واحترام الالتزامات الناشئة عن المعاهدات وغيرها من مصادر القانون الدولي، وأن ندفع بالرقي الاجتماعي قدماً، وأن نرفع مستوى الحياة في جو من الحرية أفسح. وفي سبيل هذه الغايات اعتزمنا أن نأخذ أنفسنا بالتسامح، وأن نعيش معاً في سلام وحسن جوار ، وأن نضم قوانا كي نحتفظ بالسلم والأمن الدولي، وأن نكفل بقبولنا مبادئ معيّنة ورسم الخطط اللازمة لها ألاّ تستخدم القوة المسلحة في غير المصلحة المشتركة ، وأن نستخدم الأداة الدولية في ترقية الشؤون الاقتصادية والاجتماعية للشعوب جميعها، قد قرّرنا أن نوحّد جهودنا لتحقيق هذه الأغراض ولهذا فإن حكوماتنا المختلفة على يد مندوبيها المجتمعين في مدينة سان فرانسيسكو الذين قدّموا وثائق التفويض المستوفية للشرائط، قد ارتضت ميثاق الأمم المتحدة هذا، وأنشأت بمقتضاه هيئة دولية تُسمّى "الأمم المتحدة". الفصل الأول: مقاصد الهيئة ومبادئها المادة 1 مقاصـد الأمـم المتحدة هي: حفظ السلم والأمن الدولي، وتحقيقاً لهذه الغاية تتخذ الهيئة التدابير المشتركة الفعّالة لمنع الأسباب التي تهدد السلم ولإزالتها، وتقمع أعمال العدوان وغيرها من وجوه الإخلال بالسلم، وتتذرّع بالوسائل السلمية، وفقاً لمبادئ العدل والقانون الدولي، لحل المنازعات الدولية التي قد تؤدي إلى الإخلال بالسلم أو لتسويتها. إنماء العلاقات الودية بين الأمم على أساس احترام المبدأ الذي يقضي بالتسوية في الحقوق بين الشعوب وبأن يكون لكل منها تقرير مصيرها، وكذلك اتخاذ التدابير الأخرى الملائمة لتعزيز السلم العام. تحقيق التعاون الدولي على حل المسائل الدولية ذات الصبغة الاقتصادية والاجتماعية والثقافية والإنسانية وعلى تعزيز احترام حقوق الإنسان والحريات الأساسية للناس جميعاً والتشجيع على ذلك إطلاقاً بلا تمييز بسبب الجنس أو اللغة أو الدين ولا تفريق بين الرجال والنساء. جعل هذه الهيئة مرجعاً لتنسيق أعمال الأمم وتوجيهها نحو إدراك هذه الغايات المشتركة. المادة 2 تعمل الهيئة وأعضاؤها في سعيها وراء المقاصد المذكورة في المادة الأولى وفقاً ‏‏ للمبادئ الآتية: تقوم الهيئة على مبدأ المساواة في السيادة بين جميع أعضائها.‏ لكي يكفل أعضاء الهيئة لأنفسهم جميعاً الحقوق والمزايا المترتبة على صفة العضوية يقومون في حسن نية ‏بالالتزامات التي أخذوها على أنفسهم بهذا الميثاق. يفض جميع أعضاء الهيئة منازعاتهم الدولية بالوسائل السلمية على وجه لا يجعل السلم والأمن والعدل الدولي عرضة للخطر. يمتنع أعضاء الهيئة جميعاً في علاقاتهم الدولية عن التهديد باستعمال القوة أو استخدامها ضد سلامة الأراضي أو الاستقلال السياسي لأية دولة أو على أي وجه آخر لا يتفق ومقاصد "الأمم المتحدة".. يقدّم جميع الأعضاء كل ما في وسعهم من عون إلى "الأمم المتحدة" في أي عمل تتخذه وفق هذا الميثاق، كما يمتنعون عن مساعدة أية دولة تتخذ الأمم المتحدة إزاءها عملاً من أعمال المنع أو القمع. تعمل الهيئة على أن تسير الدول غير الأعضاء فيها على هذه المبادئ بقدر ما تقتضيه ضرورة حفظ السلم ‏والأمن الدولي.‏ ليس في هذا الميثاق ما يسوغ ”للأمم المتحدة“ أن تتدخل في الشؤون التي تكون من صميم السلطان الداخلي ‏لدولة ما، وليس فيه ما يقتضي الأعضاء أن يعرضوا مثل هذه المسائل لأن تحل بحكم هذا الميثاق، على أن ‏هذا المبدأ لا يخلّ بتطبيق تدابير القمع الواردة في الفصل السابع.‏ الفصل الثاني : العضوية المادة 3 الأعضاء الأصليون للأمم المتحدة هـم الدول التي اشتركت في مؤتمر الأمم المتحدة لوضع نظام الهيئة الدولية المنعقد في سان فرانسيسكو، والتي توقّع هذا الميثاق وتصدّق عليه طبقاً للمادة 110، وكذلك الدول التي وقّعت من قبل تصريح الأمم المتحدة الصادر في أول كانون الثاني/يناير سنة 1942، وتوقّع هذا الميثاق وتصدّق عليه. المادة 4 ‏العضوية في "الأمم المتحدة" مباحة لجميع الدول الأخرى المُحبة للسلام، والتي تأخذ نفسها بالالتزامات التي يتضمنها هذا الميثاق، والتي ترى الهيئة أنها قادرة على تنفيذ هذه الالتزامات وراغبة فيه . قبول أية دولة من هذه الدول في عضوية "الأمم المتحدة" يتم بقرار من الجمعية العامة بناءً على توصية مجلس الأمن . المادة 5 يجوز للجمعية العامة أن توقف أي عضو اتخذ مجلس الأمن قِبَله عملاً من أعمال المنع أو القمع، عن
